title: Ravens Must Be Willing To Shake-Up Their Coaching Staff ASAP, Longtime Raiders Team Pres Amy Trask Contends
full_text:
The Jesse Minter hire wasn’t supposed to be some three-year plan.
The Ravens claimed the rookie head coach – clearly under the thumb of the front office regime that wanted a first-time staff – was uniquely positioned to be wise beyond his years because he came from their “winning culture.” He knew their systems and players and was a product of them and their front office and overarching philosophies in many ways. And now, entering the 10th game of this regime, all involved seem woefully out of their depth .
They are fielding a non-competitive football product , and once again raised eyebrows around the NFL at the trade deadline by seemingly pretending they are this contending team that they are not . They want to send a signal that things are largely okay – save for maybe benching a player or two and tweaking the lineup. But to experienced eyes around the football world – former Ravens assistants like Wink Martindale, who created the defensive system Minter is using , and Marvin Lewis, who ran the defense on Baltimore’s first Super Bowl team - big problems are obvious.
And when longtime Raiders team president Amy Trask, now an NFL analyst for CBS Sports, joined me on “The Daily Flock” this week, she made it clear that very much in the Ravens’ front office and coaching staff must be under serious review ASAP. Trask, who saw plenty of upheaval and coaching mistakes during her time with Oakland/Los Angeles, sees some major red flags and in her own understated way, agreed with how overmatched this staff has appeared to be at times, and raised the specter of the need for potential coordinator changes by 2027.
Nothing much seems pointed in the right direction on offense, defense or special teams; 30-year-old offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is as under scrutiny as Minter and general manager Eric DeCosta right now. And with four straight losses, a prediction for blowing leads and most players underachieving, Monday night is a must-win against the winless Chargers and this franchise must start embracing its new realities.
Trask, who was trained by owner Al Davis who knew the game from all angles (including coaching), sees ample cause for concern through this half season.
The fact the Ravens have already blown three games this season in which they held a lead of 10-points or more in the second half (continuing a nasty trend from John Harbaugh’s regime), and that they are the worst second-half team in the NFL (scoring the second-fewest points and allowing the most) must be addressed in a meaningful manner, she contends.
“Take a look at everything,” Trask explained. “Why is that happening? Are they not making good halftime adjustments? Is it a talent? Are there holes on the roster? … Are they doing things in the first half that are tells as is said? …
“Is the opposing team seeing things that they are doing? That is a tell. Is it a training issue? Is it a conditioning issue? Are players wearing out again? Holes in the roster, weaknesses in the roster, or is it coaching? All of that needs to be evaluated.”
As to whether the decision to pair a coaching staff this naïve with a roster this experienced with this heavy of expectations begs corrections, Trask believes corrections are in order.
“I'm a big, big, big, believer when you have a first-time head coach, you need some people around that head coach,” Trask said. “Whether it's an offensive coordinator, a defensive coordinator, an assistant head coach, an adviser to the head coach, you need a seasoned voice in the ear.
“Simply someone who's been through this and may have some observations that a first-time head coach isn't. Look, my college, my Cal bears - first time head coach, first time offensive coordinator, first time defensive coordinator. So, this is something I've been thinking a lot, as relates to my Golden Bears, who I will always love no matter the record …
“And I'll tell you, I would not be surprised if this is something the Ravens do. I wouldn't be the least bit surprised - and I would expect that they would do this - if not before then, then in the off season. Even if they retain the offensive and defensive coordinators, bring in someone senior as a defensive adviser and offensive adviser, both.  But bring some seniority in there that can give some um seasoned perspective.”
We called for reaching out to Lewis or Martindale weeks ago. We’d be shocked if the Ravens reacted in season now and made any move this bold. We agree with Trask, whole-heartedly, that considering different voices calling plays next season must be in order if this team is going to try to reach the postseason in what could be Lamar Jackson's last season in Baltimore , at all costs.
They also are going to be hard pressed not to make significant alterations to the composition of this staff barring quick and sweeping improvement, no matter what.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Jacoby Brissett Compares Learning Ravens Offense To Crash Course Ahead Of Debut
full_text:
Since landing in Maryland late last week after being acquired by the Baltimore Ravens in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick, veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett has been dialed in on learning the playbook and building chemistry with his new teammates.
Head coach Jesse Minter declared him the team's starter for their Week 10 primetime matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers earlier this week after he spent last weekend around the building with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle and other support staff getting up to speed.
"It's definitely a crash course," Brissett said.." No question. [I want to] really just come out, try to do my job to the best of my ability, be a good teammate, kind of keep things simple [and] try not to overcomplicate this thing right now and just take it one day at a time."
Brissett feels confident about the progress he's made in learning the offense and building chemistry with his new teammates, but knows there's plenty more prep work to do to ensure they are successful and can consistently execute the game plan at a high level.
"I don't think my preparation is stopping today, but I think I have the right coaches that are helping me along the way. Obviously, the players are helping me when I'm in the huddle and things of that nature, so it's been good. Like I said, I feel confident, but obviously [there's] still some work to do."
Following each of the Ravens' first two practices of the week, he spent an extended period on the field throwing to some of the team's top targets in the passing game, including two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, talented rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane and vertical speedster Devontez Walker.
"It's just going through the plan," Brissett said. "We do a bunch of walk-throughs. You see the practice, stuff after practice and things of that nature. I just think it's that, and then just them telling me what they need from me more than I need from them. They have to do the hard part. I have to do the easy part and find them and put the ball where it's supposed to go. It's just [about] the communication on both sides."
His arrival and insertion into the starting lineup will undoubtedly be a major boost for Flowers, who has only logged three catches for six receiving yards on 11 targets in the past two games after averaging just over 101 receiving yards in his first six appearances. Given Brissett's prowess as an accurate passer over the middle of the field and at the intermediate level, Lane could finally get a chance to live up to the training camp and preseason buzz he built up.
"He's a guy who's played 11 years, so he's seen a lot of football," Doyle said. "He's seen a lot of these pictures, and he'll let it rip. He can really drive the ball. Those are all things that I'm really excited about with him."
Brissett's first impressions of Doyle have been similar to those of so many others who've crossed paths with him during his ascension up the coaching ranks and since he landed his first play-calling role in Baltimore.
"He's a great football mind," Brissett said. "He's been very receptive to information from me and getting to know each other, whether that's on the field and off the field and trying to bridge the gap over a relationship that you kind of have to fast-track before Monday.
"But he's been awesome. What he's thinking as far as the play structure and then obviously how we're attacking the defense, he's very vocal about it. I think that cleans up the communication. I know what he's thinking."
Even before the Ravens and Minter issued an official statement on Friday, confirming the reports on the exact nature of franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson's thumb injury and outlining a timeline for a potential return this season , Brissett wasn't concerned with how long he'd have the reins of the offense.
"I don't even really want to get into it," Brissett said. "It's one of those things where you kind of just take it day by day, and then future things happen when future things happen. But, I'd be a fool to look forward. I'm trying to learn teammates, players, coaches, plays and get ready for a game. The last thing I'm worried about is something that's going to happen down the road."
The Ravens mark the seventh different team that the journeyman backup and stop-gap starter will have played for in his 11-year career, and this isn't the first time he's been traded for by a team looking to salvage their season. He was acquired by the Indianapolis Colts ahead of the 2017 season after their then-franchise quarterback Andrew Luck suffered a shoulder injury that caused him to miss the entire year.
Over the course of his career, he's compiled a record as a starter of 23-50 and has played in several different offensive systems, which he believes has made him very adaptable to being thrust into new environments.
"I think that's just it. You are around a lot of different people, a lot of different systems, different situations, every year," Brissett said. "Just being able to be flexible, that's what's kept me in this league for so long, and this is no different. [I'm] just excited for this opportunity, and [I'm] trying to make the most of it."

title: Buffalo Bills' Recent Improvement on Defense Comes With Major Caveat
full_text:
After starting out the season with one of the worst defenses in the NFL, the Buffalo Bills have seen quite the turnaround in recent weeks.
Over their last three games, Buffalo has surrendered just 28 points in total, and the defense has not permitted a touchdown in 11 straight quarters.
That is certainly a welcomed site after the you-know-what show the defense was over the first six games, but there's a major caveat to those showings.
There is one common bond between the Bills' last three games: the lack of quality in the quarterback play.
In Week 8 versus the Baltimore Ravens, the Bills faced rookie Joe Fagnano after both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley exited early with injuries.
In Week 9, the Minnesota Vikings were forced to start Carson Wentz because of an injury to Kyler Murray.
We foolishly thought that might actually be worse for the Bills , but Wentz went on to throw up one of the worst quarterback performances we've ever seen.
It was so bad that the Vikings turned around and traded a third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for Kirk Cousins, who was an immediate upgrade for Minnesota's offense in Week 10. Cousins was also the last quality quarterback the Bills faced for an entire game and he dropped a pair of touchdowns and 313 yards on Buffalo's defense en route to 30 points.
Then, on Sunday, the Bills knocked New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith out of the game twice , and he did not return the second time.
That led to rookie Cade Klubnik getting the football and the results were about what we expected, with Klubnik barely completing 50% of his passes for 137 yards and a pick.
Of course, the Bills can't control who they face at quarterback and it's certainly great to see the defense played well against signal-callers the unit should be able to stop, but we also know Buffalo is going to be playing a lot better competition when the games matter most, so the defense isn't out of the woods yet.
Buffalo will meet the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 11 and they will not provide a test for the Bills' defense, either.
That's because starter Malik Willis is on injured reserve, which will likely lead to another start for Kyle McCord, who was not good in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the also lowly Indianapolis Colts.
McCord completed just 53.1% of his passes for 209 yards and zero touchdowns to zero picks.
We will have to wait until Week 12 for the Bills' next true test. That game will see the Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs and superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
Mahomes needs no introduction, especially for Bills fans who have seen plenty of him during the Josh Allen era.
Mahomes has dominated the Bills in the postseason to the tune of a 4-0 record, a 74% completion rate, 290.8 passing yards per game and nine touchdowns to zero picks.
The Chiefs quarterback has actually struggled against the Bills in the regular season during his career, with Mahomes sporting a 1-5 record in six contests while completing just 61.7% of his passes for an average of 258.7 yards per game and 10 touchdowns to eight interceptions.
That said, nobody should (or will) be taking Mahomes lightly when he walks into Highmark Stadium in Week 12. We'll know a lot more about Buffalo's defense after that game.

title: Josh Allen Surpasses Peyton Manning for NFL Record in Bills' Win vs. Jets
full_text:
Josh Allen, you've done it again.
It seems like every time the Buffalo Bills ' MVP signal-caller takes the field, he's setting another NFL record .
Well, this one may be his most impressive yet.
In Allen and the Bills' eighth win of the year against the AFC East rival New York Jets, he was able to notch three more touchdowns this year. He passed for one through the air and rushed for two more on the ground, bringing his season total to 24 (13 passing, 11 rushing).
Those three scores now put him at 325 scored thus far in his career. It's a record-setting mark, passing Peyton Manning for the most in player's first 10 seasons. But what's even more impressive is thinking of how quickly Allen accomplished the feat.
Josh Allen is UNREAL 🤯 Allen is only in his 9th season, and Patrick Mahomes is currently in his 10th season 👀 pic.twitter.com/EKmqOZOIzM
What is craziest when thinking about this record is that Allen has a season and a half left to extend it for a player's first 10 seasons. It goes to show just how dominant of a player the 2024 NFL MVP has been since entering the league in 2018.
To think he's outpaced three current Hall of Famers (Manning, Dan Marino, and Brett Favre), as well as future HOF selections (Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes), showcases the caliber of player Allen has been in Buffalo.
It also goes to show that as strong as Allen has been with his arm, his legs have helped amplify his game to a legendary status.
The Wyoming product is now tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for the NFL's lead in rushing TDs. The win over the Jets marks the fourth time on the year that Allen has scored two or more TDs on the ground.
His rushing stats really are silly. The NFL's all-time rushing TD leader from the QB position is now tied for 14th in NFL history in rushing TDs at 90 with HOF running backs Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin. This is for a player who already has 233 career TD passes.
He's also notched his fourth-consecutive season with 10 or more rushing TDs, pushing his total to 52 since 2023, tied for the most in the NFL in that span with Derrick Henry.
Allen has now rushed for 10+ touchdowns in 4 straight seasons, tying Jalen Hurts (2021-24) for the longest streak by a QB in NFL history. https://t.co/hyyiUkRwWj
But what might be scariest for NFL defenders? Despite these records and the Bills being the NFL's top offense in terms of points and yards per game, Allen and the offense aren't even playing their best ball yet.
"Didn't play too well in the first half," said Allen to NFL on CBS sideline reporter Melanie Collins after the game. "In the second half, we scored on a four-play, two-play, and a one-play drive. So, the explosiveness is there. We've gotta clean some stuff up. We're 8-1, gotta find a way to learn from this one, flush it, and move on to the next week."
Buffalo's offense really has a chance to tighten things up as the season progresses. And if it does, we should expect that much more TDs from Allen to extend this record.
"He just keeps on running. He's our workhorse." Josh Allen on what James Cook means to the Bills offense. 🎤: @Melanie_Collins pic.twitter.com/yEY5eLVd8w

title: How Amani Hooker Fared in Week 10 Debut With Buffalo Bills
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills saw the debut of their newest player in Week 10 when safety Amani Hooker, who was acquired via trade last week , took the field in the 31-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.
While we knew ahead of time that Hooker was going to play in the game just days after his was acquired, we weren't sure just how much the veteran safety would see the field.
Well, according to Pro Football Focus , Hooker played a whopping 70 snaps, which was more than any Bills defender in the contest, so the Bills did not ease him in. Hooker played 49 of those snaps at free safety, 12 in the box and eight in the slot for Buffalo, so defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard used him all over.
Hooker's ability to play that many snaps and line up in different spots in his debut is a testament to how quickly he picked up Buffalo's defense.
Hooker has seen better days in coverage, but he was still solid.
The former Tennessee Titan gave up receptions on four of six targets thrown his way (66.7%) for 47 yards and no scores. He permitted 21 yards after the catch and a long gain of 17.
PFF gave him a respectable 66.1 grade in coverage, the sixth-best mark on the team. Hooker notched one pass break-up and he nearly had two picks but couldn't come down with either one.
All in all, it was a pretty solid day on the back end for Hooker, especially when you consider it was his debut.
PFF gave Hooker another respectable grade in run defense, with the former fourth-round pick notching a 64.9 in that area.
That is below his season-long mark of 83.9, but it's still pretty solid.
Hooker totaled seven tackles, the third-most on the team, and his missed tackle percentage was just 10%.
We did see Hooker get shaken up during the contest, which led to him getting a trip to the blue medical tent.
However, the new Bills safety emerged rather quickly and got back into the game and finished without incident.
We'll be keeping an eye on the injury report for him this coming week, but Hooker should be good to go for Week 11.
After the game, Hooker talked about how much it meant to him that the Bills wanted to trade for him, and he loved the fact that Buffalo trusted him to play as much as he did so soon.
"Just for the opportunity for a team that's winning to want me, to put me out here Game 1 and trust me, my job during the week was to show them that they can trust me and everyone took me in and just showed love across the board," Hooker said per WIVB's Josh Reed .
"It was a challenge and I love challenges like that," he said of his limited preparation time for his debut. "It kind of felt like training camp, where I gotta be in the book constantly non-stop. I really just wanted my guys that were gonna be out here to trust me, to know I was gonna be in the right spot. That was big for me and I think we did a good job."
As you'd expect, head coach Joe Brady was impressed with what Hooker was able to do on Sunday.
"I'm so impressed with Amani Hooker. The fact that he was able to play this whole game on a few days when we didn't practice. Kind of speaks to who he is and how much he's gonna help us and, shoot, he almost made a couple of plays on the ball," said Brady.
Hooker was no doubt impressive on Sunday and even better days are ahead the more comfortable he gets with his new team.

title: Five Winners & One Loser From Bills Rout vs. Jets in Week 10
full_text:
It was a slow start for the Buffalo Bills, who had a 10-9 lead over the New York Jets in the third quarter. Then, the offense took off.
From that point on, the Bills outscored the Jets 21-3, leaving MetLife Stadium with a 31-12 victory . Buffalo was the more physical team and improved to 8-1 on the season. They're also 5-0 on the road this year, proving to be a tough opponent no matter where they play.
With this win in the books, let's see who stood out as both winners and losers for the Bills.
New York was set to punt the ball away for the second consecutive drive as they were facing a fourth-and-six. They decided to line up to attempt to draw the Bills offside, and it worked. A hard count got Ed Oliver to move, and that led to a five-yard penalty.
The Jets converted on the fourth-and-short following the flag, and that helped them pull off a 12-play drive, ending with a 41-yard field goal from Jason Sanders to make it a 7-3 game. Overall, Oliver didn't have a bad game, but this is a play he surely regrets.
Second-round pick TJ Parker entered this game with 1.5 sacks and more than doubled that number against the Jets. Parker had plenty of success rushing the New York quarterbacks, sacking backup Cade Klubnik twice in the game. He now has 3.5 sacks as he's beginning to show why Brandon Beane made him the team's top pick this year.
New York cut the lead to 10-9 following their first drive of the second half, but the Bills were able to respond thanks in large part to Dalton Kincaid . The star tight end caught a pass from Josh Allen and took off for a 54-yard gain. That helped them score their second touchdown of the game on a four-play, 62-yard drive.
BIG PLAY DALTON KINCAID BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LcQtgpdRSJ
Against the Minnesota Vikings, DJ Moore was rather quiet with just 25 yards on three receptions. He was much better against the Jets and even topped his yardage total from Week 9 with one reception in the third quarter.
Buffalo was up 17-12 and looking to put the Jets away when Allen fired a deep pass to Moore. The veteran wideout hauled it in and scored a touchdown on a 45-yard reception. Moore finished with 90 yards and a touchdown on four receptions, looking like the WR1 Buffalo knows he can be.
ALLEN TO DJ MOORE FOR 6 BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hfrUwKQlws
Other than an ugly second-half pick, this was another strong game from Josh Allen. The numbers weren't elite, as he had just 196 yards passing, but he made the plays when they were necessary. That includes three total touchdowns and a fourth-down conversion. Allen and the Buffalo offense are good enough that they can drop 31 points like this even when he's not throwing all over the field.
James Cook was special in this one. He continued to run tough throughout the game, and when he got in the open field, he was tough to bring down. His biggest gain was in the fourth quarter, when he broke free for a 74-yard touchdown to put the game away.
74-YARD TD FOR JAMES COOK BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DFRLVP17FL
In all, Cook had 157 yards on just 18 attempts.

title: Former Bills Coach Sean McDermott Weighs in on Amani Hooker Addition
full_text:
Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane made a bold move at the NFL trade deadline, bringing in safety Amani Hooker in a trade with the Tennessee Titans.
The move has been mostly met with positive praise as the Bills shored up one of their greatest weaknesses. Hooker gives them a true centerfield-type of safety, who enters Week 10 sharing the lead for the most interceptions with five.
One person who is a big fan of the move is former Buffalo head coach Sean McDermott. While appearing on The Rich Eisen Show , McDermott was asked for his take on the trade and said he was "all for it." He added that a team looking to contend for a Super Bowl has the responsibility to identify and correct any flaws, and he believes that's exactly what this trade did.
"Yeah, I'm all for it. You know, I've I've been all for it. You know, when you when your goal as a team, and this is true for any team, when your goal is to is to win a Super Bowl, ours was last year, certainly the Bills is this year, but any team that feels like they got a legitimate shot to win a Super Bowl, then you're tasked with the responsibility of identifying what could get in the way of you winning that Super Bowl," McDermott said.
"And then going out and finding those pieces, and so you saw Buffalo do that rather quickly in the start of this offseason, going to get the receiver (DJ Moore). And then, they did it again with some defensive pieces, and now going to get Hooker, I thought was a really good move. And if you're Joe Brady, or Jim Leonhard in this case, I'm sure you're extremely happy."
Shortly after being traded to Buffalo, Hooker made his intentions for this weekend clear. After being on a bye in Week 9 for the Titans, Hooker is ready to be back in action this weekend as the Bills take on the New York Jets.
“Oh I’m gonna play on Sunday. Yeah. I’ll be ready to go," Hooker said via the Bills official X page .
Hooker didn't see a full workload given the short time he had to learn the Buffalo defense, but he was certainly noticeable in the 31-12 road win over the Jets.

title: Four Biggest Takeaways From Bills Week 10 Blowout Win Against Jets
full_text:
It was a tale of two halves for the Buffalo Bills as they took on the New York Jets in Week 10.
Buffalo had a narrow lead of just 10-6 going into the intermission as the Jets were fighting hard and the Bills couldn't get out of neutral. Things seemed to be too close for comfort as New York scored early in the third quarter to make it 10-9.
From there, it was all Buffalo. Josh Allen scored his second rushing touchdown of the game and then threw one to DJ Moore. James Cook ripped off a long run as well to score a late touchdown, giving them a 31-12 win. With this one in the books, let's look back at some of the biggest takeaways from this victory.
Buffalo has become one of the toughest teams to beat, especially when they're on the road. The win over the Jets was their eighth consecutive regular season road win, and their fifth of this season. The last time the Bills lost on the road during the regular season was in Week 10 of the 2025 campaign against the Miami Dolphins.
Hopefully, that road dominance leads to home field advantage for Buffalo in the playoffs. If not, they will have the confidence of knowing they can win against anyone on the road.
It didn't take long to see why Buffalo was willing to give up a second-round pick for Amani Hooker. Despite being with the team for just a couple of practices, Hooker was solid in coverage and played nearly every snap, while recording seven tackles. In addition to that, Hooker nearly made a huge play in the second quarter.
New York was facing a first-and-20, and Geno Smith attempted a pass toward Isaiah Williams. That pass was nearly picked off by Hooker, who made a great play to break it up.
In addition to his work in coverage, Hooker's presence allowed Jim Leonhard to move Cole Bishop around more. One example was in the third quarter, when Bishop blitzed Smith and delivered a hit on third-and-seven, forcing New York to settle for a field goal.
The Bills' offense was lackluster in the first half, but came alive in the second thanks to Dalton Kincaid and DJ Moore. First, Kincaid had a 54-yard reception, which set up the second rushing touchdown of the game from Josh Allen. That gave Buffalo a 17-9 lead, and the Jets were able to keep it close by scoring another field goal, making it a 17-12 game.
That's when Moore made his first big play of the game. Moore got deep against the New York secondary and caught a 45-yard touchdown from Allen, making it a 24-12 lead for the Bills. We know that the Buffalo offense can run against anyone, but having Kincaid and Moore both fully healthy makes them nearly unstoppable.
Rookie TJ Parker made an impact in this one, recording two sacks against Cade Klubnik. That gives him 3.5 on the season as he's been quietly putting together a solid season. He's also outperforming Bradley Chubb, the team's prized offseason signing.
Chubb agreed to a three-year deal worth $43.5 million , giving them a pass-rusher with experience in the 3-4. Through the first nine games of the season, however, Chubb has just 1.5 sacks. Bills On SI's John Green said Chubb has been one of the biggest disappointments of the season , and the fact that he's been outperformed by Parker thus far doesn't help change that narrative.

title: Bills Two Big Hits on Geno Smith Knocks Jets QB Out of Game Twice
full_text:
Geno Smith is not having a fun day against the Buffalo Bills .
As his New York Jets host the Bills in Week 10, Smith has been under constant pressure. That included taking a massive hit from linebacker Terrel Bernard near the end of the first half.
Making the hit look even worse was the fact that Smith was also being hit by rookie outside linebacker T.J. Parker at the same time. Smith went to the medical tent for some medical attention and didn't take the field to begin the second half.
Rookie fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik replaced Smith and led the Jets on a scoring drive to cut the lead to 10-9. Smith was evaluated for a concussion and was back on the field when the Jets took the field again, but Smith took another hard hit.
This time, it was a third-down blitz from Cole Bishop that knocked Smith to the ground and forced a field goal. Not only did that hit end a promising drive, but it also sent Smith back to the medical tent. After evaluation, he was then sent to the locker room for further evaluation.
Smith has completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards, and although he was sacked just one time, he took several other major hits. As the game goes into the fourth quarter, he has been ruled questionable to return, this time with an ankle injury .
Klubnik again replaced Smith and there is not a third quarterback on the roster. Their emergency quarterback is wide receiver Isaiah Williams.
New York kept it close in the first half, with the score at 10-6. Klubnik then led them on a scoring drive, cutting the lead to 10-9. Since then, the Bills have taken full control.
Josh Allen ran a touchdown to extend the lead to 17-9 and while the Jets scored another field goal, Buffalo had another strong response. This time, DJ Moore caught a deep pass from Allen, scoring his third touchdown of the year on a 45-yard play.
If this score holds, the Bills will improve to 8-1 on the season. They will also have their first win in the AFC East. Their only other divisional game was in Week 4, which was when they suffered a loss to the New England Patriots.

title: SI's Midseason NFL Report Card Misses Mark By Grading Bills Third in AFC
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are alone atop the AFC standings with nine weeks down and nine weeks to go.
Although the Bills (7-1) would be the No. 1 seed if the playoffs began today, their first-half performance was not enough to earn the highest grade amongst their AFC peers on Sports Illustrated's midseason report cards .
In fact, there are two AFC teams who earned higher letter grades than the conference-leading Bills.
SI staff writer Matthew Vederame graded the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cincinnati Bengals above Buffalo. The former earned an A+ while the latter recorded an A. The Bills settled for an A- along with the Denver Broncos.
Verderame went as far to proclaim, "the Jaguars are the AFC’s best team so far."
"Buffalo has to be considered an elite team, and one of the few with a real chance of hoisting the Lombardi Trophy come February," said Verderame commenting on the Bills' A- mark.
"The Bills have the league’s biggest weapon in football with Josh Allen, the reigning rushing champion in James Cook and a top offensive line. The big concern is the defense, which ranks at or near the bottom in a litany of important categories. Still, Buffalo is a virtual lock to win the AFC East and should make a deep playoff run once again."
First, the Bills, who are off to the franchise's best start since 1993, are presumably better than the 2025 team that went into Duval County and posted a 27-24 playoff win over Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars.
Even with their flurry of trade deadline additions, the Jaguars aren't necessarily any better of a team that lost to Buffalo last January.
Furthermore, the Bills have multiple signature wins this season while the Jaguars lost to the Broncos in their most difficult test to date.
Meanwhile, Buffalo posted road wins over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams and the 7-1 Minnesota Vikings.
"You've seen that they've shown that they can go on the road in two Monday night games, and hostile environments, and be able to perform and stick together and find different ways to win football games. I think that that's important," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady.
Buffalo, which is the NFL's lone team averaging more than 30.0 points per game, boasts the No. 1 ranked offense on the circuit (386.4).
“No game ever feels like we're ever out of it. We're going to continue to fight," said Allen. "At the end of the day, if there's time on the clock, we still feel like we have a chance no matter the situation."
Tight end Dalton Kincaid predicted that the best is yet to come for the Bills' offense.
As for the defense, which Verderame points to as a major concern, the unit is showing signs of life. It's also certainly possible that Verderame is overreacting to a slow start in a new system under coordinator Jim Leonhard.
Albeit against lesser quarterbacks, the Bills have enjoyed an historic two-game clip on defense . They held both the Baltimore Ravens and Vikings without a passing touchdown in back-to-back weeks.
Additionally, more help is on the way with the trade for veteran safety Amani Hooker.
In closing, the Bills are what their record says they are, and right now, that's the No. 1 team in the AFC. That deserves an A+ in my book.

title: Bills Week 10 Inactive List vs. Jets Includes Rare Spencer Brown Development
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are looking for their fifth win in a row and their first against an AFC East opponent in 2026 as they visit the New York Jets .
Buffalo enters this game relatively healthy, with the biggest question being starting right tackle Spencer Brown. The veteran was forced to sit out in Week 8 after a back injury flared up during the team's bye week. He returned to action in Week 9 against the Minnesota Vikings , but suffered an ankle injury during that game.
Brown was able to play every snap, but entered the weekend with a doubtful designation . He truly turned out to be a game-time decision, as Brown was seen testing out his ankle during pre-game warmups.
Spencer Brown certainly doing everything he can to play today. We’ll find out for sure in 16 minutes. #Bills pic.twitter.com/WiBRMnqdEj
After twsting the ankle, Brown said he was " good to go ," which is huge. Not only is he a far more reliable starter than Tylan Gable, but it's rare to see "doubtful" players suit up for the Bills. He's the first player Buffalo had listed as doubtful to play since 2014 and the league-wide rate is just 4.9% ( according to Banged Up Bills ).
Before looking at the full list of inactive players in Week 10, let's get a refresher on which players were dealing with injuries for both the Bills and Jets.

title: Fantasy Start-Sit Week 10: DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman
full_text:
With the Buffalo Bills set to square off against the New York Jets on Sunday, it's time for some fantasy football lineup decisions with wide receiver DJ Moore, Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir, and tight end Dalton Kincaid.
None of Buffalo's top four pass-catchers had a good game in Week 9 against the Minnesota Vikings , which wasn't totally surprising because Minnesota sports an elite defense.
Shakir led all pass-catchers with his four grabs for 58 yards, Kincaid nabbed three catches for 28 yards, Moore caught three balls for 25 yards and Coleman brought up the rear with his 17 yards on three receptions.
Now, a look at our start-or-sit advice for Moore, Coleman, Shakir and Kincaid in Week 10.
It wasn't a great week for Moore last week, but he has still been reliable in most of the games he has played in and finished.
In the three of the four contests he has finished, Moore has tallied at least four catches and 67 yards and has scored in two of them.
On the surface, this looks like a tough matchup, as the Jets are ceding the 10th-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts in 2026, per CBS Sports , but there's a logical explanation for that and it doesn't have to do with the Jets having an elite defense.
Instead, the Jets have faced the ninth-fewest passing attempts in the league this season, and five of the teams with fewer attempts against have played in one less game than New York. Meanwhile, the Jets have faced the most rushing attempts in the NFL with teams opting to attack them that way.
With everything we know, we're comfortable with starting Josh Allen's No. 1 receiver this week.
Just when we thought Kincaid would get back to his elite scoring ways after a big performance in Week 8, he came back down to Earth in Week 9 with a 5.8-point showing.
But that Week 8 peformance is a reminder of why you have to keep starting him every week. There aren't many tight ends in the NFL who are capable of what Kincaid can produce any given week.
Kincaid also ranks as TE10 overall in fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Pros , so he's a must-start in 10-team leagues by default.
The Jets present an OK matchup, with New York permitting the 13th-most fantasy points per game to tight ends.
After a strong start to the season , Coleman has cooled off over his last four games with just nine catches for 87 yards and two scores in that span, which points to him being touchdown-dependent.
This is actually a good matchup for a touchdown-dependent wide receiver like Coleman, as the Jets are giving up the 10th-most touchdowns per game to the position in 2026.
However, given what we've seen from Coleman since Week 5, when he has ranked as WR68 overall in fantasy points per game, we just cannot suggest him as a starting option, especially with Moore playing, which will cut into Coleman's target share.
As for Shakir, his game-by-game production has been better since Week 4, and he ranks as WR27 overall in that span despite having  a bye week mixed in.
That's enough to justify the veteran as a low-end flex option for Week 10.
Verdicts: Start Shakir, sit Coleman

title: Panthers Surge in Power Rankings After Monumental Division Win Over Saints
full_text:
Try as they might, the Carolina Panthers did not lose their fourth straight game on Sunday. They committed several terrible and ill-timed penalties, and the referees aided that pursuit with some mind-boggling calls against the Panthers.
Despite that, they finally got off the schneid. They went into New Orleans, a house of horrors for them lately, and emerged with a clutch, walk-off victory that never remotely felt secure. It felt like a loss was coming, and they managed to snatch victory from the literal jaws of defeat.
With that, the Panthers broke their losing streak, remained in first place, and got moving back in the right direction in the NFL Power Rankings.
The NFL Power Rankings are totally meaningless, but they generally do reflect how the team is going. A big win usually means a big move up, so even if the placement feels wrong, the direction is the real takeaway.
Last week, the Panthers fell again after a soul-crushing defeat to the Denver Broncos . It was a trend; the Panthers had tumbled lower and lower for three straight weeks after, in the eyes of some, reaching top-10 status.
It's difficult to envision the Panthers ever getting back to that level, but a win is a win and moving in the right direction again, which they are, is key.
After last week , Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer ranked the Panthers 25th. After a big divisional win, they're soaring up to 20th. We can quibble about some teams ranked ahead (Dallas Cowboys, Las Vegas Raiders), but the important thing is they jumped five spots.
"The Panthers needed to beat the Saints in New Orleans to prove why they were expected to repeat in the weak NFC South. They found a new winning formula between much-improved defense under new coordinator Todd Wash and Chuba Hubbard producing 172 yards from scrimmage," Iyer wrote.
The Panthers could get on a roll next week. They host the Baltimore Ravens, who are without Lamar Jackson, next week, and that is a game they are actually favored in. They could get back to .500, remain in first place, and slide even higher.
The five-loss Panthers are probably better than their record or placement suggests. Injuries have ripped them to shreds more than almost any team in the NFL, and they've been jobbed by the referees on more than a few occasions .
But all that matters at the end of the day is that they're moving up and are in first place in the NFC South. For the first time in weeks, both statements are true.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: 6 Winners and 6 Losers from Panthers' Gutsy Victory Over Saints
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were walk-off winners against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. It was a monumental win that felt truly in doubt late in the second half . They pulled it together, thanks to a few big performances and in spite of some others.
Devin Lloyd records his 3rd interception of the season. He becomes the first linebacker in the NFL since Wilber Marshall in 1988 to record 3+ interceptions in 3 of his first 5 seasons.
Devin Lloyd seems to often be where the ball is, and he was on Sunday. His early interception on a potential fourth-down conversion helped totally flip the momentum before the Saints looked like they were going to score. And shoutout to much-maligned Marco Wilson for deflecting it to Lloyd.
Ryan Fitzgerald is officially in a slump.
The magic Ryan Fitzgerald had last year has effectively run out. He's been bad on extra points, missed a few key field goals, and his kickoff woes keep coming up. It's not the strength it used to be, and it hurt the Panthers badly at times. Missing a field goal as well is simply inexcusable. But nailing two from beyond 50, including the stunning game-winner, was obviously clutch.
Jaelan Phillips with the fumble recovery. Was in the backfield, like he's been all game, and so was there for the scoop. Having a heck of a day: 1 TFL, 1 FR, 1 QBH. Feels like he'll get home for a sack at some point today.
It was immediately apparent how important Jaelan Phillips is to this defense. He made a TFL on the first play, and he had several pressures. His presence in the backfield led to a fumble recovery. He was maybe the most challenging Panthers defender for the Saints to handle on Sunday. And as Alex Zietlow predicted, Phillips did record a sack to end the first half and prompt boos from the crowd.
Good grief, Robert Hunt. Can't really bench him, given how much he's being paid, unfortunately.
So many times, the pocket was pushed back into Bryce Young's lap, and so many times, it was the fault of Robert Hunt. His rough season continued Sunday, as he struggled to hold up in pass protection versus the Saints' front.
How much more can we say about Chuba Hubbard ? The passing game took plenty of time to get anything going, but the Saints' defense had no answers for Hubbard all day. He was elite in the run game and very solid after the catch. He carried the Panthers to their game-winning drive literally by himself. If there were only two winners, it was Hubbard and Phillips on either side.
and now Darren Waller drops a perfect bucket touchdown
Two drops, including a would-be deep touchdown on a beautiful throw from Young, are bad. An offensive pass interference after a third-down conversion (admittedly a very weak call) is not good, either. Just an all-around struggle from Waller. The drop cost Young his touchdown streak, which had been the longest active in the NFL.
The Panthers looked like a different unit versus the run Sunday. They were filling gaps, making stops in the backfield, and getting push they haven't all year. It's the same players, though. Todd Wash has them better equipped to face the run, and they have responded incredibly well to the task.
Another week, another swathe of boneheaded penalties. They had eight in the first half, which is a step up from last week's outing. That has to change, and it comes down to coaching. Plus, Dave Canales' decision to challenge a spot call that was almost never going to be overturned on what ended up as a fourth-and-inches deep in his own territory was simply a waste, especially when he wanted to go for it on his own 27 anyway.
Kaye's Take: Chau Smith-Wade is having quite the day.
The coverage was pretty solid by everyone throughout, but Chau Smith-Wade had a number of consequential targets that amounted to nothing. He was very impressive against what had been a really solid passing attack for the Saints.
Brad Idzik's play-calling today has been horrific. I'm chalking it up to being relatively new to play-calling, but he has been a big reason why the #Panthers offense is not productive today. Very little quick game or RPO; still attempting 5- to 7-step dropbacks with…
Once again, the sequencing from Brad Idzik was not ideal. He couldn't get the offense into a rhythm and he also didn't rely on Chuba Hubbard as much as he should've. And it never felt like he was taking it to the defense, which had been a strength of his earlier this year.
What does Tracy Smith work on with his guys during practice? It's not kicking the ball in bounds. It's not how to line up on a kickoff. It's not how to return a punt without committing a bad penalty. All the fundamentals of special teams come back to bite the Panthers weekly, but especially on Sunday.

title: The Panthers Have a Serious Problem That Dave Canales Has to Fix or Else
full_text:
It wasn't without drama , but the Carolina Panthers finally got back in the win column. Carolina moves firmly into first place in the NFC South, improving to 4-5 on the season with a 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints.
Carolina won the game on the backs of huge performances on both sides of the ball. The offense started and ended with Chuba Hubbard, as he had the best game of his career on Sunday. Against the Saints, Hubbard posted 172 scrimmage yards and scored both of Carolina's touchdowns.
On defense, Jaelan Phillips finally lived up to the  $120 million contract he signed with Carolina back in free agency. Returning from a hamstring injury, Phillips posted 5 tackles, 3 TFLs, 1 sack, and a fumble recovery.
While the Panthers didn't commit any turnovers, the game was sloppy, and the penalties piled up again on both sides of the ball, costing them big plays and making it much harder than it should have been.
Penalties have been an issue all season, with constant movement on the lines of scrimmage and the depleted secondary struggling to cover opposing receivers.
However, against the Saints, those issues were amplified. The Panthers set a franchise record, committing 17 accepted penalties for 152 yards,
If Carolina does that again, they have a 90% chance of losing that game. It's a miracle the Panthers walked out of the Superdome with a win despite such a lack of discipline.
Furthermore, the Panthers have committed 10+ turnovers in four games this season, and are 2-2 in those games. Carolina has been blown out twice this season; aside from the losses to the Bears and Buccaneers, they've hung around in other games, and timely penalties have proven to be costly.
This isn't to say Canales' job is currently on the line or anything, but severe amounts of penalties will only drag the Panthers trending down, even in a bad division like the NFC South.
Frankly, it's a miracle the Panthers are even 2-2 in games with 10+ penalties. Against the Saints, the penalties directly led to points; New Orleans' second touchdown drive featured four penalties for 42 yards.
The longer this continues, the more Carolina will lose, especially as the schedule that only gets tougher. In the next month, Carolina faces the Ravens, Buccaneers, Vikings, and Saints. Minnesota is the only juggernaut on that schedule, but all those games are just as loseable as they are winnable for Carolina.
Penalties against elite defenses like Tampa Bay's and Minnesota's will ensure not only a loss, but an embarrassing loss. If this doesn't get fixed and Carolina stays undisciplined, then uncomfortable conversations will start.

title: Panthers’ Massive Offseason Investment is Finally Arriving at the Right Time
full_text:
The drought is over ; the Carolina Panthers have finally won a game after what felt like an eternity. Carolina picks up a 20-17 division win over the New Orleans Saints on a walk-off field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald.
It was an ugly game, filled with penalties, questionable calls , and a lot of Chuba Hubbard. Hubbard posted a career-high in total yards, totaling 172 yards and scoring 2 touchdowns.
Hubbard is the MVP of the game, there's no denying that, but Carolina's defense played a complete game. The run  defense has been a weakness for Carolina this year; that wasn't the case against the Saints, allowing just 49 yards on the ground and 2.1 yards per carry.
Saints' QB Tyler Shough had a rough day, throwing for just 187 yards, 1 touchdown, 1 interception, and a lost fumble. Carolina also posted 3 sacks on Shough.
One player in particular was the highlight on defense, and did exactly what Carolina broght him on to do.
Jaelan Phillips returned to action today after not playing since Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles. In his return from a hamstring injury, he was the best player on defense, and was one of the two best players in this game.
Against the Saints, Phillips posted 5 total tackles, 3 TFLs, 1 sack, 2 QB hits, and a fumble recovery. According to SumerSports , Phillips also recorded 8 pressures, which is the most by a Carolina player since Patrick Jones II posted 8 in Week 5 of the 2025 season.
Not only was Phillips elite in affecting the QB, but he made multiple critical tackles against the run, not allowing New Orleans' offense to find a rhythm.
Phillips would've had a second sack, but it was called back for a horse-collar tackle. What stuck out on the screen was Phillips' first step, his bend around the edge, and just his pure strength, bull-rushing blockers towards Shough to close the pocket.
With a performance like his today, the investment Carolina made in Phillips looked more than worth it.
After the 2025 season, when the Panthers finished with the NFL's worst pass rush, it was clear that a premier pass rusher was the No. 1 hole to fill.
Carolina knew that, and filled that hole as soon as they could, making a splash signing on day one of free agency, signing Phillips.
Phillips was expected to re-sign with the Eagles, but Carolina swooped in with a four-year, $120 million deal that was impossible to turn down. With that said, a high price tag comes with high expectations, and on Sunday against the Saints, Phillips met those expectations.
Moving forward, the best-case scenario for Carolina is that Sunday's performance is a tone setter, and Phillips brings a major impact for the rest of the season.

title: Bryce Young Report Card: Panthers QB Does Enough to Secure Win Over Saints
full_text:
Young's performance against the Saints wasn't his best , but the Carolina Panthers came away with a 20-17 victory. He finished with 200 passing yards on 17-of-30 passing, with no touchdowns or interceptions.
The offense struggled to score through the air, but Carolina found other ways to get the job done. The running game and defense played important roles in the victory, while Young did enough to avoid costly mistakes.
Young had a few good moments, but he was also sacked three times and struggled to find consistency. Against a divisional opponent with first place in the NFC South on the line, protecting the football was important. However, the Panthers will need more production from their quarterback moving forward.
There were some positives in Young's performance, particularly his ability to avoid turnovers. However, there were also stretches when the Panthers needed him to make more plays through the air. Carolina cannot continue to depend on its defense and running game to carry the offense every week.
Chuba Hubbard helped take some of that pressure off Young. He ran 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding 80 receiving yards on five catches. His production gave Carolina a reliable option on the ground and helped keep the offense moving despite its struggles in the passing game.
The Panthers also received an important contribution from their defense, which helped keep New Orleans from taking control of the game. Ryan Fitzgerald came through when Carolina needed him most, hitting a 54-yard field goal as time expired to seal the victory.
It was an important road win for Carolina, but Young's performance left some questions about the passing offense. His 200 yards and lack of touchdowns won't be enough against some of the better teams in the league. The Panthers will need more production from their quarterback as the schedule gets harder.
For now, Young gets a C+ for a performance that helped Carolina win but left plenty of room for improvement.

title: The Referees Have Some Explaining to Do As Panthers Continue to Suffer
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers make it easy for the referees to penalize them. They commit a ton of really stupid penalties that are pretty obvious. See four separate neutral-zone infraction/enchroachments from today.
But the referees also take matters into their own hands plenty. We saw it last week against the Denver Broncos, as a comically inept referee crew led a circus of events that turned a should-be DPI into an interception a whole play later. But that's neither here nor there.
this ref in the Panthers/Saints game is atrocious
On Sunday, the New Orleans Saints seemed to get the home-field advantage from refs that the Panthers didn't get last week. It was clear early on that things weren't going to be called fairly or accurately.
Here are some of the most egregious calls or misses that hurt the Panthers:
Now, all of these calls can't go in the Panthers' favor. It doesn't work like that. And it's certainly true the Panthers got away with some things. Generally, you get some calls, you don't get others. But it seems like the Panthers didn't (and haven't this year) get any of the momentous calls.
disgusting holding penalty by a backup ref group to pull that touchdown from Chuba Hubbard vile
Maybe Dave Canales heard the criticism that he's not angry enough when his team is slighted. Maybe today was just bad enough for the mild-mannered and uber positive coach to break. Either way, even one of the nicest coaches in the NFL was all over the refs for some of these misses.

There are a few instances where the referees inserted themselves into the game and it hurt the Panthers this year. The phantom roughing the passer that led to a Panthers' loss against the Browns comes to mind. That fiasco against the Broncos does, too.

Without veering into conspiracy territory, the replacement crew (thanks to the FAA shutdown) was simply not good and looked to be extremely one-sided. It somehow didn't take the Panthers out of the win column, but the NFL has more explaining to do.

title: Panthers Confidence Meter: How Much Confidence Should Fans Have in O-Line and Todd Wash's Defense?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are about to find themselves with little room for error as they hit the midway point of the 2026 season. This Sunday the Saints come to town as the Panthers look to get back on track and stay in the mix for the NFC South title. New Orleans and Carolina both enter this game at 3-5 and will be trying to separate themselves from the other.
The Carolina Panthers are on a three-game losing streak and have been getting outplayed on both sides of the ball. The key to the Panthers winning on Sunday will be how well two areas of the team perform.
The offensive line has been a major problem for the Carolina Panthers this season. Bryce Young is constantly getting hit and the blocking isn’t consistently good enough for the Panthers’ offense to start to get into a rhythm. This will be a key area for the Panthers against the Saints. Bryce Young's struggles under pressure have highlighted just how important better protection is for Carolina.
The Saints have 23 sacks so far this season. New Orleans will be without center Erik McCoy and offensive tackle Taliese Fuaga for the game against the Panthers, so Carolina’s offensive line should be able to make things easier on the quarterback.
Left guard Damien Lewis was able to practice in full on Friday and has no injury designation for Sunday’s game. Right guard Brady Christensen was officially listed as questionable for the game on Friday, after being listed as questionable earlier in the week.
If the Panthers continue to allow pressure on Young, then the Saints will be able to run away with this game.
In addition to the Panthers’ offensive line, the play of the Panthers’ defense under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash must improve in several areas, especially against the run. Carolina's defensive struggles have been a major concern during the team's recent losing streak.
The defense needs to be more physical, force more turnovers and get off the field more. This is another area of the team that has consistently let the Panthers down in recent weeks and needs to be improved.
After winning 23-22 in overtime versus the Cleveland Browns last week, New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough will attempt to build on that success. Meanwhile, Carolina must figure out how to prevent New Orleans from establishing sustained drives.
Linebacker Bobby Okereke is out. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and cornerback Will Lee III are listed as questionable. Cornerback Mike Jackson is listed as doubtful for Sunday’s game.
With the uncertainty in the secondary and at linebacker, Wash will have to find production from the players on the roster. They cannot allow the Saints to run the ball and get third-down conversions. The Panthers' defensive problems against the run are another area that needs attention.
The Carolina Panthers have the talent to win this game but need to play better in all phases of the game. The offensive line needs to give Bryce Young more time to throw, and Todd Wash’s defense needs to create challenges for Shough and the Saints offense.
As it stands now, the Panthers are still in the hunt for the NFC South title even after losing three straight games. However, a loss would make it that much more difficult for Carolina to win the division. This is a game the Panthers must win in order to continue to make a push for the playoffs.
My confidence level is 5.5/10. Carolina has enough talent to win this game but they have to play better than they have been in recent weeks and stop making so many mistakes that have cost them games throughout the season.

title: Fantasy Start or Sit: Tetairoa McMillan, Panthers D/ST, Darren Waller
full_text:
With the 3-5 Panthers traveling to New Orleans to take on the 3-5 Saints in Week 10, there are many Panthers players that can be added to your fantasy football team. However, not all of them can be started in your lineup.
Here is a look at whether to start or sit Tetairoa McMillan, the Panthers defense and Darren Waller in Week 10.
He's been one of the Panthers' top receivers this season with 46 catches for 625 yards and 3 touchdowns. In the Broncos game, McMillan had 4 catches for 56 yards and a touchdown. The Saints have been one of the worst teams in the NFL at defending the pass this season, and many receivers have had huge games against them.
McMillan has been a regular part of the Panthers passing game and remains a reliable option for fantasy football managers. He's also capable of making plays downfield and finding the end zone.
Fantasy call: Start McMillan.
The Panthers D/ST will be difficult to trust in Week 10. For one, Carolina has struggled to stop opponents from scoring all season. Now, the Panthers will be on the road against the Saints, a team coming off of a big overtime win against the Browns.
The Panthers are dealing with a host of injuries on defense right now as well. LB Bobby Okereke is out for the Panthers this week. CB Mike Jackson is doubtful to play. LB Jaelan Phillips and DE Will Lee III are both questionable to play in New Orleans.
The Panthers are still trying to figure out the defensive scheme of new defensive coordinator Todd Wash. With the injuries on the Panthers defense, as well as their poor play on defense this season, it is difficult to trust this unit in fantasy football.
Fantasy call: Sit the Panthers D/ST.
Last week, Waller had his best game of the season against the Broncos, catching eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Panthers have been throwing the ball a lot to Waller in recent games, and he has been a reliable option for Bryce Young.
Waller has a chance to put together another strong performance against the Saints on Sunday. The tight end position can be hit or miss from week to week, but Waller's recent production makes him a good option for fantasy managers.
Fantasy call: Start Waller.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit  Week 10: Jalen Coker, Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard
full_text:
With the Carolina Panthers set to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 10, it's time to make fantasy football lineup decisions on quarterback Bryce Young, wide receiver Jalen Coker and running back Chuba Hubbard.
It was tough sledding for both Hubbard and Coker last week versus an elite Denver Broncos defense .
Hubbard failed to register 100 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone and Coker tallied just 29 yards on four catches.
Young was on the opposite side of the spectrum after he finished with 276 passing yards and three touchdowns to one pick. Young's yardage output was his most since Week 6, and he scored three touchdowns in a game for the first time since Week 2.
Now, a look at what we're doing with the Panthers' offensive trio for the Week 10 game against the Saints.
After a strong start to the season , it has been tough sledding for Coker the last three weeks, as he's tallied seven catches for 74 yards and one touchdown in that span.
As a result, Coker now ranks as WR27 overall in fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Pros , which makes him a flex option who is fairly reliant on his matchup.
This week, Coker draws a matchup against a Saints defense giving up the 13th-most fantasy points per game to wideouts this season, per CBS Sports .
That's a good enough matchup to justify putting Coker into lineups on Sunday afternoon.
Young is coming off a nice bounce-back showing in Week 9 and is ranked as QB11 overall in fantasy points per contest, which makes him an every-week starter in 10-12 team leagues.
Adding more optimism for him this week, Young will meet a New Orleans unit that has ceded the 11th-most fantasy points per game to signal-callers and the 12th-most touchdowns per contest.
Young should be in lineups this week.
Hubbard has easily been the Panthers' most consistent fantasy producer this season thanks to his impressive scoring output, yardage production and involvement in the passing game.
Entering this week, Hubbard ranks as RB6 overall in fantasy points per game, which makes him a locked-in RB1 every week.
Matchup is irrelevant with Hubbard since he's a lineup lock, but it's worth noting that the Saints are giving up the most fantasy points per game to running backs this season, so Hubbard has an opportunity to blow up.

title: Will the Panthers Beat the Saints? Here Are Our Staff Predictions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have lost three straight, yet they somehow still hold first place in the NFC South . That could well change this afternoon. They're in New Orleans for what amounts to a first-place bout.
The two teams are 3-5, so the winner will grab sole possession of first once the clock hits zero. The Saints have had the Panthers' number recently, but they have yet to meet this season. How will this one go?
Here are the Panthers On SI staff predictions.
The Carolina Panthers have a chance to pick up a much-needed division win against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. However, this will be a tough road test for Carolina.
The Panthers need better protection for Bryce Young and a strong defensive performance under interim coordinator Todd Wash. New Orleans is coming off an overtime win against Cleveland and will look to carry that momentum into Sunday’s matchup. Expect a close game, but the Saints get the edge at home.
Apparently no team in the NFC South is going out of its way to want to win the title. It’s a division where every team is at least 2 games under .500 and every club has a losing home record. A year ago, the Saints won just two games, which included a sweep of the Panthers.
Bryce Young has not been super sharp as of late, but he showed a lot of resiliency last Sunday. Carolina has turned over the ball 12 times this season, but Kellen Moore’s team has been even worse. There will be a lot of bend-but-don’t-break by the Panthers’ defense, who will limit the Saints to four field goals and one touchdown, so Dave Canales’s club will eke out a one-point win.
The margins are as thin as can possibly be this Sunday. These two teams are evenly matched. The Panthers have the best win (over Detroit in Week 4), but the Saints have been better of late (coming off an OT win over the Browns). They are not separated by much.
It's almost impossible to predict this one. Will the Saints' strong pass rush make mincemeat of the Panthers' weak offensive line? Will Bryce Young shred the Saints' fifth-worst pass defense? Can Tyler Shough take advantage of a depleted Panthers' secondary? Might Chuba Hubbard plow through the Saints' fourth-worst rushing defense?
The Panthers have more advantages than disadvantages, and they could get back a number of healthy contributors. Still, it won't be an easy one.
If there's ever a time for Carolina to get right, it’s on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. This Saints defense is the second-worst pass defense Carolina has faced. New Orleans ranks 28th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, surrendering 236.6 per game. As an overall defense, New Orleans is arguably the worst, ranking 29th in rushing yards allowed per game.
Carolina may have reinforcements coming to the defense, as EDGE Jaelan Phillips and cornerback Will Lee III are both listed as questionable for Sunday. Even if the defense underperforms, this is a game where Carolina should be able to keep up in a shootout.

title: Will Luther Burden Play in Week 11? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears WR
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have an injury concern with wide receiver Luther Burden ahead of their Week 11 game against the New Orleans Saints.
The Bears notched a razor-thin 27-24 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 before the bye, but late in the game we saw Burden take a big hit to his head that resulted in a concussion and his early exit from the contest.
It looked to be a bad consussion, too, as Burden was clearly shaken-up before exiting the field.
Here's the latest on Burden and our expectations for him ahead of the Week 11 game versus New Orleans.
As previously noted, Burden is in the concussion protocol , head coach Ben Johnson announced after the win over Tampa Bay.
"Ben Johnson says Luther Burden had a concussion," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond wrote.
We've seen players return from a concussion the following week, but we've also seen players miss one or more games depending on the severity, so it's possible Burden could sit out in Week 11.
We would say Burden has a better chance to play than not. Let's say 75/25 in favor of him playing.
That's because Burden had an extra week to get right before the Bears' game this week thanks to the bye in Week 10.
It isn't clear if Burden made any progress through the concussion protocol in that time, but the week off at least gives him a better chance to not miss a game than he otherwise would have had if the Bears had played last week.
Entering the season, Rome Odunze was viewed as the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver, but he was anything but cemented in that role since Odunze had yet to fully prove himself.
Well, after nine games, Burden has clearly taken the mantle of the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver. Not only has he been more consistent, Burden is also leading the team in receiving yards with 644 to Odunze's 528. Burden also leads the team in receiving touchdowns with four.
Burden's impressive showing comes after an offseason in which both Johnson and general manager Ryan Poles raved about the second-year wideout .
There's no doubt the Bears' offense will take a hit if Burden does not play. If he does get ruled out, the Bears will need more from Odunze, tight end Colston Loveland and fellow wideouts Kalif Raymond, Jahdae Walker and Zavion Thomas.

title: Will Kyle Monangai Return in Week 11? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears RB
full_text:
It has been five whole games since the last time Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai took the field.
That was in Week 4, when Monangai ran all over the New York Jets en route to 146 yards and a 23-12 Bears victory .
Unfortunately for Monangai and the Bears, he also came down with a turf toe injury that led to him missing a handful of games, which was surprising because he wasn't expected to miss more than three after the team didn't place him on injured reserve.
Now, as we turn the page to Week 11, here's what we know about Monangai's chances of returning to the field.
The last we heard of Monangai was on the Friday before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9.
That was a huge day for Monangai and the Bears, as the second-year back turned in a limited practice , which was his first practice participation since his injury.
Monangai even drew the questionable tag before being ruled out for his fifth straight game.
There are no guarantees with Monangai at this point, but the fact that he was able to practice on a limited basis right before the bye suggests he has a good chance to return in Week 11.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai (toe) practiced today for the first time since his injury during a 146-yard game vs. the Jets on Oct. 4," The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs said. "It's a positive sign for a potential return on the other side of the bye week."
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport even went as far as to say that the Bears running back is expected to be back this week.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) won't play today, but he's expected back in Week 11. Fresh legs for Chicago," Rapoport reported.
So, all signs are pointing to Monangai indeed making his return to the field for the game against the New Orleans Saints .
The Bears' rushing attack managed to maintain its elite status during Monangai's absence, as Chicago still ranks fourth in rushing yards per game.
However, it has still been tough sledding for D'Andre Swift, who is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry this season.
Adding to that, the Bears don't have the kind of runner Monangai is in either of the players who replaced him during his absence, Roschon Johnson and Salvon Ahmed.
Before his injury, Monangai was easily the Bears' best running back and the numbers show that.
He is averaging 5.4 yards per carry, the most among Chicago's running backs, and he only trails Swift by 252 yards despite playing in five fewer games.
The Bears' offense is already playing at a high level, but things should be even better once Monangai is back in the mix.

title: Bears Could Reunite With Former Draft Pick After Steelers Cut Ties
full_text:
Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, there were multiple reports about the Chicago Bears looking around for cornerback help .
It's not hard to see why that was the case, as Chicago could use more depth at the position amid struggles from Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, and now the latter is dealing with a new injury he suffered in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Ultimately, the Bears didn't come away with a cornerback before the deadline, but that doesn't mean they won't continue to explore their options — and there just so happens to be a player available the team is quite familiar with.
Over the weekend, the Pittsburgh Steeleres decided to waive cornerback Terell Smith, the Bears' former fifth-round pick in 2023.
Smith appeared in one game for the Steelers but played only on special teams. According to Nick Farabaugh of Penn Live , the Steelers waived Smith after getting healthy in the secondary.
"When the Steelers signed Smith, they were dealing with injuries in the room and had just traded Joey Porter Jr.," he explained. "Now, the room remains healthy and the return of Doneiko Slaughter and Brandin Echols means those two players will take over the special teams role that initially belonged to Smith when he was signed to the Steelers’ roster."
Prior to his stint with the Steelers, Smith was on the Washington Commanders' practice squad but never got into a game for the NFC East squad.
The Bears cut Smith before cutdown day in August and the move came after the addition of Clark Phillips, who was acquired in the Gervon Dexter trade with the Atlanta Falcons.
Smith showed some promise as a depth cornerback over his first two years in the NFL, but a significant knee injury in 2025 forced him to miss the entire season and derailed him.
In his two seasons with Chicago, Smith posted completion rates allowed of 63% and 66.7%, and passer ratings of 93.9 and 72.7.
Certainly not great, but those numbers are actually better than those of both Johnson and Stevenson, and they are at least sufficient to be a quality backup.
Smith also offers some versatility after seeing snaps in the slot, on the boundary and even as a box safety over his 26 career games.
The Minnesota product offers special teams value, too, with 244 snaps in that area during his career.
A Smith signing remains a possibility regardless of what happens with Stevenson's injury, but if the veteran cornerback misses an extended period of time, it becomes more possible.

title: Why Chicago Bears Fans Must Become 49ers Fans Down the Stretch
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are now in third place in the NFC North , despite a 7-2 start through the bye week. Ben Johnson and Co. can't be upset at the season's first two and a half months of results, but the NFC playoff picture is already shaping up to be crowded.
The division itself is going to start eating its own, but the Bears, Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, and Green Bay Packers could all make runs for the postseason .
That goal gets easier for all of them if the NFC West continues to see its leader rule the roost down the stretch.
In particular, Chicago and the rest of the NFC North need the San Francisco 49ers to continue nabbing big division wins in the final two months of the season.
For the Niners, it's about keeping up their torrid pace.
San Francisco has been rocked by injuries all year, but quarterback Brock Purdy has guided them through with an MVP-caliber season. Purdy has 2,369 yards and 20 passing touchdowns, on 8.97 yards per attempt, and a 115.2 passer rating through nine games in 2026. He was brilliant in a 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys in America's Game of the Week.
The Bears need more of that down the stretch given the schedule in front of Kyle Shanahan's squad.
San Francisco has the Vikings next weekend in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football, plus matchups with the six-win Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams. Both of those NFC West teams picked up big wins on Sunday, against the Las Vegas Raiders and Cardinals, respectively, to climb back into the postseason conversation.
What helps is that the Rams and Seahawks have both matchups against each other remaining. On some level, those two will hurt the other one's cause.
Still, this all gets easier if the Niners could rule the NFC West with an iron fist down the stretch. It's not a particularly difficult stretch otherwise with many postseason implications for San Francisco; the New York Giants look like a soft NFC East lock, the Los Angeles Chargers are winless and already irrelevant, the Kansas City Chiefs are in the AFC, and the Philadelphia Eagles and Arizona Cardinals are also practically out of the playoff race already.
There are only so many Wild Card spots if Chicago can't win the NFC North, so it's best that rising contenders in the NFC West are subdued.
The 49ers have the key to suppressing the Seahawks and Rams and making the Bears' lives easier down the stretch. A win next Sunday night against Kirk Cousins and Minnesota wouldn't hurt either.
