title: Bears Take Bye-Week Tumble from First Place in NFC North Standings
full_text:
In case you haven't heard, the NFC North is the best division in football this year. By the end of the season, it may even be the best division in NFL history. The Chicago Bears stood alone atop their rivals as they entered their Week 10 bye, but even without playing a game, they've now tumbled down into third place.
Yes, you read that right. Despite a 7-2 record, the Bears' best start to a season since 2012, they sit in third place, only above the Green Bay Packers, who are 6-4 after today's loss to the Minnesota Vikings. As for the Detroit Lions and Vikings, they are both 7-2 but own tiebreakers over the Bears with a better division record. The Bears won't get a chance to turn the tables until Week 12 when they head to Ford Field for a Thanksgiving showdown with the Lions.
There was a chance that the Bears could have maintained first place in the NFC North through their bye week. They needed the New England Patriots to down the Lions in Germany and the Packers to defend Lambeau Field. But the Lions secured a 35-10 victory, and the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times en route to a dominant 30-10 win of their own.
There's no need for Bears fans to fret just yet. Plenty of football remains to be played, and the Bears have already proven to be one of the best, most complete teams in the NFL this year. Losing to the Vikings in Week 2 and the Packers in Week 5 hurts them, but nothing about those losses can be used to predict how the Bears will fare in the coming rematches.
For one thing, that Week 2 loss to the Vikings was played in monsoon-like conditions at Soldier Field and Caleb Williams injured himself on what would have been walk-in touchdown scramble late in the fourth quarter of a one-score game. As for the Week 5 loss to Green Bay, Williams was still sidelined by his torn hamstring and Tyson Bagent quite literally threw that game away. If it weren't for that freak injury to Williams, there's a very real chance that the Bears would be 9-0 right now.
That leaves a clear path for the Bears to follow to a second straight NFC North championship. When I predicted the Bears' final games of the season , I had them winning their last three games against the Packers, Lions, and Vikings, respectively, to finish with a 13-4 record, which should be enough to win the division. That would also take the Bears from 0-2 to 3-3 in the NFC North.
Nothing about the NFC North is easy to predict right now, especially when it comes to division standings. The Lions seem to have hit their stride, though losing Aiden Hutchinson for the season will hurt. The Packers have at times looked like the most explosive offense in the NFL with Jordan Love putting up eye-popping numbers. And since acquiring old friend Kirk Cousins in a trade at the deadline, the Vikings have now seemingly added a competent offense to an unstoppable defense.
If one of these three teams is going to dethrone the Bears, something that may not even happen, it's most likely going to be the Vikings, in my opinion. The Packers' historically bad run game is already starting to haunt them, and the loss of Hutchinson leaves Detroit's defense even more vulnerable than it already was. But the Vikings now appear to be the real deal. Their Week 18 rematch with the Bears could very well decide the division champion.

title: Bears' Division-Only Finish Gets Tougher With Micah Parsons Nearing a Return for Packers
full_text:
With the chance for a banged-up roster to get healthy, the bye week was a win for the Chicago Bears. Coming off a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football , the Bears are in a good place at 7-2.
Then again, that place is now third place in the NFC North because of Sunday's results.
The Detroit Lions handled business against the New England Patriots, blasting Mike Vrabel's squad 35-10 in Munich, Germany . Meanwhile, the Minnesota Vikings saw Kirk Cousins successfully debut in a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
Those results, in tandem, send Chicago into third place. A Packers win would've given the Lions sole possession of first place and the Bears sole possession of second place.
With another half of the season left to play, it's not the end of the world for Chicago. It's just another example of the shark tank the division is this season.
Even Green Bay won't be down for long. Star EDGE Micah Parsons should be back for the Packers before the end of the month. Parsons is coming back from a torn ACL and meniscus from last December, though he is still on the PUP list as of Week 10 and remained inactive against Minnesota .
Green Bay also returned running back Chris Brooks from an ankle injury after he missed four games. Skyy Moore had just been reactivated off the IR but left the Vikings game with another ankle injury, but there will be other returns after the Week 11 bye.
That group includes center Sean Rhyan and linebacker Zaire Franklin. The Packers should be close to full strength against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, November 25.
Green Bay has been able to maintain a decent pace in the NFC North despite an injury-riddled roster. The Bears have dealt with similarly bad luck and made their chess move with the Jeffery Simmons blockbuster , but Detroit and Minnesota have not been shaken all year. If there's going to be a bottleneck in the NFC's Wild Card race down the stretch, you're almost certain to see issues in the NFC North over the final few weeks.
Chicago has all three of its divisional foes in the final three weeks: the Packers at home, the Lions also at Soldier Field, and then a road finale against the Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium.

title: Bears Duo Fined but None Issued on Play Causing Luther Burden's Concussion
full_text:
It's uncertain yet whether Bears receiver Luther Burden will be over his concussion suffered against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in time to play against New Orleans in Week 11.
What is certain is some Bears fans won't like the fact Tampa Bay's Rueben Bain Jr. went without being penalized or fined for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Burden, causing the injury. Burden was knocked unconscious and fumbled on the play that occurred with 3:48 left to play, and Ifeatu Melifonwu's recovery at the Chicago 21 led to the Buccaneers coming back to tie the score late.
There was no penalty flag thrown, and when the league came out with fines Bain went unscathed. It's possible the league decided Burden had lowered his helmet as well, and initiated contact, but the NFL doesn't explain plays involving non-fines. At least the league didn't fine Burden for lowering his helmet  to cause contact.
Tampa Bay didn't get by without a fine in the game for using a helmet to make a tackle. Neither did the Bears.
Reports confirm that Bears Luther Burden III suffered a concussion on this hit. Never should've been in doubt. Textbook sign "no protective action when falling" A conscious man tries to fall palms down. The backs of his hands hit first, which breaks wrists pic.twitter.com/NjVVoB3mmh
And the Bears wound up with more fines in what was a very physical game with the Buccaneers.
Tampa Bay's Keionte Scott received a $6,540 fine for using his helmet in stopping Bears receiver Kalif Raymond on an unpenalized 6-yard reception with 12:52 left in the second quarter. That was $7 less than what the league fined Bears edge rusher Austin Booker for when he was unpenalized for using his helmet with 30 seconds left in the first half. Baker Mayfield got the pass off but it was incomplete.
Did Luther Burden just get KNOCKED Out by Bain????
The fine against Booker for using his helmet was the fourth fine against the Bears this year for using the helmet. The biggest was $22,342 against Jahdae Walker in Week 2.
The NFL probably needs to be a little more consistent with how it throws out fines and penalties for plays involving helmet-to-helmet contact. Bain definitely made contact with the helmet but the play was similar to the play last year when Jordan Love was knocked out in a Packers game against the Bears on a hit by Booker. On that one, Love lowered his helmet much like Burden did, and then was knocked out. But Booker received a fine.
Austin Booker was fined $6,457 for use of the helmet from Week 9 for this hit on QB Baker Mayfield before halftime. Somehow, it wasn't flagged. pic.twitter.com/OHYMg52Fn1
The Bears predictably had another fine in the game with Tampa Bay. Zavion Thomas was penalized for unnecessary roughness/striking, kicking or kneeing, with 8:37 left in the second quarter after he struck Tampa Bay cornerback Jacob Parrish following the play during a post-play dispute. It occurred directly in front of the referees and the Bears received a 15-yard penalty.
Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie DB Keionte Scott was fined $6,540 for unnecessary roughness (use of helmet) for this hit on WR Kalif Raymond. There was no flag on this play. FWIW, OLB Rueben Bain Jr. was not fined for his hit that caused WR Luther Burden III's concussion. pic.twitter.com/N8Fu8TgF9f
The penalty on Thomas after a 2-yard D'Andre Swift run to the Buccaneers 6 moved the ball back to the 21 and the left the Bears in a second-and-long, goal-to-go situation. Caleb Williams threw his first interception of four on the next play. The penalty also was the last play Thomas was in for on offense, as coach Ben Johnson pointed out to reporters afterward.
The two fines for the Bears were their first since cornerback Clark Phillips received an $11,550 fine for using his helmet against Seattle the previous week.

title: How Chicago Bears Can Maintain First Place in NFC North Through Week 10 Bye
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are enjoying a bye this week while the rest of their NFC North competitors will be in action.
Chicago enters its Week 10 bye sitting in first place in the NFC North, but their lead is anything but secure with the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions all on their heels.
The Bears sport a 7-2 record, but both the Vikings and Lions are 6-2, and the Packers are not far behind in last place at 6-3. And, all three teams own tie-breakers over the Bears for now, with Green Bay and Minnesota having the head-to-head advantage and the Lions sporting the divisional record advantage.
Of course, the Bears will have an opportunity to erase those tie-breakers later in the season, but that's where things stand now.
Here's a look at how the Bears can maintain their grip on first place despite not playing in a game in Week 10.
1. Chicago Bears (7-2 2. Detroit Lions (6-2) 3. Minnesota Vikings (6-2) 4. Green Bay Packers (6-3)
In order for the Bears to stay in first place going into Week 11, they will need both the Vikings and Lions to lose their respective games.
A win for either team would technically push them in front of the Bears, who could fall to as far as third place, even with the same record as the Lions and/or Vikings.
The only team that cannot move past the Bears is the Packers, who would still have one more loss than Chicago even if they emerge victorious.
As we know, the Vikings beat the Bears in Week 2 , so that gives them the head-to-head tie-breaker advantage temporarily.
Meanwhile, the Lions sport a 2-0 record in the NFC North, so that's where their tie-breaker advantage over Chicago comes from. The Bears have lost both of their divisional games this season.
The Lions will square off against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning at 9:30 a.m. ET, while the Vikings draw a road matchup against the Packers at Lambeau.
There is no doubt that the NFC North is the best division in football. Not only does every team sport a winning record, but Chicago, Green Bay, Detroit and Minnesota are all sitting in a playoff sport entering Week 10.
If all four manage to make the playoffs in 2026, that would mark the first time in NFL history all teams in a division make the postseason.
Adding to that, the most wins for a division in a single season is 45, which was set by the 2024 NFC North.
Through nine weeks, the Bears (seven), Packers (six), Lions (six) and Vikings (six) have combined for 25 wins, so this year's version of the NFC North is already more than half way to the record.

title: Do the Chicago Bears Play Today? Schedule, Win-Loss Predictions for Rest of Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have played nine games of the 2026 season and the team is looking very much like a Super Bowl contender.
The Bears are in first place in the NFC North with a 7-2 record going into the weekend of Week 10 and will keep the spot atop the division if both the Detroit Lions (vs. New England Patriots) and Minnesota Vikings (vs. Green Bay Packers) lose.
Not only has the Bears' offense been playing at a high level thanks to Caleb Williams' ascension to elite status, but the defense has been playing better-than-expected football, also.
Entering Week 10, the Bears rank top 10 in total yards, rushing yards and points allowed per game, and their pass defense has been pretty good, with Chicago ranking 14th.
And there's hope for even better moving forward, as the Bears may be getting Dayo Odeyingbo back soon, and the addition of Jeffery Simmons has already provided a major boost and will continue to do so the rest of the way.
No, the Bears do not have a game in Week 10. That's because Chicago is enjoying its bye week.
But the rest of the NFC North will be in action, and with the Bears owning a loose grip on first place, we'll be paying close attention to what their division rivals do.
The Lions play the Patriots in Germany at 9:30 a.m. ET, and the Packers are hosting the Vikings at Lambeau in the 1p.m. ET window.
Here's how we see things shaking out for the Chicago Bears the rest of the season.
Week 11: vs. New Orleans Saints - Sunday, Nov. 22, 1 p.m. ET, FOX (win)
Week 12: at Detroit Lions - Thursday, Nov. 22, 1 p.m. ET, FOX (loss)
Week 14: at Miami Dolphins - Sunday, Dec. 13, 1 p.m. ET, CBS (win)
Week 15: at Buffalo Bills - Saturday, Dec. 19, 8:20 p.m. ET, CBS (loss)
Week 16: vs. Green Bay Packers - Friday, Dec. 25, 1 p.m. ET, Netflix (win)
Week 17: vs. Detroit Lions - Sunday, Jan 3, 4:25 p.m. ET, FOX (win)
Week 18: at Minnesota Vikings - TBD (win)
Final record prediction: 13-4 (1st place in NFC North)
The NFC North is once again very competitive this season, so it might take every one of those 13 wins to secure the division.
What's important for the Bears moving forward is shoring up some of these divisional tie-breakers they are behind in. The two most important ones are head-to-head record against NFC North opponents and divisional record.
Chicago has lost games to the Vikings and Packers, so both teams hold the head-to-head tie-breaker over the Bears for now, and as a result of those two losses, the Bears are 0-2 in the division, which amounts to the worst mark in the NFC North.
The next divisional game for Chicago comes in Week 12 against the Lions, and then they'll close out the season with three straight divisional contests against the Packers, Lions and Vikings.

title: Bengals' Unique Decision Sunday Night Has Steelers, Rest of NFL Playing Catch Up
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said he didn’t think the team was trying to send a message with the unorthodox, somewhat risky decision it made Sunday night prior to kickoff.
But perhaps head coach Zac Taylor was delivering one to his players.
The Bengals won the coin toss and took a left turn away from the norm, electing to receive the opening kickoff rather than deferring the choice to the second half, a decision that barely classifies as one any more with seemingly every team opting to start the second half, rather than the first, on offense.
But when your quarterback and the offense as a whole is on the sort of white-hot heater Burrow and the Bengals have enjoyed, it feels less like a gamble and more like wagering with inside information.
Burrow and the offense cashed in by receiving the opening kickoff and going 80 yards in 13 plays for a field goal that opened a portal to hell for a Steelers defense as the Bengals scored on five of their first six possessions on the way to a 31-3 lead and eventual 38-18 victory to take over the top of the AFC North Division.
“We just wanted to come out and be the aggressor, try to put points on the board early and get those guys behind so they didn’t feel great about running it, and (then) let our defensive line go to work,” Burrow said when asked if the team was sending a message with the rare decision to receive the opening kickoff.
Sunday marked the sixth time the Bengals have won the coin toss this season, and in each of the previous five they elected to defer the choice to the second half, which comes with the possibility of scoring on back-to-back possessions if they can add points late in the first half and then again to start the third quarter.
“I don’t know if (Taylor) told everybody, but I knew that we were going to set the tone and try to get out there and score points,” wide receiver Dohnte Meyers said. “We want to score points, and receiving the ball first, that’s the first opportunity to set the tone.”
Just last week, the Bengals won the toss in Madrid and deferred their choice to second half. They fell behind 7-0 but Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase lit up the Falcons, with Chase recording 142 receiving yards in the first half alone, a new career high for the opening 30 minutes.
Sunday night, he topped it with 146 to back up Taylor's decision to shrug off the consequences and try to strike first.
Taylor has been more willing than most coaches to buck the trend of deferring after winning the toss.
The Bengals 62-63 on coin toss during Taylor’s 125 regular season games.
Sunday was the 12th time he’s elected to receive the opening kickoff.
He only did it once during his first two seasons, and it didn’t go well. The Bengals lost 27-3 at Baltimore.
In 2022 after a string of poor opening drives, Taylor attempted to mix up the formula and opted to receive the opening kick in Week 3 against the Jets, and the Bengals scored on their first possession on the way to a 27-12.
Taylor also took the ball first in a 35-17 rout of Atlanta in Week 7 of 2022, and in a 27-24 victory at home against the Chiefs in Week 14.
He did it three times in 2023, with two coming in primetime – a Week 3, 19-16 Monday night win against the Rams and a Week 9, 24-18 win against the Bills. There also was the 27-3 loss at Tennessee in Week 4.
In 2024, Taylor did it again in primetime in a 17-7 win against the Giants in Week 6.
Last year there were three instances, all late in the season after Burrow’s return – a 39-34 loss at Buffalo in Week 14, a 37-14 win against Arizona in Week 17 and a 20-18 loss to Cleveland in Week 18.
With the way Burrow has been playing, don’t be surprised if the aggressive nature of scoring first and playing with the lead continues.
“He’s just on it,” Taylor said of Burrow. “I think Joe did an excellent job keeping his eyes down the field and finding guys for some big plays. Those guys made big plays and tremendous catches — all of those guys really. Everyone stepped up and made some plays for us. Obviously, he (Burrow) set the tone.
“This is just how he is,” Taylor added. “I feel like I’ve seen him in this rhythm quite a bit. He has a lot of confidence. Like I’ve said before, the offensive line is blocking so well, it allows us to play confident. At one point we had 24 passes and six runs. It is what it is. As long as these guys are doing that and we are making our way, that’s how it’s going to be.”
After falling behind early in three consecutive comeback wins against the Ravens, Titans and Falcons, the Bengals never trailed against the Steelers.
They led 17-0 before adding another TD on the final drive of the first half to go up 24-3. And it was 31-3 heading into the fourth quarter.
In Week 3 at Pittsburgh, the Bengals won the toss and deferred. The Steelers scored touchdowns on their opening two drives and got points on their first three, and Burrow and the offense were playing catch up.
Sunday night, they flipped things, both in terms of the game and the season, forcing the Steelers and the rest of the AFC North opponents to play catch up going into the second half of the season as they sit atop the division at 7-2.
“We don’t have to worry about what anybody else is doing,” Taylor said while answering a question about the division standings, but it could have just as well have been about the edge of taking the ball first and jumping on top.
“We just have to worry about our stuff,” he added. “This obviously gave us a big lift.”

title: Bengals Moderate Road Betting Favorites Against Commanders as Hot 2026 Season Rolls on
full_text:
The Bengals are rolling in the past month, and the betting odds for next Monday night's action against the Commanders reflect that. According to DraftKings Sportsbook, Cincinnati opened as a 4.5-point betting favorite, and the point total is set at 51.5.
Another 50-plus point total for the hottest offense in the NFL. Pittsburgh came into Sunday's 38-18 Bengals hammering with the NFL's top-scoring defense since Week 5, and Cincinnati plowed through them in the snow-white uniforms.
Cincinnati is now 7-2 overall as the AFC North leaders and 5-4 against the betting spread this season. They covered the 3.5-point betting line against the Steelers and now face a Commanders team fresh off a Thursday night win over New York. Washington is 3-5-1 overall and 5-4 ATS this season.
"It's one of the biggest wins we've had here in a while, but it's Week 10. We've got a lot of football here to be played. Learn from my mistakes, celebrate the win, but we'll come back and get better," Joe Burrow said after lighting up a fifth consecutive opponent for four-plus total touchdowns.
Burrow joined Peyton Manning in 2004 as the only QB in league history to score four-plus touchdowns in five consecutive games. Manning won the MVP that year, and Burrow is right at the head of the pack for that award in 2026.
“Yeah, feels great. We really haven't been in this spot since I've been in the league," Burrow noted. "Really, we were 5-2 in 2021, and then 7-6, and then trying to climb out of it. So it's nice to give ourselves some leeway, but we certainly aren't satisfied with where we're at and want to keep getting better.”
Burrow and Zac Taylor rallied the troops to respond well after a trip overseas and make major NFL history for the team. Cincinnati became the first team ever to win a game against a team off their bye after playing overseas (other teams 0-5 in prior outings).
Now, they get an extra day to rest before a road trip to face Washington.

title: 9 Winners and 2 Losers From the Bengals' Dominant Win Over the Steelers
full_text:
The Bengals dominated the Steelers through all four quarters on Sunday Night Football en route to a 38-18 victory in Paycor Stadium . The Bengals led 31-3 at the end of the third quarter, and Pittsburgh scored twice in garbage time to make the final score look more respectable. The Bengals are now 7-2 and are in first place in the AFC North.
Here are nine winners and two losers from Sunday night's victory:
Joe Burrow played at a level far above any other quarterback in the league on Sunday night in front of the world. He methodically marched the offense downfield on the team's first two drives and led the Bengals to a 10-0 score, completing 21 passes before Aaron Rodgers even completed one.
His dominant performance continued from that point on, and he finished with 35 completions, 409 yards, and 4 touchdowns for the fifth consecutive week. Burrow is playing the best football of his career and is the clear frontrunner for league MVP.
Risner was a late addition to the injury report with an illness; that said, he played through that issue and continued to play well before aggravating a knee injury he has battled all season. Should Risner miss significant time, Jalen Rivers should continue to fill his spot on the offensive line.
Hopefully, Risner recovers quickly and can return to the lineup at full strength. Obviously making him a "loser," simply means his injury was one of the only negatives in what was a dominant night for the home team.
Chase torched Asante Samuel Jr. and the Steelers' secondary regularly on Sunday. He caught 11 balls for 231 yards in the Bengals' big victory and proved once again that he is one of the best receivers the league has ever witnessed.
He sits at 64 receptions for 878 yards and seven touchdowns on the season and now has three consecutive weeks with at least 140 receiving yards.
Gesicki's only catch of the night happened on the game's opening drive when he caught a 9-yard pass from Burrow over the middle. Aside from that, he remained a non-existent piece of the game plan on a night where the offense dominated.
Brown is officially in mid-season form and showed up as arguably the most critical piece of the offense against Pittsburgh. He had multiple big plays in pass protection, and on top of that, he had 18 touches for 83 yards and two touchdowns.
It is evident how much this offense relies on Brown at times, and he is capable of delivering at a high level in those moments.
Taylor knew his team needed a fast start against the Steelers in a crucial AFC North contest, and he delivered massively. While his first challenge was unsuccessful, after the officials ruled Germie Bernard inbounds on a catch down the sideline, Taylor threw the challenge flag once more. This time he was successful, and officials reversed the call to an incomplete pass, forcing the Steelers to punt.
Taylor had this team ready to play its best football in the biggest moment of the season at this point and called a superb game offensively.
This is the game that everyone has waited for from the Bengals' young linebacker duo. Both Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter played effectively enough to where everyone should have excitement for their growth. Knight finished as the team's leading tackler with eight total tackles, including six solo tackles. Carter, meanwhile, finished with six tackles on the night, including a solid run stop on Jaylen Warren on a 2nd & 2 in the fourth quarter.
The offensive line dominated the trenches against a stout Steelers defensive line. Throughout the night the Bengals offensive line allowed only six pressures, according to Sumer Sports. Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt in check all night, with Watt having zero pressures against Mims, while Orlando Brown Jr. allowed only one pressure from his side.
Jalen Rivers, meanwhile, held up well when he entered the game following Risner's injury, showing solid growth at right guard.
Golden's unit on defense played its best game of the season so far, holding the Steelers to just 3 points through three quarters. The defense held Jaylen Warren to just 41 yards on 12 touches, while both Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington had only three catches for 40 yards and a garbage time touchdown.
All of Boye Mafe, Myles Murphy, Jonathan Allen, and Dexter Lawrence notched sacks for a total of four on the night. The rest of the defense played with great discipline all game long, and young players showed solid growth in the middle of the field and secondary.
The most heartwarming moment of Sunday's victory happened at the end of the first half when Meyers caught his first touchdown of his NFL career on a 15-yard strike from Burrow. Meyers spent the first two years of his professional football career with the CFL Saskatchewan Roughriders before signing a futures deal with the Bengals last January. He is now a key piece of the best offense in the NFL and has become a fan favorite in Cincinnati.
Paycor Stadium hit new levels of loud for the Bengals ' white-out game on Sunday night, and the fans in Cincinnati consistently made communication for Rodgers and the Steelers' offense difficult. The Bengals fanbase showed up in the best way they possibly could.

title: Ja'Marr Chase Makes Big Statement About Bengals' Offense After Blowout Win Over Steelers
full_text:
After dominating the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, Ja'Marr Chase spoke with SportsCenter's Scott Van Pelt following the end of the game and said the Bengals offense is currently at its peak. Chase praised the offensive line and Joe Burrow for their performance.
"I think right now, we're at our peak with momentum," Chase said. "The O-line's been playing incredible right now and giving Joe enough time to get the ball out of his hands, and Joe is just trusting his playmakers to win in space."
Chase continued saying that confidence is high within the locker room and pointed to the team's victory in Madrid over the Falcons last week. He stated that he saw that game as the launching point for the offense to reach its peak.
"The confidence should be really high, especially after the Madrid game, we flew eight hours and had a great game in Madrid, after that game that's when we should see our momentum and be taking off," Chase said. "I said that last week in an interview after the game and that's what I wanna say we got it from."
Chase expanded further and emphasized how massive the additions to the defense have impacted this Bengals team. He explained that it is really what the team needed, saying that players such as Dexter Lawrence, Bryan Cook, and Boye Mafe have shown they were worth the investment.
"Those guys are such a big help, that's really what we needed this year, they're showing why they're worth it, showing why they got picked and why they've got that name on their back," Chase said.
Cook has provided an exceptional level of leadership to the Bengals' secondary, while both Lawrence and Mafe have combined for 11.5 sacks this year. Jonathan Allen has also shown up as a quality addition to the pass rush with four sacks this year from the interior of the defensive line.
Chase finished saying that the sky is the limit for this Bengals team, and that the team will continue to take each game one at a time.
"The sky is always the limit at the end of the day, but we've gotta take it one game at a time, control what we can control, and the only thing we're worried about is being number one in the division," Chase said.

title: Joe Burrow Dominates as Bengals Take Down Steelers: Instant Takeaways
full_text:
The Bengals beat the Steelers 38-18 on Sunday night. It was a dominant performance by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and a Cincinnati team that is a force to be wrecked with in the AFC.
The Bengals improve to 7-2 on the season. They've won 5-straight games and are in sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Here are our instant takeaways to the victory:
The Bengals absolutely dominated the Steelers from the start. Cincinnati built a 31-3 lead late in the third quarter. They scored on five of their first six possessions and the only time they didn't score was due to a missed field goal. Four of those five scoring drives ended with touchdowns.
Meanwhile, the defense forced punts on 5-of-6 drives to start the game. They took away the Steelers' rushing attack and Aaron Rodgers couldn't find anyone open downfield for most of the game.
Pittsburgh scored two fourth quarter touchdowns to make the score look a bit more competitive, but this was utter domination.
This is exactly what a Super Bowl contending team should do to a team like Pittsburgh. The Steelers have talent, but they have some clear flaws. The Bengals protected Burrow, got after Rodgers and the rest was history.
Burrow completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns. He finished with a 135.7 passer rating. Burrow joins Peyton Manning as the only other player to score 4+ total touchdowns in 5-straight games in NFL history. Manning did it in 2004 en route to an MVP. Burrow is well on his way to doing the same here in Cincinnati.
Burrow wasn't alone. Ja'Marr Chase led the way with 11 catches for 231 yards on 14 targets. He averaged 21 yards-per-catch. Tee Higgins finished with 66 yards on five catches. Chase Brown had eight catches for 39 yards and two receiving touchdowns.
This offense was so dominant that Joe Flacco and the Bengals' backups finished the game.
The Bengals sacked Aaron Rodgers three times. They also held the Steelers to just 62 rushing yards on 17 attempts (3.6 yards-per-carry).
Rodgers completed 15-of-29 attempts for 143 yards and two touchdowns. Most of his yards and both of his touchdowns came in the fourth quarter.
Rodgers entered the fourth quarter with just seven completions for 27 yards. Steelers star receiver DJ Metcalf didn't have a catch until the fourth quarter. Neither did starting tight end Pat Freiermuth. Both guys scored in the fourth quarter to pad their stats.
This was a dominant outing from Al Golden's unit and by far their best outing of the season.
The Bengals will try to extend their winning streak on Monday Night Football. They head to Washington to play the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23 at 8:15 p.m. ET.

title: Key Bengals Starter Ruled Out After Suffering Injury vs Steelers
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals guard Dalton Risner has been ruled out of Sunday night’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers with a knee injury, the team announced.
Risner was initially listed as questionable to return after leaving the game. Jalen Rivers entered the game in place of the injured offensive lineman.
Risner started at right guard at Paycor Stadium after having been deemed questionable to play with an illness.
The Bengals currently have a 31-3 lead in the third quarter and have scored three touchdowns since Risner left the game. That means Rivers has held up his end of the bargain. Joe Burrow and this Bengals' offense has been on fire all night long.
Cincinnati re-signed Risner in March after he made 11 starts in his first season with the Bengals. His spot is between center Ted Karras and right tackle Amarius Mims.
Risner opened 2026 with eight straight starts at right guard. The 30-year-old guard reached 100 career starts in Week 9 against Atlanta.
Pass protection has been one of Risner's strengths throughout his career. PFF gave him a 71.5 pass block grade, which ranked 17th among all guards in the NFL. He's been one of the better guards in the NFL and helped bring stability to the Bengals' offensive line.
Burrow explained this week what extra time means for Cincinnati's passing game when he spoke about the offensive line before the Pittsburgh matchup.
“Our offense is open to so many different things. We're more explosive than we have been in years and that plays a huge part of it. It's hard to push the ball down the field if you can't protect for that extra second, second and a half in order to do it.”
When two rushers cross over after the snap, Risner and Mims must recognize the exchange and pass them off before either gets a clear path to Burrow. Head coach Zac Taylor credited the time the starters have spent working through those kinda of problems together
“We've just been so fortunate with continuity, and I think that with every game they play together, every rep they take, and every look they get together, they talk about it and improve on it. And if they don't get it right, it really bothers them and bothers them to their core.”

Dalton Risner limped to the locker room after the Bengals’ third drive of the game and wasn’t on the field for the last possession. He went to the locker room. Jalen Rivers was in at right guard on that last possession. Video: @jaron_may pic.twitter.com/BZTf14p8EU

title: Cincinnati Bengals Announce Inactive List for AFC North Showdown vs Pittsburgh Steelers
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals starting right guard Dalton Risner is active for tonight’s AFC North showdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football.
The week began with concerns about starting left guard Dylan Fairchild due to a pectoral injury he suffered late in the 34-17 win against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid last Sunday.
But after going limited in Wednesday’s practice, Fairchild went full Thursday and Friday and did not have an injury designation on the final injury report.
Neither did Risner, but the Bengals announced Sunday afternoon they were downgrading him and offensive tackle Myles Hinton to questionable due to illness.
Hinton has been inactive for every game this season since the Bengals claimed him on waivers from the Philadelphia Eagles on Aug. 31.
Risner has started 25 consecutive games since coming off the bench in last year’s primetime game against the Steelers.
Pro Football Focus has Risner graded as the 10th best guard in the league this year. He’s 10th in pass blocking and eighth in run blocking.
With the Bengals only having 52 on the active roster, they only need four actives. They are safety Kyle Dugger, center Connor Lew, offensive tackle Myles Hinton and defensive tackle Landon Robinson.
Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati.
The Bengals ruled out Dugger on Friday, meaning he’ll miss his fifth game in the last six with a quadricep injury.
Asked if Dugger, a former Steeler, is a candidate to land on Injured Reserve, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he was not, indicating the safety could be close to returning to action.
Three Bengals who are currently on IR had their 21-day practice window opened Thursday, but the team is listing all three as doubtful for Sunday night’s battle for first place in the AFC North Division.
Cornerback Jalen Davis, wide receiver Andrei Iosivas and rookie guard Brian Parker II were all listed as full participants Thursday and Friday.
Parker, the team’s fifth-round pick out of Duke, has been on IR since Aug. 30 with a knee injury.
Iosivas has been on IR since Sept. 26 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards before suffering the injury in Week 2 at Houston.
Talking after practice Thursday, he sounded encouraged about his chances of playing Sunday.
Davis went on IR on Sept. 30 with a hamstring injury suffered in the first meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3.
The Bengals listed all three as doubtful on the injury report but did not activate any of them to the 53-man roster by Saturday’s 4 p.m. deadline, resulting in them being downgraded to out.
Because they are not on the 53-man roster, they are not eligible to be on the inactive list.
With Davis still at least another week away, look for Josh “Fig” Newton to get the second start of his career if Davis isn’t activated.
Newton has played sparingly in his three seasons before getting a full snap load Sunday in Madrid. Defensive coordinator Al Golden said Newton’s performance had both ups and downs.
“(Cornerbacks coach Chuck Burks) did a great job with him just bringing him along to the point where, OK, he's ready to do it. Let's see what it looks like,” Golden said. “And then Fig did the rest.
“Fig has great energy. Smart player. And he's vocal. He's a good communicator,” Golden said. “I thought he played really hard. There's some plays I know that he would like to have back, but overall, he really, really responded well.”

title: Bengals Place Key Starter on Injury Report Ahead of Sunday Night's Game vs Steelers
full_text:
The Bengals placed Dalton Risner on the injury report on Sunday morning ahead of their primetime contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Risner is officially listed as questionable due to an illness. Backup lineman Myles Hinton is also questionable due to an illness.
Jacob Bayer is listed as the Bengals' backup right guard. He would likely play if Risner can't suit up. The veteran lineman is a big part of what the Bengals have built in the trenches in their quest to protect Joe Burrow.
The Bengals are as confident as they've ever been in their offensive line during the Burrow era. Head coach Zac Taylor heaped praise on the group earlier this week.
“We've just been so fortunate with continuity, and I think with every game that they play together, and every every rep they take, and every look they get together, they talk about it and they improve on it," Taylor said. "And if they don't get it right, it really bothers them and it bothers them to their core. And it's going to carry over to their Thursday night dinner and all the stuff that they do together. That's going to be a big topic of conversation. Anytime you’ve got linemen that take pride in that, probably more so in the negatives that they've had than the positives. That's a good thing for the coach because they want to clean that stuff up. And obviously, the way the amount of times we throw the football directly shows my confidence I have in our offensive line. Because if we weren't, if I didn't have that confidence, then we wouldn't do that. We'd be looking at other ways to manufacture yardage and points. And we operate the way we do because I got a lot of confidence in how they do it."
Burrow is completing 74% of his passes this season. He has thrown for 2,386 yards, 23 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's been sacked 15 times, which is less than two sacks per game in an offense where they're throwing the ball far more than anyone else.
"I think they're all playing at a really high level," Burrow said this week. "The cohesion that they have and the trust that they have and the relationships that they have upfront is fun to be around and fun to watch and fun to be a part of. Our offense is open to so many different things. We're more explosive than we have been in years and that plays a huge part of it. It's hard to push the ball down the field if you can't protect for that extra second, second and a half in order to do it. You can find ways to do it, but it's a lot harder. The guys that we have, I mean they're lights out, they're playing some of the best football in the league and got to continue to get better and continue to improve, but we're in a really good spot."
The Bengals' offensive line was already going to be tested on Sunday night. The Steelers have one of the most talented and deep offensive lines in the NFL. Cris Collinsworth made it clear that Amarius Mims playing in 1-on-1 situations is critical for the Bengals to have success. It would be even more critical if Risner can't suit up on Sunday night.
"Amarius Mims has become that guy that can block one-on-one, the problem is that one-on-one this week is Amarius Mims against T.J. Watt," Collinsworth said on First Word . "They will take T.J. Watt and move him over to the other side a little bit, but it is really difficult to say 'I got T.J. Watt all day and nothing's going to happen', now he did well against him the last time out, but for all the stuff we want to talk about Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow and these receivers, I think that matchup may well decide the game."

title: Cris Collinsworth Reveals What Will Decide Bengals-Steelers Showdown
full_text:
Ahead of the Bengals matchup against the Steelers, Cris Collinsworth spoke about the key matchups within the upcoming AFC North clash on First Word. He emphasized that both Amarius Mims and Orlando Brown Jr. face the most pressure on Sunday because of the presence of T.J. Watt. He also clarified that Mims has developed into a capable one-on-one blocker who held up well against Watt earlier in the season.
"Amarius Mims has become that guy that can block one-on-one, the problem is that one-on-one this week is Amarius Mims against T.J. Watt," Collinsworth said . "They will take T.J. Watt and move him over to the other side a little bit, but it is really difficult to say 'I got T.J. Watt all day and nothing's going to happen', now he did well against him the last time out, but for all the stuff we want to talk about Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow and these receivers, I think that matchup may well decide the game."
In Week 3, Mims held up perfectly against Watt and the Steelers' defense and allowed no pressure at all with a 0.0% pressure rate, according to Sumer Sports.
Collinsworth added that if Mims handles Watt one-on-one, it is a good answer to Pittsburgh's effective blitz packages on defense.
"If they can truly leave Mims over there on T.J. Watt and help the rest of it [the offensive line]. They're (Pittsburgh) a blitz happy team and they are so good at it," Collinsworth said. "I think they had seven sacks or something against the Browns, and what you see is that the first three or four sacks, the guy who actually got the pressure didn't get the sack, it was the next wave that came in and got him."
While Collinsworth acknowledged Chase Brown as a solid running back, he added that Samaje Perine should show up as the primary option when the Steelers' defense doubles both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. He pointed out Perine's ability to close out the game against the Falcons last week as the main reason, with his 240-pound build as a power runner against lighter boxes as the other reason.
"Chase Brown is a good player, but Samaje Perine at the end of that Atlanta game came in and had that four minute close the game kind of stuff," Collinsworth said . "When defenses have to go lighter in the box because you got to double team everybody on the Bengals, especially Ja'Marr and Tee, so if you could put a 240lb truck and hand him the football back there, it really changes things because now you have to decide are you willing to let Samaje Perine run the ball through a lighter box in the middle there and do that to keep the double teams."
He added that the Steelers could end up with five players lined up in the box and that he does not see any scenario where the Steelers allow the Bengals' receivers to beat them deep.
"It may well be if they don't run it with a 6-man box, they could end up with five in there and really load up on the backend, I just don't see any scenario where Pittsburgh lets the Bengals get the ball consistently deep over their heads," he said.
Jaylen Warren has played as effectively as any other running back in the NFL and is the heart of the Steelers' offense. Collinsworth said that Warren and the Steelers have almost as many big plays running the ball as the Bengals do passing. He pointed out that Warren is averaging an absurd 5.9 yards per carry and that the Steelers' run-blocking scheme is a large reason why.
"Pittsburgh is going to be a real test to stop the run, this team has almost as many big plays running the ball, as the Bengals do throwing the ball," Collinsworth said. "Jaylen Warren's averaging 5.9 YPC and so they are really legit, they've got every run scheme up the middle."
He noted that Dexter Lawrence is the most critical piece in slowing down Warren, praising Lawrence as much of an integral piece to the Bengals franchise as any quarterback or receiver.
"A lot of it frankly is going to be Dexter Lawrence, Dexter Lawrence is that guy that in my mind changed the franchise almost as much as quarterbacks and the receivers have," Collinsworth praised. "Dexter Lawrence draws those double teams so now Allen and Mafe and some of those guys are getting opportunities to rush in a way that maybe they wouldn't have, but in this game Dexter Lawrence stopping the run, can they get that done?"
Warren gashed the Bengals earlier in the season for 176 yards on 20 touches with 7.5 yards per carry. If the Bengals hope to come out of Sunday Night Football with a win, they cannot allow him to have that kind of production again.

title: Joe Burrow Makes Powerful Statement Ahead of Bengals-Steelers Showdown
full_text:
The Bengals welcome the Steelers into Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football with the lead in the AFC North on the line. Joe Burrow knows precisely how crucial this game against the Steelers is when it comes to winning the division. He emphasized that it is as big of a game that the Bengals have had in Paycor Stadium in a long time during his press conference because of their loss to the Steelers earlier in the season.
"This is as big of a game as we've had here in a while, we lost to them early in the season, number one," Burrow said. "With the standings at the end of their year you want that to be split, and number two for first place outright.
Burrow also explained the advantages playing at home for the offense in games of this magnitude. He said that the ability to use the offenses cadence as a weapon in a high stakes environment offers more advantage compared to on the road.
"When you're at home you use your cadence as a weapon, you can't really do it on the road, we have a lot of different silent cadences that you can use on the road but it's not as effective," Burrow explained. "When you can use your cadence as a weapon, you get the defense to show what they're doing and get in and out of plays and get in and out of protection calls, whereas on the road that's a lot harder."
He highlighted as well that while having a crucial game in primetime at home again is exciting, one game will not determine where they ultimately finish at the end of the season.
"It's exciting but one game's not gonna determine it, six or seven wins isn't gonna get you to where you wanna be," Burrow said. "There's a long season left, its a big game this week, but next week is a big game too, and the week after that, so we are just focused on this one and trying to make this one a win and go from there."
With a win, the Bengals will move into sole possession of first place in the AFC North at 7-2. A loss would put them a game behind the Steelers in the standings and give Pittsburgh the head-to-head tiebreaker.

title: Deshaun Watson Steals the Spotlight, But This Browns Player Deserves More Credit
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns took down the Houston Texans at home in week 10.
For Cleveland, Deshaun Watson stepped up and had a huge game once again. However, there is another player who is constantly making an impact that isn't getting the credit he deserves.
Harold Fannin Jr. finished Sunday's game with 7 catches for 91 yards.
So far in this season, Harold Fannin Jr. has 37 receptions for 453 yards and four touchdowns.
This stat line comes after a slow start to the season, and multiple weeks with one catch for less than 10 yards.
Despite this, Fannin is second on the team in receiving yards, only behind rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston.
If he continues at his current rate, along with the unknown injury status of Boston, Fannin could definitely turn into the first option out of all the pass catches and potentially finish the year with over 1,000 yards.
But in the past few weeks, his production has ramped up significantly, and some of the plays he's made have changed the game.
Harold Fannin Jr. down to the 5! HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GQL0DtQAaV
Looking at the last three games, Fannin has really increased his production with the Browns.
It all starts with his career day against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In that contest, Fannin recorded his most catches in a single game with 10, and also his most receiving yards with 154.
Last week against New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders struggled to get him the ball. However, we all remember what happened when he finally did see an opportunity in overtime, taking a five-yard pass to the house and earning the "Angry Run" title.
Then, once again on Sunday, Fannin proved to be a big part of this Browns offense. Not only did he post another great stat line, but he also made another big play late in the game to set the Browns up for victory.
While some say Fannin needs to learn how to block and further develop his game, others are already calling him one of the best tight ends in the entire NFL.
Let's be honest, if Fannin keeps up his production and starts having these great games more consistently, who's to say he can't achieve that top title and be looked at as the next Travis Kelce or George Kittle?
Clearly, the skill set, playmaking ability, and stardom are already there. It really is up to the Browns and Todd Monken to utilize him more in passing plays.
Regardless, the future is bright for the young tight end.
No matter what happens, he deserves more credit for the Browns success in 2026.

title: Could Deshaun Watson be the CPOTY? Making His Case Following Browns' 6-4 Start
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have put together an impressive first half of the season and head into their bye week with a 6-4 record.
Not only are the Browns 6-4 and still heavily in the mix for the playoffs, but they’re also undefeated at Huntington Bank Field for the first time since 1963.
This is undoubtedly an overall team effort, but much of their success is thanks to quarterback Deshaun Watson. After a troublesome first few years in Cleveland, Watson is finally playing like the quarterback they had originally invested their future into.
After a massive 27-24 victory over Watson’s former team , the Houston Texans, the fans and the media are giving him his much-deserved credit for getting the team to this point. Now, Watson’s name is cemented in the running for this season's Comeback Player of the Year.
Here’s why Watson is being considered for the CPOTY award this season:
It’s safe to say that leading up to this season, most Browns fans were expecting another down year especially if Watson was the starting quarterback of this team. That’s a fair assumption considering how poorly he had played in recent years.
Fast forward to this week, Watson has played like his Houston-self and rewrote all of the narratives that had been published for years now. Multiple season-ending injuries and lackluster play contributed to that, but it doesn’t seem to be affecting him now.
Watson now has six fourth quarter comebacks this season to help his Browns secure much needed wins. His stats on the year through ten weeks include 1,800 passing yards with seven touchdowns to three interceptions.
He’s already played more games this season than he has in each of his previous three seasons, as he averaged six games played each year to this point. His stats are the best he’s seen since arriving in Cleveland, and the team is reaping the rewards of his consistency.
Watson also hasn’t topped seven passing touchdowns since joining the Browns and already has that number matched through ten games. He is the unanimous starting quarterback in Cleveland and is certainly making his case to sign an extension this offseason.
Between Cleveland’s young core of star players , both first year and second- or third-year players combined with their respectable veterans, this Browns team is looking to make noise down the stretch of a very manageable second half of their schedule.
Watson is still creating chemistry with his offensive weapons, and some weeks are better than others. However, if he continues playing at this level and orchestrating late game comebacks, there’s no doubt he should be in serious contention for the CPOTY award in February.
Dominic Pagura is from Medina, Ohio and a graduate from Kent State University.

title: Wild Stat Shows How Clutch The Browns Have Been This Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns pulled off a very inspiring victory on Sunday over the Houston Texans, winning 27-24 after Houston scored on their first three drives of the game. Cleveland then went on to score the next 20 points of the game, leading 20-17 after three quarters.
After a long missed field goal from Andre Szmyt, Houston capitalized on a long pass interference called on Myles Harden and punched it in to lead by four with nine minutes to go. Deshaun Watson then got picked off on a pass that went off Blake Whiteheart’s hands; two more three-and-outs were forced by the Browns defense.
Then it was time for Watson to do what he has done better than any quarterback in the league: go win the game. The Browns did just that, as Watson completed a strike to Harold Fannin Jr., who rumbled his way to the Houston five-yard line, and then Judkins punched it in for the eventual game-winning score.
The Browns are the first team in NFL history whose first six wins of a season all come by 4 points or fewer, according to ESPN Research.
That stat says a lot about this group and who is in the lead of the Browns: head coach Todd Monken . While some fans might not think this way of winning is sustainable, you will take any win you can get in this league.
Over the last two years under Kevin Stefanski, the Browns went 6-10 in one-score games; this season under Monken, Cleveland is 6-2 in the same criteria.
Another stat that shows how great Cleveland has been this season in terms of comeback victories, from Daniel Oyefusi, is that Cleveland now has four double-digit comeback wins this year, which is tied for the most by a team through the first 10 games in NFL history.
Watson has now led his sixth game-winning drive of the season, proving his coach right in putting him right back into the lineup after he had to miss a game with a concussion.
The Browns are keeping pace with the top of the AFC North, as the Bengals and Steelers match up on Sunday Night Football, and the winner will take the lead of the division. Cleveland will finally get their bye week next week, before staying home for the next three weeks.
Those home games range from facing up against rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in Week 12, then the divisional foe, Cincinnati Bengals, led by MVP candidate Joe Burrow; former coach Kevin Stefanski brings his Atlanta Falcons into Cleveland for an emotional matchup to cap off the homestand.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: 3 Takeaways From Browns' Nail-Biting Win Over Texans for Sixth Victory of 2026
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns love to get the nerves going.
And on Sunday, Nov. 15, they did exactly that again.
Trailing 17-0 early to the Houston Texans, the Browns rallied to take a 20-17 lead in the second half of play. They then proceeded to fall behind 24-20 before starting quarterback Deshaun Watson led the team to a game-winning drive, his sixth of the season, to secure a 27-24 victory.
On the final drive of the game, Watson, after drawing a 15-yard unnecessary roughness call, completed a 30-yard pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr., getting the Browns into position to score. He would hand off the ball to Quinshon Judkins, who punched in the eventual winner.
"The game is never over," Watson said postgame. "As long as we have time on the clock and we have an opportunity, we are going to believe we can finish it off."
“The game is never over. As long as we have time on the clock and we have opportunity, we're going to believe we can finish it off.” Deshaun Watson speaks with @MeganOlivi after the Browns’ 17-point comeback win over the Texans. pic.twitter.com/fOBKC362A5
Here are the three biggest takeaways from Sunday's victory that improved the Browns to 6-4 on the season:
The Browns always seem to turn it on a bit late, but Watson is always there to deliver.
Deshaun Watson has a game-winning drive in all 6 wins this season. Brown are 4-0 at home for first time since 1963. pic.twitter.com/V5ROnWUxBr
In all six of the Browns' wins this season, Watson has been credited with being the catalyst for the game-winning drives.
He finished Sunday's victory with 25 completions on 40 attempts, going for 312 yards on an average of 7.8 yards per reception. He did not find the end zone through the air, but added one score on the ground, along with 49 yards on eight carries.
Looking to continue making the offense more versatile, the Browns have been pushing Watson outside of the pocket more and more, hoping to see him extend drives with his legs.
He is now up over 2,100 yards passing this season , all while recording back-to-back-to-back 300-yard games.
If he can keep this up, the Browns are going to be in good hands as they search for a spot in the playoffs over the coming weeks.
Running back Quinshon Judkins couldn't be in a more confusing system.
Each week, the offensive scheme has him diving headfirst up the middle, whereas his speed and athleticism certainly have him much more suited for outside runs. However, he still made advantage of his limited opportunities on Sunday.
Scoring the game-winning touchdown on the Browns' final offensive drive, Judkins capped off his day with 10 carries for 38 yards and one score.
He is now up to over 400 rushing yards and four scores this season, but still sits below 3.5 yards per carry.
In order to get the most out of the rushing attack, Judkins either needs 10 more carries a game or more versatility in where he is expected to run. Gaining one or two yards up the gut as he crashes into a wall of bodies is just simply not getting the most out of the 23-year-old.
After falling down 17-0 through the first two quarters, not only did Cleveland's offense finally turn things up a notch, but so did the defense.
They would go on to give up just seven points for the rest of the contest, limiting Texans quarterback CJ Stroud's ability to get the offense going. They also forced him to throw an interception.
A wild juggling INT from Tyson Campbell 😳 HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o05D4nQ0We
Stroud's final score of the game came on the Texans' second-to-last drive, but the Browns' defense had held the offense to a punt or an interception on the previous six straight drives.
After allowing him to score early in the fourth quarter, the defense forced him and the offense off the field on every subsequent drive without allowing them to do any further damage:
~  3 Plays, -1 Yard (Punt) ~ 3 Plays, 0 Yards (Punt) ~ 6 Plays, 3 Yards (Turnover on Downs)
That type of production with the game on the line is so important, and also proves that this team has what it takes to compete when the stakes are the highest.
Now, they have to just turn Sunday's result into an all-game constant, rather than a late-game surge.

title: Browns Rookie Earns High Praise From Head Coach Amid Growing Pains
full_text:
There have been plenty of storylines following the Cleveland Browns all season long.
However, one that has lost some of its spotlight since the opening few weeks is the development of the team's rookie offensive linemen.
Following several struggles along the offensive line in recent weeks, most notably from veteran Tytus Howard, rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano have been overshadowed.
And honestly, it isn't hard to understand why.
Even with both Barber and Fano playing well, quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been sacked a total of 38 times across nine games , averaging out to over four sacks a game. If Cleveland wants to legitimately contend by the time the playoffs roll around, the line is going to have to be better.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke about Fano in particular, saying that the issues the line has gone through have allowed the ninth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft an opportunity to learn and grow.
"It’s so cool for him because of the way he’s wired, how he works at it — highly intelligent, very prideful, but it’s not easy being indoctrinated into playing left tackle as a rookie," he said. "And every week it feels like there is no off week, right? There isn’t an off week of these guys that are paid to get to the quarterback.
"And it really stresses your mental stamina, play after play, right? There is no ‘oh, I get a little bit of a smoke break here’. Oh, no, right. You don’t get that."
Fano currently ranks 17th out of 71 in the league in overall Pro Football Focus grade , placing him among some of football's best offensive tackles. In pass rush, there is still work to be done, with him ranking 39th out of 71, but his rushing ranking of 22nd pushes him back up towards the top of the ladder.
As Monken mentioned, even with him being moved from right tackle, which he was accustomed to in college, to left tackle, the 22-year-old has made incredible strides quickly.
He went on to say that the difference in competition is something that Fano has had to learn to be ready for, especially with edge rushers being so dynamic at the NFL level. One play he could be going up against a veteran before a shifty, young rusher comes flying his way the next.
Browns HC Todd Monken talked about the growing pains Spencer Fano is going through as a young tackle in the NFL and said there's "no smoke break" to catch your breath "It’s so cool for him because the way he’s wired, how he works at it, highly intelligent, very prideful, but… pic.twitter.com/qE0e7PTtyt
"You know, and then they roll (Jadeveon) Clowney in there, and they roll other guys that are young and trying to get the quarterback," Monken continued. "Like, that’s what’s the coolest thing about being a part of professional sports and being in professional football. Everybody’s got really good players, and it really challenges you.
"And I like his mental makeup. I like the way he’s wired. He’s only going to continue to get better."
Fano's next chance to return to the field and try to lead the Browns' offensive line comes on Sunday, Nov. 15.
The Browns play host to the Houston Texans from Huntington Bank Field at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Texans Rule Out Two Key Players Ahead of Browns Matchup on Sunday
full_text:
On Friday, the Cleveland Browns, just two days ahead of their matchup against the Houston Texans at home, announced that they would be without safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton.
Rookie Browns wideout Denzel Boston was also ruled questionable , putting the team in an even more difficult spot on Sunday against the Texans.
But the Browns aren't the only team banged up.
Following the Browns' injury report, a few hours passed, and the Texans issued their injury report ahead of Sunday's game, ruling out newly acquired wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. and defensive end Danielle Hunter.
Most importantly, the Texans may be without defensive end Will Anderson Jr., too, as the 6-foot-4, 243-pound defensive end is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury.
The #Browns won't face DE Danielle Hunter or WR Marvin Harrison Jr. on Sunday—and DE Will Anderson Jr. is in question with an ankle injury. https://t.co/wM1hRzoezb
For the Texans, not having Anderson Jr. on Sunday is something that could be a big impact, as the two-time pro bowler has put together a great season with 9.5 sacks in only eight games . Anderson Jr. has surpassed his 2023 rookie sack total (7.0 sacks) and will look to surpass the career high he set last season with 12.0 sacks.
Offensively, the Texans are looking to get Harrison Jr. involved more following their trade with the Arizona Cardinals, as Harrison Jr. became a part of the franchise on October 12 and has only been targeted 11 times in the three games played.
On the season, with both the Cardinals and the Texans, he has only been targeted 24 times with 11 receptions, averaging around 13.2 yards per reception. That is good enough for just 145 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
He hasn't had a big impact on the game this season, but missing Sunday keeps him behind the curve as he tries to adjust to the new system in Houston.
With Harrison Jr. out, the Texans will have to work in other guys on the offensive side of the ball.
While Anderson Jr. ruled questionable, the Texans know they will be without at least one defensive end in Hunter, as he is dealing with a hamstring injury.
Hunter has played in all eight games ahead of the matchup against the Browns and has played in all games since 2022, dating back to his days with the Minnesota Vikings. Hunter has been with Houston since 2024 and will miss his first game as a Texan on Sunday.
With the Texans' injury report being out and a good chunk of important pieces being on the list, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson could have bought himself another week to succeed as the starter.
Defensively, the Browns will have a much easier time at locking down the passing game with Harrison Jr. inactive.
The two sides will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 15.

title: Browns vs. Texans: 3 Matchups That Could Decide Sunday’s Game
full_text:
Houston has won three of its last four after a 0-4 start.
A Texans win would pull them within half a game of Cleveland and give Houston the head-to-head edge in the AFC playoff race.
Luckily for the Browns, the Texans are beatable, and here is why:
Denzel Boston leads the Browns with 507 receiving yards and averages 15.8 yards per catch. The Houston Texans have allowed 31 completions of 20 yards or more this season, tied for the third most in the NFL. Boston will have a chance to build on his six catches for 98 yards against New Orleans, including a 60-yard reception.
DENZEL BOSTON MOSSED HIM pic.twitter.com/ZZdzSZtnpj
The caveat comes down to blocking, as the Browns' offensive line has struggled in recent weeks and has allowed 38 total sacks this season , the most in the NFL. If Deshaun Watson has time to get the ball deep to Boston, the Browns have a fighting chance.
Rookie left tackle Spencer Fano will be central to Cleveland’s chances of keeping Watson upright. Fano ranks 17th out of 71 qualifying NFL tackles with a 74.5 overall grade, according to PFF. Fano allowed a season-high eight pressures against Pittsburgh in Week 8.
Now he faces a Houston pass rush led by Will Anderson Jr., the Defensive Player of the Year betting favorite with an NFL-high 9.5 sacks.
Love to see this. KC - orbit motion decoy (holds BS LB) Fano - down block on Simmons (All-Pro) Boston - crack block on PS safety Barber - counter kickout Fannin - counter pull for PS ILB Judkins - tight course, make CB miss Every key player mentioned here is 22yo or younger. pic.twitter.com/XW4Xue6x7h
Fano’s best game of his young career came against the Tennessee Titans, when he earned a 92.2 overall PFF grade and allowed just two pressures on 41 pass-blocking snaps.
If Fano can come close to that performance, Cleveland will have a better chance to give Watson time to attack Houston downfield.
Jared Verse’s production has been debated in Cleveland this season. Verse has just 15 pressures, according to PFF, and no sacks through nine games, despite being a key part of the Myles Garrett trade and viewed as a cornerstone of the Browns' defense.
Verse acknowledged that he hasn’t played well and said he spoke with the team psychologist about what he described as a “mental block.”
#Browns DE Jared Verse said he's reflected a lot on his struggles this season and believes he's identified areas to help him be more productive, but a lot of that work has been on the mental side. It's why he took time to meet with the team psychiatrist to help him "self-build."… pic.twitter.com/8pxPv0OxgX
His next test comes against Houston right tackle Trent Brown. Brown ranks 42nd among 71 qualifying tackles with a 64.2 overall PFF grade. Brown has allowed 19 pressures and two sacks on 342 pass-blocking snaps, according to Core Football Labs.
Even if Verse doesn’t get his first sack, forcing C.J. Stroud out of the pocket could help limit Houston’s deep passing game.
Make no mistake, the Texans are not an easy matchup. Stroud has four 300-yard passing games this season, including a 384-yard, five-touchdown performance last week against the Chargers.
If Cleveland gives Watson time to find his receivers downfield and keeps Stroud from doing the same, the Browns can head into the bye at 6-4.

title: Browns Hit With Major Injury News Ahead of Week 10 Showdown With Texans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns might have seen the return of quarterback Deshaun Watson from concussion protocol after he missed last week's game.
But the team will now potentially be without a different key member of the offense this weekend.
On Friday, Nov. 13, the Browns announced another batch of injuries ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday.
First announced by ESPN NFL Insider Daniel Oyefusi, rookie wideout Denzel Boston was listed as questionable heading into the weekend due to a toe injury.
Browns WR Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable. FB Mike Burton and S Ronnie Hickman have been ruled out.
The 6-foot-4, 215-pound rookie has been one of the Browns' most exciting offseason additions to the offense , coming out of the draft quickly and making his impact. Across his first nine games, he has 32 receptions for 507 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 15.8 yards per reception.
His connection with Deshaun Watson has been o ne of the more welcomed things this season , even though the two had no prior experience with one another before this past offseason.
Without him on Sunday, Cleveland would have to turn to a combination of Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond to slide into the final wide receiver spot.
Alongside Boston potentially being inactive, the Browns received unfortunate news that safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton would be out on Sunday. Not listed as questionable, Burton is dealing with a calf injury, while Hickman is still recovering from a concussion.
Burton missing Sunday's game is going to be a hit to the rushing attack for the Browns, an area of the offense that has struggled all season long. With him out, the workload is going to be pushed even more onto the passing attack, especially with Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson still searching for a rhythm as the back half of the season gets underway.
While having any bodies on the injured list is going to be an issue, the Browns have found a nice replacement for Hickman for the time being.
Taken in the second round of the draft this past year, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren's initial status in the Browns' defense was somewhat unknown.
However, through limited opportunities, he has shown that he has an awful lot in the tank to give the team. Through nine games, he has 42 combined tackles, three tackles for a loss and three pass deflections , all while routinely being in the right position at the right time.
His role has changed each week, but in Week 10, it seems his opportunity to become a long-term, key piece of the Browns' defense is his for the taking.
The Browns and Texans will face at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field, with Boston's final status expected to be released prior to the game.

title: Deshaun Watson’s Return Against Houston Comes With a Major Opportunity for Cleveland
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns host the Houston Texans at a pivotal point in their season. They are the AFC's eighth seed, just one spot out of a wildcard position.
If they lose, they will head into their bye week on a three-game losing streak at 5-5. However, if they win, they start their four-game home stand with a win and improve to 6-4.
#Browns Todd Monken said "the intention was for Deshaun to start." Just wanted to run it by the staff.
Todd Monken turns back to Deshaun Watson as starting quarterback after he missed last week to rest from a concussion injury. Watson returns to face the team that drafted him before things went sour and they were forced to trade him.
He is 1-0 against the Texans, winning his first game in a Browns uniform.
No game has been bigger than this one for the Browns. The Texans come into Cleveland after drubbing the Los Angeles Chargers, improving their record to 3-5. CJ Stroud has had a great season, and he is looking to translate his stat line into more wins. The Texans will come in with all the momentum and motivation, as they need this win to keep their playoff hopes alive.
The Browns return to Cleveland after a three-game road trip. Cleveland is ready to welcome them back after starting the season 3-0 in their home stadium. The Texans are 3-1 on the road, so it will be a great test of which team has the advantage.
Watson and the offense will have to start faster than normal. Their tendency is to start games slowly before turning it on in the fourth quarter and winning late in games. Houston’s offense has been high-flying, and all their wide receivers are finally healthy. The Browns’ defense has been gashed on the ground, but Houston has thrived through the air.
The Texans are probably the second-best team that the Browns will face the rest of the way, outside of the Cincinnati Bengals. If they can win this game, then the playoffs become more likely entering the bye week.
They are tied with the New England Patriots in the standings, but the Patriots earned the last wild card spot due to their record against AFC opponents. The Browns can help their cause by beating the Texans as the Patriots play an NFC team this week.
Watson also needs to beat the Texans personally. If the Browns fall and there is breathing room between them and the playoffs, then they will likely pivot to Shedeur Sanders at quarterback. After three quarters of undesirable play last week, Sanders put together an incredible fourth quarter and overtime.
Monken remained steadfast that Watson would start following his return from concussion protocol.
A similar situation arose early in the season when it was believed that the team would switch to Sanders if Watson performed poorly against Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Watson led a fourth-quarter comeback, and he kept his job.
He now faces the next piece of what is considered one of the worst trades in NFL history, with a familiar consequence on the line . The Browns will complete the revenge tour after their bye week against Kevin Stefanski and the Atlanta Falcons.
Monken took a lot of heat for naming Watson the starter at the beginning of the season, but he proved right after they started 5-2. He now goes back to Watson with full faith that he gives the team the best chance to win. Monken can earn a lot of credibility with a good performance from the offense and a win on Sunday.
Both teams in Sunday’s matchup need the win just as much as the other. The Texans tanked the Browns for four seasons after the trade for Watson. The only winning season the Browns had since was in 2023, in which Watson was injured.
It ended after a blowout loss in the playoffs to the Texans.
The Browns have their chance to bury the Texans’ season and force them to make a decision on extending their quarterback, which could alter their franchise.
Watson has returned just in time for the Browns’ biggest opportunity of the season to beat his former team.
