title: Did Dak Prescott Take Shot At Dallas Cowboys Coaching Staff After Week 10 Collapse?
full_text:
All eyes were on the Dallas Cowboys' defense after a miserable performance against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10, including an epic collapse in the second half.
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer ripped Christian Parker's unit during his post-game press conference, and star quarterback Dak Prescott was also clearly frustrated with the way things played out on Sunday evening.
After the game, Prescott sat in front of the media to answer several questions about the team's letdown at AT&T Stadium, making it clear that the status quo just isn't cutting it .
While Prescott does believe that the Cowboys have some pieces in place to have a successful team, there are clear changes that he believes need to happen in Dallas. The question is: what changes are Prescott looking for?
Safe to say Dak feels things need to look different in Dallas. pic.twitter.com/h6aPVoAmCA
While Prescott didn't say it outright, it sure seems like he would be open to changes to the coaching staff. That's the impression several members of Cowboys Nation received as well.
“Things gotta get better. Simple as that," Prescott said. "I truly believe we have the people, but something’s gotta change. We've got to find a way to change. Whatever it takes, individually. Whatever it takes is an organization . We gotta find a way to be better."
The Cowboys aren't a team that is keen on making midseason coaching changes, but if the team is unable to turn things around before the bye week, there are serious conversations that will need to be had.
Dallas has two very winnable games at home to finish off November, a Week 11 showdown against the ailing Tennessee Titans and a Thanksgiving Day clash against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles, so it's the perfect opportunity for the team to show some improvements.
Jerry Jones' patience seems to be wearing thin, so if the Cowboys miss out on the postseason for a third straight year, we could see either Brian Schottenheimer or Christian Parker sent packing.
It's a crucial time for the team and coaching staff, so we'll have to see over the next few weeks whether they are ready to answer the call.

title: Super Bowl Champion DC Destroys 'Garbage' Christian Parker & Cowboys Defensive Staff
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered a brutal reality in the team's Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . It may be time to admit that defensive coordinator Christian Parker is in over his head .
Dallas had no answers for the 49ers offense in the second half, and gave up a whopping 29 points. The team allowed 584 total yards of offense throughout the game, which is the most allowed at home in franchise history .
People are taking notice, especially after the embarrassing effort on a 70+ yard Deebo Samuel touchdown on a reverse.
DEEBO LEFT THEM IN THE DUST 💨 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/jWJ7pgBTUb
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer ripped the unacceptable performance during his postgame press conference, while star quarterback Dak Prescott called for changes to be made.
On Monday morning, the criticism of Parker and his defense continued, with ESPN's Rex Ryan, who won a Super Bowl leading the Baltimore Ravens defense, sounded off on the entire defensive staff in Dallas with an epic rant.
“This is the worst coached defense I think I’ve ever seen.” 😳 Rex Ryan with some words on the Cowboys after yesterday’s loss to the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/j7ehsnmJVk
When it came time to share his thoughts on the Cowboys' defensive struggles, Ryan did not hold back.
"Christian Parker? Really? Like, to me, that's the worst coached defense I think I've ever seen . Period. And I'm trying to be nice, whatever. What did I say? Sunday Countdown , I said, if you do too much, if you're multiple in this game, this is not the team to do that against," Ryan said. "They were just like, let's try this defense. Let's try this defense. Let's try this, like, whatever defense we can try... No. 1, the guy has no feel for the game. He doesn't know when to call things, when not to call things.
"Forget this. And I'm so sick and tired of it. These players, they act like, well, the players aren't good. Well, they were pretty good when you got them. Yeah. Why the hell aren't they good now? ... So to me, absolute garbage. You know, you can't fire them all yet, but you're damn sure better. And to me, it's the whole defensive staff. It's just not Christian Parker, okay? It's not. It's every one of those coaches on defense."
These are the kinds of harsh criticisms the Cowboys (and Jerry Jones) need to hear, because sugarcoating the reality of the situation in Dallas has done nothing to help the team over the past few years.
Christian Parker came to the Cowboys with a lot of hype, but he has failed to deliver. He hasn't even shown the ability to adjust his game plan to the flow of the game, which Ryan highlighted. After Sunday night's brutal collapse, Parker will certainly be under the microscope, and if things don't get better, we may see the Cowboys with a new defensive coordinator for the fourth consecutive year.

title: Cowboys Apparently Punished DeMarvion Overshown During Week 10 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
When going over the Dallas Cowboys' snap counts from the Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, there was an interesting note about linebacker DeMarvion Overshown.
During the loss to the Niners on Sunday, when the Cowboys had one of their worst defensive performances in franchise history, Overshown saw the field for just five snaps on defense.
Overshown also played nine snaps on special teams, the most he has played in that area during his career.
It would certainly appear that's exactly what happened.
There is really no other explanation for Overshown playing just five snaps on defense, especially when Dallas' defense was getting torched as badly as it was against the 49ers.
One might argue that Overshown got injured during the game, but there was no indication that happened.
Another possible reason is he was limited in his first game back from injury, but five snaps is not a limited workload, it's a punishment workload.
Furthermore, the Cowboys wouldn't have used nine of his snaps on special teams if that were the case.
I think we all know why: Overshown committed one of the most boneheaded penalties in the history of the NFL when he ran onto the field in Week 9 to celebrate with his teammates.
Overshown wasn't active for the game and it's against NFL rules for an inactive player to run out onto the field the way he did, which is why the Cowboys were hit with an unsportsmanlike conduct flag that cost them 15 yards.
The veteran linebacker apologized for his blunder, saying he didn't know that was against the rules.
"Honestly, I really didn't know the rule … I was running on the field and (Dee Winters) was like, 'D-Mo you can't be out here.' And that's when I looked back and I had already seen the ref pointing at me. At that point, I was like 'Im just gonna take this butt-chewing I'm about to get.' But I won't happen again," Overshown said .
"I was just caught in the moment. So, you can laugh at it now because we won the game, but in the moment – like four quarter (close) ball game a 4th quarter … you don't want a 15- yard penalty from a guy, especially if he's not even playing. So that's a lesson learned," he added.
Owner Jerry Jones wasn't buying Overshown's explanation, though.
"I don't think that (Overshown didn't know). I think that he's been involved in football at Texas and he's been involved here, and he knows that at every level a non-participant can't run out on the field," Jones told 105.3 The Fan .
We've been looking for head coach Brian Schottenheimer to do a better job holding players accountable, so it's pretty surprising he did that this time around, and especially in a tough and hugely important game against the Niners.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Goes Scorched Earth on Cowboys Defense's Miserable Second Half
full_text:
Frustrations are boiling over for the Dallas Cowboys, following the team's embarrassing second-half collapse against the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium on Sunday evening.
The stadium was overrun by 49ers fans , who got to see their team's offense destroy the Dallas defense for the final two quarters, putting up 29 second-half points. Dallas' defense allowed more than 500 total yards of offense, which was the most the Cowboys have given up at home in franchise history .
Following the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer reflected on the team's latest loss and could not hide his disgust with the team's defensive performance.
During his post-game press conference, Schottenheimer held nothing back and let his true feelings be known about just how acceptable the effort by Christian Parker's unit was, especially after giving up two 70+ yard touchdowns and another 60+ yard touchdown.
"Totally unacceptable defense." 😳 Brian Schottenheimer after the Cowboys gave up 46 points and 584 total yards against the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/aHDzjXVhpo
"I thought the second half was unacceptable. Tackling was atrocious. And we got to do a deep dive on the film and see why," Schottenheimer told the media. "You can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win in this league.
"So do a deep dive on the film, see the problems. But yeah, totally unacceptable defense in the second half... At the end of the day, we tackled like sh*t .”
What that means for the future of Christian Parker in Dallas remains to be seen, but the Cowboys are going to need to start holding people responsible for the lack of improvement and adjustments throughout games. There have been far too many miserable performances from the defense, and you should never lose a game when your offense hangs 40 points on the 49ers defense, including five touchdowns from Dak Prescott.
Up next for the Cowboys is the second of a three-game home stand, welcoming the lowly Tennessee Titans to AT&T Stadium. Dallas opens as a heavy favorite in that game, but you can never trust the Cowboys not to play down to the level of their opponent. Then, the team has a quick turnaround to face off against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

title: 3 Winners & 3 Losers From Cowboys Physical Beating Against 49ers in Week 10
full_text:
Once again, we saw how important coaching is in the NFL, even if Jerry Jones doesn't want to admit it . The Dallas Cowboys played hard for the first 30 minutes against the San Francisco 49ers , going into the half trailing 17-16.
In the second half, the 49ers completely took over. Kyle Shanahan proved to be an elite play-caller and made the Dallas defense look ridiculous. You could see how he set the Cowboys up with one strong run after another, followed by misdirection and bootleg plays, which left players with wide-open space to work with.
As for Brian Schottenheimer, nothing changed. His offense continued to rely too heavily on players winning individual battles, and in the end, the Cowboys were left with another loss. Of course, the players did their best to make it close, but fell short in the 46-40 loss.
The 49ers were the far more physical team, evidenced by their 214 yards on the ground (and average of 7.37 yards per carry). That was the difference and now, let's look at who stood out as winners and losers for the Cowboys in Week 10.
Wide receiver/return man KaVontae Turpin has been out due to injury and has not played since the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers. He was back this week, but made an early blunder that could have been devastating.
On the second drive of the game, Turpin had a short pass thrown to him, and he would have had some room to pick up decent yardage. That didn't happen, with Turpin dropping the easy catch. Dallas ended up scoring on the drive still, but had to convert a fourth down to keep the drive alive. That play shouldn't have been necessary if not for Turpin's gaffe.
Much has been made of the lack of targets thrown at George Pickens , and Dallas clearly wanted to fix that issue in Week 10. Pickens was targeted seven times on the first two drives, and while he was unable to make a big play on the opening drive, that changed on the second. Pickens caught a seven-yard reception on third-and-eight, setting up a fourth-down conversion by Dak Prescott. Pickens then capped off the drive with a 35-yard touchdown reception, giving the Cowboys a 10-7 lead.
We LOVE a GP TD 🔥 📺: #SFvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/vFRagrWQIb
He wasn't done there as Pickens made another huge play in the first half. A couple of plays after dropping a pass in the middle of the field, Pickens made up for his mistake as he took a short pass from Dak Prescott and turned it into a 39-yard touchdown, with an assist from CeeDee Lamb who made an excellent block at the end of the play. That gave the Cowboys a 16-10 lead with just over four minutes to play in the first half.
GEORGE PICKENS SCORES ANOTHER SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hITd6CtBqp
Pickens finished with 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns. It was an elite game, but not enough for a victory. He also does deserve some criticism for a taunting penalty on the final drive, which makes no sense when you're getting beaten up. Still, it was an elite performance from Pickens overall.
Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams is in the midst of a great season as he entered this game with five sacks, including four in the past four games. He added to that number when he sacked Brock Purdy in the second quarter. That was a key play on second-and-goal, which forced the 49ers to settle for a field goal to tie it up at 10, rather than take the lead.
. @QuinnenWilliams GETS TO THE QB 💥 📺: #SFvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/KtkQjzYMIW
Williams had 10 tackles and nearly made the play of the game. With Dallas trailing by six and the 49ers trying to put the game away, Williams forced a fumble when tackling Kaelon Black. The San Francisco running back got the ball back, but it could have been a winning play with the right bounce.
After making a clutch interception in Week 9, Caleb Downs went in the wrong direction this week. He was targeted often in coverage, including a third-and-two in the second half where he was beaten by Christian McCaffrey for a first down. His worst play, however, came on the opening drive in the third quarter when Kaelon Black bowled him over on a 25-yard touchdown run.
KAELON BLACK RUNNING THROUGH THE DEFENSE SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/G9ZWuR4cLB
At times, it's easy to forget Von Miller is even on the team.
Dallas added Miller as a veteran pass-rushing presence, and with Malachi Lawrence and Donovan Ezeiruaku out, they needed Miller. Not only did he fail to record a single tackle, but he was beaten badly by Christian McCaffrey for a 66-yard touchdown that sealed the win for the 49ers.
It's not often a quarterback throws for five touchdown passes and leads his team to 40 points in a losing effort, but that's what happened for Dak Prescott. While he had an ugly interception, he still threw for 343 yards with his five touchdowns and added a two-point conversion as well.
Prescott proved he can put up points in a hurry and did so against a top-tier defense. Unfortunately, it wasn't enough since their defense gave up 46 points.

title: DaRon Bland, Tyler Booker Injury Updates Could Spell Doom For Cowboys After Week 10
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered another brutal loss at home, thanks to a second-half collapse against the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium. Dallas' defense allowed 29 second-half points and 584 total yards of offense throughout the game, which is the most allowed at home in franchise history .
Before the game even started, there was an embarrassing moment when Dallas was booed at home by an overwhelming amount off 49ers fans.
After the game, things got even worse when head coach Brian Schottenheimer provided injury updates for two key starters, mauling guard Tyler Booker and starting cornerback DaRon Bland.
Both men suffered ankle injuries during the game that ended their nights early, and Schottenheimer classified their setbacks as "big ones" after the game.
According to Schottenheimer, Bland and Booker will both undergo further testing on Monday , including x-rays and MRIs. X-rays. If either man is forced to miss extended time, it's very possible that they could be shut down for the remainder of the season.
There are eight weeks left in the season, but the Cowboys just took another step back in the NFC East title picture. If the Cowboys fall any further behind while Bland and Booker or sidelined, the right call would be to place them on injured reserve.
Both players have already missed time this season due to injury, so there is no reason to risk any long-term damage, especially for a young rising star like Booker. Bland, meanwhile, could be staring at the end of his Cowboys tenure.
We will find out more about the extent of Bland and Bookers' injuries later in the week when the team returns to practice and the Cowboys' coaching staff and front office speak to the media. For now, all anyone can do is hope for the best.
Up next for the Cowboys in Week 11 is a clash with the lowly Tennessee Titans, which is a game that the team should win, before turning around on a quick week to face the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. It's not too late to save the season, but a loss in either of the next two weeks could be the nail in the coffin for Dallas before we even reach the team's bye week.

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys Defense Officially Cements Place As Worst In Franchise History
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have taken another step back after suffering a brutal loss to the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium in Week 10. The Cowboys fell to the 49ers, 46-40 (a Scorigami !), but the final score doesn't reflect the physical beating Dallas took throughout the game.
Dallas' defense couldn't stop a soul and was picked apart for all four quarters. The Cowboys did outscore San Francisco, 21-15, in the fourth quarter, but it wasn't enough to overcome the embarrassing third quarter performance where they were outscored 14-3.
There is nothing to blame but the defense for the dreadful performance, with the team allowing a 74-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey and a 70-yard touchdown run to Deebo Samuel. It was the first time in team history that the Cowboys allowed a 70+ yard pass touchdown and a 70+ yard rushing touchdown in the same game.
And close your eyes, Cowboys Nation, because it gets even worse.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on DC Christian Parker pic.twitter.com/IEeJiq11Cu
The Cowboys allowed 370 passing yards and 214 yards rushing for a total of 584 for the 49ers' offense. It is the most yards allowed at home in team history.
San Francisco averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play.
The most discouraging part of the Cowboys' defensive performance is that there seem to be no signs of improvement, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker has shown no capability or willingness to adapt.
Presented without comment pic.twitter.com/aOhrXB7M84
Jerry Jones was asked to offer his thoughts on Parker and the defense's performance when speaking to the media after the game, and he offered a seemingly defeated response.
"Again, this is, it's what it is," Jones said. "He's a young coach in his first year of coordinating and basically calling the plays. And so you would have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last that we lost, and I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators that ended up on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."
It will be interesting to see what happens with Parker after the season if the Cowboys' defense continues open the floodgates for opposing offenses, but judging by the first 10 weeks of the season, it may be best to move on and bring in a more experienced coordinator moving forward.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys' Predictable Week 10 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
Almost nobody gave the Dallas Cowboys a chance to beat the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10 and the Cowboys lived up to that expectation in a 46-40 loss on Sunday.
We'll give the Cowboys credit for putting up a good fight against an elite team, but that fight simply wasn't good enough because, per usual, the defense just couldn't stop the Niners' offense enough to make the offense's showing stand up.
With the loss, the Cowboys fall to 4-6 on the season and miss an opportunity to gain ground in the division.
We'll talk about that and much more as we go over the biggest takeaways from the Cowboys' loss to the 49ers.
The 49ers ripped off explosives plays again and again and again and again and.... well, you get the idea. The 49ers notched a total of 11 explosive plays, including three that went for 60-plus-yard scores.
The Cowboys' defense was actually getting good pressure against San Fran's offensive line and totaled five sacks, but Brock Purdy was able to escape several times and extend plays, and the Cowboys weren't disciplined enough to maintain coverage, leading to some big gains through the air for the Niners.
The Niners averaged an obscene 9.4 yards per play. The 584 total yards the Cowboys gave up amounts to the most Dallas has allowed in a home game in team history.
We might very well be watching the worst defense in Cowboys history.
Scoring 40 points should always be enough to win a game, but this is the 2026 Cowboys we're talking about here.
Dak Prescott certainly wasn't perfect, but he threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns and the Cowboys actually averaged four yards per carry, which isn't great but better than what we've witnessed in most games this season.
Our biggest gripe with the offense was not putting together enough long drives to keep San Fran's offense off the field.
When you consider all of the big plays the Niners had, there's no way they should have won time of possession, yet they did just that.
Pickens was an absolute menace in his first game back en route to his best game of the season.
Pickens finished the game with 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns, with six catches, 97 yards and two scores coming in the first half.
Unfortunately, Pickens' big game wasn't anywhere near enough for the Cowboys to beat the Niners. It was yet another reminder that having two really good receivers means jack if the defense stinks.
With the New York Giants losing on Thursday night, Dallas had a chance to gain ground in the NFC East.
Instead, the Cowboys squandered that opportunity and the deficit they went into Sunday with remains intact.
What makes this outcome even more frustrating is the fact that the Giants have a tough game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 11 and the Cowboys have a very winnable game against the Tennessee Titans, so Dallas could have realistically gained even more ground next week.

title: Cowboys Booed at Home as 49ers Fans Take Over AT&T Stadium in Embarrassing Scene
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have a tough opponent visiting them this week as they host the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Ahead of the showdown, former NFL player Gerald McCoy said the Cowboys needed to make sure they didn't allow the "bully" to come into their house and push them around.
McCoy's take was right, but there was one flaw in his statement. He said the Cowboys would have the fans behind them since they were at home, but that's not the case.
As the Cowboys took the field at AT&T Stadium, boos were pouring down on them. The Athletic's Jon Machota was surprised by the noise, and as he pointed out, this isn't due to the fans being sick of the poor performance from Dallas. Instead, it was due to the fact that San Francisco fans took over the stadium.
I’ve never heard the Dallas Cowboys booed at home like today by all of the 49ers fans at AT&T Stadium pic.twitter.com/IeA0v7s22v
The fans continued to make noise, even erupting into a chorus of cheers when a first-quarter sack from Kenny Clark was called back due to a penalty on Caleb Downs. They also cheered loudly as Deebo Samuel scored a first-quarter touchdown against the Cowboys.
One thing Cowboys owner Jerry Jones takes pride in is how popular his franchise is. Even with their 30-year Super Bowl drought making their team a punchline, Jones hasn't flinched, as his team remains wildly popular.
That's why it's beyond embarrassing to see the takeover in the house that Jerry built.
This 49ers takeover is real. never seen this many opposing fans be this loud of the start of the game at @ATTStadium Never #DallasCowboys
Jones took immense pride in building AT&T Stadium, and it has to be killing him seeing all the red in the seats. It's surely even more infuriating to hear his team being booed for simply running onto the field.
The 49ers are among the most popular teams in the NFL, and they enter this game as the No. 1 seed in the NFC. Their fan base travels well, which is expected. Even in the past, there has been a strong showing from their fans while in Dallas.
This season is different, however, thanks to the poor play from the Cowboys. Fans are surely growing tired of the team's lack of competitiveness as they enter the week with a record of 4-5. Making matters worse, they haven't scored back-to-back wins or defeated a team with a winning record since last Thanksgiving.
That should be a major warning for Jones, who continues to accept the mediocrity that Brian Schottenheimer is breeding. But we all know that if the next game in Dallas feels like a home game, he won't care.

title: Why Do Dallas Cowboys Have Red Stripe On Helmet vs 49ers?
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys take center stage for America's Game of the Week when they welcome the San Francisco 49ers to AT&T Stadium in Week 10.
Sunday evening's game is the first of three consecutive home games for the Cowboys , and the hope is to get everything off on a high note. It won't be easy for Dallas, however, because the 49ers enter the game with a 7-1 record and are the current favorites to win Super Bowl 61 .
With such a tough test ahead, the Cowboys brought out their Sunday best and added a special twist to their traditional home white uniforms .
Dallas added a red stripe to the helmet, giving America's Team an all-American look for America's Game of the Week. Pretty fitting, right? But why do the Cowboys have a red stripe on their helmet for today's game? Let's take a look.
Turn your TVs on https://t.co/DpAFKp2khw pic.twitter.com/c9XaIttOWO
The Dallas Cowboys have made their red, white, and blue helmets a part of their annual uniform rotation as part of the NFL's Salute to Service initiative honoring military members, veterans, and National Medal of Honor recipients.
The Cowboys originally introduced the red stripe during the 1976 NFL season to celebrate the United States Bicentennial. The team reintroduced the red stripe in 2021 and wears it for its annual Salute to Service game.
"This will truly be a special day for all of us as we salute the men and women around the world who protect and defend our country," Cowboys' executive vice president Charlotte Jones, who is also chairman of the National Medal of Honor Museum Foundation, when the red stripe was revived . "We are honored to have our Medal of Honor recipients in attendance, representing the 3,508 recipients of the nation's most prestigious military decoration, who made heroic sacrifices, many the ultimate sacrifice, while preserving our freedom.
"The red stripe on the helmet provides a beautiful ribbon to wrap around this salute to those who currently serve our country's military -- and the patriotic love and appreciation that we all share for those who came before them."
Thank you to our @UPS Driver and Navy Veteran Rich Williams for not only delivering the game ball to @ATTStadium safely, but for his dedicated service to the community as a UPS driver of 30 years. #SFvsDAL | #ThanksForDelivering pic.twitter.com/UGnRYzhxLP
The Cowboys are also honoring UPS driver and Navy veteran Rich Williams before the game. It's a great gesture and tribute from the team.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and 49ers is set for 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX.

title: 5 Unsung Broncos Free Agents Who've Made Their Case to Stay in 2027
full_text:
The Denver Broncos currently have 25 players set to hit free agency after the 2026 season ends. Some of Denver's free agents will be unrestricted, while others will be of the restricted and exclusive-rights variety.
The Broncos have several key players who could be extended before the 2026 season ends , though with the bye week ending without such a deal, the likelihood has diminished. However, looking past this season, the Broncos have several players who should be retained in 2027 for low-cost deals, even if some of them are better suited as depth or special teams.
These players don't need to be extended before the end of the season, but they should be up for either restricted free-agent tenders or short-term deals as free agency is about to get underway in the spring.
With half the season in the books, let's examine five such players who shouldn't be overlooked when the Broncos start making decisions in 2027.
Key is set to become a restricted free agent in 2027. The Broncos could go in one of two directions: tender him at the second-round level or sign him to a short-term deal.
The second-round tender is estimated at $6.26 million, which is a bit high for a depth and special -teams player, even though Key has been decorated as a third-phase All-Pro. However, if Denver tendered him at the original-round level, another team could sign him to an offer sheet.
The best move for the Broncos is to sign Key to a two-year deal. The original-round tender is $3.82 million, but the Broncos could come in between the two tender levels and give Key, say, a two-year, $9.5 million deal as a reward for his contributions over the past two seasons.
Adkins was a restricted free agent in 2026 whom the Broncos signed to a one-year deal at the veteran minimum. He made the 53-man roster and has proven to be a good blocking tight end and a solid pass-catcher.
The Broncos would be wise to retain Adkins, who might get more than the veteran minimum this time around. A possibility could be a two-year, $7.5 million deal, similar to what Adam Trautman got in 2024.
Speaking of Trautman, it will be difficult to move on from him in 2027 because of his guaranteed money, but the Broncos could cut him in 2028 without much trouble. Keeping Adkins in the fold would give the Broncos an option to eventually take over Trautman's role in the offense.
Tillman is set to become a restricted free agent in 2027. He has proven to be valuable depth on defense, particularly when Jonathon Cooper missed time on the commissioner's exempt list to start the season.
In Tillman's case, the second-round tender would be fine, as $6.26 million is a reasonable salary to pay for what he brings to the defense. But the Broncos could opt for a two-year deal here as well.
A two-year deal for $10 million might be possible and a way to recognize Tillman for his contributions and continued role. It would also allow the Broncos to keep the edge rusher around for more than one season.
It might seem odd to list Badie here, but let's look at the facts. J.K. Dobbins might not be with the Broncos in 2027 , and though Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey would form a good pairing, the team still needs reliable depth.
Badie would give the Broncos an experienced back who could be the No. 3 or No. 4 option in the backfield, particularly with his pass-blocking ability, and would be a much cheaper alternative to Dobbins, who is due $8 million in 2027. Badie has also been good on special teams.
Badie will be a restricted free agent and isn't worth the second-round tender, but the Broncos should be able to keep him for the veteran minimum.
Skinner has had a few highlights on defense , but his play hasn't been good enough to warrant a starting role. However, he's been valuable on special teams.
While the Broncos do have seventh-round pick Miles Scott on the practice squad, they should keep Skinner around because of his experience. That would put less pressure on Scott to fill an immediate hole in 2027.
Skinner will be an unrestricted free agent, and like Badie, is a player the Broncos should be able to retain at the veteran minimum.

title: 5 Broncos Veterans Whose 2027 Futures Are Suddenly in Doubt
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have a handful of veterans whose future may be in question after this season, even though they're under contract next year, and in some cases, beyond.
The Broncos aren’t in a bad salary-cap situation, with $29.5 million in cap space projected in 2027. However, that 2027 figure accounts for just 38 players under contract, so some of that cap space will be taken up by players signed to futures contracts after this season ends.
The Broncos also have some players with expiring contracts they might want to extend, as well as restricted free agents to decide on, so they will need to find ways to clear cap space for 2027.
With that imperative in mind, there are five Broncos whose 2027 contract status is currently in question, three of whom might be asked to convert base salary into incentives. One is trending toward being released, while another's future is dependent on a criminal case against him that is still pending.
Let's break each one down.
McGlinchey's run blocking has always been reliable, but pass protection is his weakness. He was good overall in 2025, but his play has slipped this season .
The Broncos have already shown they will renegotiate with an offensive lineman in the final year of his contract, as they did with left guard Ben Powers . But Powers missed much of 2025 with a biceps injury, while McGlinchey has played all but four games since joining the Broncos in 2023.
Also, the Broncos aren't in a great position regarding potential McGlinchey replacements already on the roster. Alex Palczewski has some experience at right tackle, but now seems to be viewed as a guard, while Frank Crum — who's been on injured reserve all season — may be better suited to the left side of the line.
Still, there's a chance the Broncos will approach McGlinchey about reducing his $16.99 million base salary and converting some of it into incentives. Even if they don't, the Broncos need to draft an offensive tackle who can eventually compete for the right tackle job.
Jones has been a solid player for most of his time with the Broncos, but it's fair to ask whether he's worth the $12.235 million base salary he's due in 2027.
I've previously suggested that Jones is a candidate to have his base salary converted into incentives next season. His play this season hasn't been bad, but the Broncos have more depth on the defensive line, with Malcolm Roach and Tyler Onyedim — both younger players — being good against the run.
As evidenced by his four sacks this season, Roach is also a good pass rusher, while Onyedim has potential there.
It might make sense to approach Jones about renegotiating his base salary to convert it into incentives, but his play hasn't reached the point where the Broncos would have to cut him if he doesn't renegotiate.
Sutton is due a $19.325 million base salary for 2027, $10 million of which will become fully guaranteed if he's on the roster on March 10, 2027. The Broncos already chose not to exercise his option bonus for 2026 , with that money being paid out as base salary instead.
The option-bonus decision might indicate the Broncos are prepared to move on from Sutton in 2027 if it comes down to that. It doesn't help that at the midway point, he's on pace for a career-low season, with just 25 receptions on 46 targets for 266 yards (10.6 avg) and two touchdowns.
A straight cut would free $10.225 million in cap space, with a $15.85 million dead-money charge, while a post-June 1 designation would free up $20 million (but not until after June 1), with $6.075 million dead. A trade can't be ruled out, but a trade would take immediate effect on the salary cap.
In Sutton's case, it would make sense to ask him to convert some of his base salary into incentives in exchange for more than $10 million becoming fully guaranteed. That would free up some space and still allow the Broncos to easily move on from him in 2028.
Dobbins signed a two-year extension during the offseason, but he hasn't played well. Between his play and the Broncos' other running back injuries, the team explored trading for a running back before last week's deadline.
As things stand, this will be the easiest decision the Broncos will make in 2027. Cutting Dobbins would free $8 million in cap space with just a $2 million dead-money charge.
An offseason trade can't be ruled out, but if it doesn't happen, all signs point to Dobbins being released.
Cooper missed six games on the commissioner's exempt list due to a criminal case he was charged with this past summer, but he's still awaiting trial. His trial was postponed, and he was activated ahead of Week 7.
Cooper's outlook depends on what happens in the jury trial. If he's found guilty, the Broncos may opt to release him, likely with a post-June 1 designation, to save $13.5 million in cap space with a $4.055 million dead-money charge.
If Cooper is exonerated, the Broncos will likely keep him. If that's how it shakes out, Denver is unlikely to ask him to renegotiate his salary.

title: Jensen's Judgment: Broncos Fans Wanted a RB Trade, But George Paton Knew Better
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were heavily linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of last Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Instead of a backfield weapon, the Broncos ended up agreeing to a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, though the deal fell through after he failed his physical.
It makes you wonder how interested the Broncos really were in running backs, and how much of it was a smokescreen to throw teams off ahead of the deadline. All the Taylor rumors led to speculation in the blogosphere and on social media about several other running backs and whether the Broncos might also be interested in them.
Tony Pollard was one of those running backs. Before the deadline, there wasn't solid reporting on the Broncos being interested in Pollard, but that was then.
Now, a few days after the deadline, we know the Broncos were actually interested in Pollard. According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Broncos "checked in" on Pollard, but the Tennessee Titans' asking price of a third-round pick scared them off.
It's curious that the Titans wouldn't part with Pollard for anything less than a third-rounder. He's in the final season of the three-year, $21.75 million contract Tennessee gave him, which means that, if he departs in free agency in the offseason, the Titans can expect to get a compensatory draft pick back from the league.
But a third-rounder? Not likely for a running back who will be turning 30 shortly after the 2027 free-agency window opens. He's playing at a high level this season, but at his age, he's unlikely to be offered a contract next year that'll put him in the top-35% salary threshold at his position.
It's possible if Pollard stays healthy and continues to produce at high level for Tennessee's guttering offense. But whether he'd return a comp pick to Tennessee at all — let alone a third-rounder (the highest possible) — will also be dependent on how the Titans spend in free agency.
When it comes to Taylor, the Broncos reportedly backed away when the Colts began asking for first-round value. Barring that, Indy was looking for Christian McCaffrey-type compensation.
The San Francisco 49ers gave the Carolina Panthers a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick for McCaffrey back in 2022, but he was younger then than Taylor is now and nowhere near as close to the 2,000-carry milestone.
If the Colts had been more reasonable with their asking price, the Broncos likely would have been more serious about Taylor. Alas, for Colts fans, the team's decision robbed them of the chance to add to their rebuild war chest. Taylor will turn 30 after next season.
The Broncos made the right call in not paying through the nose to acquire a running back. Giving up a third-round draft pick for a soon-to-be 30-year-old running back in a contract year, when the Broncos have two young players on the rise — Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey — would have been questionable.
Pollard would have certainly helped the Broncos' offense in what remains of this season, but he would have been a short-term rental. The third-round draft pick is more valuable to the Broncos in the grand scheme of things.
Don't get me wrong; Pollard is having a big season, with 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns. He's on pace to post his fourth straight 1,000-yard rushing season, with a legitimate chance at resetting his career high (1,082 yards).
But at the end of the day, the Broncos believe they have the horses in the running back stable (pardon the pun) to turn the rushing ship around down the stretch, and that includes J.K. Dobbins. Denver knows that fixing the blocking up front is likely to be the catalyst to maximizing the investments it has already made in the backfield.
Harvey was a second-round pick. Coleman was a fourth-rounder. The Broncos are paying Dobbins $8 million this year. And they made these investments for a reason, believing they had the foundation in the trenches to make some hay with these backs.
Sean Payton's remarks to Colin Cowherd earlier this week, the day after the trade deadline, hinted at how the Broncos view their lack of rushing success as a team this season. It's more of a blocking deficiency than a talent shortage at running back.
Sure, given the Broncos' blocking issues up front, it would have been nice to add another running back like Coleman who could create for himself, but with the deadline coming during the team's bye week, Payton must have been confident that he and run game coordinator Zach Strief would have the breathing room to get to the bottom of the O-line problems.
Payton issued a veiled threat to his blockers in his conversation with Cowherd, pointing to the Broncos' O-line depth and hinting that personnel changes aren't outside the bounds of the possible during the bye.
I'll be surprised if Denver benches any of its starting five, but if there are technical or schematic explanations for the troubling regression of center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey, it's now or never for Payton and Strief to identify it.
I would have liked to see the Broncos add one more running back ahead of the trade deadline, mainly because Harvey is on injured reserve for two more games. Taylor may have been worth a third-rounder and then some because of his unique talent and ability to create, and the fact that he's under contract beyond 2026.
A third-rounder for Pollard, though? No way.
That's a deal that only a desperate team makes, not the Broncos. And it turns out the Titans couldn't find any suckers willing to take that deal, so they bypassed the opportunity to stockpile some draft picks in yet another lost season.
First-round value or a McCaffrey package for a nearly 29-year-old Taylor? No. And certainly not when the Broncos have two young backs just scratching the surface of their NFL potential.
With the schedule opening up coming out of the bye — only one plus-.500 opponent until Christmas — the Broncos will have plenty of opportunity to get their fledgling ground attack rolling in time for the true stretch run.

title: Broncos' 3 Toughest Remaining Opponents—and One Sneaky Trap Game
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are enjoying the fruits of a well-timed and well-earned bye .
The 7-2 Broncos are in control of the AFC West and are the favorites to repeat as division champions after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8. The Broncos had to take care of another opponent that was in the playoffs last year — the Carolina Panthers — before hitting their bye, but they took care of business on the road .
After successfully navigating a grueling early gauntlet that was the toughest slate of opponents in the NFL, the Broncos now face one of the league's easiest remaining schedules. However, three of Denver's eight remaining games are against a plus-.500 opponent.
Today, we're breaking down the Broncos' three toughest opponents coming out of the bye, plus another that's flying under the radar. If the Broncos sleep on this opponent, they could get caught in a dreaded trap game.
This is a weird game, as it's one of the NFL's new forays into Black Friday. It's strange to imagine a Broncos football game being played on a Friday, but it's what the NFL wants.
The Steelers have exceeded expectations under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy. His reunion with Aaron Rodgers, while far from the explosive heights the two reached at the height of their Green Bay Packers tenure, has borne fruit for the Steelers.
Pittsburgh leads a competitive AFC North division, and aside from a veteran quarterback, it has a top-ranked defense to hang its hat on, led by TJ Watt. The Steelers' defense ranks fourth in points and yardage. They're also tied with the Broncos with the fourth-most sacks this season.
The Broncos are different offense when they're on the road, especially against quality defenses. This is a game that looked far more forgiving before any football was played. As it inches closer, it's looking tougher.
But as a conference opponent, the Broncos will have to bring their A-game against the Steelers. That's one thing fans shouldn't doubt about Sean Payton's team: the Broncos can be relied upon to elevate their game against quality opponents, though they're not perfect, especially on the road.
Both of Denver's losses this season were stinkers on the road against opponents that are above .500 currently. The takeaway? Don't overlook this matchup.
If the season ended today, the Broncos would be the No. 2 playoff seed in the AFC. The Bills would be the No. 1 seed.
It feels like these two teams are on a collision course to decide AFC playoff-seeding supremacy this season. And after last year's divisional round matchup between these two clubs ended with a Broncos overtime win at Mile High that cost them Bo Nix , you can bet Buffalo will have its dander up for this one. But so will the Broncos.
Now, the next two weeks should be a breeze for the Bills, but that's the calm before the storm. They'll face the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots (road), Green Bay Packers (road), and Chicago Bears before traveling to Mile High for their rendevouz with the Broncos.
There's a good chance the Broncos will be in control of the No. 1 seed by the time they host the Bills on Christmas Day. But it's still sure to be a doozy of a matchup with big-time AFC playoff implications.
Josh Allen is still playing at the top of his game with Joe Brady as his first-year head coach — the same guy who's been calling the Bills' offensive plays for a few years now. The Bills can gash you in an number of ways on offense, whether it's through the air or on the ground with Allen and James Cook.
Defensively, though, the Bills are vulnerable. Jim Leonhard's first year as an NFL defensive coordinator hasn't gone swimmingly thus far, with some calls for the Bills to fire him. Brady has stuck with Leonhard, who served as the Broncos' secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator for the preceding two years.
The Bills are a juggernaut offensively, though, and that's allowed them to overcome their defensive foibles. Thankfully, this one is Denver, but it's going to be a dogfight.
The Patriots are above .500 currently, but they've got several tough opponents between now and their Week 17 home game vs. Denver. The Patriots are home against the Detroit Lions this week, followed by their bye.
The Patriots get a small Week 12 reprieve in the form of a road game against the Los Angeles Chargers, then it's back-to-back home games against the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings, before going back on the road to face the Chiefs. Who knows what New England's record will be come Week 17, but the fact that it's a road game against another 2025 playoff opponent means all bets are off for the Broncos.
Nix would love nothing more than the opportunity to show how differently the AFC championship game would have played out if he hadn't gotten hurt. And you know Nik Bonitto, Zach Allen, and the Broncos' pass rush would love to balance the scales against Drake Maye.
Again, though, the Broncos can be a different team on the road. As it stands, the time and broadcast channel for Broncos-Patriots is currently to be decided, but if New England is still alive in the playoff hunt come Week 17, this game could get flexed to primetime, especially with the Nix vs. Maye storyline to bring in the eyeballs.
Roll your eyes, but there are three reasons to be wary of this game. One, Nix has faced the Jets twice before, and both games were ugly, requiring fourth-quarter heroics, though he came out on top.
Two, it's an East Coast game scheduled for the NFL's early slate, and the Broncos haven't been great in those areas traditionally. However, under Payton, Denver has improved dramatically in early-start East Coast games, but it's a factor.
Three, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn knows Payton and his schemes and philosophies. Glenn played for Payton in New Orleans back in 2008 and he coached under him for five years as the Saints' defensive backs coach.
Glenn's familiarity with Payton was a big reason why the Broncos struggled against the Jets in England last year, escaping with a narrow 13-11 victory . Glenn's team is only 2-7 this season, and his future as the head coach is cloudy, but he'll have the Jets' dander up for the Broncos.
Geno Smith isn't blowing the doors down in his return to the Big Apple, but he's played an efficient brand of ball, with 2,078 yards and 12 touchdowns thus far. He's only been picked off three times.  Statistically, Smith has had a better season than Nix (1,730 YD/11 TD/3 INT), though the Jets' schedule has been a complete softball compared to what the Broncos have faced.
After last year's experience across the pond vs. Glenn's Jets, I doubt Payton's Broncos will be overlooking them, especially on the road. But this game has some of the 'trappings' of an upset.

title: How Close Broncos Came to Acquiring RB Tony Pollard Before Deadline
full_text:
Jonathan Taylor wasn't the only running back who interested the Denver Broncos prior to Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Saturday that Denver "checked in on" Titans RB Tony Pollard but were rebuffed by Tennessee's apparent price tag of "anything less" than a third-round draft pick.
"The Packers and Broncos checked in on Titans running back Tony Pollard, whom Tennessee would not have traded for anything less than a third-round pick," the report stated.
This tracks with what league insider Jordan Schultz previously reported -- that the Broncos (and New York Giants) were among the teams in the short-lived Pollard sweepstakes.
"But Tennessee was adamant for weeks that they were unlikely to move him, as he’s been vital to the locker room and the continued development of Cam Ward," Schultz wrote on X on Nov. 10.
A prototypical dual-threat back, Pollard has accounted for 665 yards from scrimmage (595 rushing yards, 4.5 yards per carry) and six total touchdowns (all on the ground) across eight appearances this season.
Pollard was among several NFL RBs who were viewed as potential trade candidates prior to the deadline, along with Taylor , the Jets' Breece Hall, the Eagles' Saquon Barkley, and the Ravens' Derrick Henry. In the end, none of these players were moved by their original clubs.
It's clear that Denver was seeking an upgrade to pair with ascending rookie Jonah Coleman and pass-catching extraordinaire RJ Harvey. What's more, had they acquired Taylor or Pollard, the Broncos likely would've made veteran J.K. Dobbins available for trade .
Obviously, none of that transpired, and the club now heads into the second half of its 2026 campaign with the status quo at the position: Coleman and Dobbins on early downs, with Harvey seeing extensive third-down opportunities once he returns from injured reserve.
The Broncos will hope the trio can find their collective groove following a less-than-impressive statistical start prior to the bye. Entering Week 10, the rushing offense ranks 29th in yards per carry per game and 27th in total yards per game.
"Those runners are going to be important," head coach Sean Payton said after last Sunday's victory over the Panthers. "I'm not going to answer running-back depth questions, and certainly our running backs are not going to sit in front of a 15-minute interview about their playing time. Man, those guys are really important. [Running backs] J.K. [Dobbins] played, Jonah [Coleman] played, RJ [Harvey] will be back here shortly, and I'm glad we got both of them. I didn't feel like we ran it particularly well with either of them, and it wasn't back driven. It was ‘Oh, that was a Buffalo front.’ Like, it took us a minute. And now, we threw it better for chunk plays than we ran it, but we got the runs when we needed it later."

title: Broncos Midseason Awards: MVP, Breakout Star, and Biggest Disappointment
full_text:
The NFL put the Denver Broncos' bye week at an ideal spot, about as close to halfway through the season as is possible in a 17-game campaign.
The Broncos are 7-2 entering Week 10's bye, leading the AFC West. They're favored to win the division , though one or two slip-ups down the stretch could change that, and the AFC's No. 1 playoff seed is still very much on the table.
The bye has offered us a chance to breathe and take a deep dive into the Broncos, from cumulative player grades to rookie report cards and five warning signs . Today is a day for superlatives, though; we're handing out midseason awards to the deserving Broncos, and there's been plenty of sample size to feel confident about each one.
Let's start with the most important award.
I know, I know. Nix has had a weird campaign, returning from the broken ankle that ended his 2025 season and torpedoed the Broncos' championship ambitions on the doorstep of the Super Bowl. He doesn't rank highly in any of the common quarterback stats, and most of the advanced analytics aren't kind to him.
However, Nix remains the Broncos' most valuable player. Even amid a step-back of a third season, without him, this team's outlook would immediately fall into the gutter, just as we saw in the AFC championship game last year.
Nix was bad at times against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, and Seattle Seahawks, but as a thought exercise, imagine how those games would have shaken out if Jarrett Stidham had been the quarterback. Yeah. That's right. Denver loses all three of those games without Nix.
Even amid his early-season struggles, the one thing that no one could take away from Nix is his clutch-time excellence. There isn't a better NFL quarterback when the chips are down, and that clutch-time will to win is a big reason why the Broncos were able to weather their early-season gauntlet of a schedule.
CHUNK PLAY MARVIN MIMS JR. DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o13qfZGfzC
Since Week 7, Nix has been improving by leaps and bounds. His confidence is back, and he's no longer so painfully hesitant in his decision-making. In fact, he's hunting with the football again .
There's every reason to believe that Nix's upward momentum will continue coming out of the bye. He wanted to be peaking at the right time, and the stars are aligning for the Broncos to get the best possible version of their young franchise quarterback down the stretch and into the playoffs.
Waddle hasn't exactly been an off-the-charts producer, but he's been the Broncos' most important non-quarterback player on offense. Amid Nix's early slump, Waddle bided his time, finding ways to make an impact in Denver's low-percentage passing attack.
But even when the ball doesn't go his way, or isn't intended to go his way, Waddle's presence on the field has changed the math for opposing defenses. It has opened things up for other players, and will continue to do so as the Broncos' schedule opens up down the stretch.
Jaylen Waddle gets his first big play as a Bronco! 🐧 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FAioYbx0Fs
Waddle has dealt with some minor injuries and he suffered a concussion in Week 9, but he's appeared in all nine games, leading the team with 30 receptions on 52 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns. He's also made some big plays on two-point conversions, without which, the Broncos don't come back in two of their one-score victories this season.
The Broncos don't have any buyer's remorse after giving up a first- and third-round pick to acquire Waddle. He's just getting started.
Allen is in the middle of perhaps his best season as a pro, which is saying something, given that he's been an All-Pro in each of the past two seasons, and was a first-team selection last year.
Allen is near the top of the NFL in pass-rushing metrics, including quarterback pressures, and his 4.5 sacks are tied with Nik Bonitto for the team lead. Allen affects the quarterback on every snap, commanding double teams, which frees up other guys to make plays. He even blocked a field-goal attempt in Week 4.
IT'S BLOCKED! 📺: @CBSSports / @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/8wHodVFVIN
He makes his own fair share of plays, even against double teams because Allen is just that good. Against the run, he's one of the NFL's best interior defenders, too. He's just an all-around elite player at the point of attack. Without him, this defense wouldn't be nearly as formidable.
Only two of Denver's 2026 draft picks have actually seen the field this season, but Coleman has easily been the club's top rookie. That's saying something, given that he missed four games on injured reserve with an ankle sprain.
In four of the five games he's dressed for, Coleman has touched the ball and has been a key contributor. In fact, the Broncos haven't lost a game yet in which Coleman has touched the ball, so Sean Payton may want to remember that.
Coleman has 47 times for 191 yards and three touchdowns, averaging a team-high 4.1 yards per attempt. He's also caught 13 passes for 128 yards and six first downs.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
As the Broncos' new RB1, the sky is the limit for Coleman, especially if Payton is able to get to the bottom of the offensive line's blocking issues, as promised to do during the bye. It's a pretty distant thought, but with eight games left to go, the rookie still has the chance to rush for 1,000 yards, though it will take the O-line stepping its game up significantly.
Wide receiver Pat Bryant may have been my choice here, were it not for his missing four games with an ankle injury. He's been a tremendous player for this offense and has taken some big steps forward since his rookie year.
What Bryant and Robinson have in common is they're both in Year 2. Robinson has appeared in every game thus far — another illustration of his improvement, given that he was a healthy scratch in 11 games as a rookie — and without him, I'm not sure Denver would have been able to weather Jonathon Cooper's absence so successfully.
Robinson has 28 tackles (12 solo), three tackles for a loss, one fumble recovery, and a tipped pass. He's tied for third on the team with 25 pressures, despite not being a starter.
Zach Allen leads the pass rush 😤 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/awIGMbyXcq
The Broncos love Cooper, but given his off-field drama and cost, if the team was of a mind to move on in 2027, Robinson's emergence would likely be a big reason why. The 2025 fourth-round pick out of Alabama has been an absolute stud in Year 2.
This is a bit of a cheat because it's not an individual player, but the Broncos' offensive line was billed as the NFL's best unit entering the 2026 season. Alas, this O-line has been far from it.
Nix faced the most pressure of his career through the first six weeks of the season, and the Broncos still haven't been able to generate at reliable run game, Coleman's emergence notwithstanding. The presence of All-Pro tandem Garett Bolles and Quinn Meinerz hasn't been enough to elevate the unit, not with center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey playing so poorly.
The Broncos have a lot of money tied up in Wattenberg and McGlinchey, which is why fans shouldn't expect any personnel changes over the bye, even though Payton threatened it earlier this week . Left guard Ben Powers has gotten a lot of grief from fans this season, but he hasn't been the biggest culprit in the O-line's blocking inefficiencies, and has taken on more responsibility to cover for Wattenberg's foibles.
The continuity Denver has maintained up front is rare, fielding the same starting five for the third straight year, but the O-line, as a unit, hasn't been able to capitalize on it. There's time yet, though. Let's hope the Broncos are able to get to the bottom of the problem during the bye.

title: Broncos' Season Has Exposed a New 2027 First-Round Draft Priority
full_text:
At 7-2, the Denver Broncos are enjoying a well-earned bye week .
The Broncos remain one of the NFL's deepest and most talented rosters, but halfway through the 2026 season, some of the holes have become obvious. This team could use reinforcements and upgrades at tight end, inside linebacker, safety, and running back.
But offensive tackle may be rising to the top of the Broncos' list of needs, especially as it pertains to the first round of next year's draft. NFL Draft On SI 's Justin Melo seems to be evolving on this subject, going from projecting Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson in several of his most recent mock drafts to offensive tackle.
Projecting the Broncos to be picking at No. 29 overall (as it currently stands), Melo mocked Texas offensive tackle Trevor Goosby to the Mile High City.
"Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby now faces a complicated pre-draft process after suffering a season-ending knee injury. The Denver Broncos can afford to be patient, but need an eventual successor for the aging Garret Bolles. With Mike McGlinchey underperforming, the Broncos could address both offensive tackle spots," Melo wrote .
Listed at 6-foot-7 and 325 pounds, Goosby would step in as the biggest and likely the longest tackle on the Broncos' roster. For his size, he's extremely athletic, and balances that with a fair amount of power.
Goosby was named first-team All-SEC last year, which is no mean feat in that Conference, and has been Arch Manning's blind-side protector at Texas. Goosby has played in some big games and has excelled against quality opponents.
As a red-shirt senior, this will be Goosby's last collegiate season. It will be interesting to see how he tests at the 2027 NFL Combine. He could go earlier in the draft than No. 29 overall.
Both Bolles and McGlinchey are well on the wrong side of 30. At 34, Bolles is still performing at an All-Pro level , and while he's getting up there, he's actually young for his age, given his late foray into football after serving a two-year LDS mission.
Meanwhile, McGlinchey will turn 32 in January. He's never been an All-Pro-caliber talent, but up until this season, he's been a competent and reliable right tackle.
That has changed rather dramatically this season. McGlinchey's run blocking has devolved and as a pass protector, he's become a liability for Bo Nix.
Bolles isn't showing any signs of slowing down. With McGlinchey, though, alarm bells have to be ringing at Broncos HQ — so much so that it wouldn't completely shock me if the coaches were to make a change at right tackle during the bye and give Alex Palczewski a crack at the job.
It's unlikely to happen, given McGlinchey's $23.775 million cap hit — the highest on the team this year — and his leadership. Teams often fall prey to the sunk-cost fallacy, where the highest-paid players simply have to play, and the Broncos aren't immune to this flawed line of thinking.
He may not be a team captain, but McGlinchey is very much a leader that guys look to on offense, and that will always factor into any conversation about potentially benching him.
The Broncos started thinking ahead by drafting Kage Casey in the fourth round earlier this year, anticipating the coming departure of left guard Ben Powers. Denver's center situation isn't great, with Luke Wattenberg playing poorly on a second contract and backup Alex Forsyth hitting free agency after this year, so it wouldn't be a shock to see the team prioritize interior offensive line in the draft.
If you're going to invest a first-round pick, though, it should be offensive tackle; a position that Denver hasn't drafted since Bolles in 2017. Casey was a career tackle at Boise State, but the Broncos drafted him to play guard.
As we inch closer to draft season, fans will likely be pounding the table for a tight end, running back, or linebacker, but don't be surprised if the Broncos finally go back to the offensive tackle well in Round 1.

title: Broncos Rookie Report Card at the Bye: The Hits, Misses, and Surprises
full_text:
The 7-2 Denver Broncos are on bye this week. And given how the NFL placed Denver's bye about as close to the season's halfway point as it gets, it's a perfect opportunity for evaluation.
We've already covered the Broncos' player grades at the bye , with nine weeks of data to factor in, and we've also scrutinized GM George Paton's top extension candidates . Today, it's time for a Broncos rookie report card at the bye, including a grade.
Until last week, Coleman was the only Broncos rookie with meaningful playing time. The Broncos made seven draft picks last spring, and four of them — including Coleman — made the 53-man roster.
Coleman has been active for five games this season, but he didn't touch the ball in his first-ever game, which was Week 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs. In Week 2, the rookie suffered an ankle injury on his first career touch, and though he exited the game for a spell, he returned to play a key role in scoring the go-ahead touchdown and grind out the clock against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
That ankle injury turned out to be more severe than it seemed, and the Broncos placed Coleman on injured reserve. After four weeks, though, the rookie was ready to go, so the Broncos activated him for their road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
Coleman carried the ball nine times for 54 yards in Arizona and caught two passes for 15 yards. That game set a new precedent in the Broncos' backfield, with the rookie outearning J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in snaps and touches.
It's been that way ever since. Coleman is the Broncos' new RB1. He has totaled 191 yards and three touchdowns on 41 carries (4.1 avg), with 13 receptions for 128 yards. He's made a big impact in every game in which he's touched the ball.
Despite swirling rumors linking the Broncos to the running back trade market , the team stood pat at the deadline because of Coleman's emergence. With veterans J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey (when he returns from IR in Week 13) behind him, Coleman is poised to play a major role in the Broncos' offense down the stretch.
Coleman's four-week stint on IR is the only reason he doesn't get an A+ at the bye.
Despite being the Broncos' highest draft pick this year (Round 3), Onyedim was a healthy scratch for two months, until finally getting to dress last week against the Carolina Panthers. He played 10 snaps , finishing with a tackle and a forced fumble, and was the Broncos' highest-graded run defender of the day, per Pro Football Focus .
Given how badly the Broncos have struggled against the run this season, it makes you wonder why they waited so long to dress Onyedim. He was one of the 2026 draft class' top run-defending defensive tackles, and he proved exactly why in his first career game.
It May have taken an injury to Eyioma Uwazurike to spark some change at Broncos HQ, but here's to hoping the team has realized that Onyedim is perfectly capable of contributing. If this team stands a chance at making another deep playoff run, this defense has to get better against the run in a hurry, and Onyedim can help it do just that.
Onyedim would have a higher grade if he'd seen the field more. He gets a passing grade, for now, but I expect far more to come.
Casey made the 53-man roster, but is yet to dress for a game. He's viewed as the future at left guard, but with Ben Powers on the final year of his contract, the Broncos seem content to let him finish out the season.
However, head coach Sean Payton hinted that personnel changes up front could be coming over the bye, but it's unlikely to be Powers. Casey was impressive during the preseason, playing both guard spots, and if the Broncos decided to look his way, I'd be encouraged about his outlook.
Alas, I doubt it happens. Even if the Broncos made a change at left guard, Matt Peart would likely be the next guy into the fray. Unless they have to, Payton's Broncos don't love playing rookies, especially in the trenches, but Casey has a bright future beyond 2026.
Like Casey, Bentley has been a healthy scratch all year long. He was the fourth and final tight end to make the roster, and so far, he's remained in developmental mode as the Broncos play veterans Evan Engram, Adam Trautman, and Nate Adkins.
Bentley is much closer to seeing the field than Casey, though. All it would take is one injury ahead of him on the depth chart, and the Broncos would have to dress Bentley.
Time will tell, but the Broncos like their seventh-round tight end out of Utah a lot. He didn't do much during the preseason besides block, but he earned a spot on the roster, beating out fifth-round tight end Justin Joly, who was waived and claimed by the Miami Dolphins.
Katsis didn't make the 53-man roster out of camp, but he was retained on the practice squad. In Week 3, with Marvin Mims Jr. injured, the Broncos elevated Katsis for a key home tilt vs. the Los Angeles Rams.
The undrafted rookie had quite the NFL debut, returning three punts for 39 yards and four kickoffs for 107 yards. Katsis's 146 total return yards were the most by a returner making his debut in franchise history.
If that's not a positive harbinger for what the future could hold for Katsis, I don't know what is. That being said, the Broncos haven't elevated him since then, as Mims has managed to stay healthy, though the veteran returner is having a career-low year.
There's a reason why the Broncos loved Katsis after the draft, making him a priority free-agent signing. His presence could explain, in part, why the Broncos have yet to extend Mims.
Like Onyedim, Katsis only has one game under his belt, but he set franchise records, so he's at a C+. Still too small of a sample size to justify a higher grade.
Undrafted out of Cal, Austin competed in camp and the preseason and earned a spot on the practice squad. He was elevated for Week 5's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers, and while he didn't see the field on defense or special teams, the Broncos like him a lot.
Austin is very physical for his size and has a nose for the ball. The Broncos have prioritize the first-year Sean Fresch Jr. of late, when it comes to practice-squad elevations, mainly due to his returner versatility.
At this point, Austin is angling for a futures contract after this season, which would buy him another opportunity to compete in training camp next year in hopes of making the 53-man roster.
Austin was elevated for a game, but he did not see the field, so he remains ungradable.

title: Why Re-Signing Sean Fresch Jr. Is an Important Move for Broncos
full_text:
Sean Fresch Jr. is back with the Denver Broncos.
When the Broncos thought they were acquiring Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley via trade, they waived Fresch to make room on the 53-man roster. Then Henley failed his physical, and the trade fell through , which leaves a roster spot currently open.
Meanwhile, Fresch passed through waivers unclaimed, so the Broncos quickly re-signed him to the practice squad, where he's spent all but one game this season competing. He's appeared in four games this season — making his NFL debut in Week 5 against the Chargers — and was actually promoted to the Broncos' 53-man roster ahead of Week 9's game against the Carolina Panthers.
Out of the gate, the 5-foot-9, 181-pound defensive back returned the opening kickoff in Carolina 41 yards to set Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense up with great field position. Fresch would finish the day with 62 return yards on two attempts, averaging 31 yards each.
Counting the three previous games Fresch appeared in as a practice-squad elevation, he's totaled six kick returns for 153 yards (25.5 avg). He has also made three solo tackles on special teams, covering punts and kicks.
Fresh originally went undrafted out of Rice last year. No team offered him a contract as a priority free agent after the draft, but the Kansas City Chiefs invited him to try out at their rookie minicamp. Alas, he didn't receive an offer.
So, Fresch bided his time and eventually took his talents to the UFL, signing with the San Antonio Brahmas. When the Brahmas went under, he entered the UFL draft, where the St. Louis Battlehawks selected him in January 2026.
Fresch went on to lead the league in punt return yardage, earning All-UFL honors. The Battlehawks made it to the playoffs, but lost in the semi-finals to the Louisville Kings.
That game was on June 7. The Broncos signed Fresch on June 15 , along with his Battlehawks teammate Hakeem Butler. Both former UFL stars shined early in OTAs and minicamp, but when training camp arrived, Fresch continued to ascend while Butler fell off and was eventually waived.
The Broncos knew they were getting a playmaking returner in Fresch, but they may have slept a little bit on what he brought to the table as a defensive back. He looked good in the preseason, and when the final roster cuts came, he may not have made the 53, but the Broncos quickly re-signed him to the practice squad.
Fresch's 25th birthday was on Wednesday — the same day the Broncos waived him to make room for Henley — but I'm sure the discussion centered around the team's intention to keep him in the fold if he cleared waivers. And that's exactly what happened.
With Marvin Mims Jr. and Ja'Quan McMillian being in a contract year , the Broncos have some post-2026 options in case they're unable to re-sign either. Fresch could check both boxes, in terms of his upside, especially as a returner.
As a defensive back, Fresch still has much to prove, but now that he's back on the practice squad, the Broncos are going to give him the opportunity to do just that. It wouldn't be a surprise if they promoted him again to the 53-man roster before Week 11's home game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Even if they don't promote him, Fresch's three practice-squad elevations have reset, so the Broncos can use him on game day for the foreseeable future.
