title: 6 Winners, 3 Losers From Jaguars' Week 10 Victory over Titans: Josh Cameron's Day
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars kept things rolling and scored 40 points for the second time in three weeks on Sunday ... and it did not feel like it was close to their best game.
The Jaguars took the Tennessee Titans down i n a 40-23 win in Nashville on Sunday, though the score was even closer than the Jaguars really should have allowed considering a few self-inflicted mistakes that kept the Titans in the game.
But at the end of the day, the Jaguars are 7-2, are still a threat to the rest of the AFC , and had another record-setting blowout. So, who are the winners and the losers of the latest Jaguars win? We break it down below.
Parker Washington had career numbers in just the first two quarters alone, and he finished the day with seven catches for 152 yards and a touchdown. He had a direct impact on all 16 of the Jaguars' first-half points, and he was one of just two Jaguars players to get more than five targets in the balanced, spread the ball around offensive style that the Jaguars like to play. Trevor Lawrence clearly trusts him deeply, and that trust has led to Washington pcking up some of the Jaguars' most important offensive plays of the season.
What a day for Jaguars rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron. He caught all three targets that came his way for 67 yards, including a 25-yard touchdown in the fourth-quarter to give the Jaguars their biggest lead of the game and a 28-yard catch down the sideline on the first drive of the game. Add in the several impact plays that Cameron had as a blocker in the running game, such as on Bhayshul Tuten's six-yard touchdown run, and this was one of the best games the rookie receiver has had all season.
The Jaguars continue to win the Travis Hunter trade, eh? Hunter had his third interception of the season on Sunday with a third-down ballhawk of Cam Ward in the first-half, giving him some of the best production of any cornerback in football this season. He also had a very strong game as a tackler and added two catches for 16 yards for the heck of it. He continues to be one of the most impactful players not only on the roster, but in the entire NFL.
Players over the last 25 years with 3 defensive INT and a Rec TD in a season 2026 Travis Hunter 2004 Troy Brown 2001 Brian Urlacher pic.twitter.com/al14XEo170
Trevor Lawrence continues to look like the best player on the field more often than not when the Jaguars play. He threw three touchdowns for the fifth time this season, throwing scores to Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, and Josh Cameron while also picking up several clutch gains on the ground on scrambles and quarterback sneaks. Lawrence's interception was tipped at the line of scrimmage, and he spent the rest of the game taking aggressive shots while also keeping the ball from getting in harm's way. This was another big day for Lawrence, who is making a new case for the MVP every single week.
The Jaguars lost veteran center Robert Hainsey to an injury during the first-half, which led to the Jaguars leaning on second-year center Jonah Monheim at the anchor spot on the offensive line for the second-half. While Monheim was in the game, the Jaguars' operation looked clean, they got a few key conversions in short-yardage situations, and the Jaguars were able to still hit plenty of explosive plays. Monheim has simply always been able to just get the job done, and that is exactly what he did against the Titans on Sunday.
Cam Little was 4-of-4 on field goals on Sunday, and he has missed a field goal since Week 3. That field goal, by the way, was a 70-yarder that nearly made it. Little was automatic for the Jaguars in a game where all of his kicks came before it was a blowout. If the Jaguars had a lesser kicker, the Titans might have had a few more chances to stick around toward the end of the game. But Little once again proved to be one of the NFL's best and most reliable kickers, just like he has been doing over the entire course of the 2026 season.
It is clear that Sunday was the last game that Rayuan Lane is going to start for a bit since Jessie Bates III will be taking his spot in the lineup next week. That is nothing against Lane, of course, but is instead just the natural order of things now that a blue-chip safety has joined the Jaguars on the defensive side of the ball. With that in mind, Lane could have done more on Sunday to go out on a high note. He had a few poor tackle attempts in space, including on the Tony Pollard touchdown, that were a reminder of why the Jaguars went out and made sure they added to the safety spot.
The Jaguars did not have a great day of running the ball in general, but this was one of the most one-sided dominations of the backfield the Jaguars have had all season. Chris Rodriguez Jr. had just four carries on Sunday compared to Bhayshul Tuten getting 26 carries, along with three catches. That means Tuten out-touched Rodriguez 29 to 4 and out-gained him 113 to 5. Rodriguez has become a smaller and smaller part of the offense over the last two games, despite Tuten facing injuries.
Unless Tuten is outright not in the football game, it seems unlikely Rodriguez will see a bigger role than him. But seeing even a similar role to Tuten would be an upgrade for Rodriguez right now, and it is not happening. Tuten did not have a great game and he is clearly not 100%, but the Jaguars still leaned on him the entire way for a reason. When teams tell us what they think and who they are, believe them. The Jaguars are telling us something.
Foyesade Oluokun didn't have a bad game by any measure, recording 10 tackles, a tackle for loss, and helping set the physical tone for the Jaguars from the jump. With that said, Tony Pollard's 32-yard touchdown might have been the most inexcusable touchdown the Jaguars have allowed in all of 2026, and Oluokun's missed tackle after the catch was what set it all off. He was far from the only Jaguar to not make the tackle, but he is held to perhaps the highest of all standards in the Jaguars' defensive locker room. Missed tackles like that one need to prove to be a one-off, because the Jaguars need him to be more than that.
Tony Pollard slips tackles for a 32-yard score! JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FPR0vlha2W

title: 8 Instant Observations on Jaguars' Week 10 Win Over Titans: Travis Hunter's All-Pro Case
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have won, again.
The Jaguars are one of the NFL's best teams and were widely expected to pull away from the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, and that is exactly what they did with a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. So, what did we see against the Titans on Sunday? We break it all down below.
It is easy with all of the big moves around the Jaguars over the last week to forget that the Jaguars already have another big move in waiting with fourth-year wide receiver Parker Washington. Washington has been the team's top receiving option since halfway through the 2025 season, and he has been able to prove his worth to the Jaguars consistently since. This was certainly the case against the Titans, with Washington recording six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown in the first half, including the game's opening two-yard touchdown catch. Washington never had 148 yards receiving in a game before Sunday, let alone in a half.
Washington is such an important part of the Jaguars' offense that it continues to look like there is just no real scenario where the Jaguars do not keep Washington for the long-term future. The rest of the Jaguars' pass-catchers combined for seven targets in the first-half, the same total that Washington saw himself. That is the sign of a team's No. 1 receiver, even if it looks a bit different than most definitions of the spot. Washington's value continues to rise as this season rolls on.
Parker Washington turning DBs 360 degrees pic.twitter.com/WOCBpP7b5j
Travis Hunter is a special player. That much has already been made clear some time ago, but he continues to look more and more like a true playmaker for the Jaguars as their No. 1 cornerback. Hunter recorded his third interception of the season with his first-half third-down pick of Cam Ward, which might have been his most impressive pick yet. Hunter made up ground on the Titans wide receiver on an across-the-body throw from Ward and ended up making an incredibly athletic grab to secure possession and set the Jaguars up for a field goal.
Travis Hunter dives for the interception! 🔥 JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RKvGzhsi9H
Only seven other cornerbacks in the NFL had three or more interceptions entering Week 10, and one of them is Hunter's teammate in Jourdan Lewis. The Jaguars have seen Hunter not only improve his down-to-down consistency at cornerback, but more importantly they have seen him become one of the best playmakers at the position in the entire NFL. It is hard to make an argument for another AFC cornerback ahead of him on the All-Pro lists outside of Denzel Ward right now.
We have mentioned a few times this season that game management is still one area Liam Coen is still growing in, which is only natural considering he entered Sunday with just 25 games under his belt as a head coach. Coen showed some real growth in that area at the end of the first-half for the Jaguars, using his timeouts and the field positioning to put the Jaguars in a strong spot entering halftime with a 16-10 lead over a scrappy Titans team.
After making sure the Jaguars got the ball with a timeout left, Coen saw his offense pick up 58 yards over three passes before spiking the ball with 11 seconds left. After Jakobi Meyers then ran out of bounds with seven seconds left, Coen had one more play called to throw the ball into the end-zone and kill five more seconds. This left just two seconds on the clock when Cam Little hit his third field goal of the half, killing any chance, no matter how small, of the Titans doing something with it. That is textbook.
Trevor Lawrence continues to play the best football of his entire career. The lone black mark on his production from Sunday is an interception that, per usual this season, was not even on him after it got batted away at the line of scrimmage. Hunter was otherwise stellar against the Titans, going big-game hunting for big play after big play and routinely finding them after uncorking passes into some tight windows downfield.
With two touchdown passes today, @trevorlawrence has 20 on the season, tied for the third most in the NFL. He is the fastest in franchise history to reach 20 passing touchdowns in a season (nine games). pic.twitter.com/gnNLBChIVy
Lawrence has been on a heater for the Jaguars all season. The only game I can think of where he just did not play well above average was in Week 2 against the Denver Broncos, and he still had some high-level flashes that game. He simply is the reason the Jaguars can look like any offense they want week in and week out, because he puts them in the positions to thrive regardless of the down, distance, or situation.
The reasons the Jaguars wanted to add Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III are clear. The Jaguars wanted to add to their playmaking potential at both safety and defensive tackle, especially in the wake of injuries to Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray a few weeks ago. These are two spots where the Jaguars started backups for the second week in a row on Sunday in Matt Dickerson and Rayuan Lane.
Dickerson had a quarterback hit and a pass deflection, but the Jaguars have been better inside against the run. Lane had a so-so day when it came to making tackles in space, which is exactly where the Jaguars are hoping Jessie Bates can make an impact right out of the gate . The Jaguars need both players during the playoff run , and Sunday helped make that clear.
The Jaguars' running game has felt off since they ran all over the Indianapolis Colts. Part of this has to do with the fact that Bhayshul Tuten is clearly not at 100% , practicing just once in the last two weeks. Part of it could also be due to offensive line injuries, with Anton Harrison being lost for the seaspn in London a month ago and Robert Hainsey leaving during the first-half with an injury. Regardless of the why, though, the run game of the last two weeks has been nothing like the consistent and efficient running game the Jaguars had during the first seven games of the season.
Where the run game was the most concernign Sunday was in the short-yardage. The Jaguars had several short-yardage situations both in the red-zone and on third-down that simply got shut down, no matter if it was Tuten or Chris Rodriguez Jr. in the backfield. The only short-yardage play that worked for the Jaguars was the quarterback sneak, which is something they need to figure out badly.
One of the big long-term questions facing the Jaguars is the future of their safety position. The Jaguars have a potential dynamic duo on their hands in Jessie Bates and Antonio Johnson, and Johnson showed exactly why against the Titans. Johnson has had a strong season in general, but it felt like Sunday was one of his best games with several strong tackles and then a third-down sack of Cam Ward.
The turnovers aren't in Johnson's direction the same way they did a year ago, but I would argue that he has been a better week-to-weekand down-to-down player in 2026 than he was last season when he had his breakout year. Keeping Johnson around for the long haul would be wise, because he is a perfect fit for Campanile's defense. Sunday was just the latest example for that.
Josh Cameron might not be getting a massive package of snaps as a rookie, but he has certainly made the best of them every week. Cameron has made a big play seemingly each time the Jaguars have gone his way during his rookie season, and this trend continued in a big way with perhaps his best performance against the Titans, especially considering the way he did it. Jacksonville has not had much of a downfield passing game all season long, but Cameron changed that Sunday.
Cameron made two catches of over 20+ yards Sunday, catching a 28-yard pass down the right sideline on the game's opening drive. He then followed it up with a 25-yard touchdown catch on Lawrence's third touchdown pass of the game with 9:44 left in the game to make it 30-16. Cameron is a…

title: Jaguars' Bold Trade Deadline Moves Have Clearly Put AFC Contenders on Alert
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars aren't going to debut the top prizes of their 2026 trade deadline haul in Week 10, but that hasn't stopped the moves from already making an impact.
The Jaguars sent a first-round pick, two second-round picks, and a fifth-round pick over the next three drafts to the Philadelphia Eagles and Atlanta Falcons during their trade deadline fireworks, landing Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III in the process.
The moves signalled the Jaguars were all-in to the rest of the football world, including some of their top foes in the AFC in the Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills.
It was clear when the Bills later traded a second-round pick for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick that the move was made in some kind of direct relation to the Jaguars landing Bates. Bates and Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker were the two biggest names on the safety market ahead of the deadline, with Hooker as the clear third-best option.
Baker was not traded, though reports have indicated the Bills and Jaguars each expressed interest. Then the Jaguars made the first move by landing Bates from the Falcons on Monday, with the Bills' response of adding Hooker coming the next day. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Bills and Jaguars were the two teams pushing the hardest for Bates ... and the Jaguars, of course, landed him.
Then there was the Davis deal. There has been a question externally for who exactly else would have been in the market for Davis and, according to Schefter, it was once again the Bills and general manager Brandon Beane. Go back to last year's deadline when the Bills were in the running for Jakobi Meyers, and there is quite the trend now on James Gladstone getting deals done over the Bills at the deadline.
The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles. The two teams most aggressive for former Falcons safety Jessie Bates also were the Bills and… https://t.co/A9jxCTvPTB
The Jaguars and Bills met once last season, with the Bills getting a close win over the Jaguars in the Wild Card round in Jacksonville in a game that changed hands multiple times in the fourth quarter. They are once again two of the top teams in the AFC, and all roads to the Super Bowl through the conference may go through these two teams.
Both the Jaguars and Bills made it clear at the deadline that they think they can win the entire conference. The fact the Jaguars beat them to two different targets is worth keeping in mind moving forward. And then there are the Denver Broncos, who ended up making zero deals at the deadline after their lone deal fell through.
The Broncos are up there with the Jaguars and Bills as the top-three teams in th AFC, and they have split two games with the Jaguars since the 2025 season. Broncos offensive quality control coach Willie Snead took to social media to react to the Jaguars' big deals in a since-deleted post.
Broncos OQC coach Willie Snead tweeted (since deleted) that the Jaguars "still can't beat us" after the big trades ahead of the deadline. pic.twitter.com/lM3MRtZV5V
The Jaguars have caught the eye of the rest of the AFC with their explosive trade deadline additions. Now, the Jaguars will have to finish the job over the next few weeks as they look to make their push in the AFC.

title: Jaguars-Titans Week 10 National Predictions Roundup: Why Jacksonville Can't Overlook Tennessee
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have an important AFC South battle in Week 10, with a chance to keep their momentum rolling as they battle for seeding in the AFC.
But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts.
The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week.
“I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week.
"It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice."
How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below.
Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars
Matt Bowen: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                       Mike Clay: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                     Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                  Dan Graziano: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                  Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                   Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                     Jason Reid: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                          Ben Solak: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                           Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                   Seth Wickersham: Titans
Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars
Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars
The Jaguars do not get the sweep here, earning 29 of 30 votes. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans.
Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late.
The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate.
But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. The Jaguars can't afford to treat the Titans like the Ravens a week ago, but this should still be a game that they control.
On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one.

title: Jaguars Week 10 Rooting Guide: How Jacksonville Can Propel Themselves in AFC
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars could take a serious step toward the No. 1 seed in the AFC with the right results in Week 10.
That, of course, starts and ends with the Jaguars getting the job done against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday. But as long as the Jaguars do what they are supposed to do against the TItans, there is a real path toward their position in the AFC strengthening this week.
So, what else do the Jaguars need to happen this week, outside of a win against the Titans? We break it down below.
The Jaguars have several teams elsewhere in the AFC who they are set to be fighting for the top spot in the AFC. One of those teams is the Chiefs, who are sitting at 6-2 entering a game with the Atlanta Falcons. The Chiefs do not have that many wins over quality opponents this season, but the middling Falcons teams are also not really a quality opponent, are they? The Falcons will also be without Jessie Bates III after the blockbuster that sent him to the Jaguars, though the Chiefs will also be without Kenneth Walker.
A Chiefs loss and a Jaguars win would put the Jaguars firmly in front of the Chiefs in the AFC standings moving into Week 11. The Jaguars need any edge and momentum they can get, and this would certainly be a good way to start building some momentum during the start of the second-half push.
The Jaguars will obviously be rooting against the Houston Texans each and every single week until the scenario actually occurs where they are in the Indianapolis Colts/Tennessee Titans category of “oh, who cares.” It is far from a guarantee that happens since they have a relatively easy second-half schedule and still have a very talented quarterback, but they have lost several games already this year that they never should have let happen.
The Browns upsetting the Texans would be far from the most surprising result of the 2026 season. The Texans are set to be missing a lot of key players due to injuries. The Texans have the quarterback advantage by far with Stroud over Deshaun Watson, but the Jaguars would really be boosted by a Texans loss in any shape or form this week.
This one ... does not feel like it is going to happen! It is the NFL, and stranger things have happened I suppose. But the Jets have been one of the NFL's biggest losers over the last few seasons and I do not think Aaron Glenn's group is going to suddenly figure things out against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, who have simply found ways to win this year.
There will still be chances for the Bills to tumble over the next few weeks and months ahead. With that said, they have several easy games against the AFC East, and this is one of them with some certainty. This should not be an issue.
Rooting Interest: Steelers
This one really could go either way since the Jaguars are in a race with both teams to the top of the AFC. The reason why I say the Steelers here instead of the Bengals is because I am of the belief that the Bengals are the greater threat to the Jaguars for the No. 1 seed, especially considering their schedule for the rest of the season. The Bengals losing feels like it would be good news for the Jaguars.
The Jaguars will get to face off against the Steelers in a few weeks, too. For right now, they are 3-0 against the AFC North. Getting the sweep against the four teams up north after a win against the Steelers would put the Jaguars in a good spot when it comes to tie breakers.

title: Grading Every Jaguars Starter Halfway Through the Season: From Bhayshul Tuten to Ventrell Miller
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are at the halfway point, and the second-half of the season is set to be even more critical than the first stretch of the season was.
The Jaguars are sitting at 6-2 and as one of the top team's in the AFC entering their ninth game of the  season, a clash with the Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday. So, how has each of the Jaguars' key pieces played a part in that climb to the top of the AFC South? We break it down below by grading each starter and key depth player who might as well be counted as a starter ... of which there are several.
So, which Jaguars have been at the top of their game this season as the Jaguars are set to go all-in? We break it down below.
We have said it once, we will say it again. Trevor Lawrence has played at an MVP-level during the 2026 season, and for our money he has been the best player on the Jaguars' roster this season. Lawrence is having the best season of his career and he could see his numbers go up even more in the weeks to come.
If Trevor Lawrence has been the best player for the Jaguars this season, than Bhayshul Tuten's name is not far behind. He has been one of the best and most productive running backs in football this season. Tuten is the entire spark behind the Jaguars' running game.
It has not been all bad for Brian Thomas Jr. He caught a touchdown in a close win over the Cincinnati Bengals, is one of six Jaguars with multiple receiving touchdowns, and has been on the winning side of some important blocks throughout the season. The drops and dip in production bring him down to this grade, though there is time to turn things around still.
Parker Washington's production has not completely exploded this season, but the first- and second-half splits make it clear that this is the result of the Jaguars getting in blowouts and just killing the clock during second halfs of most games. He has been the Jaguars' No. 1 receiver and best big-play threat when all things have been equal.
Jakobi Meyers has been terrific for the Jaguars as a middle of the field target, which is exactly where Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence have been looking to attack defenses in the passing game. His numbers would be even better if he got a higher volume of passes. He is still playing really, really good football.
Brenton Strange looks like he is on the verge of another career season. He has been explosive in the passing game and has once again been a weapon for the Jaguars in the running game and as a blocker in space.
Walker Little has been one of the best pass-blockers in football since he stepped into the starting lineup for an injured Anton Harrison a few weeks ago. He will need to continue to give the Jaguars such a boost as they look to make their playoff run, but he has been rock-solid thus far.
Emmanuel Pregnon has made a strong impression for the Jaguars as a rookie, even if he is one of the lower-graded starters. He has done a good job to help improve the running game, especially in between the tackles. He has to clean up the penalties, but he has a bright future.
Robert Hainsey has once again been reliable for the Jaguars. He has not had many operational mistakes outside of the Eagles game, and he has done a good job spearheading some of the space blocking the line does in Coen's scheme.
Ezra Cleveland has once again been solid for the Jaguars, offering them efficient and quality play as both a run-blocker and pass-blocker. He has had a few reps where he has been beaten, just like any other offensive lineman, but he has been a key piece of the offense as a whole.
Cole Van Lanen had a bit of a slower start to this season, which was expected considering he was coming off of injury. But he has had some real quality performances as of late, and his best football should still be ahead of him.
Josh Hines-Allen has seen his numbers go down as a pure pass-rusher, but he has been the top play-maker of the defensive line considering the pressures that have led to turnovers that he has produced. He has also had a very, very strong year against the run once again.
Davon Hamilton looked like the MVP of the defense until his season-ending injury. Losing him as the anchor of the defense is the reason they went out and made the Jordan Davis move, after all. Hamilton was having the best season of his entire career.
Arik Armstead has made some big plays for the Jaguars this year as a pass-rusher, though there have also been the few games where his impact has been more hit and miss than it perhaps was last season.
Travon Walker has been the Jaguars' most productive pass-rusher and he has once again had a very strong season against the run. Finishing on a few more of his pressures would have him even higher on this list.
Foyesade Oluokun is playing some of the best football of his career lately. He has made big plays as a blitzer, against the run, and in coverage. He has also been on the right end of some of the biggest plays of the season, such as his red-zone interception of Joe Burrow in the Week 4 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
Ventrell Miller has not just had the best season of his career, but he has been one of the top linebackers in football on a down-to-down basis. He simply does not make many mistakes, and his physical brand of football lets him fly around and get in on the action frequently. He is a plus-run defender and blitzer/
Dennis Gardeck has done some truly good things for the Jaguars as a rotational pass-rusher off the edge and he has been rock solid at the outside linebacker spot like he was a year ago as well. He is simply just a good football player.
Travis Hunter has been everything the Jaguars could have ever hoped for at cornerback. He has two interceptions, both of which came in clutch moments in the red-zone. He also had an interception negated against the Bengals and has been extremely close to interceptions in games against the Denver Broncos and Indianapolis Colts. He is a true shut down cornerback.
Jarrian Jones has seen a lot of passes go his way as teams have stayed away from Travis Hunter for long stretches, and he has played much better than anyone has really given him credit for. A few missed tackles are the only reason his grade is even just a B.
Montaric Brown's numbers have been better in recent weeks, though he certainly did not have a hot start to the season. An early-season hamstring injury also limited his impact, but he has had two terrific performances in back-to-back weeks since coming back from the bye week healthy.
Jourdan Lewis has once again been strong in the run game and as a blitzer, and he also has recorded three timely interceptions this season. He has once agaain been a reliable piece of the Jaguars' defense.
Eric Murray or Rayuan Lane was the option here, but Murray has started more games and played more snaps. I thought Murray was having a solid season before his season-ending elbow injury, playing at about the same level he played for the Jaguars last season. He is now set to be replaced by Jessie Bates next week.
The turnovers have perhaps not been there for Antonio Johnson so far the way they were a year ago, but he has been a key piece of what the Jaguars do. He can play in the box, cover tight ends, making an impact as a blitzer and in the running game. He has had his best year as a pro in terms of simple down-to-down consistency.
Cam Little has once again had a strong season for the Jaguars, and he is just a few missed kicks away from being perfect. He has missed one of his 26 extra point attempts and two of his 16 field goal attempts, though one of those would have been a record-breaking kick so let's not ding him too much for it.
The simple truth is that Logan Cook has not had to punt very much. Of all players with at least eight appearances at punter this seasom, Cook ranks No. 21 in punts but still ranks top-9 in yards per punt and net punting. 15 of his 28 punts have been touchbacks, and his 8.1 yards allowed per punt return is…

title: Believe It or Not, Josh Downs Had a Career Day in His Chiefs Debut
full_text:
In the first week of play with the annual NFL trade deadline in the rearview mirror, teams had the first chances to see how their new additions would boost their lineups. The Kansas City Chiefs, who addressed their most pressing need last week, got some positive early returns.
Wide receiver Josh Downs had a limited workload in Sunday's 35-13 drubbing of the Atlanta Falcons, but the former Indianapolis Colts standout made a huge impact. In a handful of key offensive snaps, his new team already received a glimpse of what he's capable of.
Head coach Andy Reid is encouraged by what he saw in Week 10, especially considering it's just the tip of the iceberg.
"Our new guy, Downs, it looks like there's a connection there," Reid said. "They worked well today, and that's on two days of practice. Look forward to incorporating him maybe a little bit more into the offense as we go along."
In all, Downs finished with five targets, four catches and 53 yards. He also scored his first touchdown as a Chief on a beautiful throw from quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Late in the first half, Mahomes saw Downs in a favorable position and gave his newest weapon a chance to capitalize:
Mahomes steps up and drops a dime to Josh Downs for a TD! KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dwTMy1qZYC
Speaking to the media on Sunday afternoon, Mahomes walked through the sequence and tipped his cap to Downs for making his presence felt.
"Yeah, he kind of got matched up one-on-one with the nickel, and that was the play," Mahomes said. "Xavier (Worthy) did a great job of running that post route, grabbing the corner and bringing the safety with him, getting two guys. Before the corner could redirect back there, I gave him a chance to make a play one-on-one, and he made the play.
"Like you said, we haven't got a ton of reps, and that's why I think there are some times you're going to see on tape where he was open and I didn't give him chances. But whenever you do it in a game, those are are the best reps to get. I'll be able to have that trust as the season goes on."
While Downs didn't produce career-best volume stats, he managed to set two personal records elsewhere right out of the gate.
According to NFL Pro , Downs' 62.5% target rate on eight routes and his 7.6 yards per route run were both tops for his time in the league. He also ran each route from the slot, with the yardage total being his second-most from such an alignment in the 2026-27 campaign.
The 25-year-old has posted some gaudy numbers before, going for double-digit targets on six occasions since entering the league in 2023, and he's went for 100-plus yards twice. From an efficiency standpoint, though, this is the best he's ever fared in a single game.
Considering that Downs is weeks away from mastering the Chiefs' offense and was essentially flying by the seat of his pants on Sunday, it's hard not to think this was close to the best-case scenario. Mahomes, on the other hand, believes there was some meat left on the bone.
"I kind of said I think I need to do it even more," Mahomes said of trusting Downs. "It was earlier in that game I didn't trust him to win on a leverage that wasn't a great leverage for him, but he ended up winning. You see it on the tablet and you're like, 'Alright, he won.' So then later on that drive, the next drive, I threw it to him on a trust play like that.
"You get one-on-one, and you've got to let your guys go out there and make plays. He's here for a reason, and it's to make those plays, so I've got to trust him to go out there and make the play. He proved that he can do it."
If week one of the Downs era was any indication, this trade could shape up to be a heck of an in-season transaction .

title: Chiefs Say Rookie Emmett Johnson Did This to Set Up Successful First NFL Start
full_text:
Just like they have been all season long, the Kansas City Chiefs were shorthanded heading into their Week 10 showdown against the Atlanta Falcons . This time, however, it wasn't a wide receiver or offensive line injury that put the team behind the eight-ball.
It was a groin ailment for star running back Kenneth Walker, who's been one of the best players at his position since coming over to Kansas City. Normally, losing someone of his caliber would be so detrimental that it played a role in the upcoming game being much closer than expected.
Not in the Chiefs' case, though. Rookie Emmett Johnson stepped right up to the plate and essentially hit a home run in the process, going off for a pair of scores in his first NFL start. There wasn't much decline, if any, from Walker's production from a qualitative standpoint.
What prepared Johnson for such an outstanding showing? Speaking to the media following the 35-13 win, head coach Andy Reid pointed to him simply being prepared.
"So I look at the players," Reid said. "The players have confidence in him. The players, they're going to tell you the whole story. When a kid comes in and he's good, you know he's good. Obviously, he's doing the right things as far as protections go, so the cerebral part of the game, he's taking care of that part. Knowing the plays, the direction of the plays, how to set up the plays, all of those things, he's got. And then he has that skill that goes with it. And he wants to be in there. He's a great kid that way."
Quarterback Patrick Mahomes echoed that sentiment. Being ready to meet the moment goes a long way in Kansas City, and the former Nebraska man followed that to a T.
"Yeah, I mean, he did a great job," Mahomes said. "He runs tough, he runs hard, he breaks tackles. And then whenever he gets chances in the receiving game, he catches the ball and makes plays there too as well. I'm happy for him, because he comes in with the right mindset every single day. I've talked about it — he has a smile on his face, he wants to be great, he wants to contribute in any way possible.
"Obviously, [with] what happened to Kenneth and how great he's playing, he hasn't gotten as many opportunities. But when his number got called, he stepped in and made the plays happen. That's going to be great to have as the season goes on and we get Kenneth back, that one-two punch."
Johnson toted the ball 22 times on the ground for 101 yards, good for a 4.6 yard-per-carry average. He also was one of Mahomes' top receiving options, converting on six of seven targets for 70 yards and two of the superstar quarterback's five touchdowns on the afternoon.
In the victory, Johnson joined the San Francisco 49ers' Christian McCaffrey as the only halfbacks this decade with at least 100 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns in the same game.
The impressive stats don't stop there. Per NFL Pro , Johnson forced 10 missed tackles and gained 80 of his 171 scrimmage yards after doing so. He owns a higher forced missed tackle rate (45.6%) than any player at his position with 50 or more touches.
Kansas City expects Walker, who missed Friday's practice, back for next Sunday's contest against the Arizona Cardinals. If anything changes between now and then, the club can rest assured knowing it has a more than capable replacement.
Johnson has plenty of skill, as Reid alluded to, but the secret sauce is him pairing that with having adjusted to life in the NFL at a lightning-fast pace. It makes everyone around him more confident, with Mahomes at the top of the list.
"For sure, and he's put in the work for that," Mahomes said. "I don't think anyone can replace Kenneth and the special ability he has running and catching the football, but to have someone who can do it in their own way and can make plays happen and break tackles, that's what you want on the team is guys to be able to step up and make plays. It was late notice, obviously, with everything happening, but he was ready and prepared to go out there and have a great day."

title: Chiefs Avoid Major Travis Kelce Injury Scare in Blowout Win Over Falcons
full_text:
In the Kansas City Chiefs' convincing 35-13 victory over the Falcons today, they didn't exactly come away unscathed. An injury to right guard Trey Smith in the first half knocked him out for the remainder of the contest.
As if losing another starter on the offensive line wasn't enough, KC also watched Travis Kelce go down with an injury scare in the first quarter. The Chiefs were already short-handed offensively entering Sunday's matchup with Kenneth Walker III unavailable , making the situation even more concerning. Kelce's left leg was rolled underneath him awkwardly on a tackle by DeMarcco Hellams on his first catch of the afternoon. After walking off under his own power and briefly being checked out by the training staff, Kelce went to the locker room to receive further evaluation.
Travis Kelce #chiefs Left leg/ankle gets rolled up on. Being evaluated on the sideline pic.twitter.com/Sa7Z5icOqw
Thankfully, Kelce was cleared to return and made his way back to the field in the second quarter, finishing the day with two receptions for 30 yards. He wasn't relied upon heavily, considering the score was largely out of hand by the second half.
After the win, head coach Andy Reid confirmed that Kelce has indeed avoided the worst-case scenario with his lower-leg and referred to it as a minor calf ailment.
"Kelce left for a bit with a calf [injury]. He's been battling his ankle, which is kind of part of it," Reid told reporters during his postgame media availability. "He got landed on during that first catch and twisted up a bit." It was an all-around dominant showing for the Chiefs at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, totaling 470 yards of offense and three passing touchdowns thrown by Patrick Mahomes. Kelce wasn't able to get in on his usual share of the action, though, as he was clearly playing through significant discomfort.
During the Chiefs' Week 6 victory over the Chargers, Kelce had his ankle worked on throughout the first half with a similar issue. Just like today, he would return to the contest and occasionally head to the sidelines for treatment.
Although the initial update from Reid is encouraging, it remains to be seen whether Kelce will be limited at all during practice this upcoming week. Kansas City knows it must be extremely cautious with its veteran tight end, especially with the postseason quickly approaching.
Fellow tight end Jared Wiley also injured his ankle in the opening half and was ruled out shortly thereafter. Reid later revealed that he fractured it, which could effectively end his season. Kansas City can't afford to be without Kelce with its depth already being tested.
At 37 years old lugging around 250 pounds of body weight, lower-body injuries are always concerning at this stage of his career. However, the hope is that Kelce can play through it without it hindering his play too much down the stretch. Even with lingering pain below his aging knees, Kelce still looks like one of the NFL's premier tight ends when he's active.

title: 10 Instant Observations From Chiefs' Dominant Win Over Falcons
full_text:
After hanging 35 points on the New York Jets in Week 9, the Kansas City Chiefs must've liked that performance so much that they figured they'd do the same thing against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10.
In a 35-13 triumph on the road, Kansas City's offense was more than good enough to secure a statement victory. Thanks to an elite showing from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and an awesome afternoon for Steve Spagnuolo's defense, head coach Andy Reid's crew made it look easy.
With the win, the Chiefs capture their second in a row and rise to 7-2 on the year. Let's jump into 10 instant observations and takeaways from Week 10.
In our milestones story prior to kickoff on Sunday, it was mentioned that tight end Travis Kelce needed just 18 receiving yards to become the fourth player at his position with 500 yards in 13 separate seasons. He managed to surpass that mark on the opening drive of the game, although the accomplishment was immediately thrown to the wayside due to an injury.
On his 23-yard reception in the first quarter, Kelce got wrapped up by Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams around the ankle area. The superstar has been nursing an ankle issue for weeks and appeared to have aggravated it on the play.
Travis Kelce is limping after he appears to re-injure his ankle. pic.twitter.com/1vdmGkS1tN
Kelce was originally deemed questionable to return, and making matters worse was fellow tight end Jared Wiley being carted to the locker room and subsequently ruled out. The future Hall of Fame pass catcher ultimately returned in the second frame, but this seems to be something that will bother him down the stretch of the season.
Speaking of injuries, the Kansas City offensive line was already in a rough place before this one even started. 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons is eligible to come off the injured reserve list soon, but his continued absence leaves Kahlil Benson in at left tackle. On the right side, Jaylon Moore's ankle injury held him out of practice all week, rendering him inactive for Week 10.
In the first half, things got even worse. Star right guard Trey Smith was knocked out of the game and evaluated for a concussion, then the team announced he'd miss the remainder of the contest. Fill-in Mike Caliendo struggled in relief, making it more difficult to move the chains and sustain a viable passing attack.
That, paired with Benson's struggles, underscored the harsh reality of the offensive line in Week 10.
The Chiefs got some bad news late in the week when running back Kenneth Walker III sustained a groin injury in practice. That left his status for Sunday in question, only for him to get downgraded to out on the injury report on Saturday. With the team exercising some caution with its biggest playmaker this season, rookie Emmett Johnson was thrust into the spotlight . He made the most of it right off the bat.
On the first offensive possession of the game for Kansas City, the fifth-round pick had runs of 10, six, 12, four (on a third-and-1) and four yards. He also notched a 12-yard receiving touchdown to cap things off. The Nebraska product was excellent right out of the gate and finished his first professional start with 28 touches, 171 scrimmage yards and two scores — a terrific day at the office.
We knew the Falcons' offense was up-and-down in nature. On one hand, quarterback Michael Penix Jr. had a hot streak earlier this season upon debuting and looked to be a promising piece for a bit. On the flip side, he's gotten exposed in recent weeks, and Atlanta came into this one ranking 28th ( RBSDM ) in EPA per dropback. Not even the threat of running back Bijan Robinson has been enough to save this group at times.
The Falcons repeatedly shot themselves in the foot in the first half, but the Chiefs' defense also deserves credit for doing its job and helping make the opposition look inept.
Penix missed a pair of throws on the opening drive, and defensive end George Karlaftis shut down the second possession with a sack. The third and fourth series featured penalties and a deep ball that didn't convert. With 12 plays for 22 yards to open the game, it was the first time Atlanta started a game with four consecutive three-and-outs since the year 2000.
In his three years as a member of the Chiefs, tackle Jawaan Taylor drew plenty of flags for false starts and illegal formation infractions. No one's been penalized as much as him over the last handful of seasons, and playing in a multitude of prime-time outings in Kansas City got lots of eyes on him. Some of those woes have carried into his time with the Falcons this year, especially on Sunday.
On a third-and-12 in the first quarter, Taylor's false start led to a third-and-17 that fell incomplete. Coming out of the halftime break, he had another one on second-and-4 that was followed by a two-yard loss on the ground and a failed third-down conversion. Taylor may not have been suited up for his old team in Week 10, but he assisted them in their winnings efforts.
The Chiefs made a splash at the trade deadline by sending a fourth- and fifth-round pick in next year's NFL Draft to the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for wideout Josh Downs and a seventh-round offering. It was a move that many believed wouldn't necessarily save the season, but it was a necessary transaction for a club that desperately needed help at the position.
Boy, did it pay off in a limited sample size on Sunday.
Even while still grasping the playbook on offense and muffing a punt on special teams, Downs was an overall positive in his first game on a new team. He hauled in multiple passes from quarterback Patrick Mahomes for chunk gains in the opening half, including a back-shoulder beauty for an 18-yard touchdown right before the intermission:
Mahomes steps up and drops a dime to Josh Downs for a TD! KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dwTMy1qZYC
As Downs' workload grows over time over the next few weeks, more and more production could be in the cards. Considering what he was able to do on short notice in hostile territory in Week 10, fans should feel great about the pickup for the moment.
Speaking of Chiefs wide receivers who did good things in Sunday's game, rookie Cyrus Allen finally had his breakthrough moment. Coming into Week 10 with just five receptions for 65 yards on the year, the former Cincinnati man left some to be desired in the box score standpoint. After a catchless game versus the New York Jets in Week 9, he responded in a big way here.
Allen was held in the first quarter and had a chance at a one-handed touchdown grab, but he made up for it in the second half. On Mahomes' first completed pass of 20-plus air yards since Week 4, Allen torched cornerback A.J. Terrell for a 39-yard score to punctuate a quick scoring drive:
Cyrus Allen with a nasty double move to cash in the long TD🥵🥵 Sully gonna have to leave the app pic.twitter.com/M8GfmtekqM
For an offense that's struggled with verticality in the passing game in recent weeks, that play was much-needed. The same could be said for the club's promising young wideout.
The Chiefs' defensive line picked up its play in a big way against the Jets last week, recording five sacks and making quarterback Geno Smith have a terrible afternoon. Penix wasn't under nearly as much duress in Week 10, but multiple members of the front were effective on the road, including fifth-year defensive end Karlaftis.
Coming off a one-sack showing in Week 8 and a two-sack effort in Week 9, Karlaftis had the aforementioned second-down sack and joined tackle Chris Jones for a half-sack later on. He also ended a drive with a third-and-10 batted pass. The latter has become a patented play of his, and anyone around will tell you he can put his water polo background to good use.
Karlaftis is emerging as a true difference-maker for Kansas City, which is a welcome sight as the second half of the year rolls on.

title: Live Game Thread & Updates for Kansas City Chiefs vs. Atlanta Falcons in Week 10
full_text:
The Chiefs and Falcons are set to square off in a pivotal matchup in Week 10. Fresh off a rout of the Jets, Kansas City will look to keep rolling against an incredibly inconsistent Atlanta squad on the road at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. For those who are interested in keeping up with the action but can't watch, we've got you covered. At Chiefs on SI, we will keep tabs on every major development and key moment from the contest. Our coverage will begin at kickoff.
Pregame: The Chiefs win the toss and elect to differ. The Falcons will open today's contest with the ball. 14:01: Kansas City forces a three-and-out to open the afternoon. Nohl Williams came up with a nice tackle on third down to keep Kyle Pitts behind the first-down marker. The Chiefs will open their first offensive possession at the 20-yard line after a touchback punt. 12:16: Emmett Johnson has looked the part early in his first NFL start in the backfield. He's taken three carries for 28 yards, including a pair of bursts for over 10 yards. Patrick Mahomes found Travis Kelce over the middle of the field for a big gain as well. 8:53: After a failed designed run for Justin Fields on second down, Mahomes found Johnson wide open on the left sideline for a 12-yard walk-in receiving touchdown. Not too shabby of a drive for the rookie! Chiefs lead, 7-0. 7:19: It's another three-and-out for the Falcons as the boo birds begin to chirp in Atlanta. George Karlaftis continues to wreak havoc in the backfield, as his second-down sack put the third-down try out of reach. Josh Downs muffed the punt on his first-ever touch as a Chief, but he recovered it and the offense will start its next drive at its own four-yard line. 5:02: Johnson was able to make a few nifty moves on a third-down screen pass, but he came just short of the line to gain. Matt Araiza boots it away 58 yards to give Atlanta another chance to get something going offensively. Injury Report: Travis Kelce is questionable to return with an ankle injury. He came out the game after his first catch of the afternoon and is being checked out by the medical staff. 3:04: An absolutely disastrous first quarter for Atlanta, which has failed to record a first down yet. A holding call and false start set the Falcons back and forced them to punt for the third time today. 3:00: There it is for Josh Downs. He gets open in the middle of the field and picks up 21 yards for his first reception as a Chief. Quick injury note: Trey Smith is in the medical tent and Mike Caliendo is in at right guard. 1:29: Johnson is unable to come up with a jumping catch on third-and-long, sending Araiza back out to punt. Not a great start to the day for Caliendo, who was called for holding on third down after getting beat off the line. 0:00: You guessed it — another punt for the Falcons. They go three-and-out for the fourth time this quarter after Michael Penix couldn't connect on a deep pass with Drake London. The first play of the second quarter will be a punt.
13:28: Another empty possession for the Chiefs after Mahomes can't hit Xavier Worthy on third down. Is this the drive the Falcons will pick up a first down? 11:23: Jahan Dotson takes a slant into the red zone on a third-and-long conversion. Falcons offense starting to pick up some steam. title: Chiefs Stats and Milestones for Week 10 vs. Falcons: History Awaits Mahomes, Kelce
full_text:
Of course, the Kansas City Chiefs' main goal for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons is to escape with a victory. That doesn't mean some of their individual players can't hit new milestones along the way, though.
This afternoon, it's the tried-and-true duo of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce that has the potential to further bolster resumes. The club's two biggest stars are within striking distance of reaching even more rarefied air at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, adding some intrigue to the action on Sunday.
Let's take a look at the top benchmarks to keep in mind for the Chiefs in Week 10 of the regular season.
It's been a heck of a career to this point for Mahomes, who's also seeing a bit of a rebound statistically. After averaging 6.2 adjusted net yards per attempt with a 4.5% touchdown rate and a 5.46% sack clip in the last three seasons, those respective marks are 7.6, 5.3% and 4.01% in 2026-27. The passing game is far from perfect, but No. 15 is doing his part to produce positive results.
On Sunday, Mahomes can level up in a huge way with just one touchdown pass against Atlanta.
Per the NFL's official Week 10 preview and capsules, a throwing score would give Mahomes 328 for his career, including the postseason. That'd put him in sole possession of first place for the most by a signal-caller in his first 10 seasons, passing Hall of Fame man Peyton Manning.
There's a case to be made that Mahomes has enjoyed the best start to an NFL tenure ever. He can help solidify that argument this weekend.
Speaking of Chiefs who are assisting in keeping the offense afloat, Kelce's turned back the clock to the tune of a career-high 14.6 yards per catch and 10.0 yards after catch per reception. The 37-year-old remains one of football's better tight ends, and his legend grows with each passing game. A connection or two from Mahomes on Sunday could get him into another tight end Mount Rushmore.
Kelce needs just 18 receiving yards in Week 10 to join Tony Gonzalez, Antonio Gates and Jason Witten as the only players at the position with 500-plus yards in at least 13 seasons. Considering that Kelce already leapfrogged Gonzalez for career yardage (playoffs included) earlier in the year, this feels inevitable.
The future Hall of Fame pass catcher has only finished below that 18-yard mark once this season, logging 15 yards in Week 4's win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He's averaged 59 yards per game since then, potentially setting the stage for a big-time accomplishment down in Atlanta.

title: Chiefs vs. Falcons: NFL Week 10 Preview, Score Predictions
full_text:
As the 2026-27 season rolls through to Week 10, the trade deadline and over half a campaign of play are in the books. It's been mostly positive on the results front for the Kansas City Chiefs, who come into Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons sitting at a healthy 6-2 overall.
Although Atlanta seems to be trending in the wrong direction, it's still in business to compete in a lackluster NFC South. Could that lead to an inspired home performance against visiting Kansas City, or will it be smooth sailing for head coach Andy Reid's group?
With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 10 of the regular season.
Joshua Brisco: The loss of Kenneth Walker impacts how the Chiefs may choose to manage this game, but it shouldn’t change the final result. Kansas City still has the advantage on both sides of the ball, even though Atlanta has punched above its weight twice this season. Ultimately, I expect the Chiefs to navigate through a relatively tough game and return home with the win.
Jordan Foote: Being down Walker undoubtedly could make life more difficult for the Chiefs, but rookie Emmett Johnson's been nothing short of awesome when on the field. Look for him to leave attempts at tackles behind on Sunday afternoon and factor into a passing game that has a less-than-100% Xavier Worthy but a new addition in Josh Downs.
The real intrigue, in my view, comes on the defensive side. Can Steve Spagnuolo's unit find a way to slow down running back Bijan Robinson and wideout Drake London? If so, putting the fate of the game in quarterback Michael Penix Jr.'s hands seems like a losing formula for Atlanta.
It may not be as pretty and resounding as Week 9's throttling of the Jets was, but it should be another victory regardless.
Joshua Schulman: Coming off a much-needed bounce-back win at home, the Chiefs will hit the road against a perplexing Falcons squad. They have defeated the 49ers at home and put up 45 points on their division rival Saints on the road, yet they were also shut out by the Buccaneers in a four-interception outing from Michael Penix Jr.
Ultimately, I think this will come down to the version of Atlanta that shows up. The Falcons rank in the bottom half of the league in both rushing and passing defense, so I’m expecting Emmett Johnson to wreak havoc on the ground despite Kenneth Walker’s absence. It’ll also be Josh Downs’ first appearance in the red and gold after he was acquired via trade from the Colts.
I do think the threat of Bijan Robinson and being away from home will keep this close, but I have Kansas City pulling away in a narrow finish.
Tyler Brown: Nothing like a Week 9 win against the Jets to trick the mind into thinking Kansas City turned the corner after an explosive second half, but that might be what happened.
Setting aside the Harrison Butker and Josh Simmons drama, the Chiefs looked like an inspired team led by their old faithful stars. Travis Kelce and Chris Jones both posted big performances, and Rashee Rice and George Karlaftis are becoming key cogs in their respective units. A mid-season acquisition like Josh Downs can also provide a shot in the arm for a team.
This game will be won in the trenches. Atlanta has Robinson, the NFL’s leading rusher, so the Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers will need a big day to contain him. If they do, Penix, the worst quarterback in the league when facing pressure, will be forced to beat them.
On the other side, Walker’s injury leaves the Chiefs’ rushing attack in question. With Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu starting at tackle, the Chiefs will need a big day from Johnson.
I think they get it done, kicking the Falcons while they’re down in the same week they traded away their best center and safety. Don’t get me wrong, Atlanta has a lot to play for, just a half-game back in a weak NFC South despite being 3-6. They are getting further and further away from their wins over the 6-3 Packers and 7-1 49ers, however.

title: What Might Josh Downs’ Workload Look Like in His Chiefs Debut?
full_text:
After the Chiefs broke out of an offensive slump in last week's drubbing of the Jets, Kansas City made a splash before the trade deadline passed by adding Josh Downs . This move bolstered KC's questionable receiving corps and gave it an elite separator in the slot.
While the underwhelming production from Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy has left plenty to be desired this season, midseason receiver acquisitions historically take a while to become acclimated to the offense. Downs only has a few days of experience within Andy Reid's offensive scheme and likely doesn't know a good chunk of the playbook despite his efforts to get up to speed . As Kansas City's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons approaches, Downs is set to make his debut in a red and gold uniform tomorrow. His workload may not be as substantial as many people think.
The Chiefs may implement a more pass-heavy game plan than usual due to the absence of running back Kenneth Walker . Even so, that doesn't mean Downs will immediately be thrust into a high-volume role in the passing game.
Rice and Worthy will still account for a large portion of the snap count, and there may be certain packages where Reid isn't comfortable deploying him yet. At 5-foot-9, 171 pounds, Downs isn't exactly the type of receiver built to play every down. Across nine games in Indianapolis, Downs caught 33 passes for 354 yards and one touchdown . He was catching passes from Daniel Jones in the Colts' anemic passing attack, but he's never been much of a big-play threat. Downs is at his best when he's breaking down opposing defensive backs in man coverage.
The North Carolina product should be heavily featured on third downs and short-route concepts, which is where he excels most. Where he shouldn't be expected to produce much is on longer-developing plays and rushing formations.
Between the three receivers the Chiefs have traded for at the deadline (Kadarius Toney, Mecole Hardman, DeAndre Hopkins) in the past half-decade, none of them surpassed two receptions or 30 yards in their first Kansas City game — Hardman being an asterisk since it was his second stint with the franchise. Regardless, Downs could be in for a quiet afternoon if that trend continues.
Since Worthy is active while he battles back from a hamstring injury and Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen remain in the mix, there's little reason for the Chiefs to keep Downs on the field every play.
After he spends a few weeks with the coaching staff and learns the ins and outs of the offense, Downs will be in line for a larger role. Until then, though, this transition period could take some time for the former Colts standout.

title: Without Kenneth Walker, Emmett Johnson is Key in Chiefs vs. Falcons
full_text:
The New York Jets were fully capable of being feisty last week, and the same can be said this week, perhaps even more so. The Chiefs passed Week 9’s test resoundingly, but this is also a road game for Kansas City, and Atlanta has a ton to play for.
The Falcons are 3-6, but the division is so weak this year that they're only half a game behind the 3-5 Carolina Panthers and the New Orleans Saints. Their wins include a 21-point victory over the 6-3 Green Bay Packers and a nine-point win over the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers.
They may have just signaled how good or bad they think they are by trading away safety Jessie Bates and starting center Ryan Neuzil, but they are still in the thick of the NFC South race, and they seem to be playing hard for first-year head coach Kevin Stefanski.
Plenty of weapons will be on the field Sunday at noon. Atlanta has wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts, while the Chiefs have Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and newcomer Josh Downs . But make no mistake: this game is all about the trenches and the run game on both sides. Let’s dig into those two matchups.
A wrinkle emerged in the Chiefs’ rushing-game plans late Friday afternoon when Kenneth Walker sat out of practice with groin tightness. Andy Reid said at the time that they would not put him at risk, and it appears Kansas City's brass is exercising caution.
Sources: #Chiefs star RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is OUT for Sunday’s game vs the #Falcons . I’m told the injury is not a long-term concern, but the team is playing it safe. pic.twitter.com/ODtxiueYp1
With Walker officially inactive for Week 10, rookie Emmett Johnson will draw the start. Walker is second only to Bijan Robinson in rushing this season, has already passed 1,000 yards from scrimmage, and has 11 total touchdowns, so his absence will hurt. Still, his long-term outlook matters more than a midseason game in Atlanta, and Johnson has proven to be a worthy backup.
Johnson does not get many opportunities, but when he does, he makes the most of them. The fifth-round pick out of Nebraska has only 26 carries, but is averaging 4.3 yards per carry and has one rushing touchdown.
He has been even more impressive through the air. Thanks to a big game against the Denver Broncos, Johnson has more receiving yards than Walker, on 19 fewer targets and 12 fewer receptions. He has three catches of more than 20 yards, is averaging 16.9 yards per reception, and has a receiving touchdown.
Perhaps the most impressive part of his game has been his forced-missed-tackle rate. According to PFF, he has amassed 22 missed tackles forced on his 42 touches. If the offensive line blocks for Johnson the way it did for Walker last week, it should be a big day for the ground game.
Atlanta is in the middle of the pack at 118 rushing yards allowed per game, but near the bottom of the league at 4.4 yards allowed per carry. Kansas City will need to establish the run because its starting tackles will be Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu , who were third and fourth on the depth chart heading into the season. Establishing the run game will only help Patrick Mahomes and his tackles in the passing game.
The Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers have the toughest matchup on the field, facing the NFL’s leading rusher, Bijan Robinson. He is a touchdown waiting to happen on any given play, on the ground or through the air.
He is averaging 5.2 yards per carry with 880 yards and five touchdowns through nine games. He also has 250 receiving yards and a touchdown this year, after posting over 800 yards and four touchdowns as a receiver last season. That means linebackers Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill need to be at their best.
The Chiefs had a terrific run defense in 2024, weaponizing players like Leo Chenal, and that year, they held Robinson to a jaw-dropping 1.9 yards per carry, just 31 yards and a touchdown. This year, Kansas City ranks 10th in rush defense at just over 97 yards per game, and sixth in the NFL at 3.6 yards per carry.
While all of that is true, they have faced the 27th, 15th, 12th, 31st, 16th, 18th, and 20th-ranked rushing offenses. This is by far their biggest test of the season, and it is not easy to prepare for when you also have to worry about London on the outside.
Still, Kansas City is best off centering its game plan around stopping Robinson, given how poorly quarterback Michael Penix is playing. If the Chiefs force the Falcons into passing situations, the defense will have a much easier job.
According to PFF, Penix is the worst quarterback in the league under pressure, with a 28.8 completion percentage, one touchdown, three interceptions, and a 13.8 percent turnover-worthy play rate. For perspective, Trevor Lawrence has the next-highest rate at 9.2 percent. It may not be possible to do to Robinson what Kansas City did in 2024, but if the Chiefs can limit him to some degree, they should coast to victory.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Quentin Johnston to be Strong Flex Option on Monday Night Football
full_text:

Not every option is worth putting into your lineup , so knowing who could make the most of their opportunities is important .
Here are the decisions you should make ahead of the Monday night football matchup.
Johnston is one receiver I’d give serious consideration to this week. The main reason is the absence of Ladd McConkey.
He has the ability to create separation and make something happen when the ball comes his way. With an opportunity to contribute in the passing game, he could be a useful flex option for fantasy managers.
The Ravens won’t make things easy obviously, but Johnston has enough playmaking ability to make him worth taking a chance on.
Gadsden is another name worth keeping in mind for this matchup. He’s shown that he can be a reliable option when called upon, and his receiving ability gives him a chance to contribute in the red zone.
This year has been weird for everyone on this team, but I think it's only a matter of time until he has another big game. Tight end production can be unpredictable, but Gadsden has the potential to put together a solid night. If you’re looking for an option with upside at the position, he’s worth considering.
Herbert is a difficult fantasy decision heading into Monday night.
He’s dealing with a finger injury, and his recent performances haven’t made him an automatic choice for fantasy lineups.
Hebert has been a risky option all year to be honest. Unless you don’t have another dependable quarterback available, I’d consider looking elsewhere this week.
Mitchell is someone I’d be careful about putting into a starting lineup. Although he brings plenty of speed and explosiveness, his workload remains a concern with multiple running backs competing for opportunities. It’s difficult to count on consistent fantasy production when the touches aren’t guaranteed.
Vidal is another player I’d leave on the bench for this contest. The competition in the backfield makes his weekly workload difficult to predict, which isn’t ideal when fantasy managers need dependable production.
The truth is that he could be a great dependable back. He can contribute when given opportunities, but there are too many questions surrounding his involvement to make him a comfortable start.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: The Ravens Present Another Big Challenge For LA
full_text:
Well, the Los Angeles Chargers are under the bright lights in a matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. Former Jim Harbaugh protege Jesse Minter will be looking for a passing of the torch moment.
The Bolts face another uphill battle , which is nothing new this year. Justin Herbert and the offense are still searching for their identity. When things get bad, they get real bad for this franchise and we could possibly see another beatdown come game time.
The biggest question will be, if the Chargers can stop this new and improved offense backed behind quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
The Baltimore Ravens enter this matchup with a major change, acquiring Jacoby Brissett via trade.
Now Brissett has an opportunity to provide some stability to an offense that desperately needs direction. For the Chargers, preparing for Brissett creates an interesting challenge. He is not a quarterback who needs to rely on spectacular plays to make an impact. His experience gives him the ability to recognize defensive looks, make adjustments, and take what the opposition gives him.
A huge factor or game changer you could say is the defensive line. If Mack, Mesidor, Tuipulotu, and others can put pressure on that offensive front, more mistakes are bound to happen for a new guy trying to learn a different scheme.
The Bolts will need to be disciplined in coverage and avoid giving him easy opportunities to keep Baltimore’s drives alive. Allowing him to settle into a comfortable rhythm could make the evening much more difficult. Overlooking them because of its quarterback situation would be a mistake. The Ravens still have experienced playmakers who can make life difficult for a defense. He did beat them the first game of the season, so there's that.
However, there is an adjustment period that the Chargers should look to take advantage of. Brissett is joining a new locker room, learning a different offensive system, and developing chemistry with receivers he has not spent an entire season playing alongside. Communication and timing will be especially important. If the Bolts can create pressure and force Baltimore into uncomfortable situations early, it could disrupt the Ravens offensive plans.
The defense has done an incredible job this year and with a hot start they might just be on their way to a win. Anything opposite of that, you might as well kiss the win goodbye.

title: Chargers' Future, Justin Herbert Status Speculated by Ian Rapoport
full_text:
Though they have kept the messaging consistent about staying the course , it feels inevitable that the Los Angeles Chargers will look at major changes this upcoming offseason.
It’s a point that’s hard to argue given the 0-8 start and the lack of any games left on the schedule to feel very comfortable about right now.
Big changes could mean anything too, really. While the organization is worried about sending the right messages around the trade deadline disaster, one would think that Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz could be in danger next offseason.
Jim Harbaugh and his Chargers coaching staff, with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel topping the list, will likely face severe hot seats and the front office blowing up the whole thing and starting over wouldn’t be that shocking.
Granted, these are just presumptions based on what outsiders can see. But even major reporters are saying the same thing.
Is this a case of smoke pointing to an obvious fire?
During an appearance on ESPN, Ian Rapoport called the Chargers the “most stunning thing of this entire season,” and suggested that the team could be looking at massive changes soon.
“I would expect a pretty wholesale look at everything after the season,” Rapoport said. “This is a place that really should win games…the acclimation process should be over. Everything that could go wrong has gone wrong.”
A big disclaimer, though: Everything doesn't include moving on from Justin Herbert. Rapoport added this on Herbert: “I’ve gotten zero sense that they would move on from him at all.”
Zooming out, the Chargers struggling this season isn’t that big of a surprise. The front office sat on loads of free cap space and tried to find bargains, leveraging the now for a “future” the current regime might not even see. McDaniel was a splash hiring, but the personnel department never matched his speedy needs and he’s made some odd decisions, like steering away from first-rounder Omarion Hampton.
If one had to guess, Harbaugh and his staff will be gone after the season no matter what ownership has to pay. Starting over yet again around Herbert and continuing one of those problematic themes of his career stinks, but indeed, even the worst of projections would’ve never been bold enough to suggest the Chargers would end up like this.
