title: Vikings Report Card Week 10: Grading Every Position After Beating the Packers in Kirk Cousins's Return
full_text:
It appears the Vikings just have the Packers' number, finishing their season series at 2-0 while averaging 34.5 points per game.
Kirk Cousins made his return to Lambeau, the place where his first tenure with the Vikings ended, and simply played quarterback the way Minnesota needed QB to be played.
The defense was suffocating; the offense was watchable ; the Vikings are now 7-2 with two wins over the Pack. Here's how Cousins and the rest of the team graded out in the win.
The gaudy video game numbers weren't there, but the third-and-23 and third-and-15 conversions during the first half showed exactly why the Vikings brought in Kirk Cousins. The Minnesota offense finally looked respectable after weeks of misery, and it's in large part due to the steady play of Cousins. A midweek trade and just days to assimilate weren't enough to stop "Kirko" on Sunday.
Yeah, the Vikings probably should have made a trade for a back at the deadline . Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason were once again decent enough with 106 combined yards, but it's clear Kevin O'Connell doesn't trust his backs with the constant screens and bubbles on third-and-short. Cousins elevates the passing attack, but the run game still isn't scaring any defenses.
Funny how the offense moves when Justin Jefferson gets his touches. Cousins looked his way a season-high 13 times, and Jefferson looks very much back on track. Myles Price notched his first receiving touchdown, and the Vikings survived without their No. 2 and No. 3 receivers. Things are only looking up once the corps gets healthy.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
With no T.J. Hockenson, Gavin Bartholomew reeled in his first career touchdown on a 20-yard strike from Cousins. No other pass-catchers besides Jefferson had played with Cousins before today, so seeing the young guys get involved was certainly encouraging. Rookie TE Ben Yurosek added a reception as well.
The offensive line continued to be just good enough once again, but hasn't been a strong piece of this offense by any stretch of the imagination. Cousins was dropped three times, and even the strengths of the line—tackles Christian Darrisaw and Brian O'Neill—were each beaten badly off the edge on plays that resulted in sacks.
The Packers were utilizing six offensive linemen at one point during the game, trying anything and everything to slow down the Vikings' pass rushers. The defense notched eight sacks on Jordan Love while allowing just 56 yards on the ground, and the defensive front was at the forefront of the effort.
Caleb Banks was quiet in his first start with just two tackles, and his outlook remains undecided for now .
The Vikings were without Blake Cashman, and Ivan Pace Jr. wasn't especially productive with just a pair of tackles, but Eric Wilson and the edges stepped up in a big way. Wilson led the team in tackles, adding a sack as well, and Andrew Van Ginkel's strip in the first quarter set the tone for the entire game.
Andrew Van Ginkel just took it right from him! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qROgreyURh
Harrison Smith notched his 41st interception, and the secondary as a whole held strong against the league's leading passer. Love was held to under 230 yards for just the third time this season, and even a fluky, pinball reception to Savion Williams wasn't enough to ignite the Packers' lethal passing attack.
Will Reichard was steady as usual, but the star on special teams today was the rookie Jakobe Thomas, formerly the No. 8. Wearing his new number after gifting away the eight to Cousins, Thomas popped out the ball on a late kickoff return, setting up the Vikings' drive to ice the game.
Even the @Vikings ' special teams is forcing turnovers! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F8HXXTeFb4
Not bad for a season debut.

title: 3 Most Important Vikings Takeaways After Week 10's Statement Victory vs. Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, W.I. — Less than a week ago, the Vikings took the field on primetime TV and put up one of the most embarrassing offensive performances imaginable. The resulting loss sparked a whirlwind 24 hours that eventually led the team to reacquire their long-time quarterback , Kirk Cousins, in a trade with the Raiders.
On Sunday, Cousins retook the offensive reins after only a few days back in Purple and Gold. With Blake Cashman, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson all ruled out , “Kirko” and crew would certainly have their work cut out for them.
Would the move immediately pay off? Would Cousins’s rust in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense define the day? Would the Vikings' defense put up another stellar showing against a talented offense?
Let’s break down the most important takeaways from the Vikings 2026 Border Battle-sweeping 30-10 win on Sunday.
If you were wondering how long it would take Cousins to get comfortable, the answer was not long at all.
After a few unspectacular plays early on, Cousins found Myles Price with a precision toss for a 38-yard touchdown late in the first quarter.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
With no Addison or Hockenson and a lack of familiarity with many of his new teammates, Cousins was able to work wonders given how stacked the odds were against him. He would throw for 207 passing yards and two touchdowns (with one interception) in his first game back in Purple and Gold.
Justin Jefferson had another relatively quiet day, a fact not helped by Addison’s absence. He did manage to bring in a few key catches on a drive that ended with a Gavin Bartholomew score. Jefferson finished the day with nine catches for 74 receiving yards—better than your average WR, but not enough for what Vikings fans want from the star playmaker.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit came out swinging early.
Dallas Turner bullied Packers left tackle Jordan Morgan by throwing him into Jordan Love for an early sack; then Harrison Smith snagged his 41st career interception on the first play of the second quarter. Levi Drake Rodriguez and Eric Wilson also brought Love down on back-to-back plays early in the second.
Jalen Redmond with a sack. The Vikings have brought down Jordan Love SEVEN times. There are 8 minutes left in the third. pic.twitter.com/N1OSx9gbjk
The sack attack continued early in the third, even as Green Bay finally got on the board with a 32-yard passing TD. The Vikings’ eight sacks on the afternoon are the most by any team in the NFL this season, as they held the Packers to 10 points one week after they scored 45.
The circumstances were less than ideal for the Vikings, yet they put together their most complete team performance of the season to end a two-game losing streak. With a difficult battle against the 49ers in Mexico City on the horizon, this week will be a crucial opportunity to get healthy and continue to get the offense in sync.
If Sunday was any indication, this revamped Vikings squad can hang with anyone.

title: Vikings Can’t Ignore the Looming Jalen Redmond Decision They Should Make ASAP
full_text:
The Vikings will face many difficult decisions to make after the conclusion of the 2026 NFL season, but the decision of what to do with defensive lineman Jalen Redmond shouldn't be complicated .
Redmond is scheduled to become a restricted free agent after this year, and the Vikings shouldn't wait until the last minute to get an extension done with the third-year defender since he has made himself such a valuable part of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit.
Heading into Week 10's showdown vs. the Packers, Redmond has an 81.5 Pro Football Focus grade , which ranks him as the third-best interior defensive lineman in the NFL. Additionally, his 90.1 run defense grade makes bringing him back to Minnesota essential.
The only reason the Vikings should even consider waiting to re-sign Redmond is if Minnesota feels comfortable with the other pieces on the defensive line. At the moment, there are still enough questions about rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange to make them want to extend Redmond, who's up to 25 solo tackles, 20 pressures and 15 run stops across 416 snaps, according to PFF .
Jalen Redmond was incredible against the Bills. 5 pressures, half a sack, and his usual great run defense. He's playing at an All-Pro level this season. pic.twitter.com/7bEsuRnyDV
For Redmond, staying in a defense where he thrives would be smart, but only if he feels he is being compensated fairly. For 2026, the Purple and Gold are getting an absolute bargain , employing the 27-year-old for $1.075 million on a one-year deal.
A significant pay raise is in order, and the longer Minnesota waits to make him an offer, the more the price tag will increase. NFL salaries are skyrocketing at an alarming rate, and allowing Redmond the opportunity to hear offers from other teams that the Vikings would then have to match is a scary situation.
According to Spotrac, the Vikings are projected to have $28.4 million in cap space next offseason , along with a list of unrestricted free agents that includes:
If Redmond is allowed to test the market as a restricted free agent, a team that needs a run-stuffing defensive lineman will likely throw a lot of money his way to get his services, even if it means potentially losing a draft pick in the process.
One of the only ways Minnesota could safeguard itself from Redmond leaving is to give him a first-round tender. That would cost the Vikings $4.149 million for 2027, but teams would likely not want to part with a first-round pick to take him from Minnesota.
Redmond is young, productive and important enough to offer an extension before he becomes a restricted free agent. That would show the young defender that the Vikings appreciate what he does for the team, but it would also reward him for his play and give him stability for one more year in Purple and Gold.

title: Potential Hollywood Brown Flyer Leaves Vikings With Nothing to Lose (And Everything to Gain)
full_text:
Kirk Cousins's return will elevate the Vikings' passing game, but there's only so much the veteran quarterback can do. With Jordan Addison banged up, Jauan Jennings ruled out for Week 10 and Justin Jefferson needing more help, adding wide receiver depth when possible isn't a bad idea.
Interestingly, an opportunity to add reinforcements may have fallen in the Vikings' lap.
On Friday, the Eagles released veteran wide receiver Marquise "Hollywood" Brown . He played only four games for the NFC East team before being let go.
We have waived WR Marquise Brown and T Fred Johnson. pic.twitter.com/S4ieutMSfU
Brown wasn't used much in Philly. He played a total of 120 offensive snaps in four games for the Eagles, catching five of eight targets for 63 yards and running the ball twice for 12 yards. Considering that he had over 1,000 receiving yards in 2021 with the Ravens, it is surprising to see his contributions to a team fall so far.
Now that he is a free agent, he is free to sign with any team. While Minnesota doesn't make a lot of sense at first for the 29-year-old receiver, he might be exactly what the Vikings need to spark their passing offense.
There is little debate that the Vikings have one of the most anemic offenses in the NFL. As of Sunday morning, they are currently 31st in yards per game (266.8), 31st in passing yards per game (160.8), 27th in points per game (18.3), and 26th in yards per target (6.4).
Brown has been known for his ability to stretch the field and open up plays for underneath players. Now that Minnesota traded for Cousins , this could be an opportunity to add a deep threat to take pressure off Jefferson and Addison.
Brown would also have a friendly face upon joining the Vikings' locker room: now-backup QB Kyler Murray. The duo was on the 2022-23 Cardinals together, connecting for 62 receptions, 699 receiving yards and three touchdowns across the 13 games they shared the field during that stretch.
Since entering the league in 2019, Brown has averaged 11.7 yards per reception and 7.0 yards per target. Even while underused in Philadelphia, he turned all five receptions into first downs for the Eagles.
That is significant because the Vikings are dead last in the NFL with 14.8 first downs per game. That number is even worse over the last three games, when Minnesota averaged just 13.7 first downs per game.
Jennings has struggled to make an impact for the Vikings after signing as a free agent this offseason, catching six passes for 54 yards this season. Odell Beckham Jr. has played only two offensive snaps since coming to the team and has not been targeted once.
Unless one of those players steps up to become a contributor soon, the Vikings would be silly not to take a hard look at Brown to see if he would be a good fit for Minnesota. If he ends up being a valuable offensive piece, that would be a huge help to a 6-2 team in the most competitive division in the NFL.

title: The Vikings' Best, Worst and Most Likely Outcomes vs. the Packers in Week 10
full_text:
The Vikings won't need any extra motivation this weekend when they take on the rival Packers, but their playoff chances will take a huge swing with either outcome . A win puts the Vikings at a 92% chance to make the postseason, while a loss drags that number all the way down to 68%.
Kirk Cousins was brought in at the deadline to ensure that those odds only go up, but he'll face an ascending Packers team that just steamrolled the Patriots in Week 9.
Still, it's always interesting with Green Bay regardless of the stakes, so here are the best, worst and most likely scenarios for the game.
Cousins is essentially coming into Week 10 having to play the hero already. The Vikings offense has been listless the last few weeks, and now Cousins will be asked to play at a high level despite just a few days of practice and a speed run through the playbook. And yet, most Vikings fans fully believe he's going to pull it off. But is that hopeful ignorance, or just sheer desperation?
Maybe that answer doesn't matter, but if Cousins actually does come in on a short week and looks like 2023 Cousins, there's nothing the 2026 Vikings can't accomplish. Besides the short timeline, Cousins will also be without T.J. Hockenson, Jauan Jennings and possibly even Jordan Addison. That's really not ideal, and it may pour some cold water on the Vikings' dreams of reigniting things right off the bat.
Still, even a marginal improvement in Week 10 is something to build on, and 7-2 with two wins over the Packers is a feeling that can't be beat.
On paper, the Vikings now possess a top-2 defense and a top-15 offense with the addition of Cousins. That's a winning formula, but the games also need to be played. Cousins is playing some great football, but relying on him to completely salvage the season comes with its challenges.
If the Vikings—and specifically Cousins—come out flat against Green Bay, it's hard to see the banged-up defense saving them in this one. Minnesota will be without Blake Cashman and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, and already allowed 387 yards to Jordan Love back in Week 1
. If the injuries continue to stack up and the Vikings enter a date with San Francisco at 6-3, the season could start to spiral before the calendar turns to December.
The bar for Cousins to clear is remarkably low, so even an average game from him on Sunday will be encouraging—at least for the long term. But the Packers, much like the Lions and the Bills, will eventually find ways to score, and the Vikings' defense has begun to show some fatigue after carrying the team for nine straight weeks.
This game just feels like an ugly one, with turnovers both ways, penalties, and two teams who are already feeling desperate in a crowded NFC North. Cousins likely shows more juice than Murray or Wentz offered, but there will be growing pains. Hopefully, the defense can find ways to slow down a Green Bay offense that has averaged 36 ppg over its last two wins.

title: Caleb Banks Doubts Have the Opportunity to Be Squashed vs. Packers in Week 10
full_text:
So far this season, rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks hasn't been much of a factor for the Minnesota Vikings. That is disappointing since the team selected him with the No. 18 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Minnesota's first-round pick has played 107 defensive snaps this season, which is approximately 25 percent of the team's total defensive opportunities. He was a healthy scratch for the Vikings last week against the Bills, but that looks to change on Sunday against the Packers .
While speaking with the media on Friday, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell shared what Banks' role will be against Green Bay, saying that the young defensive lineman is going to "play a ton this week" in a post from the team on X .
The Vikings might need Banks to be on top of his game on Sunday, given the team's current injury situation. On the injury report , starting defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins has already been ruled out for Week 10 after not practicing all week due to an ankle injury.
Ingram-Dawkins being out is a big loss for Minnesota. He has started every game for the Vikings since Week 2. He is averaging 36.75 snaps played per game this season, which leaves plenty of work for Banks to get opportunities.
Minnesota's six-foot-six, 327-pound rookie is already having his place in Minnesota questioned by KSTP's Darren Wolfson, who has discussed whether Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley and the front office like him.
Based on O'Connell's statement about Banks playing in Week 10, it doesn't sound like the 23-year-old defender is in the team's doghouse. In fact, it sounds like Sunday's game will be an opportunity to measure his development since joining the team.
Through seven games, Banks' stat line is unimpressive. He has 12 tackles, including one for a loss. Since defensive linemen in a 3-4 defense play to take up space and fill gaps, statistics aren't always a great measure of effectiveness. However, his 30.5 Pro Football Focus grade this season is concerning.
There is a silver lining. The big rookie defender has three quarterback pressures this season that have resulted in three hurries, giving a glimpse of his potential as a pass rusher. He has also shown proficiency as a run stopper, being credited with seven solo tackles against the run.
Banks has an opportunity to silence critics on Sunday in a big game on the road against a division rival. Hopefully, he will rise to the occasion and show why the Vikings selected him with their first pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

title: Kirk Cousins Trade Doesn’t Change That Vikings Will Still Have QB Needs in 2027
full_text:
Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley and head coach Kevin O’Connell made the right decision earlier this week by trading a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders for Kirk Cousins, who was officially named the Week 10 starter on Friday . With a championship-level defense and an offense barreling off a cliff, something needed to change.
Thanks to the trade, the team returns to a familiar, safe face, and it’s clear the locker room and fanbase are optimistic about the potential of an all-in run for the Lombardi this season. If it works, I’m not sure many Vikings fans will care much about what comes next.
The quest for a quarterback has been a decades-long process for the Vikings, and odds are, it is nowhere near finished.
It probably isn’t shocking to anyone to say that a 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is unlikely to be the Vikings starter three to four years down the line. While making roster moves in a vacuum is typically a bad idea, this one simply had to be done. The Vikings defense has made this team a contender, and while the offense may not suddenly turn into the 2007 Patriots upon Cousins’s arrival, any bit of added consistency will help immensely.
Does this mean Teasley is kicking the QB can down the road? Not exactly. The first-year GM was asked what this move may mean for the future during his media availability on Wednesday, and he made it clear that they are still exploring all options.
LIVE: GM Nolan Teasley https://t.co/dLFPTysolV
It’s clear that Teasley understands his burden, and while Cousins may elevate the Vikings right now, there are still plenty of questions to answer for the future. The simplest path is to bring Cousins back and draft a QB for him to mentor, something he once seemed hesitant to do as he sought out a long-term deal in 2024. His current contract includes a two-year, $80 million option after this season, but the Vikings would almost certainly void it before negotiating a new contract.
Other options include soon-to-be free agent Mac Jones, whose youth and schematic fit may be appealing. Then there’s the big fish. The Vikings reportedly checked in on Justin Herbert before the trade deadline, but the Chargers quickly ended the call. I wouldn't be shocked if they call once again this offseason.
The #Vikings also inquired about Justin Herbert, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith before striking a deal with the #Raiders for Kirk Cousins, per multiple league sources. The Colts listened but did not want to move Jones, while the Jets felt Smith was too important to the team and the… https://t.co/UwF8tzZDU7 pic.twitter.com/4ghV7bd7JV
Whatever the path may be, the team is in desperate need of their quarterback hero, especially after their latest attempts have failed disastrously.
O’Connell and former Vikings GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah were tasked with finding and developing a long-term answer at the QB position when they were hired in 2022. Although the process took some time, they eventually took a swing at J.J. McCarthy with the tenth overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft just over a month after Cousins left in free agency.
With Adofo-Mensah fired, McCarthy on the Giants , and Cousins back in Minnesota after stops in Atlanta and Vegas, it’s safe to say the plan was unsuccessful after only two years.
The Vikings signed Kyler Murray to a one-year minimum deal this past offseason, hoping the 29-year-old could be their answer for years to come. After only five full games as the starter, that dream came to a harsh end. Now, the Vikings turn back to Cousins, hoping for a run to the Super Bowl while they prepare for whatever comes next.
Let’s hope that Teasley and O’Connell have a better plan this time around.

title: 3 Most Important Things Vikings Fans Must Watch for in Week 10 Road Clash vs. Packers
full_text:
There’s new hope in the Minnesota air after an embarrassing passing performance on Monday Night Football led to the reacquisition of former Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.
Now, the Vikings head into Week 10’s matchup against the Packers with a fighting chance to showcase a competent offense , something that seemed impossible just a few days ago. With playoff seeding slipping away and the back half of a brutal four-game stretch now upon them, the urgency has never been higher for Cousins and the 2026 Vikings.
Here’s what to watch for as the Vikings look to get back in the win column.
It was a late October Sunday in 2023. Cousins and the Vikings had overcome a 1-4 start and were looking to complete the climb back to .500 with a win in Green Bay. Everything was clicking, even without an injured Justin Jefferson. Then, in the third quarter, disaster struck as Cousins hobbled off the field with a torn Achilles, ending his time in purple.
Vikings @ Packers this Sunday… Scriptwriters couldn’t have planned it any better. pic.twitter.com/PxPF9pMg0a
Even if he faces a hiccup or two after being named the Week 10 starter on Friday, the alternatives seem far worse , even as Cousins reacclimates. Safe to assume, then, that he’ll be making his return to the Vikings on the exact field he last donned the horned helmet on.
It’s hard to project exactly what we’ll see after only a couple of practices, but it will likely be a massive improvement over what we’ve witnessed with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.
If Cousins and Co. can walk away with a win, his teammates may have to bust out the chains and Rolexes again on the short flight home.
Sunday will mark the 10th matchup between Kevin O’Connell and Matt LaFleur since O’Connell took over as head coach in 2022. Both have been touted as two of the best offensive minds in the NFL, even as their own fan bases often criticize their play-calling and decision-making. Ironically, most NFL teams would gladly drop their current coach for a shot at either of them.
O’Connell will look to add a seventh win to his 6-3 record against the Packers, while LaFleur will be looking to make his series record a tad more respectable. With divisional and conference seeding in the balance, Sunday’s battle of the offensive minds should provide plenty of fireworks. That is, if another elite coach doesn’t have his say …
Make no mistake: the Vikings do not defeat the Packers in Week 1 without a stellar day from Brian Flores’s defense. Their ability to create short fields and turnovers set Wentz and the Vikings' offense up for a 39-22 comeback victory. But the Green Bay offense they’ll face this Sunday won't be the same as it was two months ago.
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
The Packers' offensive line is healthier and much improved after allowing four sacks in Week 1. Their 17 sacks allowed through nine games are the 12th-fewest in the NFL this season. Their passing game is also finding its stride, with wideouts Christian Watson and Matthew Golden posting massive performances in a 45-27 victory against the Patriots last week.
Needless to say, the Vikings defense will need to bring its A-game against Jordan Love and the Packers offense on the road. Hopefully, their offense will now be able to get them some rest by sustaining a drive or two.

title: Patriots Get Horrible Update on Drake Maye's Ankle Injury
full_text:
As if the 35-10 result on the Munich scoreboard wasn't bad enough, the New England Patriots might have just seen their season slip away on the field as well.
According to NFL Network, quarterback Drake Maye — who left the game in the first quarter with an ankle injury — is believed to have suffered a significant lower leg injury that could "keep him out for an extended period of time." It's possible that the injury knocks Maye out for the remainder of the season.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Patriots fear that Maye fractured his ankle and that he's going to be out indefinitely.
Maye got sacked by Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson with just under 10 minutes to go in the opening quarter. Hutchinson got hurt celebrating the play, while Maye headed to the New England sideline and talked with head coach Mike Vrabel. After a brief discussion, he walked to the Patriots locker room with several trainers.
"Obviously wasn't able to finish the game, so we'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has," Vrabel said postgame.
After Maye went down, the Patriots offense looked like a shell of itself . Backup Tommy DeVito came in and didn't play well enough to push the ball downfield. He did lead a touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, but it was well into garbage time.
"Yeah, it was pretty quick," DeVito said about how fast everything happened with Maye's injury. "It was kind of just, looked at me, it was good, and said I was rolling, so that was kind of that."
Now the Patriots , currently sitting at 5-5, don't have a pretty outlook on the horizon. After their Week 11 bye, they'll have some really tough games on the schedule (Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos).
With a backup quarterback and no expectations for Maye to come back into the lineup, the postseason might not be in New Englnad's future this season.
On Monday morning, Vrabel spoke on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show and gave a travel update on Maye.
"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back. He'll be traveling back here shortly," Vrabel said. "But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."
Maye's injury is the worst possible news for a team that's been banged up beyond belief this year. Now, they'll have to rely on DeVito and rookie Behren Morton under center.
"My concern level anybody gets hurt is the same," running back Rhamondre Stevenson said about Maye. "I want everybody to be available, so, yeah, tough one there. Hopefully he gets healthy soon."

title: 5 Losers, 0 Winners in Patriots' International Embarrassment vs. Lions
full_text:
Even in another continent, the New England Patriots could not escape another poor performance. The team had arguably its worst performance of the season in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.
New England fell back down to a .500 record and made a few substantial additions to its grocery list of injured players.
Here are the five biggest losers, and no winners, from the Patriots' rock-bottom performance against the Lions.
A 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. That is what the Patriots had to give up to acquire Brown from the Eagles to be their top pass catcher. Since then, the 29-year-old has appeared in four games, and has played from start-to-finish just twice.
On his 26 targets this year, he has tallied just 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns. On Sunday, he totaled 27 yards on his pair of catches. However, as has been a recurring theme for Brown, he also had a drop what should have been a routine grab.
AJ Brown drop in his Week 10 return pic.twitter.com/UEZ7z4N9vO
Plus, the receiver did not finish the game due to a hamstring injury.
"Wasn't able to finish," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said when asked about Brown. "We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there."
After starting quarterback Drake Maye went down at the end of New England's first drive of the day, DeVito came in and played the remainder of the game. In that span, the Patriots put just seven points on the board.
The 28-year-old finished Sunday with just 81 yards on 24 attempts. That total marks the few yards by a Patriots single-game passing leader since former New England quarterback Mac Jones' three attempt, 19 yard performance in the snow against the Buffalo Bills on Dec. 6, 2021. Not to mention, the signal caller also had a brutal interception with a clean pocket and multiple open receivers.
Nobody at Fox noticed the Patriots WR running down the left side of the field WIDE OPEN on the DeVito interception that he threw into 3 guys. pic.twitter.com/nI6o15UDch
"Not good enough are the words I would say," DeVito said. "Offensively, just never really got going; never really was able to get into a rhythm, really get drives going. Too many three and outs and just hurting ourselves. Even the one drive that we had that resulted in a touchdown took 16 plays and there were still errors on that that happened."
At this point, "LOSER: Injuries" can be pre-penciled into this article on a weekly basis. On Sunday, the depleted Patriots squad lost Maye, Brown, edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones (cramps), linebacker Robert Spillane (illness) and cornerback Charles Woods (undisclosed).
Fortunately, New England has an extra week to get healthy . However, for the Patriots to lose their top QB, WR, LB and one of their best EDGEs, is a disastrous development for a squad which has already dealt with countless injuries.
"We'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has," Vrabel said when asked about Maye.
New England's run game was borderline non-existent against Detroit. Kiner was the team's leading rusher ...with 25 yards on his 10 attempts. Yet, somehow, his abysmal 2.5 yards per carry looks elite in comparison to Stevenson's final tally. The 28-year-old had four yards on six rushes, good for .7.
Plus, neither player helped much through the air. Kiner had no receptions, while Stevenson had just one catch which he picked up a single yard on.
"We got beat," Stevensons said. "We didn't play well enough as a unit. Really that's offense, defense, and special teams. We didn't play good enough. We have to go back and watch the film and see what we can pick."
Sunday's performance for Gonzalez can be chalked up to a less-steep stock down than the rest of the names on this list. However, after a career-worst performance last week, another poor showing from the 24-year-old is far from encouraging.
On the bright side, Gonzalez hauled in his first interception on the season. Even still, his most memorable play of the day was allowing a 56-yard catch-and-run touchdown to Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who made the Patriots defender look like he was on a Slip 'N Slide.
AMON-RA ST. BROWN 56-YARD TOUCHDOWN IN GERMANY NEvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/47fPY2mHzx
"Again, he slipped and the guy made a play," Vrabel said. "Nobody else helped him get the guy on the ground, so they're going to catch passes on everybody. It's good to see him come back and respond and challenge guys and get an interception and try to get a turnover."

title: The Good, Bad, and Ugly from Patriots' Brutal Loss to Lions
full_text:
The New England Patriots' trip to Germany didn't quite go as they had hoped, falling to the Detroit Lions, 35-10. New England drops to 5-5 heading into its Week 11 bye, with plenty to reflect on after a disappointing performance on both sides of the ball.
After orchestrating a promising opening drive, completing 3-of-4 pass attempts for 48 yards and picking up a first down with his legs, Maye was sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in the red area following a pair of New England penalties. While New England trotted out its field goal unit, Maye was seen limping toward the sideline before heading to the locker room. He was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game with an ankle injury.
This was Drake Maye's final play before leaving the game questionable with an ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/Yi1rQYpMeW
Injuries have headlined a frustrating season for the Patriots, but losing Maye proved too much to overcome. Their offense failed to consistently replicate the success of their opening drive and will await a status update on their young signal-caller heading into their bye week. "That he couldn't function," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters when asked about the decision to rule Maye out without knowing the severity of the injury. "Couldn't play, couldn't run, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level."
Coming off their worst defensive performance of the season against the Packers, a game in which they surrendered 478 yards and 45 points, the Patriots hoped to bounce back in Munich. That didn't happen. Defending an offense as talented as Detroit's was always going to be a challenge, but it wasn't even close. New England was thoroughly outmatched, allowing the Lions to move the ball at will. Detroit finished with 494 total yards of offense . Running back Jahmyr Gibbs looked unstoppable, rushing 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns, adding another 99 through the air. He led Detroit in rushing and receiving.
Another Gibbs TD, this time from 28 yard out 🔥 NEvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r3d1sVUKu5
And for wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, a dual citizen of the United States and Germany, he couldn't have asked for a better showing. Four catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. Combined, Gibbs and St. Brown accounted for 350 yards of offense, more than double the Patriots' entire offensive output of 151 yards. Over the last two weeks, New England has surrendered 80 points and 974 yards of offense. "There's a lot that we have to fix," Vrabel said. "You play good teams in this league, and you don't play well, you have no chance. And again, we know that."
AJ Brown is headed to the locker room. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/W6U11AHev3
It's been a difficult season for Brown in 2026, having appeared in just four games through 10 weeks while dealing with ankle and knee injuries. Through his first five targets, Brown had managed just one catch for 6 yards while also being flagged for a false start. His fortunes appeared to be turning when a slant route turned into a 21-yard catch-and-run, something he had consistently done so well throughout his career. However, Brown was slow to get up after the play. He made his way to the sideline, shaking his head as the Patriots medical staff prepared the blue medical tent. Brown eventually headed to the locker room with a hamstring injury and did not return for the remainder of the game. "Wasn't able to finish," Vrabel said. "We'll see what the severity of that is when we get back and kind of go from there."
Despite the poor defensive showing, the Patriots forced two turnovers, something they've struggled to do all season. After allowing a catch to St. Brown, Gonzalez was left on the wrong end of a nasty juke from the Lions wideout as he scampered for a 56-yard score. It looked like another rough outing for Gonzalez after his poor showing against Green Bay. But later in the second quarter, Gonzalez undercut an in-breaking pass from Jared Goff intended for St. Brown, recording his first interception of the season. "(St. Brown) made a play, I came back and made a play," Gonzalez said. "Obviously, we want to win; it's not about me getting an interception or someone scoring or something like that. We went out there two weeks in a row and played bad. So I mean, we just gotta get to the drawing board and be ready for two weeks." Kevin Byard added another pick with 0:12 remaining in the first half when Goff threw a pass over the middle, right into the safety's waiting hands. Goff hadn't had a multiple-interception game this season before today.
Without Maye, Tommy DeVito and the Patriots offense just couldn't get it going. DeVito struggled to manage the offense. He threw an ugly interception over the middle on a pass intended for Mack Hollins, while Kyle Williams was wide open along the left sideline. "Not good enough," DeVito said. "Offensively, just never really got going, not really was able to get into a rhythm or get drives going. Too many three-and-outs and kind of just hurting ourselves." The offense managed only 151 yards and reached the end zone all but once on a 10-yard Lan Larison reception.

title: Patriots Offense Doesn't Exist Without Drake Maye at QB
full_text:
The New England Patriots dropped their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions and lost their franchise quarterback on the way to a 35-10 defeat.
After Drake Maye brought the Patriots into the red zone on their first and most productive offensive drive all day, the third-year quarterback was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson and left the game with an ankle injury .
The 60-yard drive that Maye orchestrated was the second-longest drive the Patriots had all game. After Maye left the game, the Patriots offense was seemingly broken, putting up 91 total yards in the remainder of the game.
"I don't think Drake being in or not would have really — I mean it may have," head coach Mike Vrabel said postgame.
Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito entered the game in the first quarter for Maye, who was ruled out mid-game for the first time since sustaining a concussion his rookie year.
With DeVito at the helm, New England struggled to move the ball downfield, having nine out of 10 drives end in either a punt or a turnover. The Patriots also failed to keep the offense on the field, holding the ball for just 27 minutes and three seconds during Sunday's contest.
DeVito finished with just 81 passing yards, while Maye threw for 48 on the opening drive. The fourth-year quarterback completed half of his passes, and threw both a touchdown and an interception.
Maye's withdrawal from the game put a lackluster Patriots team on full display Sunday morning. Following his exit, it was clear that the Patriots can't succeed without their franchise player.
Maye has thrown for 2,282 yards this season , with 18 touchdowns in the air. Maye has faced criticism for his tendency to put the ball in defenders' hands as his 11 interceptions are tied for a league high.
The Patriots are nothing without Drake Maye. pic.twitter.com/m1ECGHp3T7
However, after watching DeVito attempt to operate the offense, it's obvious that the Patriots can't compete without their star quarterback, despite his turnovers.
Maye was the runner-up for MVP a year ago , and led the Patriots to their first Super Bowl appearance since 2018.
New England will return from Germany and enter the bye week, with its next game happening in Week 12 on Sunday Night Football against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.
After the game, Vrabel refused to provide specific information about his quarterback's injury, and said that the team would assess the severity of Maye's diagnosis when they return to the United States.
If Maye's ankle injury causes him to miss an extended amount of time, the 5-5 Patriots may need to look outside of the organization for a solution at quarterback — especially if they want to compete for a playoff bid.

title: Drake Maye Hurt and 6 More Instant Takeaways from Patriots' Loss to Lions in Germany
full_text:
It's hard to imagine that the New England Patriots would have had a worse game than their 45-27 loss last week. But it somehow happened.
In their second-ever game in Germany , the Patriots got thrashed — and injured even more — as the Detroit Lions boat-raced their way to a 35-10 win in Munich. Drake Maye would end up leaving the game with an ankle injury suffered in the first quarter and the Patriots offense, reeling from that, couldn't muster up anything that looked productive.
They're now losers of two in a row and will go into next week's bye sitting at .500 — and limping into what could be a really interesting stretch run these next two months.
Here's what happened, and what it means going forward.
The Patriots came out firing. Maye went 3-for-4 for 48 yards and picked up several first downs to Hunter Henry and Mack Hollins (on a flea flicker). They were driving down the field and looked poised for an opening drive touchdown.
But then pre-snap penalties — a false start on Will Campbell and a delay of game — backed them up from the three-yard line to the 13-yard line. Then Aidan Hutchinson broke through on third down to sack Maye and force the Patriots to settle for a field goal.
On the sack, Hutchinson would go down with an injury as he was celebrating. He'd be ruled out with an knee injury. But it would get much, much worse...
A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson were back in the lineup after injuries, so the Patriots' injury luck had to be turning, right? Nope. It got worse.
After Maye was sacked on the first drive, he would get looked at on the sideline . He'd slowly make his way to the locker room with what the team announced was an ankle injury. Maye would be ruled questionable to return and wouldn't end up coming back.
In his place, second-string Tommy DeVito would come in and not have much success. He'd go 12-for-23 with 81 passing yards, a touchdown, a really bad interception to Roger McCreary over the middle and a couple of hospital passes. He'd also add 19 yards with his legs.
After a game where he allowed 11 receptions to Matthew Golden and Christian Watson , the Patriots cornerback had the perfect opportunity to rebound from the worst outing of his career.
On the opening drive, covering Amon-Ra St. Brown on third down, Gonzalez got juked as the Lions wideout made one cut and took it 56 yards to the house.
He'd eventually get his get-back in the second quarter, undercutting St. Brown across the middle for his first interception of the season — one of two they got in the game.
Would that help the Patriots get some more momentum? Nope, they'd punt it away almost instantly. The Lions would tack on a touchdown on a Jahmyr Gibbs five-yard touchdown up the middle to take a 21-3 lead into halftime.
After missing the last two weeks, getting Brown back was supposed to help elevate the Patriots' passing attack. In his first three games, he combined for nine total receptions and 101 yards. Without Maye throwing him passes and the offense as a whole out of sorts, Brown wasn't able to break out of the funk.
He finished the day targeted five times and caught two passes for 27 yards. On his second target, he dropped a pass on third down that forced the Patriots to punt it away. He would also get called for a false start in the third quarter to back the Patriots up into a 3rd-and-12.
Brown also recovered a fumble after Reggie Gilliam lost control along New England's sideline. He'd also suffer a hamstring injury and leave the game in the fourth quarter.
There's a reason Gibbs is one of the league's best players. He ran the ball 22 times for 153 yards, caught seven passes for 99 yards, scored two times and was untouchable all game. His 252 total yards of offense easily outpaced the Patriots, who were only able to muster 151 net yards all game.
On the drive that ended in Gibbs' first touchdown, the Lions running back amounted for a 50-yard catch-and-run that set them up inside the Patriots' 10. Then Gibbs would punch it home from five yards out for his 12th touchdown of the season.
Maye got hurt and that will be the headliner. But the Patriots — who have started a league-high 42 different players this year — also had a lot more players get banged up in the loss. Offensive tackle Morgan Moses would leave the game for a bit with a knee injury, but would come back.
Several other Patriots had to get medical help.
It took until deep into the game, but the Patriots finally scored a touchdown. After a defensive penalty helped set the Patriots up deep into Detroit territory, DeVito connected with running back Lan Larison for a 10-yard touchdown.
That score was the first of Larison's young NFL career , and felt similar to other obscure Patriots touchdowns to happen in international games in recent years (JaMycal Hasty and K.J. Osborn both scored against Jacksonville in 2024).
The Lions weren't deterred. Gibbs struck once again, bouncing off the right side of the line and scored from 28 yards out. The lead then ballooned to 35-10, meaning the Patriots had allowed 80 points in the last two games.

title: Patriots Week 10 Inactives vs. Lions: How Will Rhamondre Stevenson Look Following Knee Injury?
full_text:
Happy spieltag, or game day! The 5-4 New England Patriots are just 90 minutes away from their second-ever game in Germany, and their first in Munich. On the other side are the 6-2 Detroit Lions, who have never played a game in the country.
Both teams are sitting in second place in their respective divisions heading into the game and are both gunning for spots in the playoffs. Something will have to give. It's a big week for the Patriots, coming off a big loss last week and needing a valuable win heading into their bye week. But injuries continue to malign them .
Here's a look at who was announced as both the Patriots and Lions inactives for Week 10:
QB Behren Morton (emergency third QB)
OG Walter Rouse (concussion protocol)
S Brenden Schooler (hamstring)
The biggest storyline is the Patriots getting both Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) back in the fold. They were questionable this week, and Brown will suit up for the first time since Week 7 in Chicago. It will be just the fourth game the wideout will play since coming over in June's trade with the Philadelphia Eagles.
Walter Rouse and Brenden Schooler were both questionable, but won't end up going. Behren Morton will only play if Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito both exit the game with injuries and offensive guard Andrew Rupcich — yesterday's practice squad elevation — will make his season debut.
Last week, Stevenson got banged up and was limited all week with a knee injury. National reports said that the running back was dealing with a knee tendon issue and might miss several weeks. Not so fast, he said!
Stevenson was listed as questionable on Friday, and after the Patriots placed TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve and declined to elevate Terrell Jennings from the practice squad, the writing was on the wall for Stevenson's active status.
How much he'll play is up in the air right now , but seeing Stevenson out on the practice field this week was inspiring for his teammates.
"I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time,” Maye said this week. "And just a guy that wants to be out there, wants to be back for his team and we’re in the midst of trying to make a make a run here and win a big one before the bye. This is a time for players, a lot of the players on this team that are trying to get out there, play with their teammates and knowing that he’s a great player and can help us out."
Prior to the game, the Patriots made several roster moves. Two of those included officially activating fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive guard Greg Van Roten off of injured reserve and onto the 53-man roster.
Getting Van Roten back in the fold is a big get for an offensive line that's continually been banged up with injuries beyond belief — especially at the interior spots. Since Van Roten got hurt in Week 3 in Jacksonville, the Patriots have had to start Matt Pryor, Ben Brown and Rouse at guard.
Brown injured his knee last game against the Green Bay Packers and Rouse was questionable all week as he worked his way through concussion protocol — which he didn't clear. Van Roten, with 106 career starts under his belt, should end up sliding in at left guard.
It was a rough showing for the Patriots defense a week ago, allowing 45 points and really letting the game get out of hand quick. They were without Charles Woods, who was downgraded pregame with a hamstring injury — something he'll play through today.
But they'll also be without Carlton Davis, who's been hit with a lot of injuries so far this season. That will elevate Woods into the CB2 role and potentially mean more playing time for rookie Karon Prunty. The Wake Forest draft pick didn't have the greatest of showings a week ago, allowing a touchdown on his first drive, but will have a chance to bounce back.
The Patriots will also need some players to step up to help defend Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions rushing attack. If the defensive tackle trio of Milton Williams, Christian Barmore and Cory Durden can help plug up the gaps, that opens up the defense for New England to get after the quarterback.

title: 3 Key Storylines to Watch in Patriots' Week 10 Matchup vs Lions
full_text:
The New England Patriots are looking to put last week's disappointing loss to the Green Bay Packers behind them as they prepare for a difficult matchup against the Detroit Lions. At 6-2, Detroit presents one of New England's toughest challenges of the season, and the Patriots will need a strong all-around effort to come away with a win in Munich, Germany. Here are three key storylines to watch heading into Sunday's matchup:
After allowing 11 catches on 12 targets for 192 yards and a touchdown in their Week 9 loss to the Green Bay Packers, Gonzalez is looking to rebound against Detroit. "When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," head coach Mike Vrabel said when asked about Gonzalez's performance. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more."
Gonzalez, who became the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history when he signed his historic 4-year, $135 million contract extension in September, understandably faces different expectations than others week in and week out. However, a bounceback is a tall order against a Lions team featuring wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, catalysts of a Detroit offense ranking eighth in passing yards per game (252 yards/game). And with veteran cornerback Carlton Davis ruled out with a knee injury, more responsibility lands on Gonzalez's plate. "As confident as I always am," Gonzalez said. "It's a week-to-week league, like I've told y'all all week, it's a new week. It's the same confidence that I always have, the same confidence I'll always go in with."
On Saturday, the Patriots activated both offensive guard Greg Van Roten and Fullback Reggie Gilliam from injured reserve to the 53-man roster. Van Roten (thigh) was placed on IR after their Week 3 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and Gilliam (knee, ankle) has been on IR since Week 4 after suffering an injury against his former team, the Buffalo Bills. Their returns should provide some much-needed depth and starting-level play to an offense that has struggled to stay healthy. Van Roten and Gilliam aren't the only Patriots who could be nearing a return, either. New England is also monitoring several other key players, including wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson. Brown has missed the Patriots' back-to-back games and six of their first nine contests this season while dealing with ankle and knee injuries. After the Patriots sent 2028 first- and fifth-round picks to acquire him in June, Brown has recorded just nine catches for 101 yards since arriving in New England. He traveled with the team to Munich and is listed as questionable. His potential return and integration into the offense would be a shot in the arm for a receiving corps marred by injuries.
From Friday: WR A.J. Brown (1) warms up at practice. Seemed comfortable. Fellow WR Pop Douglas shared how nice it has been to have Brown back, saying he is their leader. Mike Vrabel said the plan was to talk with head athletic trainer Jim Whalen, and Brown, and then set a plan. pic.twitter.com/RIrem3QRKR
Stevenson, meanwhile, exited Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. ESPN's Adam Schefter later reported that the running back was dealing with a knee tendon issue that could sideline him for a short period of time. Despite this, Stevenson missed Wednesday's practice, then returned as a limited participant Thursday and Friday. His status is also questionable. "The more that we can get everyone back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team," Vrabel told the media. "One guy certainly doesn't make the difference, but it's certainly the more that we can get guys back, It's exciting that, you know, the pieces can start to build and come together."
One thing these two teams have in common is their lack of takeaways this season, with both recording just eight forced turnovers (tied for 25th in the NFL). However, New England gives the ball away at a much higher rate, as their 19 giveaways tie them for last in turnover differential (-11). "We got a tough challenge looking ahead of us, but certainly can't win playing that way, turning the ball over, not creating turnovers defensively, and giving up X plays," Vrabel said after their Week 9 loss. And while the Patriots certainly are hoping their fortunes change in Germany, forcing a turnover against the Lions is no easy feat. Quarterback Jared Goff has only thrown two interceptions through eight games, and as a unit, the Lions have only given up the ball five times. In a matchup between two teams that have struggled to create takeaways, New England will need to find a way to win the turnover battle. Against an offense as efficient as Detroit's, even one extra possession could prove to be the difference.

title: 5 Players to Watch in Patriots vs. Lions Matchup in Germany
full_text:
The New England Patriots' matchup against the Detroit Lions early on Sunday morning may turn out to be one of the most important of the season.
New England currently stands in the playoff picture, but a slurry of losses against its tough remaining schedule could complicate things.
But until then, here are five players to keep an eye on this Sunday when New England and Detroit take a trip to the game field in Munich.
Last week against the Green Bay Packers, Gonzalez had the worst performance of his career. The 24-year-old allowed 11 receptions for 192 yards to Green Bay receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson alone.
This week, the challenge does not get any easier. Lions pass catcher Amon-Ra St. Brown sits fifth in the league in receptions (61) and 11th in receiving yards (657).
"When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said last Sunday when asked about Gonzalez. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else."
New England has a tall task ahead in trying to slow down Detroit running back Jahmyrr Gibbs. The 24-year-old sits top-3 in the NFL in rush yards (847) and rush touchdowns (nine). Who better to apply the brakes than Elliss?
The 27-year-old leads New England's defense with 65 tackles. Plus, he sits second on the team in tackles for a loss with 5.5. If Elliss plays at his best tomorrow, the Patriots could have a chance at victory.
As is the case with a substantial chunk of the Patriots' roster, their running back room has plenty of uncertainty around it due to injuries. Starter Rhamondre Stevenson is questionable for Sunday due to a knee injury which was reportedly expected to hold him out for multiple weeks. Plus, top backup TreVeyon Henderson was placed on injured reserve on Saturday.
With New England not opting to make a gameday practice squad elevation at the position, that could point toward Stevenson being good to go against Detroit. However, with the likelihood of him not being at full health, I still expect Kiner to have a substantial role against the Lions.
"I think Corey is working extremely hard,"  Vrabel said on Monday. "I think Corey has done a really nice job. But there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on, ust like a lot of guys, as far as recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure that we saw (last Sunday), for example."
Against a well-rounded Lions offense, the Patriots may need to rely on their well-rounded edge rusher. Ponder leads New England with 7.5 sacks and 9.5 tackles for a loss this season.
He's also been a turnover machine this season. The 24-year-old accounted for one of the Patriots' six forced fumbles this year, while also leading New England's defense in fumble recoveries with two.
Against a top-tier pass and rush attack on the other side, the Patriots may need Ponder to bump the Lions offense backwards a few times on Sunday.
The Patriots' left guard spot has been on a rollercoaster in recent weeks. Walter Rouse had taken over the gig until he was benched midway through New England's matchup against the Miami Dolphins. That's when Ben Brown took over, who then started against the Green Bay Packers.
However, he suffered an injury against Green Bay which will force him to miss this week's battle against Detroit. Fortunately for New England, Greg Van Roten was activated off injured reserve on Saturday and could step into the starting role over Rouse.
Regardless, whoever gets the starting nod will have a tough challenge ahead. The Lions have tallied the third-most sacks in the NFL with 27. Expect them to bring the heat against the Patriots' depleted offensive line.

title: What TreVeyon Henderson's Move to IR Actually Means for Patriots
full_text:
The New England Patriots announced a slew of roster moves ahead of their Week 10 game in Germany, one of which included placing running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve.
The second-year player, who's officially listed on the injury report with an illness, has dealt with a neurological issue that's kept him off the field (and in the hospital).
"I talk to TreVeyon every day, and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back," Mike Vrabel said this week when asked if there was a status update on Henderson's health. "And when that is, I don’t know. I don’t have a timetable. So, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how it’s going."
Henderson opened the year as one of the team's most electric players on the offensive side of the ball. Now, he'll be forced to the sideline for a larger chunk of time as the Patriots look to right the ship heading into the stretch run.
Here's what placing Henderson on IR will mean for the Patriots, both in the immediate short term and moving forward in 2026 as a whole.
Henderson's speed and skills are some of the best on the Patriots. His ability to evade tacklers and outrun anyone was on display all last year as a rookie. But he hasn't looked the same this year. An ankle injury in a practice leading into Week 1 forced him to miss the opener, and he suffered another ankle injury later in the year as well .
The Patriots have Rhamondre Stevenson, who'll continue to carry the load out of the backfield. But his elusiveness and breakaway speed don't line up to Henderson's. The Ohio State alum also had the capabilities to catch passes out of the backfield, though that wasn't a major part of his game when healthy this year.
Overall, Henderson is one of New England's best young players. Without him for a playoff push, the offense will have to adapt when it comes to using their running backs in a variety of ways.
Henderson has missed the last two games with the illness and was already ruled out for this week's game against the Detroit Lions. He, along with Ben Brown and Carlton Davis, didn't take the trip to Munich for the game. Being placed on IR means he'll also have to miss more than just this week.
Considering the Patriots' bye week looms right on the horizon, Henderson will remain out of football activities for Week 10 vs. the Lions, the Week 11 bye, Week 12 vs. the Los Angeles Chargers, Week 13 vs. the Buffalo Bills and Week 14 vs. the Minnesota Vikings. The earliest he could return is for Week 15 against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Patriots have used five of their eight IR return to play designations to this point in the year, and with Romeo Doubs, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Dell Pettus all working their way back, that could also mean that Henderson's sophomore year in the NFL may already be over. They'll get two additional designations if they make the postseason.
Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are the three running backs on the Patriots active roster heading into Week 10. Terrell Jennings remains on the practice squad as the top backup option.
With Henderson out of the picture for more than a month, it's going to put some stress on that trio — especially Stevenson, who's questionable for Sunday's game with a knee injury. Considering he returned to practice in a limited capacity and the Patriots didn't elevate Jennings for the game, that is a good sign for Stevenson's health moving forward.
But Kiner and Larison, two players who have added value on special teams, will have to be larger factors on the offensive side of the ball. Kiner scored his first-career NFL touchdown in Week 9 against the Packers (in garbage time, albeit), but has shown he can carry the ball consistently. Larison hasn't gotten a large role yet, but may be called upon more in the wake of Henderson's IR placement.

title: Saints Find Another Way to Lose as Panthers Steal NFC South Victory
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had chance after chance to build momentum and secure their first consecutive wins of the season. Instead, it was another game that left a sour taste in everyone’s mouths like tomatoes in gumbo.
Kicker Ryan Fitzgerald connected on a game-winning 54-yard field goal as time expired, lifting the Carolina Panthers to a 20-17 victory over the Saints on Sunday afternoon at the Caesars Superdome.
The loss dropped New Orleans to 3-6 under second-year head coach Kellen Moore , while Carolina improved to 4-5 and strengthened its position in the NFC South standings.
Despite overcoming a sluggish first half and taking a fourth-quarter lead, the Saints couldn't finish the job, and Carolina escaped with a crucial divisional win.
Tyler Shough went 25-for-36 for 187 yards, with a touchdown and an interception, while rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson had a breakout game, leading New Orleans with 11 receptions for 80 yards.
Running back Alvin Kamara provided the Saints' biggest offensive spark, scoring twice in the second half on a 3-yard touchdown run in the third quarter and a 4-yard touchdown catch in the fourth.
However, New Orleans struggled offensively throughout the opening two quarters, committing two turnovers and failing to score before halftime.
Shough's first interception came on the Saints' opening possession when cornerback Marco Wilson deflected his fourth-down pass intended for Chris Olave , and linebacker Devin Lloyd intercepted it.
The Saints' defense kept Carolina from capitalizing, with Carl Granderson sacking Bryce Young on fourth down near the goal line.
Another costly mistake came in the second quarter when Shough and Audric Estime mishandled a handoff, allowing Panthers linebacker Jaelan Phillips to recover the fumble.
Carolina capitalized on the turnover with a 2-yard touchdown run by Chuba Hubbard , taking a 7-0 lead into halftime.
New Orleans finally found some traction in the third quarter.
Kamara capped a nine-play, 64-yard drive with a 3-yard touchdown run, tying the game at 7-7 with 6:33 remaining in the period.
However, Fitzgerald answered with a 55-yard field goal to restore Carolina's three-point advantage entering the fourth quarter.
The Saints responded with their best offensive sequence of the afternoon.
Shough connected with Kamara on a 4-yard touchdown pass, giving New Orleans its first lead at 14-10.
That advantage proved short-lived.
Hubbard scored his second touchdown on a 1-yard run, putting Carolina back ahead 17-14 late in the fourth quarter.
New Orleans refused to go away, with kicker Charlie Smyth drilling a clutch 55-yard field goal to tie the game at 17-17.
But Young and the Panthers orchestrated one final scoring opportunity, setting up Fitzgerald's game-winning kick as time expired.
Young finished with 200 passing yards, while Hubbard rushed for 92 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries.
For the Saints, the defeat represents another frustrating setback in a season defined by inconsistency, offensive mistakes and an inability to capitalize on opportunities.
The Saints will now prepare for a road trip to the Buckeye State to take on the Cincinnati Bengals .

title: Saints vs. Panthers Predictions: Will New Orleans Win Its Second Straight Game?

The New Orleans Saints (3-5) return to the Caesars Superdome on Sunday looking to build momentum following last week's victory over Cleveland as they host the Carolina Panthers (3-5) in a crucial NFC South showdown.
With both teams looking to turn their seasons around, the Saints will need another strong performance from quarterback Tyler Shough and their defense to secure consecutive victories for the first time this season.
Here are our Saints ON SI staff predictions for Sunday's matchup between New Orleans and Carolina.
I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints.
While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season.
On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns).
The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key.
Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility.
However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude.
Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease.
Prediction: Panthers 21, Saints 14
I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places.
On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all.
Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much.
Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line.
Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column.
Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the New York Giants .

title: Saints Activate Travis Etienne Jr. From Injured Reserve Ahead of Panthers Game
full_text:
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. will be activated from injured reserve for the New Orleans Saints ' Sunday game against the Carolina Panthers , according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer.
The 3-5 teams face off for sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Etienne has not played since Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sept. 27, when he suffered a hamstring injury.
Upon returning to practice this week, Etienne fully participated by Friday and was listed as questionable.
In New Orleans, Etienne is expected to share backfield responsibilities with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara . Estime posted a team season-high 72 rushing yards last week against the Cleveland Browns , while Kamara has recorded 157 yards with a 3.3-yard average through seven games.

The 27-year-old running back joined New Orleans during free agency on a three-year contract after four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars , who selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Etienne topped 1,000 rushing yards in three of his four years with Jacksonville. A Louisiana native out of Jennings High School, he played at Clemson, earning All-America honors three times and twice winning ACC Offensive Player of the Year.
In additional roster adjustments, New Orleans placed defensive lineman Christen Miller on Injured Reserve. The team also promoted tackle Easton Kilty from the practice squad to the active roster and elevated kicker Charlie Smyth for Sunday's matchup with the Carolina Panthers.

The Irish kicker provided all nine of the Saints' points through three quarters in a low-scoring battle against Cleveland, going 3-for-4 on field goals with conversions from 30, 27, and 48 yards.

title: Saints Stock Up: Audric Estimé Makes a Statement, Pass Rush Keeps Rolling
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints gave their home crowd reason to celebrate on Sunday at Caesars Superdome, clinching a thrilling 23-22 victory in overtime over the Cleveland Browns .
While improving the Saints to 3-5 and snapping a home slump, the win was far from flawless.
The result grants head coach Kellen Moore a brief reprieve, but ongoing flaws demonstrate that his standing stays uncertain.
With a tough slate ahead, New Orleans needs to fix key errors to sustain progress.
Below are the Saints players and units whose stock rose after Sunday's thrilling finish.
Despite rejoining the Saints via waivers after getting cut after training camp, running back Audric Estimé made a compelling argument for an expanded role in New Orleans' backfield despite being back in New Orleans for a week.
The second-year running back rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per attempt.
His biggest contribution came late in regulation when he powered into the end zone from 2 yards out to give New Orleans a 16-13 advantage.
Beyond the touchdown, Estimé provided the physicality and downhill running that the Saints have struggled to establish consistently.
Charlie Smyth made the most of his opportunity after he became the starter after the Saints released Daniel Carlson .
The Irish-born kicker connected on three of his four field-goal attempts against Cleveland, converting from 30, 27 and 48 yards.
With both offenses struggling to finish drives, Smyth accounted for all nine of New Orleans' points through the first three quarters.
His 48-yard field goal in the fourth quarter briefly gave the Saints a 9-6 advantage.
The Saints' pass rush continues to emerge as one of the team's biggest strengths, with Carl Granderson and Chase Young leading a pass rush that made life miserable for Cleveland quarterback Shedeur Sanders .
Granderson recorded two sacks against the Browns, extending his streak of games with multiple sacks to four. According to the Saints, he became the first NFL player since 2013 to accomplish that feat.
Young added his eighth sack of the season, while Kaden Elliss and Khristian Boyd also got into the action as New Orleans finished with five sacks.
The Saints' defensive front also made its presence felt against the run, limiting Cleveland to 95 rushing yards while consistently disrupting the Browns' offensive rhythm.
Perhaps the unit's most impressive moment came near the goal line, when New Orleans delivered a critical fourth-down stand to keep Cleveland out of the end zone.
Although the Saints' secondary remains vulnerable to explosive plays, the defensive front has become a reliable source of pressure and physicality.

title: Former Scout Weighs In on Vikings’ Trade of J.J. McCarthy to Giants
full_text:
By all accounts, the New York Giants are very happy to have acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings, and McCarthy seems eager to use a fresh start to show the NFL world he’s not the draft bust that seemed to be taking shape in Minnesota.
But not only was McCarthy’s road to respectability difficult due to various factors, such as his season-ending knee injury in his rookie campaign and struggles running the offense that saw him sink to the bottom of the position’s depth chart, but former scout John Middlekauff also offered a rather shocking opinion on the relationship between McCarthy and Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell.
“If you’re a Vikings fan watching (the Giants-Commanders) game tonight, you have to be asking yourself—and I’m not trying to play Monday morning quarterback, it’s just a reality—the move was made because he didn’t play well and the coach hated him,” Middlekauff opined during a segment on the 3 and Out podcast last Friday.
Middlekauff didn’t stop there, continuing his criticism of O’Connell, whom he also acknowledged “by all accounts is a nice guy,” and pointing to McCarthy’s success in New York as an indication that maybe the Vikings thought the quarterback was better than he was.
“I wanted to speak for you regarding J.J. McCarthy; you hated his guts as a player,” Middlekauff alleged. “You couldn’t (expletive) stand him because you were clearly the driving force for making him the third quarterback and helping the GM: ‘We gotta get this guy out of here. Fifth-round pick, I’ll drive him to the airport.’
“Then a couple of weeks later, when you’re starting Carson Wentz, who couldn’t hit water from the middle of the ocean, and then J.J.’s making plays like that for (Matt) Nagy and Greg Roman, you’re like, ‘No one is acting like this guy is Joe Montana, but this is way better than what we had.’”
McCarthy led the Vikings to a 6-4 record as a starter and currently has a 2-1 record as a starter for the Giants. In just two NFL seasons, the former University of Michigan signal-caller has a 59.4% career completion rate and has thrown for 2,547 yards, 13 touchdowns, and 16 interceptions, with a 41.7% overall success rate.
Thus far with the Giants, McCarthy, in five games played (three starts), has a 63.5% completion rate and has thrown for 915 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions, with a 43% success rate, and head coach John Harbaugh’s confidence in McCarthy is growing by the day.
“I think he’s proven that he’s capable of winning games and making the plays, and I probably feel more strongly about that now than ever,” Harbaugh said last week after the Giants’ loss to the Washington Commanders.
“It was his third game; I think maybe now starting. So we’re definitely in the process of building that confidence. … I’m excited about where he’s going, going forward, and our chance to close out some games.”
