title: Giants Incentives Check-In: Which Players Are on Pace to Earn Bonuses?
full_text:
One of the New York Giants ’ new approaches this past offseason was adding a slew of “not likely to be earned” (NLTBE) incentives to player contracts.
NLTBEs can benefit a team’s cap because, if the player reaches them, the charge doesn’t hit until the following year’s cap. An NLTBE incentive differs from a “likely to be earned” (LTBE) incentive because it’s based on what the player achieved in that statistical category the year prior.
For example, if a contract promises $1 million based on a player achieving 50 receptions in a season and that player achieved 55 receptions the prior season, the incentive is classified as an LTBE because the player has already reached that mark recently.
As an LTBE, the bonus counts against the current year’s salary cap; if the player doesn’t earn the incentive, the team gets a credit toward the following year’s cap space.
But if that same $1 million promise is based on 50 receptions and the player, in the prior season, had only 40 receptions, it becomes an NLTBE because the player didn’t reach the milestone the year prior. And if an NLTBE incentive isn’t earned, it doesn’t count against the following year’s cap.
The Giants offered players $28.3 million in NLTBE incentives. With 10 weeks of the NFL season in the books, thus far the team owes the players involved $2.25 million or roughly 8% of that total.
Who is set to cash in and who isn't? Here is the rundown with data provided via Spotrac .
Newsome, who recently signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension with $36 million guaranteed, originally had a chance to earn up to $2 million in incentives if he hit playing-time metrics.
Thus far, Newsome has played in 80.2% of the team’s defensive snaps, so he’s currently on pace to earn $1 million of the $2 million originally promised to him.
If he finishes having played in 90% or more of the team’s snaps, he’ll earn an additional $1 million in incentives for a maxed-out total of $2 million.
Winston is currently on pace to earn $500,000 of the $2 million max attached to a playing-time incentive. The quarterback has participated in 59.8% of the team’s offensive snaps.
He’s 0.2% away from hitting the next payout in that metric (60% playing time), which, if he hits it, will pay out another $250,000, boosting Winston’s incentives to $750,000.
Reader has two incentives in his deal, one for playing time and one for sacks. He has already picked up $250,000 of the max $750,000 for playing time, having taken part in 56.8% of the team’s defensive snaps (the minimum criterion was 53% of the snaps).
He also needs two more sacks to reach three, which would trigger a $500,000 incentive payout.
Likely, who is having a breakout year this season, is on pace to hit a number of his contract incentives.
He has already picked up $250,000 for hitting seven receiving touchdowns, which crossed the first criterion of a minimum of six. If he records one more touchdown, that total will double to $500,000. And if he hits 10 receiving touchdowns, he’ll max out at $750,000 in that metric.
He has likely also met half of a playing-time/playoff incentive. He needs to participate in at least 60% of the offensive snaps, and the team needs to make the postseason for him to get an additional $150,000.
Likely has already met the first part of that criterion, having played in 75.4% of the snaps. He needs the Giants to win the division, which will secure a postseason spot and trigger that incentive payout.
There are two more incentives that Likely is on pace to reach. The first is receptions. Likely needs five more receptions to hit 60, which would then trigger a $250,000 payout. He can max out at $750,000 if he hits 80 receptions.
The other incentive is receiving yards. He can max out at $750,000 if he reaches 850 receiving yards. Currently, he has 575 and is just 75 yards away from hitting the first benchmark, which would pay him $250,000 if he hits 650 receiving yards.
Pancake Pat has a playing-time incentive in his deal, and he has already hit the first benchmark: playing in 30% of the team’s offensive snaps.
Ricard, having played in 36.4% of the snaps so far, has hit $250,000 in incentives. If he finishes with 40% of the team’s offensive snaps, he can max out at $450,000 in that incentive.
McFadden has up to $2 million in playing-time incentives, and he’s well on his way to hitting the first benchmark: $250,000 if he plays in 35% of the defensive snaps.
McFadden has stepped in for the injured Tremaine Edmunds, and he rarely comes off the field. He’ll earn an additional $250,000 if he plays in 40% of the defensive snaps and then $375,000 per tier for hitting the following playing-time benchmarks: 50%, 60%, 70% and 75%.
The following Giants are unlikely to earn their contract incentives.
Thomas can earn up to $500,000 for a Pro Bowl and first-team All-Pro nod. Unfortunately, thanks to a groin injury, he’s not having a promising season and is unlikely to earn either of those honors.
Burns had an opportunity to earn up to $1.8 million if he reached 12.5 sacks, earned first-team All-Pro honors, or made the Pro Bowl. Unfortunately, a season-ending knee injury suffered in Week 3 ended those hopes for this season.
Austin had three incentives (receiving yards, receptions and playing time), each paying out $1 million apiece. Unfortunately, he never made it to the regular season after tearing his ACL in training camp.
Golston stood to earn up to $500,000 if he reached 10 sacks. His first level, though, was six sacks, which would have brought him $125,000 had he reached it. Unfortunately, Golston is on season-ending injured reserve with a neck ailment.
Mooney has $7 million in incentives at stake between playing time, receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns.
Currently, he’s not close to hitting any of those incentives, which include $250,000 for playing time, a minimum of $375,000 for 35 receptions (max is $2.5 million for 75 catches), a minimum of $375,000 for at least 450 receiving yards (he has 175 at the moment) and a max of $2.5 million if he tops 900 receiving yards, and a max of $1.75 million for nine receiving touchdowns (he can earn $375,000 for three touchdowns).
Singletary needs to hit at least 56% of the offensive snaps to earn a $250,000 payout (he’s currently at 27.3%). With Cam Skattebo as RB1, Singletary is facing an uphill battle there. He’s also facing an uphill battle to hit the minimum 1,100 scrimmage yards needed for a $125,000 payout.
Holland has been playing lights out for the Giants this year, and if he finishes strong enough to earn both Pro Bowl and first-team All-Pro honors, he’s looking at up to $500,000.
Adebo can earn $500,000 each if he makes the Pro Bowl and earns first-team All-Pro honors. Given that he’s not only lost his starting job but also been a healthy scratch a few times this year, he’s clearly not reaching that incentive.
Robertson-Harris suffered a ruptured Achilles in the spring, so he obviously has zero chance to earn up to $250,000 in playing-time incentives this year.
Barnes is a mainstay on special teams, where he has performed well this season. Unfortunately, that won’t help him earn the $400,000 incentive in his contract, which he would earn for playing 45% of the defensive snaps.

title: Harbaugh Preaches Resiliency as Giants Chase First Playoff Berth Since 2022
full_text:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh knows who is on the schedule in the coming weeks. And while the focus is on winning one game at a time, Harbaugh emphasizes a recurring theme with his players.
“You’ve watched us play. People have watched us play. You know where we are. We’re going to do everything we can do to try to win the game. Our guys are going to fight like crazy. They’re going to compete, and we’re capable of making plays,” he said.
The NFC East-leading Giants don’t always make things easy on themselves, which is probably why they still have their fair share of doubters. Currently slotted as the third seed in the NFC postseason race, the Giants have a 50% chance of making the postseason for the first time since 2022.
But Harbaugh, unfazed, believes his first Giants team has as good a chance as any team to make some noise, and he’s not quaking in his boots about the tough opponent Big Blue faces next weekend when it hosts the Jacksonville Jaguars.
“It’s pretty obvious that we can make plays on both sides of the ball. We’re chasing consistency, just like every single team in this league is chasing consistency,” he said.
“The so-called heavyweights, I’ve seen them play bad games too. I’ve seen them have plenty of bad plays. There’s no perfect team in this league. Is that pretty obvious to everybody? This is a tough league. It’s pretty even. We’re in it just like everybody else. We’ll be fighting there just like everybody else.”

title: Why Giants Fans Should Be Rooting for the 49ers on Sunday
full_text:
Whether you’re enjoying a rare autumn Sunday without New York Giants football or you’re tuned into the slate of games, if there is one game Big Blue’s faithful might want to keep tabs on, it’s the San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys clash.
If the Cowboys (4-5) pull off the upset over the 49ers (7-1), that moves Dallas to 5-5, with a game the following week against the Tennessee Titans, who were 1-7 at the start of Sunday’s 10 games.
The 5-3-1 Giants, who lost to the Washington Commanders 24-21 on Thursday night, host the Jacksonville Jaguars, 6-2, at the start of Sunday’s slate.
New York, however, does hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over Dallas thanks to the teams’ Week 1 game. Still, the circumstances can quickly change who is at the top of the NFC East if the Cowboys upset the 49ers.
However, if the Cowboys lose this week, they fall to 4-6, and the Giants, who have the head-to-head tiebreaker, will gain more cushion in their division lead, which should carry them into early December.
The Giants, per Tankathon, have the seventh-most difficult remaining schedule, with their upcoming opponents holding a combined .543 winning percentage.
Dallas, meanwhile, has the 14th-most difficult remaining schedule, with its upcoming opponents holding a combined .507 winning percentage at the start of Week 10’s games.
The Cowboys and 49ers kick off their game at 4:25 p.m. ET.

title: Giants Face Stretch of Tough Opponents, but Harbaugh Says Expectation Stays the Same
full_text:
The good news for the New York Giants is that they still lead the NFC East with a 5-3-1 record. Their wins have come against teams that, except for the Los Angeles Rams, all had losing records heading into their Week 10 games.
The bad news is that things are about to get real for the Giants, schedule-wise. New York is set to face teams with winning records in five of its next six games: Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland and Detroit (with a Week 12 game against the struggling Colts sandwiched in there).
Four of those five opponents, except Cleveland, rank in the top 10 league-wide in point differential. Jacksonville is the runaway leader at +108 heading into Sunday’s Week 10 games.
The Giants aspire to win the NFC East despite their 24-21 loss to Washington on Thursday night. If they also hope to hang around in the postseason once they get there, the quality of opponents they’re about to face over the next few weeks will make for a good litmus test of what this group is really made of for head coach John Harbaugh and company.
Harbaugh said his confidence is high in every opponent they face and in their chances of winning, noting that the expectation is to win every single game.
“Every game that we go into play, we’re taking the field planning to win,” he said. “We’ll be preparing that way, and that’s what we’ll be doing. We’re going to win as many of them as we can. If we win them all, we win them all, but we’ll win as many as we can.”
And lest anyone think the pressure to win against the tougher opponents is any higher for the Giants at 5-3-1 than it would be if they were 6-2-1, it is not.
“We don’t live in that scared world. I said it was an important game before the game for that very reason. But now you don’t sit back and go, ‘Oh no, we’ve got to beat a heavyweight or whatever you want to call it,’” he said.
“It’s the National Football League. We’re planning on going out there, playing, and winning the game. So we don’t look at it from that perspective.”
In other words, it doesn’t matter what record the opponent brings to the table when it comes up on the Giants’ schedule. The stats don’t matter either.
“These guys are going to go play the game. They’re not going to go into the game saying, ‘Oh man, this is going to be a tough one for us to win,’” Harbaugh said.
“They’re all tough to win. Every single one of these games is going to be a big challenge. Every single one of these games is going to be really hard to win. It’s tough to win football games in this league. I think we all understand that, don’t we?
“So we’re going to be fighting in every single one of those games to win every single one of those games when they come up, starting with the Jacksonville game. That will be our focus. We’re going to expect to win the game.”

title: Giants’ Sneak Over Tush Push Call Remains a Head-Scratcher
full_text:
Most New York Giants fans agree that the team’s decision to run a quarterback sneak on a 3rd-and-1 rather than a classic tush push in its 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders was a head-scratcher.
And apparently, if the stats are to be believed, the questions are justified. According to TushPush.fyi , the Giants have run three tush push plays this season, all of which were successful.
What about quarterback sneaks? Per PFF’s advanced data , quarterback Jameis Winston ranks fourth among quarterbacks with 11 sneaks, and his eight first downs on sneaks also rank fourth in the league.
Given the success of the tush push, then, why not go for that play on 3rd-and-short rather than a sneak?
There are a couple of potential reasons. The first, as head coach John Harbaugh noted to the media on Friday, is that the offensive line did a much better job run-blocking against a banged-up Washington defensive front.
While Harbaugh didn’t say much, perhaps offensive coordinator Matt Nagy felt more confident calling for a sneak than a tush push, given how the offensive line was blocking.
Statistically, the Giants averaged 4.3 yards per rush attempt against Washington, with two rushing touchdowns in the loss. Against the Eagles, they struggled to run the ball, averaging 2.6 yards per carry without Cam Skattebo, who was inactive.
In addition, against the Eagles, the Giants had eight rushing attempts that went for zero or negative yards. Against Washington, they had only two such unsuccessful attempts.
Along those lines, the Giants averaged 4.16 yards per attempt on rushes between the tackles in the loss to Washington. In contrast, against Philadelphia, they averaged 2.2 yards per attempt between the tackles.
All that being said, the question of how they decide between a sneak and a tush push is the one Harbaugh sidestepped when it was put to him on Friday.
“We have four or five of those different types of calls and motions and pushes—not pushes, check-with-me plays. There are different things that we have. One of those was called,” he said.
“We have different calls that go with quarterback sneaks, so we didn’t call the same one that we’ve been calling. That’s really the only answer I have for you.”
The other unanswered question is whether Winston checked out of a play. Asked about the 3rd-and-1 on which Skattebo stayed in the backfield for almost two seconds, Harbaugh clarified that the play “was a normal quarterback sneak and a certain check involved in it that is part of the play.”
The bottom line is that the play, regardless of what was called versus what was executed, failed to convert. It could be one that Nagy wishes he had back, and he will almost certainly be asked about it the next time the coordinators speak with the media on Thursday.
That play itself isn’t why the Giants lost, but it added to a night of frustration for fans who were expecting a Big Blue win in a critical divisional game.

title: The Inches That Are Affecting Giants’ Rookie Kicker Dominic Zvada's FGAs
full_text:
The New York Giants head coach is not ready to give up on rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada despite the former Michigan kicker’s inconsistencies over the last few weeks, which have seen him go 8-for-14 after making his first nine field-goal attempts.
Zvada’s recent woes have come from the right hash, including his lone 33-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide left in the Giants’ 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night. That 33-yard miss was his first under 40 yards this season.
“There’s a technique issue there with his plant foot that we’re kind of looking at,” head coach John Harbaugh said on Friday. “And he needs to clean that up from a consistency standpoint. He knows that. Popped up again in that one kick there. I had a chance to watch it this morning. There is an issue on the right hash, no question.”
Harbaugh didn’t go into detail on what the issue is with Zvada’s plant foot, but according to retired Giants kicker Lawrence Tynes, the issue may be that Zvada’s plant foot is too deep and close to the ball.
Tynes, in a social media post on Oct. 14 referencing one of the rookie’s misses from the right hash, said Zvada’s plant foot is “too deep and close to the ball.”
He added, “Out in front and close to the ball can cause you to hook or push it.”
One on left is a make. Ankle in plant leg is lined up with the ball. This is good. One on the right is a miss. Plant foot is too deep and close to the ball. Out in front and close to the ball can cause you to hook or push it. Not good. Can be caused by trying to go too hard… pic.twitter.com/q6diGyURZL
Tynes further explained that Zvada’s issue in front of the ball can be caused by trying to go too hard at the ball to create power on longer kicks. “You get too deep and close with the plant. We are talking about inches here.”
Assistant head coach and special teams coordinator Chris Horton told reporters last month, after Zvada’s struggles on Washington’s wet grass field, that the playing surface can also affect a young kicker’s effectiveness.
“Footing is definitely a lot different,” he said. “Obviously, the turf, your plant foot sticks a little bit; it sticks a little bit better. When you’re on grass and things like that, your foot might slide a little bit more.”
Tynes, who called himself “a huge fan” of Zvada’s, endorses the patient approach Harbaugh and the Giants are taking, despite any frustration over the lost points.
“He is an elite talent learning how to become a consistent NFL kicker,” Tynes told New York Giants On SI .
“His leg talent does not grow on trees. He has more talent in his pinky toe than I ever had. Patience is required.”

title: Giants 2027 NFL Draft Watch: Four College Prospects to Track This Weekend
full_text:
As the New York Giants (5-3-1) absorb their 24-21 Week 10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football at MetLife Stadium, several Big Blue scouts will be watching closely. College football’s Week 11 slate is about to unfold.
While several potential targets make their case for being selected in the 2027 NFL Draft, the team’s biggest needs are becoming clearer.
In addition to their most pressing need at defensive tackle, coach John Harbaugh and his staff may also want to add players who can bolster their depth charts on offense and on special teams.
Here are four players the Giants may be keeping an eye on this weekend.
Gilliam is rapidly becoming one of the nation’s most fearsome defensive tackles, as evidenced by his rising draft stock.
The 6-foot-2, 305-pound lineman has amassed 26 total tackles, six sacks and two forced fumbles in nine games this season with the Volunteers.
His ability to hold his position against the run, combined with his elite first step when rushing the passer, should make him an immediate upgrade on any NFL defensive line he joins in 2027.
Because he projects best as a three-technique in a 4-3 scheme, Gilliam may not be the big, two-gap tackle the Giants are expected to pursue during the draft.
However, he could be an effective weapon in sub-packages within the Giants’ 3-4 defense, especially when the unit shifts into four-man nickel fronts on passing downs.
With Tennessee set for a marquee matchup against Texas A&M, Gilliam is expected to play a major role in disrupting the Aggies’ offense, led by quarterback Marcel Reed.
Should the Giants prioritize power when scouting potential interior offensive linemen, Knapp is likely to be among their top prospects. The Roswell, Ga., native has appeared in eight games this season at left guard for the Fighting Irish.
With experience in both zone and gap schemes, the Notre Dame product appears ready to make an impact in any pro-level offensive system.
With the Irish set to face Boston College’s aggressive defense, Knapp will be called upon to remain a reliable presence in both pass protection and run-blocking alignments.
With John Michael Schmitz likely heading to free agency after being replaced in the starting lineup by Bryan Hudson, the 6-foot-4, 305-pound Knapp could be an intriguing option for New York, with the versatility to play either guard or center.
While Brown may not be the three-down workhorse New York reportedly coveted at the trade deadline, his skill set could be an intriguing fit within their current stable of running backs.
At 5-foot-9 and 190 pounds, Brown is a bit on the lighter side to handle lead-back duties at the pro level. Still, he could be an impactful change-of-pace option or an effective pass-catcher out of the backfield.
If the Giants show interest in Brown, it may be to pair him with Cam Skattebo.
With Skattebo as their physical, between-the-tackles runner atop the depth chart, Louisville’s standout could add an explosive dynamic to New York’s backfield.
If he’s effective against North Carolina’s defense under coach Bill Belichick, Brown may force the Giants to take a good look at him come draft time.
Given rookie Dominic Zvada’s continued struggles, the Giants have been the subject of rumors at kicker. Fortunately for Big Blue, several college kickers could draw interest, including Woodring.
In nine games for the top-ranked Bulldogs this season, Woodring has made 9 of 13 field goals, with his longest coming from 49 yards. He has also made a perfect 47 of 47 extra-point attempts. In 2025, Woodring connected on 17 of 19 field goals (89.5%), with a long of 53.
Despite his struggles this season, including a 49-yard miss against Ole Miss in Week 10, Woodring has the power and consistency to be a reliable kicker in his rookie season. While the Giants have expressed their support for Zvada, they are likely keeping their options open.
If Woodring can score points on Saturday against Missouri, it may help improve his draft stock with positionally needy teams like the Giants.

title: Why Cam Skattebo Stayed Put on Giants’ Key Third-and-1 Against Commanders
full_text:
To the casual observer, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo looked like he had fallen asleep at the snap, staying in his stance for nearly two seconds on a third-and-1 rushing play by quarterback Jameis Winston that did not pick up the first down.
But the play, which many assumed was a tush push given how often the Giants have run it this year, wasn’t what it looked like, and Skattebo did what he was supposed to do.
“That wasn’t a tush push. That was a different kind of play,” head coach John Harbaugh explained.
“It was a normal quarterback sneak and a certain check involved in it that is part of the play, but it wasn’t a tush push. So (Skattebo) wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”
Weirdest play of a weird night. If you’re going to run the Tush Push, you have to … you know … push. 🤷🏻‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/Sf65ZJ1vrF
The play occurred with the Giants leading 21-17. After a third-down try that initially appeared to give Winston the first down before officials reversed the call, the Giants tried to draw the Commanders offside on fourth-and-1. Still, it didn’t work, and a delay of game penalty led to a punt.
Given the Giants' success with the tush push, it was surprising they didn’t bring extra bodies to help Winston get the first down.
The Giants have converted first downs on 43.5% of their quarterback rushing attempts, which is the fifth-best mark in the NFL.
While that stat doesn’t differentiate between tush pushes, sneaks, designed runs, and scrambles, it shows the Giants have succeeded when deploying their quarterbacks to do so.
Only Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy know the logic behind running a sneak over a tush push. Still, it raised eyebrows, given Skattebo’s late arrival to the play and the fact that fullback Patrick Ricard was also not involved in Winston’s attempt to move the chains.
“We have four or five of those different types of calls and motions and pushes, not pushes, check-with-me plays. There are different things we have. One of those was called,” Harbaugh explained.
“We have different calls that go with quarterback sneaks, so we didn’t call the same one that we’ve been calling. That’s really the only answer I have for you. We didn’t call the same play. He wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”
But with that call not resulting in a first-down conversion, questions will linger over whether it was the right call to make at that juncture.

title: Giants Mailbag: Malik Nabers, Kayvon Thibodeaux, and More
full_text:
Welcome to the weekly New York Giants On SI mailbag! From offseason moves to game-day strategies, we'll do our best to answer your questions. (Some questions have been edited for brevity and clarity.)
If Nabers fancies himself as one of the best in the league, he needs to play like it.  No more dropping touchdowns.  No more fumbling the ball.  No more temper tantrums.  Time for him to ascend.  Will anyone have an honest conversation with him?
Mike, I asked Nabers about that in a round about way. Here was his response: "I had a talk with (Quarterbacks) Coach (Brian) Callahan, and we had a good talk and he said some things in our conversation. He was just like, ‘Just play the one play that we call, don't try to do too much.’ Don't try to do a lot on the play, we just need you to be you. So just be you at the end of the day.
"And like I said, just not pressing. I'm getting a lot of different coverages on my side. I'm getting a lot of cloud, getting a lot of double teams. So, every opportunity I have to get the football I think I'm just trying to do too much with the football instead of just let the game come to me and just play the game. So, I think just like Coach Calli said, just playing that one play, just locking on that one play and then focus on the next play when it comes."
Now that the Giants did not trade Thibedeux what are the chances that he is resigned. Hopefully it will not be another Saqoun situation.
Moose, my gut says they don't re-sign Thibodeaux. He's going to want a top-dollar deal, and I think someone will give it to him.
I could see a world where Arvell Reese gets more snaps on the outside, and you also have to remember that Thibs has been playing in his natural spot ever since Brian Burns's season-ending injury. So I think Thibs moves on in free agency.
Why do you suppose o-line got away from pulling guards, and running trap plays like week one against Dallas. Seems like more straight up blocking to me now. Did Dart's injury force a change to the blocking scheme?
The injury to Dart may have had something to do with it — remember, they have only now run what, three games with J.J. McCarthy under center, a guy who can run the RPO game unlike Winston?  But I think the bigger issue was the injuries at running back.
First, you have Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR, and of course you had Skattebo miss a game due to injury (as well as one due to a quasi-benching). As a result, the Giants leaned a little bit more on inside zone runs.
Second, I think they've leaned more on a pistol formation in their running game, with the fullback serving more as a trap blocker while the o-line has focused on DUO blocking.  The Giants only ran the pistol on 1.1% of their plays in Week 1.
Since then that perentage has jumped up to 3%, which might not seem like a huge jump but actually is considering how many rushing attempts they average per game.
What are the future ramifications to the Eagles salary cap since they are the biggest users of voidable years. How will it impact their rebuild.
Jim, I cover the Giants, not the Eagles so I can't sit here and tell you how their cap is going to be impacted down to the penny.
What I can tell you is that they have a lot of draft picks next year which means they'll have a lot of players on rookie deals -- two first rounders, one second, and a projected third round comp pick are their premium picks.
The cap is also going to rise so whatever dead money they accrue as a result of voidable years won't be as harsh in terms of the bite it takes out of their cap as it might be if it the hit were taken this year.
John Harbaugh says that Zavada has a problem on the right hash. Are you able to go back to see how many of his misses were from the right hash?
Kris, I was the one who mentioned Zvada's misses this year coming from the right hash, something Harbaugh didn't disagree with.
I brought up the question because I noticed they all came from the right hash. So to your question—I already did the groundwork on it, not that I was the only one to do so, I'm sure.

title: Dissecting the Jets' Most Important Quotes After Bills Loss Sends Gang Green to 2-8
full_text:
Jets fans have had it. They were already tired of the same answers and style of play throughout the team's five-game losing streak, but Sunday's loss to the Bills was just the next stage of their frustration.
Gang Green competed hard against their AFC East rivals, but still lost by three scores in a 31-12 romp to the Bills. Many of the same problems fans have watched this season reared their heads at the worst possible time.
As head coach Aaron Glenn and the rest of the roster continue to try and find a solution to their struggles, the reality is the Jets have simply run out of answers.
Here are some of the biggest quotes from Sunday's loss.
Arguably, the biggest problem for the Jets right now is that their philosophy as a team does not match the talent that they have.
Glenn wants his team to be able to run the football and play excellent defense. There's just one problem with that: their defense isn't good enough to be the key cog of things. New York needs to be able to put up points in order to give their defense a buffer, but they make mistakes and play calls that are at odds with what they need.
For example, the Jets had four scoring drives in Sunday's loss that were deep inside Buffalo territory. Instead of going for it on fourth down, they opted to kick field goals. The Bills then traded those field goals for touchdowns.
And after the game, Glenn has to explain why his offense is unable to score where and when it matters.
New York was just the second team this century to have four scoring drives but still get blown out by three scores in back-to-back games. That's a sign of a team that wants to play conservatively on offense, but aggressively on defense.
It simply doesn't match what the team is. Even if players continue to defend the current staff.
"It comes back again on that execution," Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson said. "The plays are there to be made, and at the end of the day, it does tighten up in the red zone. So, knowing that, we have to be that much more on our stuff, and we haven't been up to this point."
Sunday was supposed to be the first time since Week 1 that the team had their entire starting offense together on the field.
That lasted for a single play. Rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. and veteran guard Dylan Parham left the game in the first quarter, and even quarterback Geno Smith went into concussion protocol before leaving the game entirely due to another injury .
#OmarCooper @nyjets Rolled up on from behind while engaged in block Worry for mild high ankle injury Off IR for ankle earlier this season Came in with ankle on injury report pic.twitter.com/e52gJUbs3d
After the game, Glenn gave a clear injury update.
" Coop had an ankle , (Dylan) Parham had a knee, same knee, and Geno (Smith) had an ankle. Those are the injuries they had in the game," Glenn said. "I’ll end up getting that information sometime next week."
No news is good news in this case, but we'll know more as the week progresses.
We've already talked about how the Jets were without GenSmith in the game. That meant fourth-round rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik saw his first NFL action.
The Clemson product was pretty solid throughout, completing 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards. He was tagged for an interception late in the game, but he did use his legs in solid action (three rushes for 26 yards).
Cade Klubnik's first NFL pass is a completion to Garrett Wilson! BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cyxg8tuqzq
Based on the context as a mid-round rookie and getting his first action, Klubnik impressed his coaches.
"I thought he did a pretty good job," Glenn said. "That first drive that he did was pretty impressive. Some of the throws that he had were pretty impressive. His ability to maneuver around the pocket and evade some of these guys, and make plays with his feet were impressive."
The jury is still out on what kind of quarterback he can be. Klubnik's mobility is a superpower of his, and he certainly has the arm talent to make every throw. But his anticipation and decision-making are still very raw for an NFL signal-caller.
He is as close to a project as you will find for a rookie. Which is why getting him some playing time in a lost year is perfectly fine.
"It was fun to be out there, but the fun’s in the winning," Klubnik said. "I wish we would’ve come out with a win, and it felt like we were really close the whole time, until the very end. I thought we did some good things. We definitely have to clean up a lot of stuff."
We've talked about how the Jets failed to put up points on Sunday, but their current drought remains one of the worst we've seen.
New York has gone through nine straight quarters since its last touchdown. The last TD score was a Braelon Allen run with eight minutes to go in the third quarter in their loss to the Raiders. It's left players frustrated over their lack of success.
The Jets' struggles in the red zone are twofold. New York's coaching staff appears unable and unwilling to figure out ways to get the football to all of their talent. The players who do get chances, though, aren't able to make the most of those opportunities either.
It's an ugly rotating list of struggles that the team simply hasn't been able to figure out through 10 games.
"I'm frustrated because I know our offense is better than the amount of points that we've been scoring, and it shows in the stats because we're able to move the ball up and down the field how we want, so that's frustrating," Jets running back Breece Hall said. "You get down there, players have to make plays; it's not super special play calls that you make."
There is too much offensive talent for the Jets to not score a touchdown in one game, let alone for nine quarters. It needs to change immediately.
After their eighth loss in nine games and fifth in a row, some of the Jets' leaders tried to put their struggles into perspective: by thanking them for their loyalty and showing up to watch them play despite all the travel problems over the weekend with the FAA shutdown.
"I know it was a lot of traveling issues that are out there, so before we get to the game, I really want to make sure I acknowledge fans that had to persevere and the people who are out there having issues with traveling," Jets linebacker and captain Demario Davis said. "Just knowing that you guys are in our thoughts and prayers."
Davis is right to appreciate the fans. New York fans deserve more than what they have seen over their last 16 years of futility.
But they also deserve a stadium that is going to be full of their own fans. Sunday was overwhelmed by Bills fans who made the game feel more like a road game for some of New York's players. That isn't the fault of Jets fans either. Their players need to actually win to bring fans back.
But for those who traveled not only to see their Jets, only to be rewarded with a blowout loss and their stadium overrun by the opposition, they deserve so much more than what they have been given.

title: 4 Jets Duds & 4 Studs in Sunday's Blowout Loss to Bills: Glenn Sinks Lower Despite Bailey's Standout Effort
full_text:
The numbers keep getting worse. At this point, there's very little left to save the Jets or their head coach.
New York fought hard for three and a half quarters against their AFC East rivals, but made similar mistakes as in the last few weeks and ultimately were blown out by the Bills 31-12. They have gone two games without scoring an offensive touchdown and haven't won an AFC East game in three years.
The numbers are what they are.
As always we have plenty of studs and duds to break down from Sunday's loss. Let's go through it now.
New York got what they needed from their stars on offense . Breece Hall recorded 100 yards from scrimmage, including 67 yards receiving. He finished second on the team in that category behind Garrett Wilson, who added seven receptions for 106 yards. Throw in another five yards per carry average from Braelon Allen, and the Jets offense remains solid when it comes to the talent on offense.
Breece Hall now ranks No. 5 in receiving yards among running backs in franchise history pic.twitter.com/eghbq1rRGf
The Jets have a collection of talented pieces on offense that will make finding a quality quarterback next season easy for them. They appreciate the 1-2 punch at running back they have with Allen and Hall. They also like the fact that their receiving room is deep.
New York's stars showed up on Sunday. The frustrating part is that few others did, especially their coaching staff.
If you feel that the Jets have played the same football game in each of the last two months, you aren't wrong. New York has battled hard through the first half of each game they have played this season, only to be outschemed and outcoached in the second half.
On Sunday, the Jets were down 10-6 at the half. They had kept the Bills' offense in check for most of the afternoon. Then in the second half, they were outscored 21-6. New York was comfortable trading field goals for touchdowns and was burned throughout.
The loss moves Jets head coach Aaron Glenn to 5-22 in his career and 0-9 in the AFC East. By the time his tenure is over at the end of the year, he will go down as one of the worst winning percentages not just in team history, but in NFL history as well.
The biggest example of that came in the fourth quarter. The Jets were down 12 late, but the offense was moving well inside Bills territory. The Jets opted for a hook-and-ladder play that Wilson missed the lateral player by two yards. Buffalo picked up the fumble and, on the next offensive play, scored ona  74-yard touchdown run.
Glenn's time with the Jets is ending soon . And that two play sequence tells the whole story as to why.
The Jets didn't get much pressure on Josh Allen throughout the game. Bailey's performance today should be listed as "average" and nothing more.
However, he continues to find ways to make high-impact plays. In Sunday's loss, Bailey recorded two pass deflections early in the contest, highlighting his ability to read what the quarterback wants to do outside of the pocket. On one of the deflections, he seemed in play to even pick the pass off but ended up dropping the pass (h/t Glenn Naughton).
David Bailey juuuuust misses a pick six.  DROY candidate keeps making plays.  The @nyjets force a punt and have the ball for the first time today. pic.twitter.com/p6rHVQzehc
No edge rusher is working on ball drills in practice. But there's still a lot to like about what the second overall pick is putting out on the field.
Going into the game, the Jets were throwing out their full collection of offensive talent for the first time since Week 1.
By the end of the first quarter, though, they had lost Omar Cooper Jr. and Dylan Parham. By halftime, Geno Smith had entered concussion protocol . New York lost several starters across both sides of the ball in Sunday's loss, but it's uncanny that in the first game, all their starters are set to play together, they get nothing more than a single play or drive.
It's another microcosm of the team's poor season.
New York's defense is devoid of many star performers. They also lack just pure starters at this point.
Some of that conversation, though, changes with the play of second-year cornerback AZ Thomas. The Florida State cornerback has been solid through his first full year as a starter. His best play came in Sunday's loss when he leaped over a Bills receiver on a deep throw to pick off a Josh Allen pass.
Azareye'h Thomas with an INT BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oSsC1E1ChR
Thomas got banged up after the play, but it was the kind of athletic showing that provides New York hope that their former third-round pick can be another starter for the team.
And that the outlook for the defense's future is far better than anyone may admit.
Today highlighted the inconsistencies of officiating when it comes to the Jets. This isn't to say that the refs cost the Jets a game, but one can be critical of the officiating and still understand they had no impact on the game itself.
The biggest play in question came before the first half when Buffalo injured Smith, when a defender launched himself into Smith up high while another defender went low. "High-low" penalties don't exist on tackles, but targeting and unnecessary roughness penalties do exist, and that should have been called.
Here's the play in question:
Geno Smith is down on the field after taking this hit. pic.twitter.com/yLMaYc5ZGN
And here is Glenn's response, clearly highlighting that the call would have been different if Allen were the player who got hit.
“Here’s my problem with that, if that was Josh Allen every flag on the field would be thrown” Aaron Glenn is right. #Jets pic.twitter.com/pk8fYHaB3F
Glenn is absolutely right. There's a double standard in how referees call penalties against them and other teams.
New York has gone nine straight quarters without scoring an offensive touchdown. You'd think that would be impossible with how much talent the collective unit has. Alas, that is the current situation.
Thank god for Jason Sanders.
The Jets' kicker was 4-for-4 again on kicks today and has moved to 21-for-24 on the season. He's been one of the few bright spots this season for New York's special teams and remains a player the team should consider keeping around beyond 2026.
Stop me if you've heard this before, but the Jets' run defense remains one of the worst in the league. Buffalo recorded 201 yards on the ground and over six yards per carry. James Cook ran for over 150 yards and a touchdown during the game as well.
There are many reasons for this, of course. New York's linebackers are a major hindrance to the team's success at this point. Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood collectively have been poor over the last several weeks and were washed out on several runs on Sunday.
Making matters worse, the team also didn't get much production at all from their defensive tackles. This defense simply isn't good enough, and everyone knows they can be beaten by running the ball.

title: Geno Smith Injury News Could Force Jets to Look at Free-Agent QB Trio After Week 10
full_text:
It's safe to say that the Jets' Week 10 clash with the Bills isn't going as planned. Not only was rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. ruled out after leaving with an ankle injury in the first quarter , but veteran quarterback Geno Smith was also forced to leave the game with a concussion, thrusting his outlook into uncertainty.
Smith left the game and was evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter after being hit by two Bills defenders . The unfortunate exit led to rookie QB Cade Klubnik making his sooner-than-anticipated NFL debut, in which he completed three of his first seven passes for 48 passing yards and an interception.
Geno smith sandwiched .. should be just wind knocked out pic.twitter.com/ElqPUjH46C
Smith eventually cleared concussion protocol and returned to the game... only to exit again as he "limped" out of the game and entered the blue medical tent , according to SNY TV 's Connor Hughes. The 36-year-old signal-caller eventually headed to the locker room before a commercial break, further fueling speculation about his immediate future and down the line.
At 3:46 p.m. ET, the Jets officially ruled Smith out of the game with an ankle injury.
Geno Smith (ankle) has been downgraded to OUT
Given that Klubnik was expected to be a project prospect, while the in-game emergency QB was wideout Isaiah Williams, it's safe to say the Jets might want to add another quarterback. Sure, Will Levis is on the practice squad , but too many arms is never a bad idea.
Aaron Glenn says that Geno Smith and Omar Cooper both have ankle injuries. They are both ankle injuries. He doesn’t know yet if high or low. pic.twitter.com/QxPoJo0mF9
Here are three free-agent QBs that New York can target as Smith's outlook remains a question mark.
When it comes to available QB options, few have as much experience as Jimmy Garoppolo. The former 2014 second-round pick has started in 64 of his 85 regular-season appearances while also making six postseason starts (4-2 record), and that's without mentioning the two Super Bowl-winning teams he got to be a part of in New England.
Injuries and circumstances have led to Garoppolo being more of a supporting cast member in recent years, but that doesn't mean he can't help the Jets in a time of need. He completed 65.2% of passes for 1,539 yards, nine touchdowns and 10 interceptions in seven starts over three seasons with the Rams, and having him around would help New York avoid throwing Klubnik into a situation he isn't ready for.
Although imperfect, the Jets could do a lot worse.
Continuing the unintended theme of former Patriots quarterbacks, Bailey Zappe is one potential option whom the Jets know well. New York signed the Western Kentucky product to a future contract back in January to compete for the QB2 job. He was re-signed after being part of the last wave of roster cuts , only to be released again to make room for Levis.
Even though he was dumped twice, the Jets might feel like going with the familiar face makes the most sense at this point in the season. Zappe appeared in two preseason games for Gang Green this summer, going 14-of-23 (60.9%) for 135 passing yards with two INTs. Far from an impressive performance, but the chance to right those wrongs may motivate Zappe to put in a stronger effort.
How about someone whom the Jets previously showed interest in but didn't sign? After all, it was back in April when Hughes reported that New York was interested in Cooper Rush's services ; however, a deal never materialized and Rush eventually signed a one-year contract with the Falcons.
Rush's time in Atlanta was short-lived, though, and he found himself back in the unemployment line in October after a pair of forgettable starts. The Falcons lost both of his appearances as Rush went 22-of-39 (56.4) for 229 passing yards, one TD, four INTs and a 42.5 passer rating. Obviously, those stats don't illustrate a great picture, but the Jets don't exactly need an MVP-caliber performance.
The last two seasons haven't been kind to him, but Rush's time with the Cowboys proved that he can be one of the NFL's better backup quarterbacks. If he can even get back to being a semblance of that guy, he'll still be better than what Jets fans were used to before Smith came to town.

title: Omar Cooper Jr. Injury Tracker: Every Update After Rookie Jets WR's Early Exit vs. Bills
full_text:
It didn't take long for things to go poor for the Jets in Sunday's Week 10 clash against the rival Bills.
Just as the offense was slowly becoming healthier, rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. left the early matchup with an ankle injury in the first quarter. The injury occurred when multiple players fell on Cooper's ankle (h/t Banged Up Bills ) while he was blocking for fellow rookie Kenyon Sadiq on a catch-and-run play.
WR Omar Cooper Jr. (Right Ankle) Cooper gets rolled up on again, this is the same high-ankle that he injured in Week 1, sent him to IR, returned, and injured again last week. pic.twitter.com/N9BtGAUFog
Cooper was seen sitting on the sidelines, looking dejected after being forced to step out of the game. Unfortunately, the situation took a turn for the worse a few moments later, leaving Jets fans worried that the promising first-year WR's campaign would be derailed yet again.
Update #2 (Nov. 15, 4:23 p.m. ET): Per Hughes, head coach Aaron Glenn confirmed that Cooper (along with quarterback Geno Smith) is dealing with an ankle injury and that more testing will be required to determine if it's a "high or low" situation.
Update #1 (Nov. 15, 2:51 p.m. ET): Cooper has officially been ruled out of Sunday's game , according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo.
As seen in the video above, Cooper's outlook appeared grim the second multiple players landed on him. He seemingly struggled to put weight on it, which eventually led to the Jets confirming that he'd be questionable to return with an ankle injury.
Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return with an ankle injury
Considering that Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell have also been dealing with injuries this season, the last thing the Jets need is for Cooper to be out long-term. The Indiana product had just played a season-high 54 offensive snaps against the Chiefs in Week 9, only to be limited to just one passing route before being forced to leave against the Bills.
That said, Cooper still hasn't been ruled out at the time of writing, making it crucial for Jets fans to stay locked in for each of the upcoming updates on Sunday and beyond.
Although he oozes talent, it's hard to ignore Cooper's history with the injury bug—especially after his latest issue.
Injuries have been an obstacle for Cooper dating back to high school, when he tore his ACL . He also occasionally dealt with ankle issues during his time with the Hoosiers, including when he missed three games in 2023.
Much to everyone's dismay, Cooper has continued to miss time at the pro level. After making an impressive 30-yard catch in his NFL debut against the Titans, Cooper suffered a high-ankle sprain that forced him to miss four games. Back-to-back 100-yard performances after getting off the injured reserve left Jets fans excited about his outlook, but it seems like his promising rookie year will likely be on pause again.
Before Sunday's exit, Cooper was up to 306 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 20 catches in five games.
Assuming that Cooper misses any time, the Jets will continue looking to Wilson and Mitchell as their top wide receivers. The dynamic duo is capable of flipping any game on its head, which means any success will hinge on quarterback Geno Smith's ability to get them the ball. Tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor have also proven they can step up.
It'd also be nice to see Isaiah Williams step up during Cooper's potential absence. The veteran WR has still been solid as a returner; however, his receiving numbers have left much to be desired this season. The same could be said for fellow elder-statesman wideout Tim Patrick, who was a healthy scratch on Sunday.
Cooper's injury could also mean more opportunities for UDFA WR Malik McClain, who hadn't received a target before Week 10. There's also a chance that New York could elevate one of Sterling Shepard, Jamaal Pritchett or Joseph Manjack IV off the practice squad.

title: Jets' Mixed Week 10 Injury Report Still Sparks Optimism Heading Into Bills Matchup
full_text:
The New York Jets are in rare territory when the team takes the field Sunday against the Bills .
For the first time since Week 1, the team will have a chance to see their entire starting offensive roster on the field together for an entire game. Over the first nine games, New York has seen injuries to Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, Omar Cooper Jr., their tight ends, and the offensive line.
It's among the many reasons why the Jets sit at 2-7 and are major underdogs against the Bills , who are favored by 8.5 points despite being the visitors , according to DraftKings Sportsbook .
As the team walks into MetLife Stadium on Sunday, though, some of the more prominent Jets leaders have spoken out regarding their current injury situation.
Here's the situation for New York: only one player on their injury report has been listed as "OUT" for Sunday. Backup linebacker Trevin Wallace is dealing with a groin injury and won't suit up. Outside of him, there are eight players listed as game-time decisions.
That is five starters and seven role players. The good news is that there is hope that the Jets will see many of these players hit the field without any issues.
"For guys that will be limited today: Omar (Cooper Jr.), (Joseph) Ossai, Garrett (Wilson), Nashon (Wright). Those guys are doing well, but they'll be limited today," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday.
Of note, while Phillips is listed as questionable, he did not practice through the end of the week. There is some doubt that New York's captain on defense will be able to suit up against the Bills' top-ranked offense.
New York focused heavily this week on getting players healthy. They held a walk-through that caused controversy amongst the fanbase due to their poor record. But with a bye week in Week 13, the team believes that further rest is needed for their veterans.
Among the players trying to work their way back is New York's leading receiver: Garrett Wilson. The veteran wideout is recovering from a concussion. In order to play on Sunday, he will need to pass through the final piece of protocol ahead of warmups. There is optimism that he will. But it's still a wait-and-see game there.
For the most part, it's believed that all of New York's "questionable" designations will play on Sunday.
If so, the offense will have their full collection of talent together since opening day.
And it adds a new wrinkle to what should be a successful day against a Bills defense that has been mediocre for most of the year.

title: D'Angelo Ponds Has Sudden Chance to Erase Jets' Concerns in Week 10
full_text:
Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets believe it's time to turn the starting nickel job over to their second-round rookie.
But if D'Angelo Ponds is going to take the next step in his development for his coach and team, merely getting starting reps will not be enough. New York's intended starter, Jarvis Brownlee, is dealing with an illness. If Ponds is to keep his job once Brownlee is back healthy, he'll need to produce.
The good news for New York is that a strong performance against the Buffalo Bills could give Ponds the confidence needed to begin to excel like many other players in the 2026 draft class.
Through the first two starts of his NFL career, Ponds has been a quality starter for New York. While Pro Football Focus has graded his outlook at a struggling 27.2, his coverage grades are far from that of a struggling player. He simply hasn't had enough snaps to see how good he can be.
In last week's loss to Kansas City, Ponds was targeted once, and gave up a reception for seven yards. He was also penalized for a second time this season that gave the Chiefs a first down. In his last start against the Miami Dolphins, though, Ponds was targeted three times, gave up one reception, and was called for a penalty that gave the opposition a first and goal.
The penalties are obviously a program, but these numbers are far from alarming example of Ponds being unable to perform. If anything, they highlight the fact he needs more reps to get comfortable on an NFL field.
"We can only play so many people. You see that across the league a number of hot picks... [Fernando] Mendoza hasn't played at all. We have some other good players on the team. He's going to get his shot. He's a damn good player. We all know that. Just be patient, and give him a little time. He's going to get a shot to play," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said.
We have finally reached that part of the season with Ponds getting consistent playing time.
But context is also important. This is a rookie cornerback playing a new position (Ponds was used in the boundary during his college career), and didn't have a training camp to get acclimated. The bright spots shown on the field so far is what New York should be hoping to see.
He may not have broken out like Omar Cooper Jr. or David Bailey have, but Ponds seems on his way to being a productive member of the organization. He just needs the grace and time to be able to reach that mark.

title: 3 Logical Will McDonald IV Trade Destinations for the Jets This Offseason
full_text:
The Will McDonald IV experiment may be over after this season. The defensive end whom New York drafted 15th overall in 2023 requested a trade right before this year's deadline . While the Jets opted to keep McDonald, the writing may still be on the wall.
New York has three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. There has already been talk of Gang Green using one of those picks on a talent like Dylan Stewart or Colin Simmons. McDonald cited playing time as one reason for his request. It does not look like the road to more snaps is getting any shorter.
If the Jets decide to move on from McDonald this offseason, look for these names as potential suitors for the former first-round pick.
The Jaguars have already expressed interest for the Jets' edge rusher. Jacksonville allegedly made a "significant offer" for the defensive end before the trade deadline. It would be hard to believe they would lose interest before the offseason.
McDonald is a pure pass rusher. He wasn't drafted for his run-stopping abilities; rather, he was drafted for his ability to get to the passer. That ability would be well utilized on a Jacksonville team that has constantly been playing with a lead in 2026. Regardless of how the Jags finish their season, Will McDonald would be a good addition to a team hoping to contend for years to come.
Jacksonville should also be intrigued by landing a talent who has had a 10-sack season rather than drafting one next April. Jacksonville could address its middling offensive line in the draft if they send some capital to New York. McDonald was obviously appetizing to the team at the deadline, and that interest should hold as the year progresses.
McDonald could also find a new home in San Francisco this offseason. The former first-rounder was a pick from the Robert Saleh regime. A regime that developed roots in San Francisco. That connection could see McDonald in red and gold in 2027...
Saleh's defense still lingers in San Francisco. The former Jets head coach even returned to his old job with the 49ers before the Tennessee Titans hired him. McDonald could slot into a defense that is more like the one he was originally drafted to play. That, however, may not be the only reason the Jets and 49ers could find a trade.
The 49ers have had an injury bug that seems to have followed them for years. Nick Bosa has been one of the 49ers to be bitten. The former Defensive Player of the Year hasn't played a full season since 2023. Bosa is no doubt a lethal pass rusher, but that is only when he is actually on the field. McDonald would be welcome help for a team that always needs more bodies.
The Bears addressed a big need on the defensive line by trading a haul to Tennessee for Jeffery Simmons. Despite the deal's magnitude, Chicago still has holes on the outside of the line. There were some rumblings that the team would bring back Khalil Mack in a deal that ultimately did not go through.
Mack will be 36 next season; McDonald will be 28. If the Bears are looking to bolster their pass rush, a player like McDonald may be a perfect fit. McDonald is on a rookie deal that extends to next season, so Chicago could treat it as a prove-it deal if they so desire. The Bears are another team entering a championship window who could benefit from McDonald's talents.
An explosive edge like McDonald could be the perfect pairing with Ben Johnson's team. He is a young player who the team could either extend to ride out the championship window or drop him with little regret after 2027. Either way, McDonald could be an interesting watch if Chicago looks to shore up their d-line this offseason.

title: 3 Jets vs. Bills Matchups That Will Decide If New York Pulls Off the Week 10 Upset
full_text:
Coming off another disappointing loss, the Jets will look to get back on track when they host the Bills in Week 10. Buffalo has arguably been the best team in the league this season, led by 2024 MVP Josh Allen, who is making a strong case to win another with his performance this season.
Meanwhile, New York is on a four-game losing streak, and head coach Aaron Glenn’s hot seat continues to get warmer with each week . If Glenn wants to save his job, he’ll need to string together a few wins, particularly against the AFC East, where he’s compiled a 0-8 record.
For the Jets to pull off a miracle against the Bills, they must win these three key matchups.
Through nine weeks, Josh Allen is widely regarded as the front-runner for MVP thanks to his dual-threat dominance. The four-time Pro Bowler has been extremely efficient through the air, completing 66.1% of his passes for 2,057 yards, 12 touchdowns, and six interceptions.
He’s been equally dominant on the ground, leading all quarterbacks in rushing yards (285) and rushing touchdowns (9). Allen’s ability to make off-schedule throws, extend plays out of the pocket, and exploit opponents with his mobility makes him a defense’s worst nightmare.
Slowing Allen down will be a challenge for the Jets, considering their defense hasn’t done well this season. However, if New York wants to improve their chances of beating the Bills, it must keep Allen in the pocket and prevent him from hurting the defense with his legs.
We saw the Vikings do this on Monday night against Buffalo by bringing the house on Allen, blitzing him on 68.6% of his dropbacks and limiting him to just 15 yards on the ground. Although Minnesota lost, they held the Bills to their lowest-scoring total of the season (23) and sacked Allen four times.
Byron Murphy Jr. picks off Josh Allen 🔥 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/8FrX0GWR8f
While the Jets don’t have pass rushers of similar caliber to the Vikings, they’ve had some success generating pressure this season. Through nine games, New York ranks 12th in sacks (22) and 13th in pressure rate (24%). They also boast one of the highest blitz rates, ranking third at 34%.
Simply sending an extra defender won’t be enough to contain Allen. The Jets can’t be undisciplined when blitzing, as Allen can hurt them with his mobility.
New York’s edge rushers must maintain the edge and not over-pursue Allen, something we’ve seen them struggle with against Malik Willis a couple of weeks back. The interior defenders and linebackers must also remain disciplined in their rush lanes and continue attacking the pocket, or the Jets won’t be able to collapse it.
Getting to Allen early will be critical, as we’ve seen him make costly mistakes when under pressure.
After getting to Allen a few times in the first quarter, the Vikings forced him to make an early decision that resulted in Byron Murphy making an incredible interception. If New York can force Allen into playing hero ball, it could create opportunities for turnovers and give the Jets a better chance of pulling off the upset.
The Jets insisted on keeping Breece Hall for several reasons; one was that he forms a dynamic backfield duo with Braelon Allen. Hall has explosive home-run play ability and is a great receiving back, while Allen is a physical downhill runner who excels at picking up yards after contact.
New York’s offense is at its best when it establishes the run, which opens up opportunities for offensive coordinator Frank Reich to dial up deep shots downfield. That was evident in the Jets’ wins over the Titans and Browns, as well as their narrow defeats to the Dolphins and Raiders. When the running game is clicking, the offense can dictate the tempo and keep opposing defenses on their heels.
However, we’ve only seen Hall and Allen play three full games this season. With Hall back, Reich must make a better effort to utilize both running backs and stick with the ground game, even if it doesn’t produce early. The Jets did this early against the Chiefs last week, particularly during their first few possessions, but abandoned the approach once they were down two scores.
Running the ball will be a challenge against the Bills. Buffalo ranks seventh in rushing yards allowed per game (91.6), 10th in yards per carry (3.9), and is tied for ninth in fewest rushes of 10-plus yards with 20. Over the last four games, they’ve allowed just 269 rushing yards.
Even though New York’s rushing attack hasn’t been as productive this season, ranking 20th in rushing yards per game (105.2), sticking with the run game will be critical in this matchup, along with finding ways to get their runners to the second level.
The Bills use a lot of five-down sets and rank 13th in stacked box rate, per Next Gen Stats. To counter this, New York should emphasize attacking the perimeter and bringing in extra blockers.
Reich has primarily used Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods in multi-tight end sets when running the ball, and the pair have done well as run blockers. However, Reich must also consider doing this with Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor to keep Buffalo guessing and prevent the offense from becoming predictable.
If the offensive line and extra blockers can clear a path for Hall and Allen to get to the outside on counters or sweeps, they could get to the second level and hurt Buffalo with their playmaking ability. Allen, in particular, would benefit from getting to the perimeter, where he has been effective at breaking tackles and picking up extra yardage.
Buffalo allows 3.4 yards after contact per attempt, the third-highest mark in the league. That could play right into Allen’s strengths and give him an opportunity to exploit one of the Bills’ biggest weaknesses.
While all eyes will be on David Bailey and Allen, among others, one of the most important individual matchups will be between Armand Membou and Gregory Rousseau.
Through the first eight weeks, Membou made a strong Pro Bowl case, giving up just two sacks and 16 pressures. However, that came to an abrupt halt last week , as he surrendered three sacks and four pressures against a Kansas City pass rush that was tied last in sacks (9) and ranked 29th in pressure rate (19.3%) entering the game.
The Jets desperately need Membou to bounce back this week against Rousseau, who’s been one of the most productive pass rushers this season. The former 2021 first-round selection leads the league in pressures (51), per Pro Football Focus , and is tied for second in sacks with eight.
Greg Rousseau's 8th sack of the season ties him for second in the league 😤 BUFvsMIN on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OyIU25yJbs
New York’s top priority should be limiting Rousseau’s impact, as Buffalo’s other pass rushers have largely struggled to generate pressure. Behind Rousseau, Bradley Chubb and Deone Walker have combined for 50 pressures and just 2.5 sacks.
Even though Membou struggled last week, the Jets should not overreact to one bad outing and should have complete trust in their second-year tackle to hold his own against Rousseau. However, in obvious passing-down situations, New York should give him some extra help through double teams and have their tight ends chip Rousseau before releasing into their routes.
Reich also must consider mixing in some quick throws or screen passes to neutralize Rousseau and give time for Geno Smith to take downfield shots. Limiting Rousseau’s impact will be critical to giving Smith time to operate and preventing them from being in obvious passing situations.

title: Jets Shouldn't Hesitate to Throw VJ Payne Into the Fire If He Debuts vs. Bills
full_text:
After staying put at the trade deadline and deciding not to make any significant moves, the Jets turn their attention to a Week 10 home tilt against the Bills on Sunday as the second half of the NFL season gets underway.
Aside from the lack of adjustments and execution problems that continue to plague this coaching staff, injuries have been a recurring issue all season for Gang Green. That said, head coach Aaron Glenn provided an encouraging update on Friday that suggests this could be a much healthier team than it has been in a while.
"When it comes to injuries, the only person that'll be out will be Trevin Wallace ," Glenn said (h/t Jets). "Everybody else will be full: Jarvis Brownlee (Jr.), Harrison Phillips, Omar Cooper (Jr.), Joseph Ossai, Nahshon (Wright) and Garrett (Wilson). Garrett still has one more step to go through before he's cleared, and I see that happening. And then VJ Payne is still going through his process, so we'll see how that operates."
Coach Glenn provides an injury update ahead of #BUFvsNYJ pic.twitter.com/S3BPO6JHmo
That is a much better injury report than the Jets have had in recent weeks, and with back-to-back full practices under his belt, everything is pointing to rookie safety VJ Payne potentially making his NFL debut on Sunday after spending the start of the season on injured reserve due to a bone bruise in his knee.
His 21-day practice window has since been opened, and a potential return certainly appears to be on the horizon following the departure of former Jets safety Andre Cisco to the Lions.
Even though Payne was the last player selected in Gang Green's draft class after going 228th overall in the seventh round, the Jets should not hesitate to get him on the field as often as possible , even though he has not played yet.
After all, he has the speed, versatility and overall intangibles to be a solid contributor when that time comes and is more than deserving of getting an opportunity to show what he has, especially with the lack of depth that now exists on this roster.
To their credit, offseason acquisitions Dane Belton (76) and Minkah Fitzpatrick (53) rank second and fourth, respectively, in total tackles on the team this season and Fitzpatrick has the lone interception.
At the same time, the secondary has struggled with blown coverages and hasn't been the Jets' best unit. Combine that with the fact that Malachi Moore is the only depth piece they have behind them, and it becomes clear how much Payne's outlook could improve if he can have a strong showing when the opportunity comes his way.
The Jets have designated rookie safety VJ Payne to return from IR. Could help on kick coverage. pic.twitter.com/bnC5TMQeV4
While Glenn has doubled down on the process despite his 5-21 record in Gotham and an 0-8 divisional record against AFC East opponents, this season is lost at this point and it is not like they have much to worry about by putting an unproven rookie in Payne out there.
Not only will more snaps be available following the Cisco trade, but any snaps Payne potentially receives against an elite Bills offense could be a valuable learning experience.
While the Buffalo defense allows the fourth-most pass yards per game (238.8 ypg) and should give this offense some opportunities to exploit down the field , the Bills have the highest-scoring offense (32 ppg) and will present a stiff test for a struggling defense.
It is easy to point to the David Bailey vs. Arvell Reese debate after the Jets took the former with the No. 2 pick in the draft ahead of the latter (fifth overall to the Giants), but there is no reason to discredit and overlook Payne, either. By no means should he be compared to Bailey or have the immediate expectation of coming in and stealing the spotlight, but the lack of depth and lost season the Jets are experiencing should force their hand to put him out there and let him show what he has.
Regardless of Payne's status, it is hard to truly know what to expect from him as someone who has been sidelined all season. At this point, what do the Jets have to lose by throwing him into the fire and letting him get the full NFL experience against an explosive offense that can test him and find out what he is made of for the rest of this season and beyond?

title: Howie Roseman's Miami Visit Is Creating Eagles Buzz It Might Not Deserve
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Eagles general manager Howie Roseman’s Miami-Duke visit created the expected noise. The calendar, family context and the broader quarterback picture for the Eagles make it more routine than it looked.
The video clip went viral pretty quickly: Philadelphia’s general manager on the field before Miami hosted Duke, briefly greeting Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah.
"Bring him to Philly!" Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman a little pregame love for Canes QB Darian Mensah @WPLGLocal10 pic.twitter.com/QkhiiNuepN
For a team that has struggled , sits with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the season by blood clots and is projected to hold significant 2027 draft capital (including a potential top-five pick and another later in the round, any Roseman-QB interaction was going to generate some “bring him to Philly” reactions.
The timing amplified it, but the context points more to business as usual. The Eagles are on their bye week , the trade deadline has passed, and Roseman has more time than he typically has in mid-November.
More significantly, Roseman’s oldest son, Jake, attends Duke and works with the Blue Devils’ football program. That family visit is the far more likely reason why the Miami-Duke game made logistical sense during the bye.
Mensah himself was the starting QB at Duke in 2025 before transferring to Miami (a move that involved an NIL dispute that was later settled). Roseman was hardly the only NFL representative in the building for a high-profile ACC game—scouts from several other teams were present—but the personal tie to Duke and the time Roseman has with the Eagles off this week are the clearest reasons he was there in person.
None of that means Mensah falls outside the Eagles’ evaluation of quarterbacks when the position could top Roseman's wanted list next April. He is a productive quarterback who has put up elite numbers at Miami after earlier stops at Tulane and Duke. He will be on the board for teams that need a signal-caller in the first round. The same is true of other names that most personnel evaluators currently place ahead of Mensah.
Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker continues to draw the strongest “upside” comments. The former walk-on has the physical tools, production, and arm talent that keep him at or near the top of many 2027 quarterback rankings. Notre Dame’s C.J. Carr is viewed as the most advanced processor of the group, according to multiple personnel evaluators who spoke to Eagles On SI .
Carr is accurate, comfortable with pre-snap manipulation, and further along in the mental side of the position than most of his peers. Texas’s Arch Manning still carries the pedigree and the traits that made him a high-profile prospect, even as his tape this season has been more uneven than some of the others.
Roseman’s job is to uncover as much information as possible with all those possibilities.
A pregame conversation with Mensah, against the backdrop of a son at Duke, does not lock the Eagles into (or out of) any particular quarterback plan.
It is one hardly-significant data point in a process that will also include Mestemaker’s high-ceiling flashes, Carr’s processing, and Manning’s pedigree.
With Hurts’s recovery timeline unclear and the Eagles' roster in flux, that evaluation work on Mensah and others who participated in the Hurricanes-Blue Devils matchup is simply part of the job—no more dramatic, and no less necessary, despite the way it might have looked to the uninitiated on a bye-week Saturday in South Florida.
