title: Fred Johnson's Release Underscores the Eagles' Personal Gong Show
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — For younger readers, "The Gong Show" was a somewhat iconic television game show from the 1970s in which often bizarre, eccentric and untrained amateur contestants performed on stage while a panel of three celebrity judges watched.
If a judge disliked an act, they would strike a massive brass gong with a wooden mallet to abruptly end the performance.
The always-interesting Fred Johnson recently introduced the percussion instrument into the Eagles' locker room to liven things up during what’s turned into a seven-game skid for an organization not used to losing.
Turns out Johnson’s gong had a shorter shelf life than A.J. Dillon’s infamous positivity bunny.
The big man eventually moved the gong into the offensive line room, but now both Johnson and his new toy will be filing a change of address form .
The last figurative clang of Johnson’s gong signaled the Eagles' waiving of a pair of veteran offensive players Friday: wide receiver Hollywood Brown and Johnson, the team’s proven swing tackle.
We have waived WR Marquise Brown and T Fred Johnson. pic.twitter.com/S4ieutMSfU
Neither player figured into the organization’s 2027 plans, so the decisions highlight the end of any realistic push for the 2026 postseason and a clear shift toward the continued evaluation of younger players who have an opportunity to be part of the solution moving forward.
The actual reasons for moving on are slightly different. With starting receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) set to return from injuries after the Eagles’ bye week, there wasn’t going to be much playing time for Brown.
An NFL source confirmed to Eagles On SI that Brown wanted to move on, and Philadelphia agreed after working out a non-injury settlement . In other words, Brown agreed to give back some of the $5 million he was guaranteed back in March for the opportunity to seek more playing time elsewhere, perhaps with a playoff contender.
Johnson, 29, is a little bit different. He has been a reliable swing tackle and backup for the Eagles in recent seasons and has garnered plenty of playing time since first joining the organization in late 2022.
Johnson contributed during the Super Bowl LIX-winning 2024 campaign (primarily filling in at left tackle for an injured Jordan Mailata) and logged a career-high 626 regular-season snaps in 2025 while starting nine games, mostly in relief of Lane Johnson.
After the Super Bowl season, Johnson left in free agency for an opportunity to compete for a starting job in Jacksonville. That didn’t work out, and the Eagles sent a seventh-round pick to the Jags to get him back just before the start of the 2025 season.
If it were a strict meritocracy, Johnson likely would have taken over at right tackle after Lane Johnson’s in-season retirement. Instead, the Eagles went with upside, inserting third-round rookie Markel Bell.
Fred Johnson appeared in seven games this season with only 24 offensive snaps, many of them as an extra tight end in a jumbo package.
The Eagles entered their bye week at 2-7 , last in the NFC East and mired in a seven-game skid. The team’s playoff odds have effectively evaporated, even in a weak NFL East.
In that context, cutting a veteran with no long-term roster value—and no trade value after the deadline—frees a spot on the 53-man roster while the evaluation of Bell continues.
These moves fit a broader pattern of roster pruning during the downtime of the bye. Earlier in the week, the Eagles also waived running back Jaydon Blue and traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis , opening multiple spots.
The organization can now promote or claim developmental players from practice squads. In-house, John Ojukwu, Kiran Amegadjie and Evan Neal could factor in as swing-tackle options behind Mailata and Bell.
For Johnson, the departure closes a productive chapter in Philadelphia. He took to Instagram after the news with a simple thank-you to the city , posting a photo from the Super Bowl celebration.
The Eagles return to action on Nov. 22 against the Steelers. By then, the roster will reflect a more explicit developmental priority—an acknowledgment that the corner on 2026 has been turned and the focus has shifted primarily to the future.
Essentially, the Eagles' 2026 season just got gonged.

title: 3 Eagles Who Should Barely See the Field After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Eagles have proven that things change on a dime in the NFL. Philadelphia entered the season with Super Bowl hopes, but enters its bye week with the worst record in the NFC (2-7). A team that has been focused on hoisting the Lombardi Trophy now needs to shift toward planning for the future .
There's been a lot of new faces wearing midnight green. That'll happen when the starting quarterback goes down, a Pro Bowl offensive lineman retires, and a star defensive tackle is traded . The Eagles have an opportunity to retool by focusing on youth and development over the final eight games.
That means decreasing their reliance on short-term veterans. Here's a look at three Eagles who stick out.
The Eagles had agreed to trade defensive end Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a sixth-round pick. That was until Cincinnati backed out when they determined the deal would result in a lost compensatory pick. Ebiketie will remain in Philly before entering free agency at the end of the season.
The fact that the Eagles were ready to part ways with Ebiketie shows he doesn't fit into their 2027 plans. The 27-year-old has failed to make much of an impact, posting 25 tackles and two quarterback hits in nine games (48% of the defensive snaps and 37% of the special teams snaps).
Shrinking Ebiketie's role in the defensive end rotation would allow rookie Keyshawn James-Newby to play increased snaps . The seventh-round pick flashed with two pressures in 20 pass-rush snaps in Week 6. James-Newby's 9.0 sacks with New Mexico in 2025 led the Mountain West Conference.
Cornerback Kenny Moore II was not expected to take on a major role in Philly's secondary when he was signed in September. That was before Michael Carter II's abdominal injury. Moore has stepped in at safety as of late, playing at least 48% of the defensive snaps in four of the Eagles' past five games.
The increase in snaps was simply injury-fueled, though. Moore has struggled in pass coverage, allowing a 158.7 passer rating when targeted. The former Pro Bowler was picked on for an eight-yard touchdown, a 30-yard completion, and a 20-yard completion during a Week 8 loss to Washington.
Moore is 31 and playing on a one-year deal. He should stay on the sideline once Carter returns. The second half of the season is also a chance for the Eagles to see what rookie safety Cole Wisniewski can add to the mix. The sixth-round pick has been a hard-hitting tackler on special teams.
The Eagles didn't even wait until the bye week to bench quarterback Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton, who had been in Philly for less than a month. This comes after Andy Dalton beat McKee for the backup QB spot in training camp. The franchise clearly doesn't view McKee as a long-term option.
It's a harsh reality for someone who has been on the roster since 2023. McKee was inconsistent in his three starts this campaign, completing 72 of his 114 passes (63.2%) for 638 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. The Eagles averaged a disappointing 15.0 points across those three contests.
"The Eagles benched Tanner McKee way too soon!" They went with Joe Milton for reasons like this. He's a dynamic athlete and behind this OL, this type of escapability is needed. This led to the Eagles third first quarter TD of the season. #Eagles pic.twitter.com/QV2BR5wiaw
The final eight games of the season should be treated as a tryout for Milton to earn a roster spot in 2027. If he plays well, he could be Jalen Hurts's backup. If he plays poorly, the Eagles could cut bait. It'll be up to Philly's coaching staff to make the most of Milton's strong arm and scrambling abilities.

title: 3 Sneaky QB Prospects the Eagles Should Already Be Eyeing in the 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Eagles' ongoing losing streak will remain where it is for now as they take a breather during a much-needed bye in Week 10. Seven consecutive losses following a 2-0 start have sucked the oxygen right out of the room in Philadelphia, and a quiet trade deadline performance further hammered home that there won't be much to celebrate this season .
With the halfway point of the 2026 season here, it's time for Eagles fans to start thinking about the future—whether that's potential offseason departures or free agency signings . Some folks are even thinking about the 2027 NFL Draft, where the Eagles' selections will happen earlier than they're used to.
That said, drafting a potential quarterback could be on general manager Howie Roseman's radar in April. Questions surround Jalen Hurts's outlook after blood clots knocked him out of the current season , and it's safe to say that Joe Milton, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton have a long way to go toward proving their long-term value.
Even if Hurts makes a full recovery, the Eagles would be wise to start thinking about the future. If Philadelphia wants to use its upcoming first-rounder on another position, there are still at least three sneaky QB prospects Roseman & Co. should consider on Day 2.
Hurts's mobility is one aspect that helps make him so great, so no one would be surprised if head coach Nick Sirianni wants his next franchise QB to have a similar trait. That's why UCLA's Nico Iamaleava could be on the Eagles' radar once the second round begins.
Standing 6'5" and weighing 215 lbs, Iamaleava boasts the size and athleticism that NFL coaches love. He's displayed a well-rounded game during his time at UCLA and Tennessee, completing 521-of-818 passes (63.7%) for 5,840 passing yards and 38 touchdowns to 16 interceptions while converting 283 carries into 1,078 rushing yards (3.8 per attempt) and 11 TDs.
Nico Iamaleava at his best is a top 3 qb in college football pic.twitter.com/S3pUYq4b01
Unfortunately, Iamaleava's 2026 campaign ended last month when he tore his ACL in a 17-15 win over Oregon, ending his final collegiate season. That said, medicine has come a long way, and there's no reason to believe that Iamaleava can't be a franchise QB in the NFL one day. If anything, his season-ending injury might help him fall to the Eagles on Day 2, depending on where they draft.
One season after leading the Big Ten in passing yards (3,711), yards per completion (14.0) and passing yards per game (285.5) en route to third-team honors, it's safe to say Jayden Maiava picked up from where he left off.
The USC product currently paces the conference with 198 completions, 2,524 passing yards and 20 TDs through nine starts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in six of his nine appearances, which includes a career-best five-TD game against Louisiana back on Sept. 12.
Jayden Maiava is quietly one of the most efficient QBs in the country 👀 ▫️ 86.5 PFF Short Passing Grade (#1 FBS) ▫️ 2,525 Pass Yards (#1 Big Ten, #10 FBS) ▫️ 20 Pass TDs (#1 Big Ten) ▫️ 1.0% Turnover-Worthy Play Rate vs No Blitz (#3 FBS) He’s no longer just the gunslinger,… pic.twitter.com/ZTeQRFhOtD
Maiava isn't without his flaws, which is why he's a projected second-round pick in most mock drafts. His play sometimes drifts into sloppy territory when he isn't completely focused, which can lead to turnovers (one interception in the first four games vs. four INTs in the last five). And, unlike Iamaleava, Maiava isn't a mobile threat, as proven by his averaging 2.4 yards on 173 carries (although he has scored 15 rushing TDs).
The offensive line has gone through injuries and departures this season, but Sirianni and his coaches know how to protect a quarterback when the pieces are there. If the Eagles can recreate that magic, Maiava is the perfect pocket passer to take advantage of that protection—especially with the weapons he'd have at his disposal (DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Eli Stowers, etc.).
Dante Moore is yet another collegiate QB whose season is lost, having sustained a season-ending concussion in September . That said, the Eagles shouldn't let any concerns keep them from drafting the Oregon product.
After all, Moore has the release and pocket presence that NFL coaches admire. His lack of mobility might be a red flag to some, but that's negligible when considering what he can accomplish without his legs being a factor. Moore racked up 39 TDs (to 10 INTs) and 4,491 passing yards in 19 games for the Ducks over the last two seasons, completing 71.4% of passes along the way. He even boasted a 9-0 TD-INT ratio before his current campaign ended, illustrating how efficient he can be.
Let's also not forget that there was a time when Moore was projected to be the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , only to return to Oregon for another season. That potential doesn't just fizzle away overnight, even if this season hasn't gone as planned. The Eagles could be big winners if they can grab Moore and tap into that potential, and other QB-needy teams passing on him might further motivate him to prove the doubters wrong.
Throw in the fact that Hurts could take him under his wing to get him to use his feet more often, and the Eagles have every reason to take a swing on Moore next spring.

title: Eagles Have Nothing to Lose by Giving One Rookie a Sink-or-Swim Test Moving Forward
full_text:
With a losing season almost a guarantee at this point , it's time to start thinking about the future in Philadelphia.
The Eagles used a second-round pick in the 2026 NFL trade to select tight end Eli Stowers from Vanderbilt. It was a relatively high pick for a tight end, but the Eagles clearly viewed Stowers as the potential future of the position in Philadelphia.
Unfortunately, Stowers experienced a slow start to his Eagles tenure. He struggled throughout training camp and was then sidelined for an extended period at the start of the season due to a combination of hamstring and quad injuries.
Stowers finally made his Eagles debut in Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday Night Football. He didn't have any catches in the game, but at least he made it onto the field, which was a dream come true for the Texas native. “It’s a dream come true just to be out there, working, getting better," Stowers said after the game. "Just to be out on the field was a blessing.”
Stowers followed his debut with a three-reception, 53-yard performance against the Washington Commanders in Week 8, then went without a reception again in Week 9 against the Giants.
The Eagles now have eight games remaining in the current campaign, and with their playoff hopes already dashed, getting increased on-field opportunity for some unproven young players should be a top priority for Philly, and Stowers should be at the top of that list.
The Eagles simply need to see whether he is the future of the TE position, and the only way to do that is by throwing him into the deep end.
Despite speculation that they would, the Eagles didn't trade veteran tight end Dallas Goedert before Tuesday's trade deadline, and there's even a chance that he could be back in Philly next season . He's also 31 years old, so the organization needs to identify a succession plan at the position. The Eagles obviously know what they have in Goedert, and with little to play for in terms of a postseason perspective, the team should let Stowers eat into a large chunk of Goedert's playing time moving forward.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
The Eagles will have to make decisions regarding the TE position this offseason. Should they bring back Goedert? Should they look to add another TE in free agency? Should they draft a TE again? The front office won't be able to answer these questions properly unless they see a larger sample size from Sowers—both in the blocking and pass-catching departments.
Whenever Stowers does see the field for Philly, his aim is to be as impactful as possible.
“ Every single play there’s something that you can do to help the offense be successful ,” Stowers said earlier this month (h/t NBC Sports Philadelphia ). “Everybody’s got a job on every single play and so it’s every single rep. How can you be intentional about what your job is? Whether it’s getting open, catching the ball, blocking for somebody, running off for somebody. How can you do that to the best of your abilities? That’s what I try to do.”
Stowers seeing the field more over the final two months of the season will be beneficial for a couple of reasons. First, it will let him gain some much-needed experience in some relatively low-stakes games. It will also provide the organization with an excellent opportunity to evaluate him—and the tight end position as a whole—heading into the offseason.

title: What Fred Johnson & Hollywood Brown's Releases Say About the Eagles’ Plans Moving Forward
full_text:
There could be tumbleweeds blowing through the Eagles' locker room next week. That’s only a slight exaggeration, but there will be plenty of vacant lockers after some roster destruction during the bye week.
The latest move involved the release of veteran swing tackle and sometimes guard Fred Johnson on Friday. That came on the heels of the release of receiver Hollywood Brown , which came on the heels of the release of running back Jaydon Blue earlier in the week. Combine that with the trade of Jordan Davis, and the Eagles have four open roster spots.
The #Eagles are releasing veteran OT Fred Johnson, source says. He's been with the team since 2023. pic.twitter.com/y3Ln9Jm8kN
Cutting Blue signifies that Tank Bigsby and/or Will Shipley could be returning in time for their game against the Steelers on Nov. 22. Bigsby has been on injured reserve since Oct. 6, when a core muscle injury sidelined him. Shipley has been on IR since Oct. 16 with a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot. Both have missed the required four games.
As for the release of Brown, the Eagles are likely to get both DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks back after the bye. Smith has played in just four games this season while battling a hamstring injury, and Wicks has missed three straight games with an ankle injury.
Neither player was placed on IR, so they can return at any time.
Brown wore the number 0, which has become a jinx of sorts since the NFL allowed that number to be worn. Nobody who has worn it since has lasted more than a year. Eagles who wore it previous to Brown are:
Johnson had been with the Eagles for nearly four seasons. He played in six games this year, but played in all 17 games in his previous three years with the team, making 14 starts.
His release signals the Eagles’ readiness to turn to younger players on the offensive line. There is an intriguing prospect on the practice squad who could be summoned. That is Yale’s Kiran Amegadjie, who is 6'5" and 326 lbs. John Ojukwu could also be a possibility.
The Eagles may not be done unloading veterans, either, as they transition to a team that wants to see the younger players play.
Safety Marcus Epps could be in jeopardy, with the possibility that seventh-round pick Cole Wisnieski could see time. Also, the Eagles could release Arnold Ebiketie and/or A.J. Epenesa and turn to seventh-round pick Keyshawn James-Newby. The Eagles thought they had a deal to trade Ebiketie to the Bengals at the trade deadline, but the Bengals backed out.
It might not even be a surprise if the Eagles give Uar Bernard and Josh Weru opportunities over the final eight games.

title: Failed Hollywood Brown Experiment Underscores Eagles' Costly Free-Agent Trade-Off
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles are waiving veteran wide receiver Marquise “Hollywood” Brown , according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, who framed the roster move as a mutual decision both sides viewed as beneficial.⁠
Sources: The #Eagles are waiving WR Marquise “Hollywood” Brown, as both sides agreed it would be beneficial for all involved. Brown had 49 catches for 587 yards and 5 TDs with the #Chiefs last season and is expected to land with a playoff contender. pic.twitter.com/3MGeYJnqpS
Brown, signed in March to a one-year deal worth up to roughly $6.5 million with $5 million guaranteed after snaring 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2025, managed just five receptions for 63 yards across limited appearances for the struggling Eagles offense.
The move comes as the Eagles sit at 2-7 amid a seven-game losing streak and broader roster reshaping under general manager Howie Roseman, including the recent trades of offensive lineman Cam Jurgens and defensive tackle Jordan Davis .
Brown was also widely thought to be a potential pre-deadline trade candidate, but no deal materialized. As a vested veteran released after the trade deadline, Brown must clear waivers and could draw interest from a playoff contender who needs help at receiver.
Brown’s short, unproductive stint in Philadelphia carried a longer-term cost that highlights one of the more painful free agency outcomes of the offseason.
Signing Brown canceled out a projected sixth-round compensatory pick the Eagles would have otherwise received in the 2027 NFL Draft for losing former starting safety Reed Blankenship to the Houston Texans.
Compensatory picks expert Nick Korte noted that the Eagles cannot recoup that selection by cutting Brown, as the relevant rule allowing teams to restore such picks through midseason releases was eliminated in the 2020 collective bargaining agreement. ⁠
Signing Marquise Brown caused the Eagles to cancel out a 6th round compensatory pick from Reed Blankenship going to Houston. The Eagles cannot recoup this comp pick by cutting him, as the rule to do so was done away with in the 2020 CBA. https://t.co/8CHFSdu40S
Earlier projections from PhillyVoice and OverTheCap showed Blankenship’s three-year, $24.75 million deal with Houston (averaging $8.25 million) would project to a sixth-round compensatory pick that Brown’s roughly $5 million deal would offset.⁠
In hindsight, Blankenship’s departure was about pinching pennies and hand-wringing over upside rather than his demonstrated performance and leadership capabilities.
Originally an undrafted free agent out of Middle Tennessee State in 2022, Blankenship rose to become a multi-year starter, team captain, and the secondary’s primary communicator—often described by coaches and teammates as quarterback of the back end.
Blankenship organized coverages, relayed adjustments, kept younger players aligned, and mentored emerging talents such as Cooper DeJean and Drew Mukuba in Philadelphia while contributing to the Super Bowl LIX championship defense.⁠
Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio and others have spoken of replacing his voice and leadership “by committee,” underscoring the void left in a young secondary.
That committee, which has featured Mukuba opposite Marcus Epps, Michael Carter, and Kenny Moore at times, has struggled. Blown coverages have become more plentiful without Blankenship directing traffic.
The failed Brown experiment illustrates the high stakes and moving parts of free agency with production that never materialized, a leadership piece forfeited, and a compensatory pick lost to the fog of misvaluation.

title: Kracz: Examining Eagles' Chances of Avoiding a 15-Game Losing Streak to End the Season
full_text:
It’s a question I’ve been asked a lot during the bye week: Will the Eagles win another game this year?
My guess is they will, but not many. Losing out wouldn’t be so terrible, though, because it would ensure a top-five draft pick this spring and heighten a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman secure a top-five draft choice this spring and accelerate a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman put in place with savvy moves to acquire plenty of draft capital over the next three drafts.
There’s time to debate the course of action the general manager and his staff will take in the 2027 draft, and there will be plenty of discussion. Right now, it’s about finding a way to stem what could be a soul-sucking 15-game losing streak to close out the season.
The losing streak wouldn’t break an NFL record because two teams—the Lions and Browns—had 0-16 seasons.
The eight teams remaining on Philly’s schedule are a combined 34-32-1. That’s not a murderer’s row, but the Eagles have been pushovers too many times during their seven-game losing streak. They've been outscored 179-100 since their last win on Sept. 20 in Tennessee against the Titans, and there doesn't seem to be much hope for success over the final two months.
Maybe they can find a way to defeat the Cardinals in Arizona on Dec. 6. Maybe they can beat the Colts at home on Dec. 13. Perhaps they can beat the 49ers on Jan. 3 and/or the Giants on Jan. 10, but maybe only if both teams have clinched their positioning in the playoffs.
Then there is this: head coach Nick Sirianni is undefeated coming out of a bye week at 5-0. The coach certainly knows the right buttons to push during a week off.
“This week gives us a great opportunity to spend extra time,” said Sirianni. “You're always working self-scout; you're always trying to figure out what you do well, what you don't do well. This week just gives you more opportunities for that.
“We'll use it very similarly to how we've used it in the past. Obviously, we have new pieces here that have not been here, so we'll take the good things that we've used in the past here and the good things that our other coaches have used in the past, and we'll come up with our best path.”
To move to 6-0 following the bye, the Eagles will need to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22 at Lincoln Financial Field. The Week 11 showdown was supposed to be nationally televised at 4:25 but was flexed to a 1 p.m. ET start because of the Eagles’ poor play.
As the Eagles' struggles continue, their upcoming game on CBS against the Pittsburgh Steelers has been flexed from to 1 p.m. The game was originally scheduled for 4:25 p.m. At 2-7, the Eagles have fallen from must-see TV to a team mired in disappointment, plagued by an… pic.twitter.com/h5LtlqKjM7
The Steelers will come in after playing for first place in the AFC North against the Bengals on Sunday night in Cincinnati. Maybe they will be due for a letdown after such an emotional game and turning around to play a 2-7 team.
The Eagles beat Pittsburgh coming out of their 2022 bye, 35-13. Before that, in Sirianni’s first year, Philly beat the Commanders, 27-17. They beat the Chiefs on Monday Night Football, 21-17, in 2023, eased past the Browns, 20-16, in 2024, and knocked off the Packers last year, 10-7, at Lambeau Field.
So, there could yet be some winnable games this season, but to what end? The best path might just be to lose out and secure a top-five draft pick.

title: Eagles Week 10: 3 Most Important Games to Watch During Philadelphia's Bye This Weekend
full_text:
Philadelphia's bye week has arrived at an opportune moment . The Eagles will benefit from an extra week of rest and preparation in the midst of a dreadful seven-game losing streak . While the Birds may not be taking the field in Week 10, that doesn't mean they won't be impacted by the final scores.
This weekend's 14-game slate is highlighted by an overseas matchup of playoff contenders and an intense divisional showdown at Lambeau Field. For the Eagles, the contests involving losing squads have much more meaning, though. Here's a look at three Week 10 games to watch during Philly's bye.
Sunday's battle at Nissan Stadium will mark defensive tackle Jordan Davis' first game since he was dealt by the Eagles at the deadline . Philly sent him to Jacksonville in exchange for two high draft picks. The Jaguars are hoping the massive run-stopper can take their elite defense to the next level.
Playmaker incoming 😮‍💨 📺: NFL + | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/pEiVyFUSCE
It'll be intriguing to see how well Davis gels with veteran pros like Arik Armstead and Josh Hines-Allen. Checking in on a former Eagle isn't the sole reason to watch this divisional duel. The Eagles' 2-7 record has them holding on to the No. 5 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft entering Week 10.
Tennessee (1-7) is one of three NFL teams to earn fewer than two victories through nine weeks. An upset win by the Titans would draw them equal with the Eagles in the standings, strengthening Philly's chance of landing a top-five pick. Take note that the Jaguars and Titans will face off again in Week 12.
The focus remains on the 2027 NFL Draft when highlighting a Week 10 clash between the Dolphins and Colts. Philly could rip off a few wins down the stretch, but its chances of making the playoffs are incredibly slim. Wins from teams below the Eagles in the standings suddenly carry notable weight.
Miami (1-7) and Indianapolis (2-7) are two of those four teams. A Colts' victory would catapult them ahead of the Eagles with a 3-7 record. A Dolphins' victory would place them above the Eagles for the moment, due to strength of schedule. Either way, Philly will hold a top-four pick going into Week 11.
Miami quarterback Kyle McCord will make his NFL debut on Sunday, following Malik Willis' groin injury. He grew up an Eagles fan and played high school football at St. Joseph's Prep. McCord was selected by Philly in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, before being waived after the ensuing preseason.
The Chargers join the Titans, Dolphins, and Colts (first-round pick owned by the Jets) as the four teams currently standing in the Eagles' way of the No. 1 overall pick. Los Angeles travels to Baltimore on Monday night as the only winless squad in the NFL. It is the franchise's first 0-8 start since 2000.
It's possible the Ravens could get caught off guard here. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett to be their starter after both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (turf toe) suffered injuries. Wednesday was Brissett's first practice with the team as he aims to get acclimated quickly .
There have been two winless NFL campaigns since the turn of the century. The 2008 Lions and 2017 Browns each struggled to a 0-16 record. No one wants to join that club, so the Chargers should have added motivation to compete. Any Los Angeles win moving forward benefits Philadelphia.

title: Eagles Can't Hide From Bleak Coaching Staff Reality for Much Longer
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - Nick Sirianni says the Eagles won’t change coaches just to change them. Fair enough. But that feels like it's only delaying the inevitable with Sean Mannion, Chris Kuper, and Ryan Mahaffey.
After another flat loss that pushed the Eagles to 2-7 and a seven-game skid into the team’s bye week, Sirianni was asked about potential staff moves. The head coach repeated a version of the same line he’s used before: everything is on the table, but you don’t just change for the sake of changing because the record looks bad.
Sirianni’s premise is that you look at what’s real, you need conviction, and you don’t react to outside noise. He has publicly stuck with Mannion as the play-caller and has defended Kuper in strong terms, saying the new offensive line coach is coaching hard, teaching fundamentals, and giving players tools even if the results on game days haven't show nit.
Mahaffey, the run-game coordinator and tight ends coach Mannion brought over from Green Bay, has largely stayed out of the direct spotlight, but he is part of the same rebuilt offensive group that replaced Kevin Patullo and, more significantly, the long-tenured Jeff Stoutland.
The problem is that the “real” is hard to isolate right now. Attrition has muddied every evaluation. Jalen Hurts is out for the year with blood clots. Lane Johnson retired. The offensive line has dealt with injuries, scheme changes, and the sudden absence of the coach who had been its constant. Saquon Barkley has played through multiple ailments while DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have missed time at receiver.
The quarterback situation behind Hurts has already flipped from Andy Dalton to Tanner McKee to the Joe Milton experience.
Through it all, the offense keeps failing to generate sustained drives, protect the quarterback, or establish the run. That makes it reasonable to question the scheme, the teaching, and the coordination between Mannion’s calls , Kuper’s line work, and Mahaffey’s run-game plan.
It is also fair to note that the sample is incomplete and chaotic. Injuries and personnel losses make it easier to argue that the coaches haven’t had a clean look—and harder to argue that the current setup is producing anything worth preserving.
Sirianni insists he is results-aware. The results, however, are that the offense has looked disconnected and underwhelming for most of the season under a first-year coordinator.
Claiming you care about results while continuing to operate as if this particular group is the right one creates an obvious tension.
Running it back with Mannion, Kuper, and Mahaffey next season feels increasingly untenable. The body of work, even with the caveats of attrition, has not justified another year of the same voices installing and calling the offense.
That does not mean midseason changes would fix anything. Firing or reassigning coaches now, with the season already lost and the roster battered, is unlikely to produce better football over the remaining schedule.
New voices would still be working with the same depleted personnel, limited practice time, and a quarterback situation that is not ideal.
The practical reality is that you play out the string. You gather whatever additional data you can, you keep the locker room from fracturing further if possible, and you accept that the meaningful decisions—on the offensive coordinator, the line coach, the run-game coordinator, and potentially the head coach himself—belong to the offseason, when there is time to search, hire, and install properly.
Sirianni’s reluctance to change for change’s sake is understandable on its face. But if the evaluation is truly results-driven, the current offensive staff is on thin ice.
While attrition makes the grade incomplete; it does not erase the results. The Eagles can finish the year with the group they have. The harder question is whether they should start the next one with it. The evidence so far suggests they should not.

title: Can Steelers Ever Get Out of DK Metcalf Contract?
full_text:
Another week, another disappointing outing from DK Metcalf for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The 28-year-old was nowhere to be found early in the Steelers' blowout 38-18 loss at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10. Metcalf once again failed to create separation, and on the one occasion he could've created an explosive play with a little under five minutes left during the second quarter, he dropped what would've been right around a 30-yard gain with Jordan Battle in coverage.
While Battle bailed Metcalf out with a taunting penalty before the latter came alive with 54 yards and a touchdown during garbage time in the fourth quarter, it wasn't nearly enough to completely rectify all of the issues currently ongoing with the veteran wide receiver .
Metcalf has not lived up to his four-year, $132 million deal with Pittsburgh, which he signed after arriving in a trade from the Seattle Seahawks in March 2025. Not only that, but the contract looks like a complete albatross and is up there among the worst in the league.
Is there any path for the Steelers to get out of that deal, however?
Pittsburgh restructured Metcalf's contract this past offseason in order to free up almost $18 million in cap space.
As a result, $23.7 million of his salary for the 2026 campaign was converted into a signing bonus and his salary cap charge was lowered by $17.775 million while simultaneously raising his cap charge in future seasons by $5.925 million per year (per Over the Cap ).
Metcalf is also due a $6.5 million roster cut on the fifth day of the 2027 league year and a $5 million roster bonus on the fifth day of the league year in both 2028 and 2029.
Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap).
Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money.
Should they look to cut or trade him in 2028, the dead money would remain the same while the cap savings would jump to $28 million before leaping once again to $35.5 million in 2029.
Parting ways with a player of Metcalf's magnitude might not be popular in the locker room, and it could also send the wrong message.
The Steelers traded a 2025 second-round pick and a 2025 seventh-rounder in exchange for Metcalf and a 2025 sixth-rounder. That's a rather considerable haul, and the organization could be wary of cutting their losses just two years into his tenure.
Still, if Metcalf doesn't turn things around this season, the idea of moving on from him has to at least be weighed.
His decline, most notably in terms of drops and the inability to win downfield, has come as a surprise. Pittsburgh thought it was getting a true No. 1 receiver, and instead, he's playing at replacement level in 2026.
As such, finding a taker for his contract will prove to be difficult. In fact, the Steelers might have to attach a pick just to find a suitable trade.
Releasing Metcalf feels far more probable than sending him elsewhere, but doing so comes with complications as well due to the dead money involved.
There is an avenue to move on from Metcalf, and if Pittsburgh is desperate enough it could theoretically happen next offseason even if it's not overly logical. As of right now, however, it's likely that he'll remain on the team's roster in 2027 despite the fact that he's lost a step, has provided little value this season and is on pace for 816 yards over 17 games, which would be a career low.

title: Is Steelers Season Over?
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- It's hard to recall a loss as bad as this one for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Embarrassing doesn't seem to fit how poor of a performance Week 10 was for the Steelers. Their 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals firmly removed them from contention status and put them into a freefall that makes this season feel closer to finished than anything else.
But is it really over? Well, sometimes history repeats itself, and if that's the case, this year is going to be really disappointing.
The last time the Steelers gave up more than 38 points was Nov. 28, 2021 -- at Cincinnati (41-10)
The last time the Steelers gave up more than 38 points was Nov. 28, 2021 to the Bengals in a 41-10 loss. While they avoided that mark this time around, the 2021 season ended in familiar fashion.
Head coach Mike Tomlin walked into Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City and told the world to "cut your eyelids off." The Steelers then went on to lose 42-21.
Look, a bad loss coming off of a bye week feels terrible for every fan out there. No one is sitting around smiling, enjoying the loss to the Bengals . The players felt the same way in the locker room, as the mood was gloomy, discouraged and somewhat angry.
But the Steelers are 6-3 and one game behind a team that they beat earlier in the year. So, yes, the Bengals won the second battle, but the war is still split evenly, and that's something to hold onto.
"We're gonna address it here in practice and get after it," Cam Heyward said about the loss. "That's the only way that I know how to get better. There's a lot of ball to be played and I'm looking forward to getting better because of this."
The Steelers will travel to Philadelphia next to take on a 2-7 Eagles team led by Joe Milton. They then have an opportunity to come back, potentially 7-3, and host the Denver Broncos with a shot to re-prove themselves in the AFC.
This team will still play the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens, twice, and add the Houston Texans, who are fighting for a playoff spot as well.
There's too much football to be played to say this season is finished.
"I've been a part of this league for a long time," Rodgers said. "There are big wins. There are tough losses. So, we'll deal with this appropriately."
Is it bad? Yes. Is it over? Not yet.

title: 6 Losers, 1 Winner From Steelers' Embarrassing Loss to Bengals
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers were flat-out embarrassed from start to finish by the Cincinnati Bengals in a 38-18 loss on Sunday Night Football .
Coming off their Week 9 bye while riding a four-game win streak, the Steelers felt like they had a fair amount of momentum on their side heading into Paycor Stadium in Week 10.
Unfortunately for them, however, the Bengals were also in the midst of a four-game win streak and simply outclassed them by a wide margin in each facet of the game.
Now sitting at 6-3 and a game back of Cincinnati for first place in the AFC North, Pittsburgh has a lot to ponder over and reevaluate before taking on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11.
With that, here are our winners and losers from one of the Steelers' more lopsided losses in recent memory.
This was arguably the worst Rodgers has looked all season long. The 42-year-old can still move around a bit more than he gets credit for when the pocket starts to collapse, but the lapses in his accuracy, particularly downfield, really showed against the Bengals.
Rodgers never truly looked comfortable until garbage time in the fourth quarter when he threw for a pair of touchdowns before Mason Rudolph came in. That sentiment shows in his 15-of-29 stat line, as he threw for just 143 yards while also starting the contest 0-of-8, which is the first time he had ever done so.
It was déjà vu for Samuel Jr. in this one.
Samuel Jr. had a rough go of it vs. Cincinnati in Week 3, despite Pittsburgh coming away with a 30-27 win, allowing 61 yards and a pair of touchdowns (per Pro Football Focus ) while also taking a backseat to rookie Daylen Everette late in that contest.
On a night where there were plenty of weak links for the Steelers in their rematch with the Bengals, Samuel Jr. was among the team's biggest liabilities. He gave up 134 yards in coverage (per PFF) and was also called for defensive pass interference deep down the field on the first play of the second quarter, which set up Cincinnati's first touchdown of the night.
Wilson has largely been trending up in his third season with Pittsburgh, but his outing against the Bengals really set him back.
While he did lead the Steelers in total tackles with 19, which is his new career-high in a single game and is tied for the most by any player in the NFL this season, that was more so a product of Cincinnati dominating the time of possession battle (35:09 vs. 24:51) and running 65 offensive plays (58 of which came in the first three quarters) than anything else.
Wilson missed three tackles in this contest and allowed 98 yards in coverage on 10 receptions (per PFF ), highlighting just how poor of a performance the 26-year-old turned in.
Once again, Amarius Mims completely shut Watt out.
Watt did not register a single pressure against the Bengals' star right tackle in Week 3, and the same held true this time around as well (per PFF ).
Though Watt's had a resurgence this year with 7.5 sacks, which had already eclipsed his 2025 total of 7.0 sacks over 14 games, he can't disappear against the best tackles the league has to offer if Pittsburgh's defense wants any chance of truly establishing itself as the cream of the crop or even close to it.
If there was any silver lining for the Steelers, it was that Nichols finally got an opportunity and made the most of it as the team took out its starters and turned to its reserves in the fourth quarter.
The 25-year-old had just two carries for six yards over two contests for Pittsburgh coming into this game. On six carries vs. Cincinnati, however, he ran for 43 yards while also adding a catch for two yards.
As is also the case with Rodgers, Metcalf's slight redemption from a numbers perspective with two catches for 54 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter when the game was already far out of reach meant next to nothing.
Generating separation remains a chore for Metcalf, and he's failed to haul in throws downfield at an alarming rate for a 28-year-old who is supposed to thrive in that regard while still being in his prime.
Metcalf has been a complete disappointment for the Steelers, and considering he's under contract through the 2029 season while making an average annual salary of $33 million, there might be no way  out for the organization in the near future.
Much like Watt, Highsmith was essentially nonexistent against the Bengals.
The 29-year-old recorded zero pressures ( per PFF ) in a contest for the first time since last season's Wild Card round loss to the Houston Texans. It was also just the third time Highsmith had failed to log a pressure during the regular season since the beginning of the 2021 campaign.

title: Steelers vs. Bengals Takeaways: Season Over?
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Maybe Ja'Marr Chase was right when he said the Pittsburgh Steelers versus Cincinnati Bengals rivalry isn't that strong.
The Steelers move to 6-3 on the season in the most embarrassing fashion, losing 38-18 at Paycor Stadium. This team came into Week 10 red-hot and looking to prove they're the real deal in the AFC and the leaders of the AFC North. They proved the complete opposite of both.
Now, the questions aren't about how far they can go but how low they can fall. This team struggled in every facet of the game. And these takeaways show that.
This is a real stat. Just before the two-minute warning in this game, Aaron Rodgers was 0/7. Joe Burrow was 21/26 for 245 yards and two touchdowns.
Genuinely one of the graphics of all time pic.twitter.com/jvitfuIqw0
The entire Steelers team looked bad in this loss, but none more than Rodgers. Some plays, he was rattled by the pass rusher before the ball was even snapped. Others, he was inaccurate and nearly throwing interceptions. And the cherry on top was him being so worried at times that he would instantly dump it off to a running back for negative yards.
Rodgers still shows he has it, even at 42 years old. But against the Bengals, he was atrocious. Maybe the worst player on the field.
The Steelers desperately need a WR1. Germie Bernard is the closest thing they've got, but he's not good enough yet, and DK Metcalf is not the answer.
Omar Khan's decision not to make a move at the trade deadline will continue to haunt Pittsburgh. Aaron Rodgers doesn't have the weapons and when he finds himself without anyone open, he doesn't always try to extend plays. Most times, actually, he gives up early when no one is open immediately.
This offense is in trouble without someone breaking out. Hopefully, Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. provide enough. If they don't, don't expect this offense to be able to compete against high-powered offenses like Cincinnati's.
At this point, it's hard to justify DK Metcalf playing more snaps than Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. when they return. He adds very little value to this offense and yes, he does draw attention from the defense, but that's only useful if Rodgers can find other open targets.
Metcalf can't even be relied on to catch open passes at this point.
dk metcalf drop pic.twitter.com/zvdq9PczjP
Yes, he finished with two receptions, 54 yards and a touchdown. None of that came until the fourth quarter, when the Steelers were down 31-3.
The offensive and passing-game struggles are not all of his fault, but when you're paid over $30 million a year to be an elite receiver and barely pass as a playable one, the target is going to be on your back.
Metcalf, just plain and simple, isn't very good right now. At times, he's not good at all. And the more fans are reminded of it, the more infuriated they become that the team's WR1 is an overpaid former starter who may not have "it" anymore. And the Steelers desperately need "it."
Asante Samuel Jr.'s return to an NFL starting lineup is impressive. It's great to see him bounce back and overcome a neck injury that nearly ended his career much earlier than it deserved to end. But in Pittsburgh, there are six games a year that don't fit his size or play style, and those are crucial games.
Samuel Jr. just isn't big enough to play against the Bengals. He's not big enough to battle with Tee Higgins, who continues to make it look easy when matched up against him. And for Ja'Marr Chase, no one in the NFL can say they have the upper hand over him, but Samuel Jr. doesn't even come close.
Daylen Everette is going to come with mistakes. Every rookie does. But he has the size to compete in these AFC North showdowns and Pittsburgh needs to test him out. It's not the right answer but it's something. Samuel Jr. just doesn't have it against Cincinnati.
The Steelers lost Mason McCormick to what looked like a significant ankle injury just before halftime. If McCormick is going to miss the remainder of the season, Pittsburgh's offensive line just got significantly worse, and the blow may be their second toughest to overcome.
Zach Frazier and McCormick have been Pittsburgh's best two offensive linemen this season. McCormick, a third-year fourth-round pick, has been playing at a Pro Bowl level. At times, he's been their most reliable player up front, and as the group has continued to grow together, he's been a key piece in that foundation.
The offensive line took a clear step backward against the Bengals. Now they need to navigate without one of their best players, and all of a sudden, the problems feel overwhelming for this offense.
Well, at least for now, you can put those Pittsburgh Steelers Super Bowl dreams to bed. This team is a big of a "pretender" as they come. This season, they've played two teams in the AFC playoff race on the road, and both times, they've lost in blowouts.
This team is just not serious when it comes to competing with high-powered offenses. They can't keep up in the secondary and their offense has zero juice when Jaylen Warren isn't rushing for 100 yards.
You remove the superpower of No. 30 and this entire team shuts down. And their four-game winning streak was impressive, but it was tight games against losing teams. That's not going to translate to real competition.
This season isn't over yet. But it doesn't look bright as the second-half is only going to get harder.

title: Steelers' Mason McCormick Suffers Ankle Injury Against Bengals
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' first half against the Cincinnati Bengals was a total disaster, but the worst moment came when one of their top offensive lineman suffered a serious-looking injury. Coming out of their bye week, the Steelers had the chance to send a message to the Bengals, the division and the rest of the AFC.
Instead, the Steelers completely stumbled out of the gate. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers missed the first eight passes he attempted, and the run game was stifled by the Bengals' defense. Their offense failed to match Cincinnati's productivity in the first half, punting on each of their first three drives.
Toward the end of the first half, the Steelers began to find life on offense. That's when starting left guard Mason McCormick went down with what appeared to be a right ankle injury. While trying to keep a Bengals defensive lineman out of Rodgers' face, McCormick
He looked to be in serious distress after the play, and medical trainers tended to him on the field. After placing an aircast on the injured leg, the medical staff carted him off the field. Most of the Steelers roster came to greet him and give well wishes to the starting guard before he exited the field.  Shortly after McCormick was taken off the field, the Steelers ruled him out for the game.
Mason McCormick ruled OUT with an ankle injury
Without McCormick in the left guard position, the Steelers' offensive line takes a serious blow. McCormick has been arguably the top lineman in Pittsburgh this season, and he's been a crucial piece in the team's success on the ground.
With the third-year guard out, the Steelers have to turn to their bench. Players like Spencer Anderson have experience at the left guard position, while backup center Ryan McCollum is another option who could step up while McCormick is out.
Anderson has starting experience with the Steelers at multiple positions. He's played across the offensive line, most recently starting the season as the right guard. He was replaced after the team's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, and he's been used primarily as an extra lineman in jumbo packages.
McCollum is a player who has plenty of experience and versatility as well. He's the backup center to Zach Frazier, but like Anderson, he can move around the offensive line.
The injury also brings up rookie Gennings Dunker. One of the team's recent third-round picks was placed on Injured Reserve earlier in the season. At the time, it was a tough development, but something the o-line could withstand. Now that McCormick is out for potentially a long time, the Steelers ' lack of depth at guard is becoming a problem in a hurry.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Offense Gets Their Tight End Against Bengals
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers got some good news regarding the availability of one of their top skill position players ahead of a Week 10 clash against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
Tight end Pat Freiermuth, who was added to the injury report and listed as questionable the day before the game with an illness, will be active vs. Cincinnati.
The Steelers appear closer to getting wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) back from the reserve/injured list. With both remaining out for the time being, however, Freiermuth's importance to the team's offense remains heightened for a crucial battle between two 6-2 AFC North foes.
Following what was a bit of a lackluster 2025 campaign (486 yards, four touchdowns) for Freiermuth in his first year working with Aaron Rodgers, the hope was that he'd bounce back this season while continuing to build a stronger rapport with the future Hall of Fame quarterback.
Freiermuth was impressive during training camp and began the year on a high note with a  46-yard, one-touchdown performance in Pittsburgh's Week 1 victory over the Atlanta Falcons.
The 28-year-old has largely been inconsistent ever since, however, failing to break the 40-yard mark in a single game from that point on, outside of posting 44 yards and a pair of touchdowns in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
All in all, Freiermuth is on pace for 499 yards and nine touchdowns this season, the latter of which would represent a career-high.
He's filled his role admirably and made more of an impact than he did a year ago, though it still feels like he has the potential to take his game up another level.
Simply put, Freiermuth has owned Cincinnati throughout his career.
His 649 yards vs. the Bengals over 11 games is his most against any team by a wide margin, with his 349 yards vs. the Cleveland Browns marking his second-highest total in that regard.
Furthermore, Freiermuth's 111-yard, two-touchdown showing in the Steelers' Week 7 loss to Cincinnati on Thursday Night Football last season was just the second time in franchise history that a tight end finished a game with 100 or more receiving yards and two or more receiving touchdowns.
While he put up just 30 yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory over the Bengals earlier this season, Freiermuth's history against Cincinnati should inspire some confidence that he can turn in another standout performance in primetime at Paycor Stadium.

title: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, safety DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warm-ups at Paycor Stadium and has been ruled out vs. Cincinnati as a result.
Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati.
Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation.
Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field.
The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign.
Jaquan Brisker, Robert Spears-Jennings and Jalen Ramsey now become all the more important for the Steelers now that Elliott will be sidelined against the Bengals.
It's not unfamiliar territory for that trio, as Elliott has only appeared in two games and played 43 defensive snaps since being activated from IR ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris.
Holding up in coverage as a group on the back end of the defense against the likes of Chase and Higgins would've been a big ask even with Elliott on the field, though, and being down a veteran like that could have reverberating effects when facing a passing offense that averages the most yards per game (285.5) in the league.
Where the Steelers' safeties shouldn't have much of an issue holding down the fort, however, is against the Bengals' run game.
Cincinnati is averaging just 85.6 rushing yards per contest, which was the third-lowest mark in the NFL entering the day, while Pittsburgh allows the third-fewest yards on the ground per game at 83.9.
The likes of Ramsey, Brisker and Spears-Jennings are all capable of stepping up from the second level of the defense and making plays against the run, and with a favorable matchup in that regard vs. the Bengals, the Steelers shouldn't feel the loss of Elliott as much as they will in coverage.

title: Steelers Still Waiting to Give Veteran WR Chance
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers only made one roster announcement before their Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals, activating Derrick Harmon off of Injured Reserve.
Besides that, the only news that came from the team the day before kickoff with the Bengals was Pat Freiermuth being listed as questionable with an illness. It's still unknown if he's going to play against Cincinnati on Sunday Night Football, as the team doesn't need to make that decision until 90 minutes before kickoff.
Heading into the game, no practice squad members are playing in Week 10. The Steelers are rolling with their active roster and that's it, which has everyone thinking about one name who many believed would get his first shot of the season with the Steelers this weekend.
When Marquez Valdes-Scantling signed to Pittsburgh's practice squad , he was viewed as the potential filler for a banged-up depth chart. With Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. on Injured Reserve and Ben Skowronek missing time with a calf injury, MVS felt like the answer to the Steelers' problems.
A veteran with experience in Pittsburgh, who has plenty of playing time with Aaron Rodgers and even spent his rookie year learning from Mike McCarthy in Green Bay. It felt like the easy answer for the Steelers, as they were searching for wideout help.
So far, though, that hasn't been the case. Valdes-Scantling has yet to get a call-up from the practice squad, and the Steelers appear to be getting healthy enough to avoid making call-ups at the position. With Skowronek back in the lineup, Pittsburgh chose to let their active roster rock in Week 10.
DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, Brandon Smith, Skowronek and Kaden Wetjen will be enough for the Steelers at wide receiver in this matchup.
The Steelers clearly aren't looking for Valdes-Scantling's help now, but that doesn't mean he's not a good practice squad player to have. After struggling to stay on a roster this season, MVS probably isn't going to be poached by another team.
So, the Steelers can be patient. They can allow their room to get healthy and hope that the group is good enough to solve their struggles at the wide receiver position. If not, they can test out MVS later in the season, keeping his three call-ups available until they need them.
Don't expect Valdes-Scantling to be a name for the Steelers in the coming weeks. Instead, look for Wilson and Pittman Jr. to return . And Pittsburgh is going to keep their emergency option just that until they're forced to utilize him.

title: Steelers' Drew Allar is Turning Heads Again
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are one of several teams keeping a close eye on the 2027 NFL Draft class and its quarterback selection. But that isn't stopping their excitement about a player in-house whom they already drafted.
When Drew Allar showed up in Pittsburgh, he looked pretty bad. It's not a shot at Allar, it's just an observation. His footwork was all over the place; he was reworking his throwing mechanics and he just didn't look comfortable at all, which led to inaccurate passes and strange release points.
He was a clear work in progress and, throughout the summer, showed a little bit of it. Not a ton, but there were definitely moments when you realized Allar was taking steps forward with his accuracy and timing.
By the end of the preseason, he looked much more comfortable as an NFL quarterback than he did when he stepped on the field for rookie minicamp.
After the preseason, the talk of Allar disappeared. No one was checking in, and no one was talking about his chances of starting next year. It was just silence and a waiting game, trying to put all of the options together throughout the college football season.
Then, suddenly, Allar's name popped up again. Steelers media members started talking about him, which sparked conversation amongst fans about his future.
At this moment, I would say that Drew Allar has an 87.9% chance of being the Steelers' starting quarterback in Week 1 of 2027.
Because Allar started looking a lot better.
Over the last several days, the most notable player when watching practice has been the rookie quarterback. He's moving well in drills, throwing with a much, much more comfortable motion, and his footwork looks much more sound than it ever did during the summer or preseason.
It was like all of a sudden everyone noticed how far Allar has progressed since the regular season started. And it was a reminder that the work continues for players who don't play on Sundays, even after Week 1 kicks off.
It's hard not to agree with Kaboly, either. At least going into training camp, you have to imagine that Allar is going to be the first name to get a shot as the starting quarterback.
At first, that belief was only because Mike McCarthy hand-picked him with his first draft in Pittsburgh. But now, it's because McCarthy's work with Allar seems to be paying off, and that's with Allar acting as the fourth-string quarterback.
Imagine how much progression could come with him being the primary guy McCarthy is focusing on.
So, if you've been denying yourself the excitement of Allar, maybe it's time to let yourself be optimistic. He's showing the progression he should be. And right now, it's easy to see him taking over in 2027 for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Steelers vs. Bengals Bold Predictions: Alex Highsmith's Career Day
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers attempt to stake their claim in the AFC North and the conference playoff picture.
Taking on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Steelers can take the season series against their rival while earning their seventh victory of the season. After a bye week, the team is hoping to shake off the cobwebs before Week 10 action begins.
It’s the middle of the regular season schedule, but there is a playoff atmosphere to this matchup. The Steelers can get their seventh win of the year, and a few of these bold predictions might come true as well.
It’s been a little too quiet for veteran outside linebacker Alex Highsmith. He recorded 0.5 sacks in the team’s latest win, but he hasn’t recorded an individual sack since Week 2 against the New England Patriots.
His previous in-game highs are 11 tackles and 3.0 sacks. Against the Bengals this week, Highsmith breaks the tackles record and posts multiple sacks.
Jaylen Warren is the best piece of the Steelers’ offense, and It’s undeniable. He’s one of the best running backs in the NFL this season and he’s single-handedly carried this offense at times.
What he hasn’t done, however, is consistently find the endzone. He has just two rushing touchdowns and one receiving touchdown on the season, with two of his total scores coming in the same contest against the Indianapolis Colts.
That changes in Week 10. Against the Bengals, I predict Warren will dominate both out of the backfield and as a receiving threat. As a receiver is where I believe he will do his most damage, finding the end zone twice on passing plays.
The Bengals might have a plan to limit Warren on the ground, but that’s not enough to keep him from making an impact.
One area the Bengals have been so successful on offense is converting on third down. It doesn’t matter if they have significant yardage to gain, they tend to convert. Senior NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno shared an interesting statistic recently that sheds light on this specifically.
The Bengals are the NFL leaders at converting on third down whenever they have at least seven yards to gain. When they are facing a third and long situation like that, the Bengals are picking up the first down 39.5% of the time. It leads the next-best team, the San Francisco 49ers, by nearly 5%.
Highest 3rd & long (7+ yards) conversion rate this season: 1. Bengals – 39.5% 2. 49ers – 34.6% 3. Raiders – 31.4% 4. Panthers – 30.0% 5. Jaguars – 29.2% 6. Bills - 28.9% 7. Seahawks – 28.8% 8. Bears – 28.6% 9. Chiefs – 28.2% 10. Lions – 27.9% Lowest: 28. Vikings – 18.5%…
The Steelers are likely to put the Bengals in third and long situations throughout Week 10. The only difference between Cincinnati’s previous success and this matchup, is Pittsburgh's pass rush. While the Bengals lead the league in pass touchdowns and third and long conversions, the Steelers are the best team when it comes to taking down the quarterback. It's a matchup of two unstoppable forces, and I'm betting on Pittsburgh's pass rush to limit Joey B and the Bengals to less than a 20% success rate on third down.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Hanich Panic Meter: Seahawks' JSN Could Break Single Season Record
full_text:
In just two years, Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba became a No. 1 pass-catcher. Just one year late last season, JSN became a superstar and became the league’s offensive player of the year. He might finish up his fourth season with one of the most legendary achievements.
​ JSN, once again, played like the elite player he is and became the Seahawks’ offense to help Seattle win 21-13 at the Las Vegas Raiders. He caught eight receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Raiders. Just like he was last season, JSN is on pace to break Calvin Johnson’s single-season record of 1,964 yards set in 2012. There is a great chance he may accomplish it in 16 games as opposed to 17 games.
​Through 10 games this season, JSN has caught 79 receptions for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns. He is only 758 yards away from breaking Johnson’s record. For JSN to break the record, he would have to average 108.3 yards in each of the remaining seven games. To break the record in the same 16-game timeframe as Johnson, JSN would have to average 126.4 yards in each of the remaining six games,
​He has accounted for at least 100 yards in eight of the ten games this season. It doesn’t matter if it’s Sam Darnold or Drew Lock throwing him the ball; he finds a way to open. He has 721 receiving yards from Darnold and 486 in nearly four games from Lock. He is easily a solid path to be named offensive player of the year for a second consecutive season and, possibly, league MVP if the award were quarterback-focused.
​JSN was on pace to break Johnson’s all-time receiving record last season. Through 11 games last season, JSN caught 80 receptions for 1,313 yards and seven touchdowns. This meant he only had 652 more yards in the remaining six games to break the record. It was at that point, there was some offensive fatigue and the running game had to be re-established. JSN would only account for 480 yards during the final games to finish with 1,793 yards.
​Last season, it seemed like it was a surprise that JSN was so elite at creating enough separation and making big plays after the catch with his speed and elusiveness. This season, despite being mentioned as one of the top receivers in the league, he is still getting open so much. He has a great feel with either Darnold or Lock throwing him the ball . It seems like no matter how many times the opposing defenses game plan around him, JSN still finds ways to get open.

title: 3 Observations in Seahawks Week 10 Win vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are kicking their feet back after a 21-13 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 action inside Allegiant Stadium.
The Seahawks needed to take care of business before their bye week, and they did just that. Their matchup against Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza proved exactly why the Seahawks have the top defense in the league and propelled them to victory.
Here's a look at three observations from the matchup.
Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued to flex his dominance this season. He added 8 catches for 171 yards and a touchdown to his league-leading total, which puts him on pace to be the first player in league history to have over 2,000 receiving yards in a season.
Smith-Njigba was responsible for all but 61 of the team's passing yards, which shows the difference between him and the rest of Seattle's receiving core. The Seahawks would greatly benefit from having another receiver to take some attention off of him. Even though Cooper Kupp had a touchdown, it's not enough.
Ultimately, the Seahawks still won the game, and they will take it at this point. If he were to miss any time due to injury, it would be season-altering and the offense would struggle mightily.
Luckily for the Seahawks, they have the top defense in the league, and they made Mendoza look like a rookie in Week 10. The Seahawks surrendered just 163 total yards of offense, which will improve their average going into their bye week. The Seahawks sacked Mendoza six times during the afternoon, including two from cornerback Devon Witherspoon.
As long as the offense can take care of the football and score on a couple of drives throughout the game, the Seahawks will have a chance to be any team in the back half of the season and playoffs.
Drew Lock is now 3-0 as the Seahawks' starting quarterback this season. That could spark a debate during the bye week about whether he should be the permanent QB1 over Sam Darnold, who has struggled to take care of the football this season. Darnold's nine interceptions in seven games are an issue that Seattle's offense has been dealing with all year.
Lock has been playing well enough to spark some small whispers of conversation, but his two fumbles today likely will hand the ball back to Darnold when he is healthy and ready to go.
There is reason to believe Darnold will be available for Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. If he is, Seattle will have to make a big decision between the two. Outside of the fumbles, Lock was surgical against the Raiders, but if turnovers are the biggest issue for the quarterback and both of them have struggled in that department, the team might as well stick with the default, which is Darnold.

title: Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba Criticizes Controversial OPI Call vs. Raiders
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba got off to a slow start against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but he nearly got going much earlier if not for a questionable offensive pass interference call.
In the first quarter, Smith-Njigba was flagged for pushing off Raiders cornerback Eric Stokes on a 29-yard catch-and-run touchdown. While subjective, of course, his arm extension was pretty minimal by NFL standards, but Stokes fell at the top of the route. That is likely what drew the flag, in conjunction with the small push.
When asked postgame whether he disagreed with the call, Smith-Njigba gave his honest thoughts.
OPI on JSN pic.twitter.com/QOsXFrFI2K
“Yeah, definitely. It didn’t feel like I pushed off at all,” Smith-Njigba said. “We had some hand battling; I tend to snap off pretty quick, and he fell. That’s kind of my perspective of it. Refs are human; it sucks that they go out there and make mistakes, but it happens.”
It was similar to a play that Smith-Njigba was flagged for in the Seahawks’ Week 8 Monday night loss to the Chicago Bears. The refs appear to be cracking down on his push-offs, in particular, especially as Smith-Njigba continues to dominate NFL defenses across the league.
“It’s always the next-play mentality,” Smith-Njigba said. “You can’t sulk in the bad stuff or the good stuff. I just try to lock in every single play. That’s our mission on offense: No matter what, just keep pushing. So, definitely proud of my guys and how we went out there and fought today.”
Oh damn, surprised they called that on JSN pic.twitter.com/NvFHtA7KW2
Smith-Njigba had just 11 receiving yards in the first half before exploding for 144 yards and a touchdown in the third quarter alone. He finished the game with eight catches for 171 yards and the score.
The Seahawks superstar is still on pace to break the all-time single-season receiving record with 79 catches for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns through 10 games. He is slightly ahead of his 10-game pace from 2025 and is currently projected to total 134 catches, 2,051 yards and 20 touchdowns by the end of the season.
If he continues at the current pace, Smith-Njigba will beat Calvin Johnson’s 2012 record of 1,964 receiving yards in a single season. Opponents haven’t found a way to shut him down, and Sunday’s game proved that he isn’t slowing down anytime soon.

title: Seahawks 'Not Sure' About Injury Severity to Abe Lucas, George Holani
full_text:
Already banged up, the Seattle Seahawks unfortunately didn’t get out of their Week 10 win against the Las Vegas Raiders without new injuries.
Starting right tackle Abraham Lucas exited the game early and did not return after running back George Holani had already left . Defensive tackle Jarran Reed also exited the game and was ruled doubtful to return, but he did go back into the game.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said after the game that he is unsure of the severity of both Lucas and Holani’s injuries. He did confirm that Lucas has an ankle sprain.
“Abe is an ankle; to what degree, we’re not sure,” Macdonald said. “George is a knee; to what degree, we’re not sure.”
Backup tackle Bobby Hart finished the game for the Seahawks at right tackle, adding a third replacement to an offensive line that was already missing starting left tackle Charles Cross and left guard Quenton Nelson.
Surprisingly, even with that many changes up front, Seattle totaled 150 rushing yards — its third-most of the season — and protected backup quarterback Drew Lock well enough that he completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions.
At running back, the Seahawks only had Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price available for the rest of the game. Holani was the third running back, but luckily he wasn’t needed in the win.
Macdonald wouldn’t commit to a potential post-bye-week plan for the offensive line if Lucas is forced to miss time. Cross has already missed three games and could return after the bye, which would likely lead to Josh Jones moving to the right side if Lucas is out.
“I’m not sure what we’d do … We’ll see how serious it is with Abe, and then we’ll put a plan together, and I’ll fill you guys in when we make that decision,” Macdonald added.
The Seahawks were already missing defensive lineman Leonard Williams, quarterback Sam Darnold, backup running back Emanuel Wilson, Cross and Nelson entering the game. The hope now is that most of those players will be able to return when the Seahawks face the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
Macdonald said the team will be off until Monday, Nov. 23, when they return from the bye.
