title: 3 Winners, 1 Loser in Seahawks Victory vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are celebrating after a 21-13 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders inside Allegiant Stadium in Week 10.
The Seahawks started off rough, giving up a touchdown early to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in his first career start , but they settled down and kept them out of the end zone for the remainder of the game.
Here's a look at the winners and losers from the matchup.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued to establish himself as the league's best wide receiver. He added to his league lead in receiving yards with 171 on eight catches and a 71-yard touchdown that was arguably the play of the day.
Drew Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba is looking like a dangerous connection 👀 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/6hXecLdtM6
Smith-Njigba's presence in the offense shakes everything up for the Seahawks and they wouldn't be the same without him on the field.
Sharpe had another strong week as the team's RB1. He ran the ball 20 times for 94 yards, giving them a strong presence on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Making sure the run game was established was an important part of Seattle's game plan going into the week, and Sharpe helped execute that to a tee.
Rookie Jadarian Price found the end zone as well, which means the Seahawks' vision of having a reliable running back room with depth is reigning true.
Star cornerback Devon Witherspoon had a strong performance against the Raiders. No receiver had more than 22 yards during the game, apart from running back Ashton Jeanty, who led the way with four catches for 46 yards.
Witherspoon had a pair of sacks, which added up to six for the team in the game. He proved why the Seahawks made him the league's highest-paid cornerback during the offseason.
Drew Lock had a solid game, recording 240 passing yards and 20 rushing yards. He completed 14 of 17 passes and connected on a pair of touchdowns: one to JSN and the other to Cooper Kupp.
Lock did fumble the ball twice, including once on the team's opening possession, which has been an issue for the offense throughout the season. Limiting these turnovers is what will turn Seattle from good to great. Had these turnovers not happened, the argument for Lock to start after the bye week would have been stronger. However, it might not be the case.

title: Jarran Reed Injury Update: Seahawks Defensive Tackle Leaves in Second
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting dismantled one player at a time today. George Holani was minor enough to be barely noticed, Abraham Lucas hasn’t played well this season, but now, things are getting dire. Jarran Reed left the game with a toe injury, and as of this article hasn’t yet returned, with his return being labeled Doubtful by the team already.
This injury is a disaster for the Seahawks, who are already without Leonard Williams and have not played the run especially well so far today. Byron Murphy will have to do all the heavy lifting on the interior now, and Rylie Mills now has to play a lot. Brandon Pili might be able to fill some gaps, but this is much too thin for the Seahawks defense to be itself.
Combined with the other injuries the Seahawks have right now, you have to wonder if it's just becoming too tall of a task to win against even a team as deeply flawed as the Raiders. With Mills on the field, the Raiders are going to pound the run and take away Seattle's opportunity to force Mendoza to make mistakes. And beyond this game, well, at least it's the bye week.
Rylie Mills and Brandon Pili are the names to watch right now, as they're going to see a lot of action in this second half. Mills has been very poor so far this season, especially holding up against the run, so asking him to play in a competitive game is very risky. He's also been a relative no-show as a pass rusher, so there's no  particular upside to Mills getting more reps right now.
Pili is a little more stout, able to hold his ground against the run, but he's most certainly nothing special as far as an NFL player goes. However, this team should have expected Jarran Reed to not make it through the entire 17 game season at his age, especially with him still taking quite a few snaps. Now they just have to get Leonard Williams back to be able to survive it.
Reed has been solid and effective this season, making big contributions to the NFL's top run defense. Obviously, his age shows up on occasion, but he remains an important part of this defense as well as a great leader in the locker room. His absence will be felt as they try to punch in a second half comeback win. Again, at least we have a bye week, so at least he has extra time to get back.

title: Abraham Lucas Injury Update: Seahawks Lose Right Tackle in Second Quarter
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are down 10-7, and may now be down a starter on the offensive line. Abraham Lucas, the starting right tackle since 2022 (health permitting), went down on a play and stayed down with what seems to be some kind of leg injury. After some minutes, he was able to get up and walk off on his own, but walked to the locker room.
During some contact in the pocket between linemen, rushers, and QB Drew Lock, Lucas’s leg got injured. It’s unclear if the injury is to the knee or lower leg, perhaps the ankle, but it’s significant enough to get backup right tackle Bobby Hart onto the field for the time being. The Seahawks have already declared him Doubtful to return.
Given the speed at which the team declared him Doubtful, I can only assume they believe it's likely serious. Don't expect to see him again today, so Bobby Hart will have to step up in a big way. The Raiders have come out into a 10-7 lead, so the Seahawks won't be able to just wind the clock and get out with a cheap win. Beyond this week, well, at least we have a bye.
Obviously, this continues a season that has been derailed in part by a flood of injuries to the offensive line, making it impossible for them to build synergy and familiarity. Of course, some might point out that Lucas has played poorly this year, with many ugly reps and hits on quarterbacks allowed. The first fumble of the game by Lock came on a play where Lucas was badly beat.
In the game in two weeks? Perhaps I'd agree, when Charles Cross is back in the lineup and Josh Jones is available to step in at right tackle. But in this game, where Cross is out and Jones is already on the field on the left side? I'm not so sure. Bobby Hart has played sparingly in recent years, and his play throughout his career has been quite poor. Not excited to see this play out.
The Seattle Seahawks obviously are going to have to score some points today to win, as they already trail 10-7. The question is, how many will they be able to score with three backups now on the offensive line. I seriously doubt Lucas is back today, so the challenge is cut out for the players we still have.

title: George Holani Injury Update: Seahawks Backup RB Leaves Early
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks lost a fumble in the first couple minutes of the game today, and are in the process of getting driven down on by the Las Vegas Raiders offense right now. But the real pain right now belongs to George Holani, who departed the game after that initial drive and has not yet returned, with what the team is calling a knee injury.
Shortly after the Raiders scored their touchdown, it was announced that Holani had a knee injury, and is Doubtful to return. The speed of that declaration is obviously pessimistic, as is the status itself. Fortunately, the Seahawks do have other running backs they can turn to right now, and Holani was likely going to be kept almost entirely to special teams today.
It seemed like the injury happened while blocking on the opening kickoff, since Holani wasn't on the field for either of Seattle's two first offensive plays. It is worth noting that Holani has been playing through assorted injuries all season long, although this is presumed to be a new one as George hasn't even been listed on the injury report for several weeks.
I speculated previously that Holani would have been placed on IR if not for the fact that the team needed running backs thanks to the absence of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet. Sometimes it's felt like he's been held together by duct tape, so if the dam breaks eventually I won't be shocked. There's clearly not much room for him on the offense any more anyway.
While I don't think the Holani injury will be meaningful long-term, it's worth noting that the Seattle Seahawks have another one of their running backs on the inactive list today. Emanuel Wilson, who started and played respectably over the few games the team needed him, was a healthy scratch. So, if something were to happen to Charbonnet or Price today, things would get tricky.
Velus Jones is also no longer on the roster, so turning to him is not a possibility at this point in time. The Seahawks should be okay for today, but if this is the last straw for Holani's health this year it might merit bringing Jones back. For now, the Seahawks turn their focus to beating the Raiders with the players they do have. Expect Holani to miss some time at this point.

title: How Seahawks Inactives Change Things vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are warming up for their Week 10 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders , but a few players won't be out on the field for the team.
The Seahawks already ruled a few players out prior to the game due to the injury report, but a couple of other players have been scratched as well. Here's a look at the full list of inactives for the Seahawks and Raiders.
Darnold is on the sidelines for the second straight week dealing with quad and rib injuries, which will thrust Drew Lock into the starting spot once again. Lock pulled out a win last week as the starter against the Arizona Cardinals, so the team hopes he can get another victory against the Raiders.
Two starting offensive linemen are out in Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross. This means Josh Jones and Anthony Bradford will take their spots in the starting lineup. It's a big loss for the Seahawks, but the team likes their depth in the trenches, and it is the best the team can do going into the game.
Another big loss for the team comes with Leonard Williams being on the sidelines. This is his second consecutive game on the sidelines as he deals with a shoulder injury that held him out of practice all week long.
Rookies Avery Smith and Deven Eastern are healthy scratches, along with running back Emanuel Wilson, who has seen his role diminish with the returns of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet.
The most notable name on the inactive list for the Raiders is offensive lineman Bryce Cabeldue, who was a sixth-round pick by the Seahawks last year and joined Las Vegas back in September after Seattle placed him on the waiver wire.
The kickoff between the Seahawks and Raiders is scheduled for 1:05 pm PT inside Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: Seahawks Confidence Meter: New Winning Streak After Week 10
full_text:
This 2026 NFL Season has been difficult for the Seattle Seahawks (5-4). From costly turnovers and inconsistency from the coaching staff to injuries, the Seahawks have had some moments they wish they could take back. The lack of consistency has hurt the Seahawks so much that the team is on the verge of accomplishing something they haven’t done since Week 1 and Week 2: a winning streak.
​Seattle started the season 2-0 with wins over the New England Patriots and the Arizona Cardinals, but it has since gone 3-4. Every time the Seahawks get a win, turnovers and inconsistent play plague the team. They are coming off a much-needed 17-3 developmental win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. The Seahawks are looking for a huge win at the Las Vegas Raiders with explosive performances on both sides of the ball.
The Seahawks aren’t just looking to beat the Raiders; they’re looking for some version of themselves in terms of dominance. Tight end AJ Barner said they are still searching for their identity. The Seahawks didn’t lose too much from their Super Bowl-winning team last season, but they’ve had to go from the hunter to the hunted. They’ve shown glimpses, i.e., the 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but then they get smacked 31-17 by the Chicago Bears.
The Seahawks slowed down the game and made some big adjustments on both sides of the ball in the win over the Cardinals. On Sunday, the Seahawks have to take that momentum and expand with some explosiveness. Most of it concerns the offense, where the running game might be on the verge of a breakout performance.
​The Seahawks are facing a Raiders defense that ranked last in scoring defense, total defense and rushing defense. Las Vegas has allowed 12 rushing touchdowns and allowed a league-high 5.0 yards per rush. Seattle will have veteran running back Zach Charbonnet and rookie running back Jadarian Price share the backfield for the third consecutive game. Charbonnet had a stellar rushing performance last week against Arizona, while Price was the team’s leading receiver .
​This game is first-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury’s opportunity to unleash the full potential of the rushing offense and have it develop more for the bye week next week. This game is also a chance for wide receiver Rashid Shaheed to get back into the offense’s rhythm after missing the two games.
​The Dark Side Defense needs to continue developing, especially when it comes to defending against the short passing game. The losses to the Bears and the San Francisco 49ers showed the Seahawks’ defense could get worn down. Last week, the Seahawks took away the Cardinals’ short passing game and limited star tight end Trey McBride. Second-year nickelback Nick Emmanwori had a breakthrough performance with his ability to cover tight ends.
​The Seahawks are facing a Raiders’ offense that excelled at getting the ball to tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer, who are two of the leading receivers for Las Vegas. The Dark Side Defense can create a bad game for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza , who is starting his first game for the Raiders.
Last week versus the Cardinals was about being better on fourth down and in the red zone. Now, the Seahawks need to build more on against an offensive-minded head coach in Klint Kubiak, who was the Seahawks’ offensive coordinator last season and knows the Dark Side Defense’s weaknesses.

title: 49ers Coach Gets Candid About Keenan Allen Debut
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers debut of Keenan Allen could not have gone better for the team. It is hard to incorporate a new receiver into the mix, especially in the middle of the week. So, Allen catching five passes for 61 yards in his first game with the team is a good sign of things to come.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan made it clear he was happy with the performance .
“We involved him in a lot of stuff, and you never know how the coverages are going to go and stuff, but I thought he did a hell of a job,” said Shanahan after the game.
Shanahan noted that the team did not have many restrictions for Allen in his debut. The plan was to let him play as much as he could handle or understand in the playbook.
The 49ers coach admitted that Allen did not play in two-minute situations because he did not pick up the playbook that fast yet. Aside from that, the team let him take on a full snap share.
“We never just said it was just these plays,” admitted Shanahan on the game plan this week. “You know, we knew to be smart with him, but we told him to try to learn everything. The stuff in the game plan, he told us he had down on Saturday, and he felt good with all that stuff.”
Allen averaged a season-high 2.9 yards per route run in the win. It was the most efficient game of his season.
The 34-year-old veteran said that he leaned on his experience of being a player who can be quarterback-friendly. He did what he knows quarterbacks like, and Brock Purdy found him.
“Just be quarterback-friendly, be an outlet,” said Allen . “Always try to be in his vision, and give him all the, you know, be able to make a play. As I said, he's tried to stay in his vision.”
All of a sudden, the 49ers wide receiver corps looks much better. Allen entered the room, and Deebo Samuel returned from injury. Demarcus Robinson was in his second game back from injury, but he only needed to be depth.
That is because second-year receiver Jordan Watkins has ascended into a starter. This is with their supposed top two pass catchers, Mike Evans and De’Zhaun Stribling out with injuries. We will see how things shake up once those two come back and Allen gets more comfortable.

title: Why the Win vs. Cowboys Could Be Brock Purdy's Best Game with the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers defeated their historic rivals, the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40 at AT&T Stadium to improve their record to 8-1.
Brock Purdy threw three passing touchdowns, two to Christian McCaffrey and one to Deebo Samuel, while McCaffrey, Samuel and rookie Kaelon Black each added a rushing touchdown.
Their performances were simply sublime across the board , with all of San Francisco's offensive weapons contributing. However, Purdy was the focal point, making a compelling case for this being his best performance since taking the job as the 49ers' starting quarterback.
Purdy finished 22-of-28, passing for 389 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, despite taking five sacks. A 154.5 passer rating. Not quite a perfect rating, but an exceptional one nonetheless.
In addition, according to Next Gen Stats Purdy completed all four of his scramble pass attempts for 135 yards and a touchdown, tying Patrick Mahomes (2018) and Josh Allen (2024) for the most scramble passing yards in a game since 2018.
Plus, on a play that resulted in a Samuel touchdown, Purdy even took on the role of a fullback, helping with a crucial block to help make the score possible.
The manner of the performance is what makes this such a strong contender for Purdy's best game in red and gold. When he wasn't being sacked, his efficiency was almost faultless.
He compensated for cracks in the offensive line, scrambled brilliantly and remained remarkably calm and composed throughout despite the hits. These are the qualities of an elite quarterback.
I've never doubted Purdy's ability, but the overall manner of this performance was particularly impressive. With the 49ers' defence conceding 40 points, the pressure on the offense to keep delivering was immense. For Purdy to maintain such a high standard throughout is simply remarkable.
To produce a performance like this against the franchise's biggest non-divisional rivals only adds to its significance. Purdy clearly relishes the big occasion, and against a rivalry that has stood for decades, this was far from the first time he has risen to the challenge against the Cowboys. He's now 4-0 and remains unbeaten.
With every passing week, he continues to impress in more ways. He constantly strives to improve, with no distractions beyond his own development and that of his team, and almost always delivers in the face of adversity .
He's looking like the frontrunner for this year's MVP . But what matters more to him is winning football games.

title: 5 49ers Who Saw Their Stock Soar in Week 10
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers squeezed out a win in an offensive explosion against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10. Which players stepped up the most in the win?
The question entering the game was what the team would do at receiver with the addition of Keenan Allen and the return of Deebo Samuel. The two veterans were almost certain to impact Jordan Watkins, but the second-year receiver has been making a case to see the field more.
The results in Week 10 were Watkins leading the team in snaps and hauling in two catches for 49 yards. This was a good performance. It will be hard to take him off of the field when Mike Evans is back.
Allen is exactly what the team needed to complete the offense. He came in this week and hardly knew the playbook. Still, he hauled in five passes for 61 yards in the win. The 49ers have not had a possession slot to take on routes over the short middle of the field. They might have finally found one. It looked like he acclimated quickly and will be a nice addition.
Samuel just returned from a hamstring injury in Week 10. He ended up leading the 49ers in rushing with 78 yards and a touchdown. He also added three receptions for 31 yards and a touchdown. His impact in all areas of the field is valuable and was seen in Week 10.
The 49ers have had a three-man rotation at safety over the past two weeks. Mustapha has led the way between the three in the past two games in snaps. He has also been the most impactful player of the three safeties.
He was benched earlier in the year because he was not healthy. However, once he took the field, it has been impossible to take him off. He has to be a full-time starter next week.
Williams has 1.5 sacks and eight pressures in his first five games back from an ACL injury. Last year he had one sack and 19 pressures in nine games. He had four pressures and added half of a sack with Dre Greenlaw in the 49ers' win over the Cowboys. He was their best defensive threat up front. The 49ers need him to continue to progress.

title: 49ers Grades After 46-40 Win Over Cowboys: The Defense has Serious Issues
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers just beat the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
This was one of the best performances of Brock Purdy's career. He didn't have much pass protection -- he got sacked five times -- and his wide receivers struggled to beat man-to-man coverage, which was a big reason he was under so much pressure. And he still posted a passer rating of 154.5. Whenever he got outside the pocket, he killed the Cowboys. He's one of the most poised quarterbacks I've ever seen when everything goes wrong. He is unquestionably an elite quarterback, in the same tier as Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes and Joe Burrow. A few times, Purdy made plays outside the pocket that only a handful of quarterbacks in the world could make, and Burrow isn't one of them. Neither was Tom Brady at any point in his career. Purdy even made a key block downfield on Deebo Samuel's long touchdown run. And Purdy needed to play like a superhero today. Otherwise, the 49ers would have lost to the Cowboys, which is hard to fathom, considering how bad Dallas is.
Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black each averaged 4.8 yards per carry and scored a rushing touchdown. They made the Cowboys respect the run even though the offensive linemen got blown off the ball repeatedly (more on them in a minute). Black had an incredible 25-yard touchdown run during which he ran over Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs. Black also fumbled late in the game and recovered the ball himself. In the future, let McCaffrey close out the win, especially when he's fresh, because his ball security is good and his receiving ability is still elite. Today, he had four catches for 161 yards and two touchdowns. Unreal.
Jordan Watkins had two catches and Deebo Samuel had three plus a touchdown catch, but they struggled to beat the Cowboys' cornerbacks man-to-man. That's a big reason Purdy took five sacks. The only wide receiver who consistently created separation was Keenan Allen, who doesn't know the full playbook yet. He memorized the game plan and caught five passes for 61 yards. He's a good addition to the offense, and he will improve with time in the system. But the biggest addition to the offense was Samuel, who's not really a wide receiver, but it doesn't matter. He finished the game with 109 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. Every offense should have its own Deebo Samuel. Just imagine how good this group will be when Mike Evans comes back.
George Kittle led the team with 9 targets and finished with six catches for 74 yards and no touchdowns. Plus, he was a key reason that the 49ers ran for 214 yards and three touchdowns. He probably would be the Comeback Player of the Year if Fred Warner didn't exist.
Sure, the 49ers scored 46 points and ran for 214 yards, so this group didn't fail. But, 70 of the rushing yards came on a reverse that had very little to do with the offensive line. In addition, this group gave up five sacks and had no answer for Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, who forced a fumble on the 49ers' final drive. It's going to be interesting to see what happens to this offensive line against a great defensive front, like the one they're facing next week when they fly to Mexico City and take on the Vikings.
They never sacked Dak Prescott. He ran out of bounds for no gain in the fourth quarter, and the official scorer gave Dre Greenlaw credit for a sack, but that was charity, and he's not a defensive lineman. Osa Odighizuwa, Mykel Williams and Keion White each hit Dak Prescott, but DeForest Buckner and Nick Bosa didn't. In fact, Bosa was a net negative. He committed three offside penalties and rushed past the quarterback countless times. The offensive tackles just pushed him out of the play, and he didn't fight back. The 49ers were counting on him and Buckner to be their big additions at the deadline, but neither made a positive impact in this game. Too bad they didn't trade for an edge rusher when they could have. Now, they have to make do with what they have and hope that Bosa isn't cooked.
Fred Warner was great -- he had 11 tackles, a quarterback hit and a forced fumble that the officials missed. He's one of the greatest defensive players of all time, and he should win the Defensive Player of the Year Award. Unfortunately for the 49ers, he can't do it all by himself, and he's not getting much help. Dre Greenlaw looks slow.
They gave up 343 yards and 5 touchdown passes to Dak Freaking Prescott, the most overrated quarterback in football. They also intercepted one pass, but that was a selfish play by Malik Mustapha, because it came on fourth down and cost the 49ers 30 yards of field position. Deommodore Lenoir got picked on all game by George Pickens, who finished with 145 yards and 3 touchdowns. Renardo Green wasn't much better before he left the game with an injury. His replacement, rookie Ephysians Prysock, gave up a touchdown catch and lots of catches. This secondary is average at best, and it's bad when one starter goes down. In hindsight, they probably should have traded for a defensive back. Now, they have to hope that Nate Hobbs can get healthy, which he hasn't done yet this season.
Eddy Pineiro didn't miss any kicks for the second game in a row, and Corliss Waitman ended the game with a beautiful punt that stayed in bounds and pinned the Cowboys inside the 20-yard line with just a few seconds left in the game. Hard to believe the game came down to that.
The first half was rough for Kyle Shanahan, as he got Purdy sacked four times and couldn't establish a run game. In the second half, Shanahan figured out how to work around his shaky offensive line and wide receivers, particularly by running with Kaelon Black and Deebo Samuel and throwing to Christian McCaffrey. Kyle Shanahan never has coached as well as he's coaching this season. Both he and Purdy are at the top of their games, which is a big reason the 49ers are considered legit contenders.
Unfortunately for the 49ers, their defense is not championship caliber. In this game, it did nothing well. It didn't rush the quarterback, stop the run or cover anyone. It stunk. And it probably would have given up more than 30 points last week if the Raiders hadn't turned the ball over five times in the second half. And it gave up 29 points to the Falcons. Raheem Morris is searching for answers he can't find. None of his blitzes worked. And as a result, his secondary got exposed. To win a Super Bowl this season, the 49ers will have to win it with their offense, which is never easy to do, because defense wins championships.

title: 7 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 10 Win Over Cowboys: Superhero Brock Purdy
full_text:
Well, that was too close for comfort.
The San Francisco 49ers defeat the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 in a thrilling shootout. There was a lot to love about the 49ers' performance, but also some negatives. Let's dive into the seven biggest takeaways from their Week 10 victory.
You cannot say enough positive things about Brock Purdy's performance today. The best and simplest way to put it is that he was magical, especially in the first half.
His highlight play of the game came in the first half when he scrambled to his right and found Christian McCaffrey for a 74-yard touchdown. Purdy had no business making a play there. He pulled a rabbit out of his hat like a true magician.
Purdy was awesome from start to finish, and he did so with his offensive line having its worst pass-protection performance of the season. He finished the game completing 22 of 28 passes for 389 passing yards, three touchdowns, and no turnovers.
Purdy's performance against the Cowboys will strengthen his MVP case. He put on his superhero cape in this game and was a major factor in the 49ers' win.
Another major factor in the win was McCaffrey. Not only was he elite in helping Purdy on the 74-yard touchdown play, but he essentially iced the game in the last few minutes with a 66-yard catch-and-score. He was wide open, too.
Someone on the Cowboys needs to get fired for that. McCaffrey may not be an elite player on handoffs, although he did have a sweet 16-yard touchdown run, but he's still a phenomenal receiver out of the backfield. Leaving him open was a choice.
The 49ers continue to look wise for drafting Kaelon Black in the third round despite a ton of noise from critics (I was one). Black was tremendous today, rushing 11 times for 53 yards and a score.
It was by far his best outing of the season, highlighted by his monstrous run where he trucked Caleb Downs and shrugged off Cobie Durant for a 25-yard touchdown in the third quarter.
Black complements McCaffrey so perfectly. He's such a tough, bulldozing runner. He gives the 49ers a dynamic that they haven't had in the running game, and it's been extremely helpful.
Keenan Allen barely joined the 49ers five days ago and hasn't had a Bye Week this year. I thought it would be a good idea if they sat him this game so he could rest and have more time to learn the offense. Boy, was I wrong.
Allen had a solid impact in this game, tallying five catches for 61 yards. His contributions were huge, especially in moving the chains. That is exactly what the 49ers brought him in for, and they're already seeing a return on investment.
Welcome back, Deebo Samuel. After missing Week 5 with a hamstring injury, Samuel returned looking better than ever. As in his last stint in Dallas with the 49ers, he haunted the Cowboys.
Samuel registered two touchdowns, including a vintage 70-yard run on a reverse handoff. The blocking on the play was perfect, too, with help from Purdy of all people. It's not a coincidence that as soon as Samuel came back, the 49ers started hitting explosive plays again.
Where is the 49ers' pass rush? Are they snoozing? They were nonexistent against the Cowboys. It's a big reason the Cowboys put up 40 points. Dak Prescott was clean throughout the game.
A pass-rushing unit that consists of Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner, and Osa Odighizuwa needs to be much better than this. It was a pitiful performance, which is a major concern for the 49ers if it doesn't wake up soon.
One of the reasons Purdy's performance against Dallas was so magical was because he did it without adequate pass protection for the majority of the game.
The Cowboys aren't a fierce pass-rushing force. Yet the 49ers' offensive line was getting destroyed in the trenches throughout the game. It felt like Purdy was under duress on nearly every dropback.
If they struggled against the Cowboys, they'll certainly be in for it next week against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings' defense. Buckle up.

title: Exclusive: 49ers TE George Kittle Opens Up On Tough Moments During Achilles Rehab
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle’s Achilles injury was one of the offseason’s biggest storylines.
People questioned whether he’d be back for Week 1 and whether he’d ever return to operating at the peak of his powers. Suffering an Achilles injury at 32, with his 33rd birthday approaching, was far from ideal at this stage of his career.
Regardless of what he went on to produce on the field, even though he's played at an incredible standard so far , an injury rehab as gruelling as his meant months of hard work to get back on track. Kittle reflected on some of the toughest moments in an interview with 49ers on SI’s Henry Cheal, pinpointing a few that stood out.
"Honestly, the first challenge I experienced was on my very first day back home after surgery," Kittle stated.
"I was still taking painkillers, and I tried to walk up a flight of stairs but almost fell back down them. That was my first really difficult day, and I realised I couldn't even walk upstairs normally.
"In terms of rehabilitation, another difficult stage was when the cast first came off. There were no more painkillers, and I was just dealing with all the aches and pains.
"I remember they cut my cast off, and I immediately started doing marble pickups and some strength exercises. I was straight out of the cast and already doing those exercises. It was painful, and I remember thinking, "This is terrible!"
"That pain lasts for a while. Eventually, it starts to ease, your body gets used to things again, and the process becomes much more straightforward."
Kittle added that having things to look forward to and future plans in place helped motivate him to get back on track.
"I think the second big challenge was learning to trust myself to walk again," he explained.
"I was following a fairly fast rehabilitation plan because, when I tore my Achilles, I had a trip to Bandon Dunes planned with my friends to play golf. There were around 14 of us going, and I thought, 'Well, I can't miss that!'
"So my main goal was to be walking by the time the trip came around, and thankfully, I managed to do it. I literally came off crutches just two days before we went.
"But trusting myself to walk that much was really strange. You just don't trust yourself, and you feel like you're going to fall over.
"Once I got through that, though, it gave me a lot more confidence. Learning to walk again was definitely a struggle."

title: Trent Williams Reveals the Benefits of the 49ers' Aging Roster
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams highlights the advantages of having an experienced, veteran-heavy roster.
Williams is one of the oldest players on the team, but many of the stars synonymous with San Francisco’s success over the past few years are either approaching 30 or already past that age range.
As a result, the 49ers have one of the oldest rosters in the league , something Williams believes can provide an intriguing recruitment model for younger players to learn from and follow.
"All our young, super talented guys that we have, pretty much every position room has a north star, somebody that they can look to and actually follow and literally learn how to do it the way we do it," Williams said on the TK Show podcast .
"I think it's a beautiful structure to the locker room, having a guy like [newest wide receiver addition] Keenan [Allen], just a guy that knows how to win.
"Obviously, he's a household name. If you play in this league any amount of time, you know who Keenan Allen is. To have another guy like that in the fold, and gritty too, one of those players that plays their butt off, carries his heart on his sleeve, a really good natural-born leader. So, just really happy to see what they did.
"It's just talent coming out of the woodwork," Williams added. "But yeah, you look in that huddle, and not only do you see the stars, the guys with all the Pro Bowls, but you see the guys with careers budding in that direction.
"I would say that this is one of the more talented teams that I've been on, and I think one of the more composed teams, too. I'll say that.
"And I think the veteran leadership definitely plays a huge part in that."
Veterans offer an abundance of knowledge, experience and insight that younger players can lean on as they develop. Williams believes this is the type of roster-building model Shanahan would favor, although it does come with potential drawbacks, as older players are naturally more susceptible to injuries.
"It does seem more and more like a team that Kyle loved, from top to bottom, is what he preferred.
"I would hope so, but it's too early to tell. We're only eight games in. We ain't even halfway there yet."
The 49ers are 7-1 and the top seed in both the NFC West and the conference.

title: 49ers Could Face Another Coaching Exit This Offseason
full_text:
It is starting to feel like every season ends with an assistant under Kyle Shanahan either getting hired as a head coach or getting head coach interviews. So, it should not be a surprise that offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak was ranked as the third best head coaching candidate in the NFL by Brent Sobelski of Bleacher Report.
Sobelski noted that Kubiak has everything that NFL owners crave when it comes to their next head coaching hire.
“If there's one thing NFL owners love, they are often smitten by young offensive minds with a pedigree,” wrote Sobelski. “Technically, that's three different qualifiers. But they're all wrapped up into one with the San Francisco 49ers' Klay Kubiak.”
Kubiak is just 38 years old. He has been with the 49ers as an offensive assistant since 2021 and he has been their offensive coordinator for two seasons. So, he is young, he coaches offense, and he has pedigree.
What might help him more than his ties to Shanahan are his family ties. Gary Kubiak, his father, was a long-time NFL coach. His brother Klint Kubiak has also had a success in his first year as the Las Vegas Raiders head coach. Owners know the family and will think it is in his blood.
Still, it is easy to tie everything back to Shanahan, especially when Gary played Kyles father, Mike, on the Denver Broncos.
Sean McVay and Matt LaFleur did not work the 49ers, but they were coordinators who came up as assistants under Shanahan.
Current head coaches who did work for the 49ers include Robert Saleh, Kubiak, Mike LaFleur, Demeco Ryans and Jeff Hafley. Mike McDaniel was hired away from the 49ers previously as well.
It is clear that teams are interested in getting a piece of this coaching tree, whether it be on the offensive or defensive side of the football.
Shanahan has had a lot of his assistants turn into coaches and hit. Kubiak has the family history on his side. He fits all of the other qualifications teams are looking for. It would not be a surprise if this was the last year that Kubiak was coaching for the 49ers. At the least, the team must prepare for him to get interviews.

title: 49ers' Trade Plans Reveal Team's Biggest Need (it's Not What You Think)
full_text:
As reports after the NFL trade deadline have started to surface, it has started to become clear what the San Francisco 49ers' biggest need actually was. While the team was linked to edge rushers and they settled on a wide receiver, the team appeared to be most interested in adding a pass-catching tight end at the trade deadline.
Earlier in the week, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN noted that the 49ers were interested in Denver Broncos tight end Evan Engram. However, Denver is contending and did not want to lose a player.
Now, Adam Schefter of ESPN has reported that the team was also interested in Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert. Schefter reported that the 49ers called, but the Eagles hardly listened.
“While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted -- Dallas Goedert,” wrote Schefter. “Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027.”
Perhaps San Francisco would have added Keenan Allen after they traded for Engram or Goedert. However, it appears as though the pass catcher they wanted was a tight end, and not a receiver.
This makes sense to an extent. They are injured at wide receiver, but all of their pass catchers should be back this season. Deebo Samuel will play this week, and Mike Evans will be back soon. De’Zhaun Stribling could be back to close out the season. When you add in Demarcus Robinson being healthy and Jordan Watkins taking a step, the team has receivers.
However, Jake Tonges has been out since Week 1, and he is not coming back this year. Luke Farrell has played more in his absence, and he is a good blocker, but he brings nothing in the passing game.
A pass-catching tight end to join the blocking-centric Farrell would allow the team to use George Kittle in a more versatile manner. Now, they need him to carry the tight end room in receiving production, taking away from his blocking value.
So, a receiver is nice, but Goedert or Engram had the chance to take the offense to another level. The 49ers missed out.

title: Buccaneers Just Got a Huge Break Ahead of Lions Matchup
full_text:
Following the events that unfolded this weekend, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers sit just one game behind the NFC South-leading New Orleans Saints for the top spot in the division.
There is plenty still to fight for if you are the Bucs, and they will have a tough test against the NFC North leaders, the Detroit Lions, on deck in Week 11.
It will be a challenge for Tampa Bay, but they will fortunately be coming off their bye week when they face Detroit, who will be coming back from an international game in Germany.
The Bucs have likely caught another break heading into the matchup, as Lions' star pass rusher, Aiden Hutchinson, suffered a serious knee injury in their win over the New England Patriots.
Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL early in the first quarter against the Patriots after celebrating a sack on Drake Maye.
Just brutal… pic.twitter.com/W6OOuamVBQ
He will miss the remainder of the 2026 season.
The injury marks Hutchinson's second serious injury of his career. He suffered a tibia and fibula fracture in his leg during the 2024 season. It's a super unfortunate circumstance for one of the best edge rushers in the league, but it will make life easier for the Bucs' offensive line.
In Hutchinson's stead, the Lions will likely rotate the likes of rookie Derrick Moore and veteran DJ Wonnum.
The Bucs have leaned on the ground game all season, and likely will continue to do so as Baker Mayfield and Zac Robinson try to figure out how to fix the passing game. However, that might have to wait, as it was reported that the Bucs are also dealing with a significant injury problem of their own after Mayfield suffered a lower-leg injury against the Chicago Bears.
If Mayfield is unable to go against the Lions, the Bucs will turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels once again.
Missing two stars in an important NFC matchup is never ideal, but for Tampa Bay, the absence of Hutchinson should give them a bit more confidence in coming away with a victory as they hunt down the Carolina Panthers in the division.

title: Something Is Seriously Off With One Buccaneers Star This Season
full_text:
Tristan Wirfs might be the best player on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Throughout his career, Wirfs has earned multiple All-Pro and Pro Bowl selections, as well as a Super Bowl ring in his rookie season. He has established himself as one of the best offensive linemen in football and is well on his way to a Hall of Fame career with the Bucs.
So why in the world is he struggling with penalties this 2026 season?
So far, Wirfs has five false start penalties this year, which is tied for the third most in the NFL. According to Greg Auman of Fox Sports, Wirfs has 16 such penalties in his previous six seasons combined. So why is Wirfs dealing with so many mental lapses this season?
Tristan Wirfs is tied for third-most false starts in the league with five. He had 16 total in six seasons before this year. Has already matched his career high for a season. https://t.co/WMEswGRpiD
Well, the first reason could be Zac Robinson. With a new offense comes new challenges, and we've seen the Bucs this year struggle with many different things offensively, especially in terms of communication. It always feels like the Bucs are late snapping the ball and getting the play off offensively. It would not be a surprise at all if the miscommunication falls into offensive line issues as well.
It may also be prudent to take a look at the center and quarterback situations. The Bucs have had two different starting quarterbacks this season with Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels, which can lead to so many differences in how the offense is run — from a Robinson standpoint and to how Mayfield and Daniels like things done on offense.
Finally, take a look at Graham Barton and how he's done this year. Yes, he's improved with regard to blocking, but one has to wonder how his communication with the offensive line has been, given the false-start issues. Is Barton struggling with offensive line adjustments before the snap? Is it Mayfield and Daniels, or is it Robinson and the coaching staff? These are some of the biggest questions that are on Bucs fans' minds right now.
While Wirfs has been playing fantastic ball this season, we will have to wait and see if these false-start issues continue. It could be a symptom of a much larger problem that has been plaguing the Bucs' offense throughout this season.

title: Buccaneers Get Concerning Development Involving Baker Mayfield
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got the week off in Week 10, resting and recovering during their bye week — but it seems like their most important player may have really needed it.
The Bucs are 3-6, and despite that, they're just a half-game back from the NFC South lead. Quarterback Baker Mayfield was absent for three of those games with a dislocated thumb, an injury he is still dealing with.
He's been back for three games, but now, he could be missing some more time with a different injury he picked up before the bye week.
NFL insider Mike Garafolo reported Sunday that Mayfield injured his lower leg against the Chicago Bears in Week 9. It is apparently serious enough that Mayfield may not play against the Detroit Lions in Week 11.
Garafolo reported that Mayfield has been in and out of a walking boot, but that the injury is not severe enough for an IR designation and that it would be short-term.
The #Lions are up big in Germany right now then head back to Detroit to face the #Buccaneers . Right now, it’s unclear whether they’ll see Baker Mayfield, as sources say he’s dealing with a lower-leg injury suffered against the #Bears https://t.co/PJvIgW0idw
It's unknown on which play or plays Mayfield suffered his lower-leg injury, but Mayfield played the entirety of the game in Week 9. He struggled, completing 18 passes in 32 attempts with no touchdowns and two interceptions — the latter of which went for a pick-six.
So far this season, Mayfield has thrown for 922 yards with three touchdowns to four interceptions. He has a QBR of 31.8, 30th in the NFL, and his dropback EPA per play of -0.297 is the worst in the NFL among qualifying quarterbacks, per SumerSports.
If Mayfield cannot go against the Lions, he'll once again be deputized by undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels. Daniels filled in for Mayfield for the three games Mayfield missed with his thumb injury, and during that time, he's put up 501 yards for three touchdowns and five interceptions with a QBR of 50.3.
The Bucs will play the Lions in a must-win game next weekend— lose, and they'll fall to 3-7 with a worse chance of making the playoffs. The Bucs gave Mayfield a three-year extension worth $55 million a year in hopes that he'd be their long-term franchise quarterback, but they may have to win that game without him next Sunday to stay alive.

title: Buccaneers Rookie Just Got Fined For Doing This
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers aren't playing football this weekend, as they're recuperating on their bye week in Week 10.
The Bucs' offense has been struggling, and it's a big reason why the team is 3-6. The defense is elite, however, and that's partially because defensive rookies like linebacker Josiah Trotter and defensive back Keionte Scott have played just as well, if not better, than the Bucs were hoping when they were drafted.
Scott has played very well, and he and the rest of the defense are on a much-needed break. He'll have a dent in his wallet during the bye week, though, because he was fined for a play that occurred in the team's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears.
Scott was fined $6,540 by the NFL for a hit on Chicago Bears wideout Kalif Raymond. Scott connected with Raymond on a head-to-head hit, but the play was not flagged during the game.
Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie DB Keionte Scott was fined $6,540 for unnecessary roughness (use of helmet) for this hit on WR Kalif Raymond. There was no flag on this play. FWIW, OLB Rueben Bain Jr. was not fined for his hit that caused WR Luther Burden III's concussion. pic.twitter.com/N8Fu8TgF9f
Scott has started at nickel for the Buccaneers all year, replacing Jacob Parrish, who kicked outside. Scott has played great football for Tampa Bay so far, netting 32 solo tackles and defending four passes in Tampa Bay.
Scott's physical style of play and tackling ability were both the more intriguing parts of his NFL draft profile coming out of Miami. It has been a positive part of his game so far, but in this case, it seemingly came back to hurt him and he'll have to literally pay the price for his hit on Raymond.
His teammate at Miami, Rueben Bain Jr., also had a hard hit on Bears wideout Luther Burden — that hit was not fined.
Scott will get one more day off on Sunday before he has to report back to One Buccaneer Place on Monday. The Bucs will face off against the Detroit Lions, and when they do, they'll try to get the win and avoid sliding down to a 3-7 start as they try to win the division.

title: Buccaneers Have One Big Thing Going For Them in Last 8 Games
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a lot of work to do to get where they hope to go. They're currently 3-6 despite being just half a game behind the NFC South lead, and they'll have to start stacking some wins if they hope to genuinely compete in the postseason and beyond.
The Bucs have won all of their NFC South contests so far, which helps, but they have four more of those games to go (including both their matchups against the New Orleans Saints). If they want to win the division, though, they'll likely have to win more than those four games.
Thankfully, their schedule is very favorable when it comes to doing that, because the Bucs don't play many good teams for the rest of the year.
The Bucs have the easiest remaining strength of schedule in football over these next eight weeks, with a combined winning percentage of just .403.
The four NFC South games, with every remaining division opponent winning just three games so far, help with that. But that isn't all — they play the Baltimore Ravens (4-5) and the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on their schedule as well. Of their remaining eight opponents, just two of them have a winning record.
The two teams that do have winning records, though, will be quite the challenge. Tampa Bay will face off against the Detroit Lions next week in Week 11, and the Bucs will hope to avoid falling to 3-7 against a talented Detroit team. They'll also play the Los Angeles Rams at home in Week 17 — that game was touted as a crucial game for Tampa Bay before the season, but their season may already be over by the time that game comes around.
Tampa Bay's schedule format is also very, very beneficial. The Bucs will not play back-to-back road games all year, and they also have two home games in a row against the Panthers and Chargers back-to-back in Weeks 12 and 13. That's another schedule quirk that could help Tampa Bay.
The Bucs need to play good football to make any of this count, though, and they'll start by trying to knock off Detroit on the road in Week 11.

title: Buccaneers' Most Outstanding Players at Halfway Point of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are sitting at 3-6 after falling short against the Chicago Bears, but head into their bye week at the midway point of the season, just half a game out of first place in the NFC South.
The Bucs have looked better than their record suggests, but despite how well their running game and defense have been, they have struggled to find much of anything in the passing game.
Now, at the midway point of the season, these are the players who are playing outstanding ball and likely the ones who will help lead Tampa Bay to a stronger finish and help reclaim the division title.
The Bucs gambled by making Zyon McCollum their CB1 this season, and boy, is it paying off in a big way.
McCollum has transformed into a lockdown boundary corner, constantly locking down opposing teams' primary threats on the outside.
McCollum has been relentless in the secondary, ranking third in the league in interceptions (4) and second in the league in passes defended (11). He is also allowing an extremely low passer rating when targeted, allowing only 21 passes to be completed against him through nine games.
The offense has struggled, but the running game has been one of the best in the league — and it's been led by Bucky Irving.
Irving has been a terror on the ground after a slow start and finds himself with the fourth-most rushing yards in the NFL (825) and sixth-most rushing touchdowns (7).
Irving has had his full talents on display, showcasing efficiency and explosiveness along the way. He is averaging 4.94 yards per carry, more than Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry and James Cook, and he has the fourth-most 20-plus-yard runs with six.
The Bucs' secondary has been key to keeping them in games this season, and along with McCollum, Jacob Parrish has been a large reason for the success.
Parrish moved from the nickel spot to the outside this season, and somehow, he has improved as a defender. He has been an elite tackler and has excelled in short-to-intermediate coverage, limiting yards after the catch.
Parrish grades out as one of the most reliable corners in the league, limiting explosive plays and currently leading the NFL in passes defended with 14. He also has two interceptions in his sophomore season.
Josiah Trotter is a rookie, but he is playing anything like that early in his career. Trotter is playing like a veteran and has been a massive upgrade at the linebacker position.
He has grasped Todd Bowles' aggressive scheme, showcasing a high run-stop win percentage and a low missed-tackle rate when in the box. Talk about gap discipline.
His total tackles have put him in elite company amongst the rest of the league. While his run-stopping has been incredible, he is still developing into a backer who can be better against the pass.

title: Buccaneers Offense On Pace to Achieve Rare NFL Feat
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers aren't dead in the water just yet despite their 3-6 record.
They sit just half a game out of the NFC South lead, but enter the midway point of the season on a bye week, where they could drop further down.
The Bucs have been great defensively and running the ball, but they have struggled to get anything going in the passing game, leading to the offense being one-dimensional.
That one-dimensional offense has them on pace for a rare NFL feat if things are to stay the course.
Tampa Bay currently has 1,475 rushing yards to 1,277 passing yards at the midway point of the season. Not a single other NFL team can say the same.
It's an interesting statistic, to say the least, and it drastically shows just how poor the passing game has been for the Bucs in today's modern NFL.
The last time a team finished a season with more rushing yards than passing yards was when the Chicago Bears did so in 2022, when they ran for 3,014 yards and threw for 2,219. They finished the season 3-14.
Baker Mayfield has not lived up to the contract extension that he made such a big deal about leading up to the season, putting up the worst statistical season of his veteran career.
Mayfield also missed time due to injury, meaning the Bucs had to rely on the ground game more with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at the helm.
The play-calling by Zac Robinson and the lack of elite weapons on the outside have also been inhibitors of the passing attack.
It would be shocking to see the Bucs outpace their passing yardage with rushing yardage, but that is how things are rolling as of now.
The hope is that things can get figured out when it comes to throwing the ball over the bye week, thus making the offense more balanced. If they are able to do so, then it will be tough for opposing defenses to try to cover every aspect of the offense, leading to more points on the board and more wins.

title: One Major Buccaneers Concern Must Be Addressed During Bye Week
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are spending their bye week searching for answers.
The Bucs are just half a game out of the NFC South, but they're 3-6 and in danger of plummeting further. Tampa Bay has an elite defense and an elite running game, but their passing game is among the NFL's worst and is dragging the whole team down.
Much has been discussed about the passing game as a whole, but there's one specific part of it that's a major concern for Tampa Bay through nine weeks — and the Bucs need to find a way to fix it fast if they want the passing game to take off.
The best teams in football — and even average ones, for that matter — find ways to pass to the middle of the field. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have failed spectacularly when it comes to this, and their pass game is paying for it as a result.
The league average for passes between the hashes is at 10.4% this year so far. The Bucs have thrown just 11 passes to the middle of the field all year (Baker Mayfield has thrown eight and Jalon Daniels has thrown three). That's just 4.9% of their attempts so far this year, and both their total attempts to the middle of the field and their percentage of throws to the middle of the field rank 31st in the NFL — only the Denver Broncos are worse in both categories, per SumerSports.
The best team in the league at finding the middle of the field is the Houston Texans in both attempts and percentage of attempts. Some of the NFL's best offenses lead the league in middle-of-the-field percentage, like the Jacksonville Jaguars (No. 2), the Chicago Bears (No. 3) and the San Francisco 49ers (No. 4), among others.
Tampa Bay's passing offense has the entire area blocked off at the moment, and the team is suffering for it. But why aren't they getting the ball there so far this season?
There are multiple factors, of course.
The Buccaneers don't seem to have any receivers who can survive in high-traffic areas and have the route-running acumen on inside-breaking routes to thrive there. This also involves physical toughness — first-round draft pick Emeka Egbuka has struggled with that for most of his NFL career to date; Chris Godwin is in the tail end of his career and his age makes it harder to take those hits; and wideout Tez Johnson is among the smallest wideouts in the NFL.
That could be making offensive coordinator Zac Robinson spooked, and could prevent him from putting first reads between the hashes in a progression-based read system. Mayfield could also be frightened to throw to the middle of the field as many NFL quarterbacks have been in the past, but with Daniels throwing there at just as little a rate, Robinson's scheming could be more of the culprit.
No matter what the reason is, the Bucs need to figure out how to unlock that part of the field in the passing game. Getting it to at least a league-average rate would be very beneficial for this team, but it will take a combination of multiple parties on the offensive side of the ball to make that happen.
Tampa Bay will play the Detroit Lions on the road in Week 11 after their bye week this weekend.

title: Why Bucs Bringing Back Bruce Arians Would Be a Big Mistake
full_text:
When many think of the idea of Bruce Arians returning to coaching, specifically to the Buccaneers, there's excitement and a desire for it to happen. I fall into this camp — Arians would give the team a jolt of energy they have missed since he left following the 2021 season.
However, there are factors that need to be considered here when we look at the entirety of the picture of what it would truly mean for this organization if Arians were to once more be the head coach of this football team..
This first question that needs to be asked — Would Bruce Arians genuinely be ok with the Bucs firing Todd Bowles so he could take his job?
Remember, Arians retired in part so Bowles could have a chance to be a head coach again, and for his health. Arians is incredibly loyal to his coaches, and Bowles has been a friend and protege to Arians for many years. I still believe the Buccaneers will move on from Bowles after this season, but it needs to be mentioned that Arians might not be keen on joining the team that fires his close friend.
The second question that needs to be asked is whether Baker Mayfield and this offense would be a good fit for Arians if he were to come back.
Tom Brady, Mike Evans and more aren't around anymore, and I think Mayfield has a great arm, but there could be a lot of similarities to the 2019 Jameis Winston season rather than the great years of Brady.
Also, how would Emeka Egbuka and the other receivers look? This hasn't exactly impressed with Zac Robinson as offensive coordinator, so would they be a good fit in Arians' offense? Would we see a big dip in usage of Bucky Irving, one of the Bucs' best offensive players? Arians loves passing the football and it always felt that the running game would get put to the side. Would you be okay with potentially the best offensive player on the team, Irving, getting the ball less?
Finally, one must consider that Arians would bring back many of his guys on the offensive coaching staff, I imagine. Byron Leftwich could be back as OC, or Harold Goodwin, or even Thad Lewis. Also, I imagine either Larry Foote, Kacy Rodgers or James Bettcher would be DC without Bowles coming back to fill the role.
It also must be said that in a scenario where Arians coaches for a couple more seasons and retires again, would the Bucs simply promote a Leftwich, Goodwin, Lewis, Foote or Rodgers to the head coaching role as they did with Bowles? Would you be okay with that potential future? I would say that this is the biggest question one would need to ask themselves.

title: Will Buccaneers Regret Not Trading Away Players?
full_text:
We are at the midway point of the NFL season, and the trade deadline has come and gone without the Tampa Bay Buccaneers making any moves whatsoever.
At 3-6, the Bucs could have decided to sell off some of their players in order to obtain some draft capital or become buyers to elevate certain positions on their roster to make a strong run at the NFC South and a playoff run.
General manager Jason Licht and company decided to do neither, standing pat with what they currently have. But was not selling and looking ahead to the future the right move?
The argument for selling usually comes from recognizing when a team's ceiling doesn't match its financial layout or expectations, allowing the front office to accelerate into its next chapter rather than trying to force a square peg into a round hole.
The Bucs' ceiling is pretty obvious at this point — potentially make the playoffs with a likely first-round exit.
For a roster that currently has aging "star" players taking up large portions of the cap with heavy extensions, injecting cost-controlled, youthful talent and draft picks into the future of the team might have been the better move. Especially given how weak the division is.
In today's modern NFL, maximizing your asset value comes at a premium, and it appears that Licht and company missed the ball on that once again when they could have received mid-to-high draft capital from contending teams for the services of guys like Vita Vea and Antoine Winfield Jr.
With how weak the NFC South currently is, the Bucs remain in the thick of things, just half a game back of the division lead. With the front office deciding not to move anyone at the deadline, they believe they have a legitimate chance of winning the division behind their strong running game and top defense.
Trading away key veterans mid-season would have signaled that the organization is looking ahead rather than fighting for its playoff hopes in the present. For Todd Bowles and his staff, waving the white flag when you still have a shot at making the playoffs would ruin the recent momentum and could fracture the dynamic within the locker room.
Whether management will come to regret not selling at the deadline will remain to be seen until the results start piling up on the field over the back half of the season.
If the Bucs somehow pull things together and make the playoffs, not selling would seemingly have been the right move.
However, if they miss the playoffs for a second consecutive season, then all aspects of the organization will come under scrutiny for not doing what it takes to either win or set the team up for a better future.

title: Titans Mill: Cam Ward's Growth is Slowly Answering Tennessee's Biggest Question of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are 1-8 and coming off a 17-point loss to the division-rival Jacksonville Jaguars at home. Seen purely from a broad, objective perspective, you could say the 2026 season is over with already. This season was hardly about making playoff push, though.
Robert Saleh's first season in Nashville was, and is, about Cam Ward. The second-year QB is the center of the Titans' operations; that was the plan coming into this year, and if it had to change, the outlook of this franchise was going to change with it.
In today's Titans Mill, I'm happy to report that Ward just had his second solid game in a row. After a career performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8, Ward completed 28 passes on 39 attempts for 231 yards and two touchdowns. Ward's one INT came early and wasn't entirely his fault.
This was the third time this season Ward hit 200 yards in a game, and the second in two weeks. In his first six contests, Ward had thrown just four touchdowns to five picks. Since that matchup with the Bengals, that ratio is a much more favorable 4:1.
Don't get me wrong, the Titans are very much trying to win football games right now. But as has been said time and time again, the team's trade deadline moves loudly hinted at a franchise mindset geared toward the draft.
Of course, Ward comes into play there in that Tennessee doesn't want to take another QB. Any sign that Ward's development is paying off should be taken and ran with; we may be a little late to receive those signs, but some teams never get there at all.
From this point forward, the important thing is to set Ward up for success to finish out the year. The key to that on offense is clear as day.
In yesterday's loss, Tennessee had an astounding 49% no-huddle rate. That's the highest of any team this season, topping their own previous bar (from Week 8) at 41.4%.
Tempo, tempo, tempo. It may be slow, and presently not leading to wins, but the Titans are figuring out what works for their young signal caller. Yesterday's progress even came without WR1 Carnell Tate and multiple offensive linemen.
Maybe it was the difficult stretch up to this point, but Ward has made two games feel like an eternity for Titans fans in the best way. Going forward, win or lose, Titans fans should be primarily concerned with Ward getting better and better.
If he enters this coming offseason on a heater, optimism should rise to a recent high given a great draft.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Why Cedric Gray’s Week 10 Performance Leaves Titans No Choice but to Start Him Over Cody Barton
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans fell to 1-8 in the 2026 NFL season on Sunday, as head coach Robert Saleh's squad suffered a 40-23 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars at home.
Though Tennessee lost by nearly three touchdowns against Jacksonville, there were still a few positives from the contest, including linebacker Cedric Gray's performance. Gray, who lost his starting gig before the season, has played a limited role on Saleh's defense despite breaking the franchise record for total tackles (164) in 16 starts in 2025.
However, with Cody Barton and Anthony Hill Jr. out with injuries on Sunday , Gray was elevated to the starting lineup and proved why the Titans need to keep him there for the rest of the year.
According to in-game data from Pro Football Focus, Gray played 68 of Tennessee's 74 defensive snaps . In those snaps, the North Carolina product led the team in total tackles (9), tallied two tackles for loss, and also knocked down two passes.
Gray also snagged an interception off Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence off a tip in the first quarter, and had five defensive stops. His 83.1 tackling grade was also team-high, and his 72.7 coverage grade was second among Titans defenders.
Gray was all over the field on Sunday, and his tenacious play should make it easy for the Titans to decide on the linebacker room moving forward.
Though Barton's veteran experience next to a young linebacker like Hill is valuable, Tennessee can't continue to keep Gray on the bench. The 24-year-old is better in pass coverage, plays with more energy, and has a more secure long-term future in Nashville than Barton, who could be a cut candidate in the offseason.
A young linebacker duo of Gray and Hill would give the Titans' defense new life and energize the position group. Barton would still be a solid veteran voice, but would be slated for a rotational and special teams role, which fits him best at this stage of his career.
Tennessee will travel to AT&T Stadium to take on the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11. We'll see whether the Titans will turn to Gray after his statement outing against the Jaguars and elevate the defense for the second half of the season.

title: Everything Robert Saleh Said After Titans' Loss to Jaguars — Blatant Officiating Miss is Addressed
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans just fell to the Jacksonville Jaguars 40-23 in a game that, based on the surface-level numbers, appears typical. The Titans allowed 40 points for the second straight contest. Cam Ward threw a first-quarter interception. Tennessee's secondary gave up 350+ passing yards.
It's all right there, but this is a Tennessee team that found themselves within once score of the Jags in the fourth quarter. The now 7-2 Jags on the path to contending for a Super Bowl. There are no moral victories to be had in Nashville, but recognizing improvement is a worthy stopping point.
After the game, Robert Saleh gave his usual postgame-presser packed with tidbits Titans fans need to be aware of. We've rounded those up right here.
Unsurprisingly, Saleh addressed the Titans' bending and breaking defense. "If you're giving up 40 a game, you're not going to compete," Tennessee's coach said plainly, before citing third-down scenarios in the red zone as specific points of emphasis.
The Titans forced Jacksonville's offense into 14 third-down positions today, which marked a season-high for the road team. The issue is, the Jaguars were able to convert on half of those; and on their two fourth downs, Jacksonville made good on both.
Titans fans don't need to hear Saleh tell them that this defense is playing below the mark, especially not after trading Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker. All the same, it'll be interesting to watch Tennessee try and make adjustments as the offense keeps growing.
"They picked," Saleh said of the Jaguars, who found Brenton Strange wide open for a touchdown in the third quarter. "They [the officials] said it was within one yard, and it wasn't." Saleh went on to call it a "missed call," adding that he still doesn't understand the roughing the passer penalty on John Franklin-Myers, either.
No words are being minced today. Given Strange's TD was Jacksonville's only score in the third quarter (the Titans scored six points), it's absolutely worth looking back and wondering what would've happened had the officials called it in the opposite direction.
CB Alontae Taylor got hung up in coverage, the Jaguars scored, and Tennessee lost. That's the reality we live in, regardless of Saleh's (agreeable) opinion on the matter. Take a look for yourself here:
Pretty clear this was a pick. https://t.co/NJ7GEgsrOw pic.twitter.com/fNyMjc3cjw
Finally, Saleh encouraged his team's play in defeat, saying he thought they "played their ----- off," going on to suggest that the final tally wasn't "indicative" of the game on the whole. Given the Titans went into the fourth quarter down just a score, Saleh makes a fair point.
There are problems without present solutions for this Tennessee team. 1-8 is a gnarly record no matter how you spin it. Yet, the Titans may have just played their two best games of the season back-to-back, save for their Week 6 victory.
Address the defensive issues, and this roster has the potential to drum up a lot of optimism heading into the offseason.

title: The 1 Takeaway Titans Fans Must Hold on to From Week 10 Defeat vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Fight. That's the word of the day after the Tennessee Titans' loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, to a final tune of 40-23. Robert Saleh's team has fallen to 1-8, and according to the result column alone, this Week 10 defeat looks no different from the rest of the losses Tennessee has taken this season.
It's important to recognize that this team is different than the constantly-losing Titans under previous head coach Brian Callahan. For the second straight contest, Tennessee played a clear playoff team close; the gap today was a runaway fourth quarter (17 to 7) after the Titans failed to convert on a critical fourth down.
After trading Jeffery Simmons, the Titans fell one touchdown short in overtime to the Cincinnati Benals. Long-term S Amani Hooker was traded next, and today, Tennessee played a competitive football game until it came time to take winning chances.
A win is what matters in the end, and you'll likely hear Robert Saleh say something along those lines momentarily in the postgame. Though that's exactly why fans should have hope in this version of the Titans.
Numbers are starting to improve for the players that general manager Mike Borgonzi kept around, and for the guys that were moved, Tennessee returned a massive haul of draft picks. The Titans fought hard today, and that will do until this roster is fully overhauled.
Cam Ward, after an interception in the first quarter, tossed two touchdowns and eclisped 200 yards for the third time this season. Tony Pollard caught one of those scores, extending his own touchdown streak to three games.
LB Cedric Gray notched an interception and - tackles covering for both Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton out with injury. Elic Ayomanor caught five passes for 79 yards without WR1 Carnell Tate leading the way for Tennessee's pass-catchers.
There are still issues, no doubt. The absence of Hooker led to Jags' QB Trevor Lawrence throwing for a brutal 352 yards and three scores. His lone INT came on a tipped pass by DT Solomon Thomas. Brian Daboll's offense getting off to a confusing start certainly limited the Titans' ultimate chances today.
Although, as fans start to look forward to the 2027 season, things feel different at this juncture than they did last season. Robert Saleh, short two near-decade leaders, has this team battling. This team may be short of the potential-contender Jaguars, but wins will come if Tennessee keeps playing this way.
If Titans fans leave with anything today, let it be that. The Titans look well-coached, are growing more polished, and Cam Ward keeps improving. That's a recipe for the sort of leap this team has been trying to take for years now.

title: Tennessee Trails Through 2: Can Titans Overcome Familiar Issues to Stun Jaguars in Second Half?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans entered today's game vs. the Jaguars already shorthanded. It goes without saying that losing Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker was bound to impact the defense negatively, and Cam Ward operating without WR Carnell Tate ( among numerous injuries ) is another knock.
Through two quarters, however, it's not necessarily been the missing of players so much as familiar issues with the Titans. Simmons' loss continues to be felt as Tennessee has struggled to produce any sort of pressure in the first half - usual disruptor Jacob Martin has the Titans' lone sack. The Jaguars lead 16-10.
Though beyond that, LB Cedric Gray managed to pick off QB Trevor Lawrence off a tipped pass. Cam Ward is making plays on the ground with this legs. There are positive things to write home about here, and the Titans remain within striking distance as a result.
Brian Daboll recovered quickly after a slow-going first quarter for his offense. For every bad decision Ward makes, he follows it up with a better one on the opposite end of the spectrum. The Titans are still trailing, but against the best team in the AFC South, this game still looks winnable.
If we look back at this game and see a defeat, it'll be because of mistakes the Titans could have avoided. Daboll opened this contest on nine straight passes; Tony Pollard didn't have a single touch in the first quarter after scoring five touchdowns over the previous two games.
Pollard had four carries in the second quarter, which diversified the offense and allowed Ward to hit a loose Elic Ayomanor for a big gain downfield. A touchdown was eventually thrown to TE Daniel Bellinger to bring the Titans within three, 13-10.
Tennessee doesn't look like a complete football team today, though that shouldn't surprise anybody. What should have folks leaning into their TVs for the second half of this contest are the strides the Titans took heading into the break.
This is a team that's improving a little faster every week. Ward's 99 yards on 11/18 passing simply don't tell the story of a QB who led a scoring drive to keep his team in this game. The aforementioned Gray has looked great in both coverage and between the gaps with a team-leading six tackles. Ayomanor had 70 yards receiving in the first by himself.
Traded veterans, multiple injuries, a Super Bowl contender on the opposite sideline and all, the Titans are in this game. We'll keep you posted heading into a hopeful second half. The Titans will get the ball first.
